3-0008-0000.sourceText:

3-0010-0000.sourceText:
I have received requests for a vote in Parliament from the ECR Group, reaching the medium threshold, on the decisions of the ECON Committee to enter into negotiations on the following file:

– Provision of digital euro services by payment services providers incorporated in Member States whose currency is not the euro.

And from the ECR, PfE and ESN groups on the following file:

– Establishment of the digital euro.

I have also received a request for a vote in Parliament from the S&D Group, reaching the medium threshold, on the decision of the ITRE Committee to enter into negotiations on the following file:

– Critical Raw Materials Act.

The votes on all these three will be held tomorrow.

Concerning the other decisions, by the ITRE Committee and jointly by the SEDE/TRAN and the SEDE/ITRE committees, to enter into interinstitutional negotiations pursuant to Rule 72(1), announced at the opening of the session on Monday 6 July, I have received no request for a vote in Parliament by Members or political groups reaching the medium threshold.

The ECON, SEDE, TRAN and ITRE committees may therefore start negotiations.

3-0012-0000.sourceText:
The next item is the debate on the Council and Commission statements on the conclusions of the European Council meeting of 18-19 June 2026 (2026/2754(RSP)).

We will start with the Commission. I will give the floor to Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič for five minutes.

3-0013-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, to follow up on the Council meetings on 18 and 19 June, the first topic which was discussed by the leaders was Ukraine. For the first time since December 2024 we had conclusions at 27. This is an important step in restoring EU unity on our resolute and lasting support for Ukraine.

We now continue our work to help Ukrainians. First, through financial support, with a first tranche of EUR 3.2 billion from the EUR 90 billion Ukrainian support loan having been disbursed. In the last week, we saw the first disbursement of the EUR 6 billion defence package to support drone procurement.

Second, through raising the costs for Russia. I welcome the Irish Presidency's commitment to reaching an agreement on the 21st sanctions package by next week, and we are banning the entry of former Russian combatants into the European Union.

Leaders were meeting just days after we opened the fundamental clusters for both Ukraine and Moldova, and we will now look to open further clusters before the summer.

Moving to the Middle East, where the interim agreement between the United States and Iran was seen as a meaningful opening towards regional stability; to ensuring freedom of navigation toll-free in the Strait of Hormuz; to making sure that Iran can never possess a nuclear weapon, while addressing concerns related to its ballistic program and regional activities; and ultimately to advancing peace and security across the region.

But events overnight show that much more efforts are needed to ensure long-lasting peace and stability. This just underscores why we see the need to develop other routes and corridors, like IMEC, the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. To that end, we will deepen our engagement with our partners in the Gulf and beyond.

We also welcome the trilateral agreement signed by the United States, Lebanon and Israel. Key next steps are the disarmament of non-state groups and preserving Lebanese sovereignty and territorial integrity. The EU is providing support, including in terms of humanitarian aid.

We are also working to improve the humanitarian situation in Gaza and the West Bank, while the Palestine Donor Group next week will be an occasion to take stock of the Palestinian Authority's reform progress and to advance discussions on Gaza's early recovery.

Turning to internal matters, leaders also discussed the next multiannual financial framework, and it is critical that we put in place the means for us to meet our ambitions. The work now needs to move forward on two fronts.

First, on sectoral files, I count on the Irish Presidency to adopt the remaining partial general approaches this month, and on this House to advance its work so that negotiations can be opened without delay.

Second, we need a robust and stable system of new own resources. I thank you, honourable Members, for your contribution to this debate.

On the topic of competitiveness and global economic challenges, leaders took stock of progress on the One Europe, One Market roadmap. The overall picture is mixed. There has been real progress with provisional agreements on the Omnibus proposals on defence readiness, chemicals and small mid-caps and digitisation, as well as on the revised FDI screening regulation and amendments to the market stability reserve. But we need to further accelerate work on simplification, EU Inc., the Industrial Accelerator Act and the savings and investments union.

On the international level, leaders had a productive discussion on the need to address structural overcapacities and global imbalances, notably with China, where the EU ran a trade deficit of EUR 1 billion a day in 2025 – and this will be even higher in 2026.

There was clear support for continuing on the path for diversification and de-risking of our relationships. Leaders also agreed on the need to strengthen the protection of our market from unfair trade practices, making more proactive and strategic use of our extensive economic security toolbox to defend European interests. We have also started preparatory work for the new country-neutral instrument that would act as a trade diversification tool.

Having said that, dialogue remains crucial, and I had constructive exchanges with my Chinese counterpart, Minister Wang Wentao, when he visited Brussels last week to launch trade and investment consultations. This is a dedicated platform to tackle in a structured way the issues we have identified together. The aim is to deliver the first tangible results ahead of the October European Council.

Last week we also took vital steps towards ensuring the long-term viability of Europe's strategically important steel industry. The regulation protecting the EU steel sector from the damaging impacts of global overcapacity entered into application on 1 July. Here, I would like to thank all Members of the European Parliament for their strong support for this measure.

Madam President, I would end my introductory remarks here, and thank you very much for the attention.

3-0014-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, le dernier Conseil européen a été l’occasion d’aboutir – enfin! – sur le sujet fondamental travaillé ici pendant de nombreux mois: celui du règlement «retour», dernière pièce de la stratégie européenne en matière d’immigration et plus spécifiquement de lutte contre l’immigration illégale.

Les médias se sont fait l’écho des débats qui ont eu lieu autour de la table du Conseil entre les chefs d’État. Sur ce sujet essentiel, nous avons travaillé, nous avons négocié, nous avons voté: maintenant, il faut agir. Et sur ce sujet clé, l’essentiel sera désormais dans la mise en œuvre concrète des mesures qui ont été validées. Dix-neuf États membres sur vingt-sept ont signé une lettre commune: 19 États membres de groupes politiques différents, certains issus du PPE, d’autres d’autres groupes de la droite, certains issus du groupe Renew, d’autres du groupe socialiste, qui ont dit ensemble l’urgence d’agir pour ouvrir des centres de retour.

Après que nous aurons subi pendant si longtemps des procès en inefficacité, des procès en illégitimité, nous voyons aujourd’hui des États prêts à se saisir de cet outil fondamental pour pouvoir garantir que, demain, plus personne ne pourra s’établir durablement en Europe sans y avoir été légalement autorisé. Quelle tristesse de voir que certains États choisissent de rompre avec cette logique, et de voir en particulier le président français déclarer que ce n’est pas son Europe.

Bien sûr, ce n’est peut-être pas son Europe. Il voudrait aujourd’hui contester ces centres de retour parce qu’ils ne seraient pas efficaces. Mais qu’est-ce qui est moins efficace que la situation actuelle quand, en France, moins d’une OQTF sur dix est effectivement mise en œuvre? Ce n’est peut être pas «son» Europe, mais c’est la nôtre, c’est celle que nous construisons ensemble: une Europe qui retrouvera la maîtrise de ses frontières et la maîtrise de son destin, une Europe qui rendra à nos démocraties le pouvoir de décider qui rentre sur leur sol et qui ne peut pas s’y établir, une Europe qui mettra fin à l’immigration illégale et à toutes les tragédies qui l’entourent. Nous sommes fiers de construire cette Europe-là! C’est l’Europe de l’avenir!
3-0014-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the last European Council was the opportunity to reach - finally! - on the fundamental subject worked on here for many months: that of the "return" regulation, the last piece of the European strategy in terms of immigration and more specifically the fight against illegal immigration.

The media have echoed the debates that took place around the Council table between the heads of State. On this essential subject, we have worked, we have negotiated, we have voted: now, we must act. And on this key subject, the essential will henceforth be in the concrete implementation of the measures that have been validated. Nineteen member states out of twenty-seven have signed a joint letter: 19 member states from different political groups, some from the EPP, others from other right-wing groups, some from the Renew group, others from the socialist group, who said together the urgency to act to open return centres.

After we have suffered for so long from trials of inefficiency, trials of illegitimacy, we see today states ready to seize this fundamental tool to be able to guarantee that, tomorrow, no one will be able to settle permanently in Europe without having been legally authorized to do so. How sad it is to see that certain states choose to break with this logic, and to see in particular the French president declare that this is not his Europe.

Of course, this may not be his Europe. He would like today to contest these return centers because they would not be effective. But what is less effective than the current situation when, in France, less than one OQTF out of ten is effectively implemented? This may not be "his" Europe, but it is ours, it is the one we are building together: a Europe that will regain control of its borders and control of its destiny, a Europe that will return to our democracies the power to decide who enters their soil and who cannot settle there, a Europe that will put an end to illegal immigration and all the tragedies that surround it. We are proud to build that Europe! It is the Europe of the future!

3-0015-0000.sourceText:
Madame President, Commission colleagues, I am really, really unpleasantly surprised that the Council is not here. What are we debating? The Council conclusions without the Council. The Commission is not the problem on defence and support of Ukraine. We are not the problem on defence and support of Ukraine. The 27 capitals are deeply lacking a sense of urgency. The Council, in its conclusions, this time called for investing better and faster together, more aggregation of demand, proper European defence markets. None of that is coming to realisation. We have heard this for years and we have no real progress other than the hugely necessary surge in spending. We are not investing better. Still no joint European approach. It harms our operational readiness and costs billions per year. Narrow and short‑term national interests will override European security. We need a real European defence union.

Oh, and another thing: condemnations of Russian attacks don't save lives or make us more secure. What helps is Member States sending the air defence systems they still have to Ukraine.

3-0016-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Asszony! Az elmúlt években, amikor megrendezték a szokásos vitákat a csúcstalálkozókról, mindig külön kitértek a magyar kormány álláspontjára, és folyamatosan aggódtak a demokrácia állapotáért. De most, hogy az új TISZA-kormány tényleg elkezdi rombolni a jogállamot, síri csend van. Hahó! Van itt valaki? Egy egyetlen soros alkotmánymódosítással eltávolítanák a köztársasági elnököt, és még csak indoklás sincs. Megakadályozzák, hogy az ellenzék vezetője még egyszer miniszterelnök-jelölt lehessen. Visszamenőleg 12 évben korlátozzák a képviselői mandátumot, így az ellenzéki képviselők nagy részét egész egyszerűen kizárják a politikai életből.

Ha itt az Európai Parlamentben lenne ilyen szabály, akkor 164 képviselő nem indulhatna újra 29-ben, nem indulhatna Manfred Weber, de a Zöldek és a szocialisták frakcióvezetője sem, mint ahogy az Európai Parlament elnöke sem. Szóval kíváncsian várjuk az ír elnökség, de leginkább a jogállamiságra különösen érzékeny Európai Bizottság álláspontját. A hallgatás annak bizonyítéka lenne, hogy valójában eddig sem a demokrácia állapota érdekelte a Bizottságot, csak az, hogy engedelmes kormányok legyenek a tagállamokban. Ellen fogunk állni.
3-0016-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In recent years, when the usual debates on the summits were held, the position of the Hungarian government was always singled out, and there was constant concern over the state of democracy. But now, as the new TISZA government is actually starting to dismantle the rule of law, there is dead silence. Hello! Is anyone here? They would remove the President of the Republic with a single-sentence constitutional amendment, and there is not even a justification. They are preventing the leader of the opposition from ever running for Prime Minister again. They are limiting parliamentary mandates retrospectively to 12 years, thereby simply excluding the vast majority of opposition MPs from political life.

If such a rule existed here in the European Parliament, 164 MEPs could not run again in '29, Manfred Weber could not run, nor could the group leaders of the Greens and the Socialists, just as the President of the European Parliament could not. So we are eagerly awaiting the position of the Irish Presidency, but most of all the European Commission, which is particularly sensitive to the rule of law. Silence would be proof that the Commission has never actually cared about the state of democracy, only that there should be obedient governments in the member states. We will resist.

3-0017-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, c'è stato un tempo in cui le tesi dei Conservatori sulla protezione dei confini e sul realismo industriale venivano derise o liquidate come provocazioni.

Le conclusioni dell'ultimo Consiglio europeo dimostrano che quel tempo è finito: oggi, l'Unione comincia a muoversi lungo il percorso che noi abbiamo indicato per anni, a partire dalla gestione dei flussi migratori.

Purtroppo non potremo cancellare gli errori del passato, quando le sinistre imposero la tragica politica delle frontiere aperte a chiunque, ma siamo consci di aver cambiato paradigma per il futuro.

L'Unione guarda finalmente alla dimensione esterna, alla gestione ferma dei flussi, al rimpatrio veloce di chi non ha diritto alla protezione internazionale: in questo modo, contrasteremo i trafficanti di esseri umani, salveremo la vita dei migranti più di quanto sia mai accaduto in passato e lavoreremo per garantire loro il diritto a non emigrare.

È il buon senso che vince e che ora deve trovare un adeguato sostegno finanziario nel prossimo bilancio pluriennale.

Lo stesso realismo serve sulla competitività strategica. La prossima settimana la Commissione presenterà la revisione del sistema ETS e noi Conservatori saremo molto attenti a ciò che verrà presentato.

Non accetteremo norme cieche, incapaci di vedere la deindustrializzazione dell'Europa e la consegna del nostro destino economico nelle mani del fanatismo ambientalista e del regime cinese. Difenderemo il principio della neutralità tecnologica e la competitività del nostro tessuto produttivo.

Dalla nostra salute economica dipende la nostra possibilità di investire sulla sicurezza interna e sulla difesa esterna, sulla ricerca scientifica, sul sistema sanitario e scolastico e sulla conservazione della natura, che, paradossalmente, sembra interessare sempre di meno agli pseudoambientalisti da salotto.

A noi Conservatori interessa proteggere la terra dei nostri padri e proteggere la vita delle persone che vi abitano. È il motivo per cui noi siamo qui.
3-0017-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, there was a time when the Conservatives' theses on border protection and industrial realism were mocked or dismissed as provocations.

The conclusions of the last European Council demonstrate that that time is over: today, the Union is beginning to move along the path that we have pointed out for years, starting with the management of migration flows.

Unfortunately, we will not be able to erase the mistakes of the past, when the left imposed the tragic policy of open borders for anyone, but we are aware of having changed the paradigm for the future.

Finally, the Union is looking at the external dimension, at the firm management of flows, at the swift repatriation of those who have no right to international protection: in this way, we will combat human traffickers, save the lives of migrants more than has ever happened in the past and work to guarantee them the right not to emigrate.

It is common sense that is winning and that must now find adequate financial support in the next multiannual budget.

The same realism is needed on strategic competitiveness. Next week the Commission will present the revision of the ETS system and we Conservatives will be very attentive to what will be presented.

We will not accept blind rules, incapable of seeing the deindustrialization of Europe and the delivery of our economic destiny into the hands of environmentalist fanaticism and the Chinese regime. We will defend the principle of technological neutrality and the competitiveness of our productive fabric.

Our ability to invest in internal security and external defense, in scientific research, in the health and school system, and in the conservation of nature, which paradoxically seems to interest living-room pseudo-environmentalists less and less, depends on our economic health.

We Conservatives are interested in protecting the land of our fathers and protecting the lives of the people who live there. It is the reason why we are here.

3-0018-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, I welcome the Council conclusions of 18 June and 19 June, and just a few observations, Commissioner. First and foremost, the commitment to Ukraine. We really appreciate the fact that the money is now being spent on two capacities, both in terms of support of the state and on defence as well. But it leads to a very fundamental question about the issue of how we fund the European Union itself.

While we're going into the multiannual financial framework discussions and trying to ensure that we have a budget that underpins and supports the values that the European Union proposes, we have to accept that, as it stands, we simply do not have the capacity to do what we must do in terms of supporting Ukraine, paying off the loans that we have taken out previously to support the European Union during the COVID‑19 crisis, and now also facing into a potential round of enlargement. I am very supportive of the enlargement process, and there are two things I believe we have to do, whether we like it or not.

One is institutional reform, and the other area is looking at how do we ensure that we have budgetary capacity in the MFF into the future to facilitate enlargement? It is simply disingenuous of us to continue to say that we will support enlargement, we want to see enlargement, we open the clusters, and yet the most fundamental issue that will be required if we want to continue with the enlargement process, is to have the budgetary capacity to do that, to support the incoming Member States, and also to ensure that citizens within the European Union, as is, have the support and funding available to them through the various sectors.

So I believe we have to have that big debate, and I hope that it happens over the next six months so that we can have an honest interrogation of our budgetary position.

3-0019-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, who else in this room has been suffering from the unbearable heat in the last weeks? Well, if we are already suffering, think about the construction workers, the people working and living in care homes, and the nurses in overheated hospitals. We need ad-hoc solutions to this heat crisis, and we need a special EUCO to discuss this. Cool spaces in cities, better protection for workers, funding for climate adaptation. But most of all, colleagues, we need nature.

We need to stop treating our nature as an enemy. Nature is the basis of our existence – we are part of nature. There are people in Europe who have understood this. Look at Albania – in one of the poorest countries in Europe people take to the streets to defend their nature. Nature over money. They say: Albania is not for sale. Instead of billionaires becoming richer with concrete luxury resorts, we want flamingos, we want birds, we want one of the richest biodiversities in all of Europe. They want Europe to speak up for them. They need European leaders and the European Commission to be at their side and defend EU laws in the accession procedure, including laws on habitats and nature protection.

The aim is very clear, colleagues, Albania should join the European Union as soon as possible, but with strong nature protection and anti-corruption laws in place. We owe it to the people who are fighting in Albania. Let us be in solidarity. Let us be by their side.

3-0020-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, l’Europe brûle littéralement. Les personnes âgées suffoquent dans les EHPAD, les enfants étouffent à l’école, les hôpitaux surchauffent au sens propre comme au sens figuré, les morgues débordent, les récoltes sont menacées, les forêts partent en fumée… Et quelle est votre réponse, à la Commission européenne? Mettre la lutte contre le changement climatique en pause.

Il fallait oser, car la canicule, quoi qu’on en dise, n’est pas juste un incident météo: la canicule est politique, et les morts de cette canicule sont le résultat de votre politique. N’est-ce pas vous, à la Commission européenne, qui avez détruit méthodiquement plus d’une vingtaine de réglementations environnementales depuis le début de votre nouveau mandat? N’est-ce pas vous, Monsieur le Commissaire, personnellement, qui signez à tour de bras des accords de libre-échange pour aller chercher à l’autre bout du monde ce que l’on sait que l’on peut produire ici?

Alors oui, vous n’êtes pas seul. Il y a les États membres, qui manifestement se cachent aujourd’hui. Mais vous vous êtes aussi embarqué dans le sillage de l’extrême droite, désormais votre complice favorite, pionnière du déni du réchauffement climatique et toujours prête à défendre les privilégiés.

Mais descendez de votre bureau climatisé et ouvrez les yeux: vous verrez que tout le monde n’est pas logé à la même enseigne. Pendant que les puissants se barricadent au frais, les plus pauvres morflent. Plus vous êtes exploité, plus vous brûlez. Ce massacre climatique est en réalité un massacre de classe. Ce sont les riches qui tuent les pauvres. Le 1 % le plus riche pollue autant que les deux tiers de l’humanité, 100 entreprises sont responsables de 70 % des émissions mondiales, Bernard Arnault émet 1 200 fois plus de CO2 qu’un Français moyen, mais, surtout, ne leur demandons aucun effort! Continuons comme avant, ne les mettons pas à contribution! Ne touchons surtout pas à leur mode de vie!

Les trois épisodes caniculaires que nous venons de vivre ne sont pourtant que la bande-annonce de ce qui nous attend dans les années à venir. Face à la canicule, adoptons les bons gestes barrières: taxons les riches et sortons de l’idéologie néolibérale! Car, à force de recul, de renoncement et d’inaction, vous nous condamnez à brûler.
3-0020-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, Europe is literally burning. The elderly are suffocating in nursing homes, children are choking at school, hospitals are overheating in both the literal and figurative sense, morgues are overflowing, harvests are threatened, forests are going up in smoke... And what is your response, at the European Commission? Put the fight against climate change on hold.

It took some nerve, because the heatwave, whatever anyone says, is not just a weather incident: the heatwave is political, and the deaths from this heatwave are the result of your policy. Is it not you, at the European Commission, who have methodically destroyed more than twenty environmental regulations since the beginning of your new mandate? Is it not you, Mr Commissioner, personally, who are enthusiastically signing free-trade agreements to go and fetch from the other side of the world what we know we can produce here?

So yes, you are not alone. There are the Member States, who are clearly hiding today. But you have also embarked in the wake of the far right, now your favorite accomplice, pioneer of climate change denial and always ready to defend the privileged.

But step down from your air-conditioned office and open your eyes: you will see that not everyone is in the same boat. While the powerful barricade themselves in the cool, the poorest take the hit. The more you are exploited, the more you burn. This climate massacre is actually a class massacre. It is the rich who kill the poor. The richest 1% pollute as much as two-thirds of humanity, 100 companies are responsible for 70% of global emissions, Bernard Arnault emits 1,200 times more CO2 than an average French person, but above all, let us not ask them for any effort! Let us continue as before, let us not make them contribute! Above all, let us not touch their lifestyle!

The three heatwave episodes we have just experienced are nevertheless only the trailer for what awaits us in the years to come. Faced with the heatwave, let us adopt the right barrier measures: let us tax the rich and break away from neoliberal ideology! For, through constant retreat, renunciation and inaction, you are condemning us to burn.

3-0021-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Einige Tausend Hitzetote haben Europa und Deutschland bereits zu beklagen, und währenddessen möchte man durch den CO2-Emissionshandel die Preise für Energie noch teurer machen, um das Klima weltweit zu beeinflussen. Genau das ist der Unterschied zwischen Theorie und Praxis; das ist der Unterschied zwischen denen auf der linken Seite und den patriotischen Kräften in Europa.

Wir glauben nicht daran, dass höhere Steuern und Mehrbelastung für die Bürger irgendetwas am Weltklima verändern würden – und dieser Ansatz ist ja auch bereits in der Realität gescheitert. Stattdessen möchten wir den Menschen ganz praktisch helfen, beispielsweise indem Altenheime, Pflegeheime, Krankenhäuser, Schulen ganz konkret und systematisch mit Klimaanlagen ausgestattet werden. Wir wollen praktische Politik statt Wolkenkuckucksheim.

Etwas anderes, was auf der Tagesordnung stand, ist die Frage nach dem Erweiterungsprozess. Der Balkan ist eine unglaublich wichtige Region für uns; sie ist strategisch wichtig für Europa. Deswegen möchten auch wir, dass der Balkan und die Europäische Union sehr viel enger zusammenarbeiten, beispielsweise durch privilegierte Handelsbeziehungen – dass diese noch weiter ausgebaut werden.

Was wir aber nicht wollen, ist, dass diese Länder bei dem aktuellen Stand in die Europäische Union aufgenommen werden. Wir wollen nicht, dass weitere Empfängerländer aufgenommen werden, die am Ende des Tages den deutschen Steuerzahler weiter und noch mehr belasten.

Schon die letzten Erweiterungsrunden sind nicht voll verarbeitet worden von der Europäischen Union. Nach wie vor gibt es große Konflikte; nach wie vor sind die institutionellen Regeln nicht auf diese Größe ausgelegt. Wir müssen erst einmal daran arbeiten, dass diese Europäische Union und die europäische Kooperation wieder arbeitsfähig werden, indem man sich auf das Wesentliche konzentriert und indem man eben nicht immer neue Aufgaben und Länder hinzunimmt.

Wir wollen, dass der Balkan näher an uns herangeführt wird, aber eben ohne den deutschen Steuerzahler zu belasten.
3-0021-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Europe and Germany already have to mourn several thousand heat deaths, and meanwhile people want to make energy prices even more expensive through CO2 emissions trading in order to influence the climate worldwide. Exactly that is the difference between theory and practice; that is the difference between those on the left side and the patriotic forces in Europe.

We do not believe that higher taxes and additional burdens for citizens would change anything about the global climate – and this approach has already failed in reality. Instead, we want to help people very practically, for example by equipping retirement homes, nursing homes, hospitals, and schools very concretely and systematically with air conditioning systems. We want practical politics instead of castles in the air.

Something else that was on the agenda is the question of the enlargement process. The Balkans are an incredibly important region for us; they are strategically important for Europe. Therefore, we too want the Balkans and the European Union to cooperate much more closely, for example through privileged trade relations – that these be expanded even further.

What we do not want, however, is for these countries to be admitted to the European Union at the current stage. We do not want further recipient countries to be admitted that, at the end of the day, burden the German taxpayer further and even more.

Even the last rounds of enlargement have not been fully processed by the European Union. There are still major conflicts; the institutional rules are still not designed for this size. We first have to work on making this European Union and European cooperation capable of functioning again by concentrating on the essentials and by not constantly taking on new tasks and countries.

We want the Balkans to be brought closer to us, but without burdening the German taxpayer.

3-0022-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Dzięki państwom wschodniej flanki i polskiej prezydencji Europa wreszcie uznała, że wschodnia granica Unii jest pierwszą linią naszego wspólnego bezpieczeństwa. Dlatego program Eastern Flank Watch nie może oznaczać samego monitorowania zagrożeń. Samo obserwowanie drona czy rakiety to za mało. Konieczne są realne zdolności obronne: systemy antydronowe wczesnego ostrzegania, zintegrowana obrona powietrzna i nowoczesne technologie.

Polska daje przykład, jak działać skutecznie. Jesteśmy największym beneficjentem programu SAFE i wykorzystujemy te środki na realne wzmocnienie bezpieczeństwa Polski, wschodniej flanki i całej Europy.

Pomimo weta prezydenta i sabotażu opozycji w Polsce wojna Wschodu z Zachodem to nie jest teoria. Jesteśmy w stanie wojny hybrydowej w Europie i w Polsce, na którą spadały ruskie drony. Zamykane były lotniska, prowadzona była dywersja na torach kolejowych, a Putin wykorzystywał migrantów jako żywą tarczę. Putin nie testuje tylko Polski, Rumunii czy państw bałtyckich. On testuje całą Unię Europejską. Dlatego wschodnia flanka musi być dziś najtrwalszą i najtwardszą linią obrony całej Unii Europejskiej.
3-0022-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Thanks to the states of the eastern flank and the Polish presidency, Europe has finally recognized that the Union's eastern border is the frontline of our common security. Therefore, the Eastern Flank Watch program cannot mean mere threat monitoring. Just observing a drone or a missile is not enough. Real defensive capabilities are necessary: early-warning anti-drone systems, integrated air defense, and modern technologies.

Poland sets an example of how to act effectively. We are the largest beneficiary of the SAFE program and are using these funds to genuinely strengthen the security of Poland, the eastern flank, and all of Europe.

Despite the president's veto and the opposition's sabotage in Poland, the war between the East and the West is not a theory. We are in a state of hybrid warfare in Europe and in Poland, where Russian drones have fallen. Airports have been closed, sabotage on railway tracks has been carried out, and Putin has used migrants as human shields. Putin is not only testing Poland, Romania, or the Baltic states. He is testing the entire European Union. Therefore, the eastern flank must today be the most durable and hardest line of defense for the entire European Union.

3-0023-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, le conclusioni del Consiglio europeo dedicano spazio alla Palestina, mentre in quest'Aula ogni proposta di dibattito o risoluzione sul tema viene sistematicamente bloccata dalla destra e dal centro‑destra.

Questo mese è stata bocciata anche la proposta di dibattito sul dottor Abu Safiya, pediatra palestinese imprigionato da 18 mesi senza processo, che sta rischiando la vita.

A giugno, i leader europei hanno scritto nero su bianco che: Israele deve ritirarsi da Gaza; la linea gialla è inaccettabile; i ministri israeliani promuovono violazioni dei diritti umani; la nuova legge sulla pena di morte è discriminatoria e inumana e va abrogata; la colonizzazione della Cisgiordania è una grave violazione del diritto internazionale.

Lo sapevamo già: caro Consiglio, oltre alle parole, però, servono i fatti. Perché non spingete i vostri ministri ad adottare delle sanzioni efficaci, come fu fatto con la Russia nel 2022?

Invece, il Parlamento deve ritrovare la voce. Il Parlamento sta in silenzio davanti a un genocidio: è un silenzio colpevole, è un silenzio pesante, è un disonore per questa istituzione.
3-0023-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, the conclusions of the European Council devote space to Palestine, while in this Chamber every proposal for a debate or resolution on the subject is systematically blocked by the right and centre-right.

This month, the proposal for a debate on Dr Abu Safiya, a Palestinian paediatrician imprisoned for 18 months without trial who is risking his life, was also voted down.

In June, European leaders wrote in black and white that: Israel must withdraw from Gaza; the yellow line is unacceptable; Israeli ministers promote human rights violations; the new death penalty law is discriminatory and inhuman and must be repealed; the colonisation of the West Bank is a serious violation of international law.

We already knew this: dear Council, beyond words, however, deeds are needed. Why do you not push your ministers to adopt effective sanctions, like those done with Russia in 2022?

Instead, Parliament must find its voice again. Parliament is silent in the face of a genocide: it is a guilty silence, it is a heavy silence, it is a dishonour for this institution.

3-0024-0000.sourceText:
Madame President, dear colleagues, I'm going to speak about our budget and the climate – no big surprise. On the MFF, the European Council had one job in June: show ambitions and directions for Europe's future budget. Instead, what we saw was a negotiation box of 27 mini priorities squeezed together. That is not ambitions for Europe and not what this House asked for. At the same time, we can look out the window and we see a third heatwave already, larger and earlier wildfires. And a Council meeting in June will not stop this, but ambitions at the meeting are needed to act.

I read the conclusion twice, searching for ambitions, and I couldn't really see them. I found one sentence squeezed in among competitiveness. But let's be honest: the 2040 target is so far from reach. We need to act. We need ambitions.

This is not a call to reopen every single line, but it is a call for the Council to come back in October with ambitions and green actions. My group stands ready to work with you on the basis of ambitions, but patience is running out.

3-0025-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, signor Commissario, nel Suo intervento, analizzando il tema del bilancio, Lei ha parlato di risorse proprie, ma io ho un messaggio chiaro da mandarle: basta tasse, perché prima si razionalizzano le spese, si tagliano i costi – spesso inutili, che anche questo Parlamento avalla – e poi si ragiona, e si tagliano gli sprechi e le inefficienze.

Perché dobbiamo essere realisti: l'industria europea è in difficoltà, ci sono tante sacche di povertà, sempre più europei non arrivano a fine mese. Parlare di risorse proprie – quindi, di nuove tasse – è totalmente fuori luogo e scollegato dalla realtà.

A livello globale ci sono dei modelli di economia, tipo l'economia argentina, che stanno basando il rilancio dell'economia sulla riduzione delle tasse. In quest'Aula, invece, si parla di aumentarle. Siamo fuori dal mondo, Commissario. Serve un'inversione di tendenza, altro che nuove tasse.
3-0025-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, Mr Commissioner, in your speech, analysing the issue of the budget, you spoke of own resources, but I have a clear message to send you: enough with taxes, because first expenses are rationalised, costs are cut – often useless ones, which even this Parliament endorses – and then we discuss, and waste and inefficiencies are cut.

Because we must be realistic: European industry is in difficulty, there are many pockets of poverty, more and more Europeans are struggling to make ends meet. Talking about own resources – therefore, about new taxes – is completely out of place and disconnected from reality.

At a global level there are economic models, like the Argentine economy, which are basing the relaunch of the economy on the reduction of taxes. In this Chamber, on the other hand, we talk about increasing them. We are out of this world, Commissioner. A reversal of trend is needed, let alone new taxes.

3-0026-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, the EU leaders are very concerned about the situation in Palestine. They are so concerned, that several EU countries are still selling weapons to Israel while they continue attacking Palestinians and the Lebanese people. I wish this was not true, but the reality is that EU countries keep selling weapons to Israel for millions of euros in 2026. This is crazy to me. Our leaders use words to say how concerned they are about Palestine, while their actions show they are just being complicit in Israel's destabilisation of the Middle East.

But I have good news: I know the EU loves sanctions. We have to put 20 packages of sanctions to Russia. Maybe it's time to pressure Israel a little bit by stopping selling weapons to them.

3-0027-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, colleagues, the EU leaders are right. We must work more intensely to control migration. The Return Regulation was a victory for the common-sense majority in this House. It sends a clear signal: if you have no right to be here, you will be returned. That is progress.

But we must be bolder still. The entire asylum process – receiving, assessing and hosting all claims – must be moved outside the European Union. We cannot continue to let illegal migrants set foot on European soil before their claims are even examined. That is the only way to break the business model of the smugglers and end the chaos at our borders.

The only mission of Frontex must be to secure our borders. That requires removing the fundamental rights activists who have captured and paralysed the agency from within. We need border guards, not bureaucrats who see their job as facilitating migration.

Large-scale deterrence campaigns must clearly warn away illegal migrants before they risk their lives and burden our societies. And yes, we must also scrap outdated international conventions that were made for a bygone era. They no longer serve the interests of European citizens in the 21st century.

It is time to take back control for our citizens who want to feel safe in their own societies, for our nations who have the right to decide who enters, and for Europe itself so that it can remain prosperous, secure and recognisable for generations to come.

3-0028-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, the European economy will experience long-lasting damage from the Hormuz crisis, and that's a fact. When fossil fuel is expensive, European industry suffers deeply – that is also a fact. When sea levels rise, my country, the Netherlands, must build expensive infrastructure or it will drown – also a fact.

In short, our fossil fuel addiction is becoming very, very expensive. We have known this for a while and still, in the weeks after your most recent European Council, your members still call for abolishing our most effective tool, the ETS. Turn this around – kick the addiction. The Green Deal is not an ideological green agenda. It is the future-proof economic growth model. Those Member States implementing the Green Deal are doing much better economically than those who don't. Look at the facts and save Europe from its fossil fuel addiction.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

3-0029-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-vraag. – Meneer Gerbrandy, u spreekt hier over Europees, over de Green Deal. Hoe reflecteert u op het feit dat de Europese Commissie in de nieuwe veehouderijstrategie heeft gezegd dat er geen verdere krimp van de veestapel mocht komen, terwijl uw kabinet nu werkt aan de liquidatie van duizenden familiebedrijven in Nederland en daarmee de voedselzekerheid op het spel zet. U spreekt over de Straat van Hormuz en afhankelijkheden, maar wat vindt u ervan als we voor dierlijke productie en andere landbouwproductie afhankelijk worden van derde landen? Heeft u daar wel eens op gereflecteerd? En wat u doet met agrarische families en gezinsbedrijven en mensen aan de keukentafel?
3-0029-0000.englishText: Blue card question. Mr Gerbrandy, you are speaking here about European matters, about the Green Deal. How do you reflect on the fact that the European Commission stated in the new livestock farming strategy that there should be no further reduction of the livestock population, while your government is now working on the liquidation of thousands of family businesses in the Netherlands and thereby jeopardising food security? You speak about the Strait of Hormuz and dependencies, but what do you think of it if we become dependent on third countries for animal production and other agricultural production? Have you ever reflected on that? And what you are doing to agricultural families and family businesses and people at the kitchen table?

3-0030-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-antwoord. – Heerlijk altijd die nationale politiek in het Europees Parlement. Voedselzekerheid: wellicht heeft u onlangs ook het rapport gelezen waarin staat dat Nederland een importeur is van voedsel. Niet vanwege menselijke consumptie, maar vanwege de enorme hoeveelheid diervoeding die wij moeten importeren om ons waterhoofd aan dierlijke productie overeind te houden. Als u echt, echt betrokken bent bij de voedselzekerheid van Europa, dan weet u dat ons dieet plantaardiger moet worden en dat de toekomst niet ligt in het nog verder uitbreiden van de veestapel, wat volgens mij het beleid is van uw partij, waarmee niet alleen onze economie, maar zeker ook onze wereld helemaal kapot gaat.
3-0030-0000.englishText: “Blue card” reply. – It is always delightful to have national politics in the European Parliament. Food security: perhaps you also recently read the report stating that the Netherlands is an importer of food. Not because of human consumption, but because of the enormous amount of animal feed that we have to import to keep our bloated animal production afloat. If you are truly, truly concerned about Europe's food security, then you know that our diet needs to become more plant-based and that the future does not lie in expanding the livestock population even further, which I believe is the policy of your party, which completely wrecks not only our economy, but certainly also our world.

3-0031-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Ein Thema ist beim letzten Europäischen Rat irgendwie erstaunlicherweise zu kurz gekommen – der zukünftige EU‑Haushalt. Dabei ist es doch das Thema, das die Grundlage bildet für alles, was wir hier an Programmen diskutieren.

Die Verhandlungen für den Haushalt ab 2028 laufen, und gleichzeitig stehen viele nationale Budgets unter Druck; das müssen wir natürlich anerkennen, und das tun wir auch. Deswegen hätte ich mir mehr Ambitionen von den Mitgliedstaaten erwartet, denn wenn es ernst wird, dann schauen alle nach Brüssel. Aber wenn es darum geht, den gemeinsamen Haushalt zu finanzieren, dann wird es plötzlich ganz still.

Dabei hat dieses Haus gute Vorschläge gemacht, wie wir aus dem Deadlock herausrauskommen, wie wir aus dieser Sackgasse der Verhandlungen herauskommen: Wir brauchen mehr und bessere Eigenmittel für den künftigen EU‑Haushalt, eine Digitalabgabe, eine Besteuerung von Kryptowährungen oder von Online‑Glücksspiel, das europaweit zunimmt.

Das sind gute Vorschläge, und ich erwarte von den Mitgliedstaaten, dass sie sich endlich zusammenreißen und diese Sachen für den künftigen Haushalt genau prüfen.
3-0031-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! One topic somehow surprisingly fell short at the last European Council – the future EU budget. Yet it is the topic that forms the basis for everything we discuss here in terms of programmes.

The negotiations for the budget from 2028 are underway, and at the same time many national budgets are under pressure; we must of course acknowledge that, and we do. Therefore, I would have expected more ambition from the member states, because when things get serious, everyone looks to Brussels. But when it comes to financing the joint budget, it suddenly becomes very quiet.

Yet this House has made good proposals on how we can get out of the deadlock, how we can get out of this stalemate in the negotiations: We need more and better own resources for the future EU budget, a digital levy, taxation of cryptocurrencies or online gambling, which is increasing across Europe.

These are good proposals, and I expect the member states to finally pull themselves together and examine these matters closely for the future budget.

3-0032-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, Colegas, o mercado único é um desígnio europeu e o 28.º regime é a melhor ferramenta para o concretizar.

Falo-vos de um regime que oferece uma via pragmática para ultrapassar a fragmentação jurídica que continua a limitar o crescimento das empresas europeias, em particular das PME e das start‑ups. Ao permitir um quadro jurídico opcional, uniforme e diretamente aplicável em toda a União, reduz a complexidade administrativa, os custos de conformidade e a incerteza jurídica, que hoje travam a expansão além‑fronteiras. Num contexto de transição verde e digital, e de crescente concorrência internacional, a União não pode dar-se ao luxo de desperdiçar ferramentas que podem aumentar a sua eficiência económica e a sua autonomia estratégica.

O dossiê do 28.º regime deve ser rapidamente retomado pelas instituições europeias. Não sendo uma bala de prata, representa um sério passo em frente que deve ser dado por uma União que demasiadas vezes teima em ficar exatamente como está.
3-0032-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, colleagues, the single market is a European project and the 28th regime is the best tool to achieve it.

I speak to you of a regime that offers a pragmatic way to overcome the legal fragmentation that continues to limit the growth of European companies, in particular SMEs and start-ups. By allowing an optional, uniform and directly applicable legal framework throughout the Union, it reduces administrative complexity, compliance costs and legal uncertainty, which today hinder cross-border expansion. In a context of green and digital transition, and growing international competition, the Union cannot afford to waste tools that can increase its economic efficiency and strategic autonomy.

The dossier of the 28th regime must be quickly resumed by the European institutions. While not a silver bullet, it represents a serious step forward that must be taken by a Union that too often insists on staying exactly as it is.

3-0033-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, het MFK staat eindelijk, zou ik zeggen, ook op de agenda van de Raad. We staan aan het begin van dit proces rond deze nieuwe meerjarenbegroting en de klassieke tegenstellingen en rode lijnen tekenen zich al af binnen de Raad, in de Commissie en ook in dit Parlement. We zouden echter best het klassieke debat overstijgen en de oefening niet beperken tot een droge discussie over meer of minder middelen.

Europa heeft in de eerste plaats nood aan bijkomende hervormingen die de efficiëntie verhogen, onze concurrentiekracht vergroten en de broodnodige investeringen aanmoedigen. De focus moet daarbij onder meer, maar zeker niet in het minst, liggen op de versterking van de interne markt, de volwaardige kapitaalmarktenunie en ook deregulering. Dit zijn, als je er even over nadenkt, hervormingen die weinig of geen geld kosten, maar die wel een hoog rendement hebben. Het debat overstijgt of zou het boekhoudkundig perspectief moeten overstijgen. Europa staat voor grote uitdagingen op het vlak van concurrentievermogen, veiligheid, defensie en geopolitiek. We pleiten voor een welomschreven prioriteitengeheel en hervormingen die toelaten een toekomstgerichte Europese begroting uit te bouwen.
3-0033-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the MFF is finally, I would say, also on the Council's agenda. We are at the beginning of this process regarding this new multiannual budget and the traditional contradictions and red lines are already emerging within the Council, the Commission and also in this Parliament. However, we might well transcend the traditional debate and not limit the exercise to a dry discussion about more or less resources.

Europe primarily needs additional reforms that increase efficiency, boost our competitiveness and encourage much-needed investments. The focus must be, among other things, but certainly not least, on strengthening the internal market, the full capital markets union and also deregulation. These are, if you think about it, reforms that cost little or no money, but that do have a high return. The debate transcends or should transcend the accounting perspective. Europe faces major challenges in the areas of competitiveness, security, defence and geopolitics. We advocate a well-defined set of priorities and reforms that allow us to develop a future-oriented European budget.

3-0035-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjednice, povjereniče, zaključci Europskog vijeća jasno pokazuje da se Europa nalazi u odlučujućem trenutku.

Rasprava o novom proračunu nije samo rasprava o brojkama, već i rasprava o tome kakvu Europu želimo graditi u narednim godinama. Stoga pozdravljam snažniji fokus na konkurentnost, na inovacije, na otpornost europskoga gospodarstva. Međutim, moramo osigurati da novi Europski fond za konkurentnost mora biti otvoren za sve i da ne smije produbiti razlike između država članica koje već danas imaju snažne inovacijske kapacitete i onih koje ih tek razvijaju. Ne smijemo ponoviti situaciju koju danas imamo u programu Obzor Europa, gdje svega šest država članica koristi 70 % sredstava.

A danas govorimo o Europi koja može biti konkurentna i mora biti globalno konkurentna samo ako raste zajedno: sjever i jug, istok i zapad.
3-0035-0000.englishText:
Respected President, Commissioner, the conclusions of the European Council clearly show that Europe finds itself at a decisive moment.

Disbanding the debate on the new budget is not only a debate about numbers, but also a debate about what kind of Europe we want to build in the coming years. Therefore, I welcome the stronger focus on competitiveness, on innovation, on the resilience of the European economy. However, we must ensure that the new European Competitiveness Fund must be open to everyone and that it must not deepen the differences between member states that already today have strong innovation capacities and those that are only developing them. We must not repeat the situation we have today in the Horizon Europe program, where only six member states use 70% of the funds.

And today we are talking about a Europe that can be competitive and must be globally competitive only if it grows together: north and south, east and west.

3-0036-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, un debate sobre las conclusiones del Consejo Europeo sin el Consejo es absolutamente inaceptable. Dígaselo y trasládele tres mensajes.

En primer lugar: apoyo a Ucrania, por supuesto. Pero cuando llegue el momento de la negociación de la paz, Europa tiene que asegurarse de estar en la mesa y no en el menú.

En segundo lugar: responsabilidades de Rusia. Para eso hace falta apoyar la activación del estatuto de bloqueo para proteger a los jueces de la Corte Penal Internacional que están siendo unilateralmente sancionados por el Gobierno de Trump de los Estados Unidos.

Y en tercer lugar, un mensaje muy claro: hemos aprobado en este Pleno del Parlamento Europeo una nueva extensión de la derogación temporal de la ePrivacy. ¿Por qué lo hemos hecho? Porque el Consejo no ha hecho todavía su trabajo de aprobar de una vez el Reglamento que el Parlamento Europeo aprobó la pasada legislatura contra los delitos sexuales contra los menores en línea. Es el momento de hacerlo. Trasládele ese mensaje, comisario Šefčovič.
3-0036-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, a debate on the conclusions of the European Council without the Council is completely unacceptable. Tell them and convey three messages to them.

First: support for Ukraine, of course. But when the time for peace negotiations comes, Europe must make sure it is at the table and not on the menu.

Second: Russia's responsibilities. For that, it is necessary to support the activation of the blocking statute to protect the judges of the International Criminal Court who are being unilaterally sanctioned by the Trump administration of the United States.

And thirdly, a very clear message: we have approved in this plenary session of the European Parliament a new extension of the temporary derogation of ePrivacy. Why have we done this? Because the Council has not yet done its job of finally approving the Regulation that the European Parliament approved last legislative term against online sexual crimes against minors. It is time to do so. Convey that message, Commissioner Šefčovič.

3-0037-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, waar is het Ierse voorzitterschap hier? We hebben gesproken over nieuwe aanvallen op schepen in de Straat van Hormuz. De meststoffencrisis kan weer verergeren. Onze voedselzekerheid komt in gevaar, maar de Commissie en de Raad weigeren en talmen met het herzien van de nitraatrichtlijn. Wanneer kunnen we die tegemoetzien? Dit huis heeft dat geëist.

Op het gebied van het MFK komt de Raad maar niet tot overeenstemming. De voedselveiligheid en voedselzekerheid zijn in gevaar. Herstel landbouw en visserijsteun. Geef meer ruimte aan dierlijke mest. Stop de natuurherstelverordening: ons platteland en onze regio's dragen de last. Zet vaart achter de terugkeerhubs. Versterk Frontex en onze buitengrensbewaking: de instroom is te groot. De regio's en het platteland dragen de lasten van de Europese Spreidingswet en de nationale Nederlandse Spreidingswet. Commissie en Raad, kom in beweging, kom in actie. Bescherm onze buitengrenzen, bescherm ons platteland, bescherm onze voedselzekerheid.
3-0037-0000.englishText:
Mr President, where is the Irish Presidency here? We have discussed new attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. The fertiliser crisis could worsen again. Our food security is being endangered, but the Commission and the Council are refusing and stalling on revising the Nitrates Directive. When can we expect that? This House has demanded it.

In the area of the MFF, the Council just fails to reach an agreement. Food safety and food security are at risk. Restore agriculture and fisheries support. Give more room to animal manure. Stop the Nature Restoration Law: our countryside and our regions are bearing the burden. Speed up the return hubs. Strengthen Frontex and our external border control: the influx is too large. The regions and the countryside are bearing the burdens of the European Distribution Act and the national Dutch Distribution Act. Commission and Council, get moving, take action. Protect our external borders, protect our countryside, protect our food security.

3-0038-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señor comisario, el Consejo Europeo cree en el derecho y en las reglas tanto como la FIFA.

Vivimos en un mundo de impunidad: Trump hace una llamada y se anula una tarjeta roja. Pero nosotros hacemos algo peor: no solo desobedecemos las resoluciones de los tribunales internacionales de justicia y de la ONU sobre nuestra obligación de frenar el genocidio, de dejar de vender armas, sino que hacemos lo contrario. Y todavía hay algo peor: permitimos que se persiga a esos funcionarios públicos, cooperamos con los Estados Unidos, sin ni tan siquiera haber recibido una llamada de Trump —o quizá nos ha llamado Trump—. La cuestión es que hay unas sanciones contra esos funcionarios públicos, hay una norma que se debe aplicar y no la estamos aplicando.

Trump es un cínico, pero nos dice la verdad. Nosotros somos unos hipócritas: decimos una cosa y hacemos la contraria.
3-0038-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the European Council believes in law and rules just as much as FIFA.

We live in a world of impunity: Trump makes a call and a red card is rescinded. But we do something worse: not only do we disobey the resolutions of the international courts of justice and the UN regarding our obligation to halt genocide, to stop selling arms, but we do the opposite. And there is something even worse: we allow those public officials to be persecuted, we cooperate with the United States, without even having received a call from Trump—or perhaps Trump has called us. The point is that there are sanctions against those public officials, there is a rule that must be applied and we are not applying it.

Trump is a cynic, but he tells us the truth. We are hypocrites: we say one thing and do the opposite.

3-0039-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, la posición que ha adoptado el Consejo Europeo con respecto al marco financiero plurianual es sencillamente decepcionante.

Mientras Europa se enfrenta a enormes desafíos como la transición climática, la competitividad, la soberanía digital o el acceso a la vivienda, la respuesta que ha dado el Consejo ha sido recortar el presupuesto; es decir, una Europa más pequeña y sin capacidad de respuesta.

No podemos hacer más con menos. No podemos hablar de autonomía estratégica y, al mismo tiempo, renunciar al Fondo Social Europeo, a la PAC o a las políticas de cohesión. Y todo por una falta de valentía a la hora de aprobar y desbloquear un paquete de recursos propios que precisamente nos dé la capacidad de tener una posición política propia en un mundo cada vez más incierto, más violento y, sobre todo, más competitivo.

Por eso, desde el Parlamento le decimos al Consejo que Europa no se fortalece desde la renuncia, los recortes y la falta de ambición, sino que se construye con la solidaridad y con recursos suficientes para dar respuesta a lo que nos reclama la ciudadanía.
3-0039-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the position adopted by the European Council regarding the multiannual financial framework is simply disappointing.

While Europe faces enormous challenges such as the climate transition, competitiveness, digital sovereignty, or access to housing, the response given by the Council has been to cut the budget; in other words, a smaller Europe without the capacity to respond.

We cannot do more with less. We cannot speak of strategic autonomy and, at the same time, give up the European Social Fund, the CAP, or cohesion policies. And all this due to a lack of courage when it comes to approving and unlocking a package of own resources that precisely gives us the capacity to have our own political position in an increasingly uncertain, more violent, and, above all, more competitive world.

For this reason, from Parliament we tell the Council that Europe is not strengthened through resignation, cuts, and a lack of ambition, but rather is built with solidarity and sufficient resources to respond to what our citizens demand.

3-0040-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, domnule comisar, vă mulțumim pentru informațiile pe care ni le-ați adus, dar vreau să mă refer la câteva puncte.

În primul rând: CFM-ul. Domnule comisar, ați spus că sunt două niveluri. Nu este clar ce facem cu resursele proprii, pentru că noi, Parlamentul, am propus de foarte multe ori de unde pot veni aceste resurse noi pentru a nu avea un CFM mai mic, pentru a nu avea un buget mai mic - nici măcar cu inflația.

Apoi, competitivitatea: o Europă și o piață. Ați spus decalajul comercial cu China, dar ce facem pentru competitivitate? Pentru că dacă vrem să susținem industria, așa cum ați spus, atunci trebuie o revizuire a ETS și trebuie cu adevărat politici de susținere - nu numai a industriei siderurgice, dar a industriei și, bineînțeles, a agriculturii, pentru că securitatea alimentară este foarte importantă.

Practici comerciale neloiale. Păi da, dar avem acorduri în care puneți taxe vamale la materii prime mai mici decât la produsul finit, ceea ce este ilogic, pentru că producătorul din Europa nu o să poată să fie atunci competitiv. Așadar, eu cred că trebuie, domnule comisar - sigur, vine concediu - dar haideți să gândim cu adevărat un CFM care să ducă la competitivitate și la reindustrializarea Uniunii Europene.
3-0040-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, thank you for the information you have brought us, but I want to refer to a few points.

First of all: the MFF. Commissioner, you said there are two levels. It is not clear what we are doing with own resources, because we, the Parliament, have proposed many times where these new resources can come from so as not to have a smaller MFF, so as not to have a smaller budget - not even with inflation.

Then, competitiveness: a Europe and a market. You mentioned the trade gap with China, but what are we doing for competitiveness? Because if we want to support industry, as you said, then we need a revision of the ETS and we truly need support policies - not only for the steel industry, but for industry and, of course, agriculture, because food security is very important.

Unfair trade practices. Well yes, but we have agreements where you set customs duties on raw materials lower than on the finished product, which is illogical, because the producer in Europe will then not be able to be competitive. Therefore, I believe that we must, Commissioner - sure, holidays are coming - but let us truly think of an MFF that leads to competitiveness and the re-industrialization of the European Union.

3-0041-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Bildung, Kultur, Wettbewerb, Sozialarbeit, Forschung, Verteidigung, Infrastruktur, Entwicklungszusammenarbeit. Aufgaben erfüllen – das wollen wir gut, aber wir kriegen dafür nicht mehr Mittel. Wenn wir uns einmal anschauen – der EU‑Haushalt, der jetzt angestrebt ist, ist nicht mal halb so groß wie der deutsche Bundeshaushalt.

Wenn wir eine handlungsfähige Europäische Union wollen, dann brauchen wir auch eine ordentliche Mittelausstattung. Horizontale Kürzungen anzustreben und die Kohäsionsmittel weiter runter zu kürzen, ist dabei das völlig falsche Signal. Es ist EU‑vertragsrechtlich geregelt, dass die Europäische Union in den Zusammenhalt der Mitgliedstaaten investiert. Mit diesen Kürzungen sorgen wir dafür, dass genau dieser Zusammenhalt in solchen herausfordernden Zeiten auseinanderdriftet; das können wir uns nicht leisten.

Wir wollen die Aufgaben gut erfüllen. Wir wollen eine handlungsfähige Union. Das bedeutet auch, dass die Mitgliedstaaten dazu angehalten werden müssen, diese Europäische Union mit ordentlichen finanziellen Mitteln auszustatten. Mitgliedstaaten müssen dafür sorgen, dass wir dieser Verantwortung gerecht werden und nicht weiter Kürzungen vorgenommen werden.
3-0041-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Education, culture, competition, social work, research, defense, infrastructure, development cooperation. Fulfilling tasks - that is what we want to do well, but we are not getting more funds for it. If we look at it - the EU budget that is now being aimed for is not even half as large as the German federal budget.

If we want a capable European Union, then we also need proper funding. Striving for horizontal cuts and cutting cohesion funds further is completely the wrong signal. It is regulated by EU treaty law that the European Union invests in the cohesion of member states. With these cuts, we are ensuring that this very cohesion drifts apart in such challenging times; we cannot afford that.

We want to fulfill the tasks well. We want a capable Union. That also means that member states must be urged to provide this European Union with adequate financial resources. Member states must ensure that we live up to this responsibility and that no further cuts are made.

3-0042-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je n’ai pas grand-chose à dire – il y aurait trop de choses à dire, à vrai dire – sur les sujets abordés. Je voudrais simplement dire à mes collègues que je suis choquée par le peu de députés présents dans notre hémicycle.

Je veux le redire: Mme la Présidente a essayé de mettre en place un certain nombre de mesures. C’est extrêmement préoccupant, y compris pour nos concitoyens. Les sujets abordés sont décisifs. Hier, nous parlions de la cybersécurité, de l’intelligence artificielle, et puis il y a tant de domaines qui sont importants, donc, s’il vous plaît, demandez à vos collègues d’être présents.

Ça a une importance, y compris pour l’image du Parlement vis-à-vis de la Commission européenne et du Conseil. Ensemble, soyons plus forts, mes chers collègues!
3-0042-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I do not have much to say – there would be too much to say, to tell the truth – on the subjects discussed. I would simply like to say to my colleagues that I am shocked by the few members present in our hemicycle.

I want to say it again: Madam President tried to put in place a certain number of measures. This is extremely worrying, including for our fellow citizens. The subjects discussed are decisive. Yesterday, we were talking about cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and then there are so many areas that are important, so, please, ask your colleagues to be present.

This is important, including for the image of Parliament vis-à-vis the European Commission and the Council. Together, let us be stronger, my dear colleagues!

3-0044-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, first and foremost, I would like to tell you that the discussion this morning very much reflects also the debate which took place among the leaders, the heads of state and government, sitting together in the European Council.

It clearly reflects the mood and the sense of priorities among European citizens, and you, as directly elected representatives, are clearly introducing these topics into the debate in this Hemicycle, and into the discussions which we have on these very crucial topics.

I would start with the references and remarks made on Ukraine. Mr Kelleher and Mr López Aguilar rightly pointed out the need of further support for Ukrainians. In my introduction I was describing to you all the aspects of the financial support, political support, but also moral support I believe we give to our Ukrainian friends to defend themselves.

But I agree with Mr Reuten and also with Ms Wcisło that, first of all, clearly would be needed to do even better when it comes to our defence capacities. How can we be more efficient? How can we pool our strength together? What can we do as Europeans in spending every single euro on these very important priorities in the most efficient manner?

Of course, especially the people from Central and Eastern Europe, feeling the heat from the conflict which is so close to their border, as Ms Wcisło brightly described, are very preoccupied by the fact that the peace which we believed, and had taken for granted for so many years, is under so much threat, even within the borders of the European Union. Therefore they are rightly calling for making sure that the eastern flank and eastern border is better protected. You have seen that this is becoming more and more one of the priority tasks which is done by the Member States, by the European Union, and which is now being discussed in Ankara as well.

So all these are very concrete priorities, which will be followed through by the European Commission, by the European Union, and we, of course, will be working on all of them very closely with you.

The second topic which was appearing in several interventions, and rightly so, because it would be definitely the top priority for the Irish Presidency – and for that ambition, I really thank them in advance – is to deliver an ambitious multiannual financial framework for all of us.

Because – as you rightly pointed out again, Mr Kelleher, Mr Nordqvist – this is the key topic for our European future. It's a key prerequisite for further progression of the enlargement, and this is also one of the key components for making Europe clearly more competitive.

Therefore, we will be working very closely with the Irish Presidency, and with you, because this is a very important, complex task, to make sure that by the end of this year, we will deliver on an MFF, and have that predictability and certainty on what is the framework for all of us when it comes to the budgetary boundaries for the next seven years. As I said, I very much appreciate that the Irish Presidency took this as a priority for themselves and want to devote all necessary resources, time and political focus on these key issues.

Of course, I fully understand and share the preoccupation of many honourable Members who raised the issue of the heatwave. We are suffering it all, and it's the issue for all our Member States. I never believe that in my country we will have temperatures which go over 40 degrees, and I can only imagine how difficult it must be in France, in Spain, in southern Mediterranean countries, where this is becoming a more and more common phenomenon.

But I would like to reassure you that for the European Commission, climate resilience and better preparedness, which you are going to discuss in a moment, especially for extreme weather events, is a priority. Therefore, later this year we will present a new European framework for climate resilience and risk management. We believe that through this measure, we can work even more closely with the Member States and with the regions to better prevent and prepare for these very often dramatic events.

I would say on this, but it applies to other topics which were also raised in this morning's debate, we also have to be fair to ourselves and to make sure that we will implement collectively – starting by the Member States, of course – what we have already agreed and adopted as our laws.

If you allow me to conclude on two topics, Ms Grapini was underscoring the importance of competitiveness and reindustrialisation. I would like to again reassure this House that there is not one College session, not one discussion among the Commissioners, where these two very important topics are not discussed.

We are looking into really alternative ways how to protect Europe from unfair competition, how to lower energy prices, and how to increase the trade among other Member States within the European Union. Because we are still trading by 10 % less than the states in the United States of America, and this could be an unbelievable source of income, of more jobs or more prosperity and more competitiveness, if our Member States among themselves would trade even more. For that, we need to improve how the single market performs. We have to lower the barriers among our Member States, and this is clearly one of the priorities we are taking on.

If you allow, Madam President, on the last point on free trade agreements addressed by Ms Manon Aubry, here I just would like to underscore that almost half of our European GDP depends in one way or another on global trading. Despite what is happening and what is going on in the world, Europe is still the number one global trader when it comes to goods and services – we trade more than China, we trade more than the US. We are the best in doing this, and this is clearly a very important position we have to defend. Not only because we like to be on the podium, but because more than 700 000 companies are benefiting from trade, and more than 80 % of them are SMEs – very often small family companies which create more than 30 million jobs in this regard.

So all these have to be taken into account, because Europe is very good at what it's doing. Our economy for decades has been developing in that regard, and therefore we are doing our utmost to open new opportunities and new markets for our entrepreneurs.

Madam President, I would like to thank all the honourable Members for their interventions. As it was suggested, I will of course pass on all the messages, not only to my colleagues in the European Commission, but also to our colleagues from the Council.

3-0045-5000.sourceText:
Rada Europejska po raz kolejny próbuje pogodzić rzeczy, których pogodzić się nie da. Z jednej strony mówi o potrzebie obniżania cen energii, odbudowie europejskiego przemysłu, konkurencyjności i zmniejszaniu zależności. Z drugiej strony wzywa do przyspieszenia dekarbonizacji i podtrzymuje zasadniczą rolę systemu ETS.

To jest właśnie źródło problemu.

Nie można jednocześnie żądać tańszej energii i przyspieszać polityki, która sztucznie podnosi jej cenę. Nie można mówić o reindustrializacji Europy i nakładać na europejskie przedsiębiorstwa kolejne koszty emisji. Nie można mówić o konkurencji ze Stanami Zjednoczonymi i Chinami, gdy sami świadomie pogarszamy warunki działania własnego przemysłu.

ETS stał się dodatkowym podatkiem od europejskiej produkcji, energii i inwestycji.

Przegląd wskaźników czy korekta zasad bezpłatnych uprawnień nie rozwiążą problemu, jeżeli sam mechanizm nadal będzie windował koszty działalności w Europie. W efekcie produkcja przenosi się tam, gdzie energię i emisje reguluje się rozsądniej. A razem z nią znikają miejsca pracy, inwestycje i potencjał rozwojowy naszych państw.

Europa musi wreszcie zatrzymać tę gospodarczą autodestrukcję.

Potrzebujemy taniej energii, neutralności technologicznej i realnej odbudowy przemysłu. Najpierw konkurencyjność, inwestycje i bezpieczeństwo gospodarcze.

Dekarbonizacja nie może odbywać się za cenę likwidacji miejsc pracy i wyprowadzania produkcji poza Unię.”
3-0045-5000.englishText:
The European Council is once again trying to reconcile things that cannot be reconciled. On the one hand, it speaks of the need to lower energy prices, rebuild European industry, competitiveness and reduce dependency. On the other hand, it calls for accelerating decarbonization and upholds the fundamental role of the ETS system.

This is precisely the source of the problem.

One cannot simultaneously demand cheaper energy and accelerate a policy that artificially raises its price. One cannot talk about the reindustrialization of Europe and impose further emission costs on European enterprises. One cannot talk about competition with the United States and China when we ourselves deliberately worsen the operating conditions of our own industry.

ETS has become an additional tax on European production, energy and investment.

A review of indicators or a correction of free allowance rules will not solve the problem if the mechanism itself continues to drive up operating costs in Europe. As a result, production is moving to where energy and emissions are regulated more sensibly. And along with it, jobs, investment and the developmental potential of our states are disappearing.

Europe must finally stop this economic self-destruction.

We need cheap energy, technological neutrality and real industrial reconstruction. First, competitiveness, investment and economic security.

Decarbonization cannot come at the price of destroying jobs and moving production outside the Union.

3-0048-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: JAVI LÓPEZ

Vice-President

3-0052-0000.sourceText:
The next item is the debate on the Council and Commission statements on the EU’s response and preparedness to protect people against recurring heatwaves and upcoming wildfires (2026/2796(RSP)).

We will follow the new format of the key debates. To start, the Council will have the floor: Thomas Byrne, Minister of State at the Department of the Taoiseach and the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade with special responsibility for European affairs.

3-0053-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, Commissioner, just two weeks ago, the most severe and widespread heatwave scorched large parts of Europe. These heatwaves are the most recent testament to the rising average global temperatures, which have been nearing 1.5 °C above pre-industrial levels. The trend is very worrying for Europe: we are the fastest warming region in the world.

Human-induced climate change is undoubtedly a major underlying cause of heatwaves, wildfires and other extreme weather events, such as floods and droughts. This is why prevention starts with strong policies to mitigate and adapt to climate change.

First, may I express my sympathies to all those who have been affected and the families of those who have died as a result of recent weather events.

On mitigation, the EU has been contributing its share to global efforts, with one of the most ambitious climate frameworks. In the same vein, the European Union and its Member States are committed to working on strengthening the capacity to adapt, building resilience and reducing exposure to extreme events. We look forward to the Commission's ideas on how to link these different strands in its upcoming European Union framework for climate resilience.

The year 2025 was a record-breaking season for wildfires, with over 1 million hectares burned across the European Union, triggering an unprecedented number of activations of the EU civil protection mechanism. It is entirely plausible that Europe could face a similar scenario this year. Southern Europe has had an early start to the wildfire season, and we have even witnessed wildfires in Greenland, which are particularly rare this early in the season.

Tackling this risk is a priority for Member States and the Council. On 29 June, the Council adopted a recommendation on integrated wildfire risk management, promoting a more coordinated and integrated approach covering the entire disaster risk management cycle. In other words, this recommendation sets out a comprehensive framework to help Member States to better prevent, prepare for, respond to and recover from wildfires.
