It also encourages Member States to strengthen prevention through sustainable land and forest management; improve preparedness by making better use of data, risk assessments and early warning systems; and enhance cooperation and interoperability in wildfire response. Furthermore, the recommendation highlights the importance of raising public awareness, supporting local communities, and strengthening governance and long-term funding for wildfire risk management.

Beyond efforts to better manage the consequences of these extreme events, let me stress the importance of efforts to increase our readiness. Enhancing our collective preparedness and resilience to major hazards, including wildfires and heatwaves, is a key aim of the European Union's preparedness strategy, tabled by the Commission and the High Representative in March last year. A number of policy actions announced by this strategy have been presented by the Commission, and we will continue to steer their careful examination in the Council.

Let me mention, in particular, the proposal for a regulation on the Union civil protection mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response, which represents an essential step to upgrade our preparedness set-up on climate-related risks and to ensure appropriate financing priorities. The Irish Presidency will continue to carry further the discussions in the Council on this proposal, with the aim of reaching a general approach during our semester, and I look forward to hearing the contributions of Commissioner Lahbib and Members here today in this very important debate.

3-0054-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, just as Mr Thomas Byrne said, Europe is the fastest warming continent on the planet and we are experiencing the impact of this scientific reality in our daily lives, from record heatwaves and droughts to devastating wildfires. This year has again broken records – only weeks after historically high temperatures in June, another major heatwave is approaching. The consequences of the recent heatwave were grave: labour productivity went down, schools were shut, workplaces closed, hospitals overwhelmed, roads damaged, rail tracks buckled and crops ravaged. People paid the highest price – at least 3 500 fatalities could be attributed to the June heatwave. On 3 July, France reported more than 2 000 excess deaths from the last week of June, and these are only preliminary estimates. To date, there has not been an activation of the EU CPM related to heatwave emergencies.

Honourable Members, heatwaves increase wildfire danger. Last year, more than 1 million hectares burned across the EU, the highest figure ever recorded, triggering 19 requests for assistance from the EU Civil Protection Mechanism – this is the largest number ever. This year, the wildfire season started unusually early, with two activations of the mechanism already in late April and early May. This requires swift action; the Commission has already taken a range of actions in the area of prevention, preparedness, response and restoration. While national authorities remain primarily responsible for civil protection, the Commission supports Member States across the entire disaster cycle. The EU invests in science, technology and innovation to monitor drought conditions, improve early detection, and enable faster action, notably through the Copernicus Emergency Management Service. We also promote prevention through analytical tools, peer reviews, funding, cross-border cooperation, and the exchange of best practices.

Last March, the Commission adopted a communication complemented by a Council recommendation on wildfire risk management. Together with Member States, we will develop implementation guidelines and an EU funding portal for integrated wildfire risk management, improve data, raise population awareness and support international engagement. We have also reinforced operational preparedness through rescEU and the European Civil Protection Pool; 22 firefighting aircraft, 5 helicopters and 22 certified ground firefighting teams are available across ten countries. In addition, nearly 800 firefighters from 13 countries are pre-positioned in Cyprus, Greece, Italy, Spain and Portugal. Following the lessons learned from last summer, we have strengthened our response capacity in the south of our Union with a new European regional firefighting station in Cyprus, so we can take immediate action when needs arise.

In recent days, Portugal and France asked for assistance due to severe wildfires. In response, nine rescue aeroplanes were deployed: three to Portugal and six to France. The European Union Solidarity Fund also remains important, providing financial support to Member States and accession countries affected by natural disasters and helping them address the burden of emergency and recovery measures. Adding to this, cohesion policy and funding play a crucial role in strengthening resilience, combining prevention and preparedness before disaster strikes, as well as reconstruction, and the Recovery and Resilience Facility includes investment and reforms aimed at increasing resilience to natural disasters.

Finally, we are also preparing a new European integrated framework for climate resilience, which will expect to adopt later this year. The road ahead is a very difficult one, but through cooperation, engagement and solidarity, Europe will move towards a collective and clear objective to raise the protection of our citizens and our territories against the growing and challenging risk landscape.

3-0055-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, señor presidente en ejercicio del Consejo, en primer lugar, me gustaría decir que estamos encantados en este Parlamento de pertenecer al Intergrupo sobre Resiliencia, Gestión de Catástrofes y Protección Civil, que está dando lugar a muchas cuestiones importantes sobre nuevas tecnologías y posibilidades para el futuro.

Por tanto, en estos momentos, este Parlamento está trabajando —y seguiremos trabajando con ahínco— en un momento difícil para los países, en el que el cambio climático está produciendo olas de calor muy dificultosas, tanto en mi país, donde hay 57 focos de incendio activos en estos momentos —en Cataluña, Andalucía—, así como en otros países de la Unión Europea de forma importante. Se trata de una crisis humanitaria y de protección civil muy importante y de un golpe al mundo rural en un momento muy crítico.

Por eso, tenemos que trabajar con seriedad y sin dogmatismo ideológico, es decir, trabajar en la prevención y trabajar también en las medidas. La Comisión Europea ha puesto a disposición el mayor dispositivo de la historia con 777 bomberos en 14 Estados y el refuerzo del rescEU y de la protección civil y los fondos que tienen que ver con ello.

Pero, en la prevención, ¿cómo lo tenemos que hacer? Hemos perdido una oportunidad única con NextGenerationEU y el Mecanismo de Recuperación y Resiliencia, porque son fondos fundamentales que deberían haberse destinado a la prevención. En cambio, países como el nuestro no han aprovechado lo suficiente estos fondos en este caso. Se renunció incluso a la compra de diez aviones de extinción de incendios en 2023. Esto es un error mayúsculo que luego se paga. Por tanto, por un lado, hay que aprovechar los fondos para los medios, pero también hay que simplificar.

Y termino con esto: flexibilizar directivas que impidan labores tradicionales como la silvicultura, el pastoreo conducido, la caza sostenible o la agricultura sostenible en algunas zonas es esencial para prevenir. Echar del campo a la gente o a la vida —como antaño— que respetaba la cuestión de la naturaleza es un error, porque sobreprotege y, al final, tarde o temprano, son pasto de las llamas.
3-0055-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, President-in-Office of the Council, firstly, I would like to say that we are delighted in this Parliament to belong to the Intergroup on Resilience, Disaster Management and Civil Protection, which is giving rise to many important issues regarding new technologies and possibilities for the future.

Therefore, at the present time, this Parliament is working—and we will continue to work hard—at a difficult time for countries, in which climate change is producing very difficult heatwaves, both in my country, where there are 57 active fire outbreaks at this moment—in Catalonia, Andalusia—, as well as in other European Union countries in a significant way. This is a very important humanitarian and civil protection crisis and a blow to the rural world at a very critical time.

That is why we have to work seriously and without ideological dogmatism, that is, working on prevention and also working on measures. The European Commission has made available the largest deployment in history with 777 firefighters in 14 States and the reinforcement of rescEU and civil protection and the funds related to it.

But, in prevention, how do we have to do it? We have missed a unique opportunity with NextGenerationEU and the Recovery and Resilience Facility, because they are fundamental funds that should have been allocated to prevention. On the other hand, countries like ours have not made sufficient use of these funds in this case. There was even a renunciation of the purchase of ten firefighting planes in 2023. This is a major mistake that is paid for later. Therefore, on the one hand, funds must be used for resources, but we must also simplify.

And I will finish with this: making directives more flexible that prevent traditional tasks such as forestry, controlled grazing, sustainable hunting or sustainable agriculture in some areas is essential to prevent. Throwing people or life out of the countryside—as in the past—who respected the issue of nature is a mistake, because it overprotects and, in the end, sooner or later, they fall prey to the flames.

3-0056-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, quiero comenzar con un agradecimiento a su persona por su compromiso en esta materia. Me consta el gran trabajo que está llevando a cabo y el trabajo que, durante el pasado verano, llevó a cabo para responder con solidaridad —que es como Europa tiene que hacerlo ante las desgracias—, en muchos países, como en mi propio país, España, donde usted estuvo en primera línea, apostando y apoyando todas las necesidades.

La realidad hoy es que hay más de 2 000 muertos en Francia, más de 1 200 en Bélgica, más de 1 000 en España y cerca de 500 en los Países Bajos. Miles de hectáreas calcinadas en Francia, Portugal y España. Carreteras que se derriten. Vías ferroviarias deformadas. Infraestructuras que dejan de funcionar.

Esto no son eslóganes, son los hechos: la realidad letal del cambio climático. Y mientras Europa enterraba a sus muertos, un ministro de la extrema derecha, aquí en Europa, se permitía bromear en las redes sociales sobre el calor, presumiendo —desde su piscina— con una cervecita bien fresca. Ese mensaje fue infame, porque cuando se frivoliza con la emergencia climática se alimenta la inacción y la inacción mata.

Por eso, hoy quiero preguntar al Partido Popular y a los falsos patriotas de la extrema derecha: ¿qué informes manejan ustedes para seguir negando el cambio climático? ¿Qué evidencia científica les permite justificar que hay que desmantelar, precisamente, las políticas que salvan vidas? Porque cada vez que atacan el Pacto Verde Europeo, cada vez que intentan acabar con el principio de «no causar un perjuicio significativo» y cada vez que debilitan la lucha contra la deforestación, ponen vidas en riesgo.

El Pacto Verde Europeo no es una carga, es nuestro escudo, es el mejor seguro de vida de los europeos, porque proteger su salud, proteger su poder adquisitivo, su empleo y su soberanía es lo que consigue el Pacto Verde Europeo. Necesitamos acelerar las energías renovables, porque es la energía más limpia y también la más barata que se puede producir.

Mitigar ya no basta, tenemos que adaptarnos. Y por eso exigimos una ley vinculante para proteger a los trabajadores expuestos al calor extremo dentro de la futura Ley de Empleo de Calidad. Y exigimos también un auténtico plan europeo de adaptación al cambio climático.

Europa no puede seguir esperando. Estamos negociando el próximo presupuesto europeo y en esa negociación se está decidiendo quién quiere invertir para proteger a las personas y quién prefiere recortar los instrumentos que las protegen, quién quiere reforzar la acción climática y quién sigue empeñado en debilitarla.

He comenzado esta intervención hablando de miles de ciudadanos que han perdido la vida y, precisamente por ellos, nuestro deber es conseguir que el próximo verano no tengamos que comenzar con este debate.

Defender el Pacto Verde Europeo es defender vidas, defender las renovables es defender la libertad en Europa y defender la transición justa es, sencillamente, defender a los europeos.
3-0056-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, I would like to begin by thanking you for your commitment to this matter. I am well aware of the great work you are carrying out and the work you carried out last summer to respond with solidarity — which is how Europe must respond to misfortunes — in many countries, such as my own country, Spain, where you were on the front line, backing and supporting all needs.

The reality today is that there are more than 2,000 dead in France, more than 1,200 in Belgium, more than 1,000 in Spain and close to 500 in the Netherlands. Thousands of hectares scorched in France, Portugal and Spain. Roads that melt. Deformed railway tracks. Infrastructures that stop working.

These are not slogans, these are the facts: the lethal reality of climate change. And while Europe was burying its dead, a far-right minister, here in Europe, felt able to joke on social media about the heat, boasting — from his swimming pool — with a nice cold beer. That message was infamous, because when climate emergency is trivialised, inaction is fed and inaction kills.

That is why today I want to ask the European People's Party and the false patriots of the far-right: what reports are you using to continue denying climate change? What scientific evidence allows you to justify that we must dismantle precisely the policies that save lives? Because every time you attack the European Green Deal, every time you try to do away with the principle of 'do no significant harm' and every time you weaken the fight against deforestation, you put lives at risk.

The European Green Deal is not a burden, it is our shield, it is the best life insurance for Europeans, because protecting their health, protecting their purchasing power, their employment and their sovereignty is what the European Green Deal achieves. We need to accelerate renewable energies, because it is the cleanest energy and also the cheapest that can be produced.

Mitigating is no longer enough, we have to adapt. And that is why we demand a binding law to protect workers exposed to extreme heat within the future Quality Employment Act. And we also demand a genuine European plan for adaptation to climate change.

Europe cannot keep waiting. We are negotiating the next European budget and in that negotiation it is being decided who wants to invest to protect people and who prefers to cut the instruments that protect them, who wants to reinforce climate action and who remains determined to weaken it.

I began this speech by speaking of thousands of citizens who have lost their lives and, precisely for them, our duty is to ensure that next summer we do not have to begin with this debate.

Defending the European Green Deal is defending lives, defending renewables is defending freedom in Europe and defending the just transition is, simply, defending Europeans.

3-0057-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, Mr Minister, actually, current EU climate policy is not able to protect EU citizens from heatwaves because it is primarily designed to reduce EU-based emissions faster than our EU global competitors and to close industrial jobs before having adequate sustainable replacement.

This is, by the way, not at all good for the climate, but mainly this policy weakens the European economy and increases electricity prices. The only way to effectively protect citizens from the impacts of climate change is to prioritise climate adaptation, and for that we need strong economy and cheap electricity – the exactly opposite outcomes than of current EU climate policy.

So you really want to protect citizens from heatwaves? Then please first make the climate policy more realistic and transfer the money to the climate adaptation.

3-0058-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signor Presidente del Consiglio, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, io ritengo che non possiamo perdere l'occasione di questo dibattito scendendo in questioni di ordine ideologico, perché la prevenzione – e la strategia per la prevenzione che si è data anche l'Unione europea – è la prima risposta che si deve dare a fenomeni come quello che abbiamo vissuto nelle settimane scorse e che assai verosimilmente vivremo nel corso di tutta l'estate.

Prevenzione anzitutto sotto il profilo sanitario, e bene hanno fatto quegli Stati membri – penso all'Italia – che hanno saputo dare sul fronte sanitario delle direttive chiare a tutte le Regioni per occuparsi in primo luogo degli anziani e della solitudine.

In secondo luogo, prevenzione significa adattare al cambiamento del clima le nostre infrastrutture, sia quelle energetiche sia quelle che si occupano della socialità. Ma prevenzione significa mettere in primo luogo la necessità che ogni investimento venga diretto per evitare che si possano verificare fenomeni che hanno un impatto sulla vita di ogni cittadino.

Vedete, Presidente e colleghi che siete intervenuti anche prima di me, l'adattamento al cambiamento climatico non vuol dire che l'uomo è una presenza non gradita nel sistema dell'ambiente. Adattamento al clima vuol dire che gli Stati – ciascun governo – devono saper adottare delle politiche e mettere a frutto gli investimenti che sono disponibili.

Allora il nostro dibattito anche su questo tema diventerà un dibattito seriamente sensato: abbandonare ogni approccio ideologico, concentrarsi – io apprezzo molto il lavoro che sta svolgendo la Commissaria – su temi pragmatici e pratici, che partono da regole che devono essere condivise.
3-0058-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Prime Minister, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, I believe we cannot miss the opportunity of this debate by descending into ideological issues, because prevention – and the prevention strategy that the European Union has also set for itself – is the first response that must be given to phenomena like the one we have experienced in recent weeks and which we will very likely experience throughout the summer.

First and foremost, prevention from a health perspective, and those Member States – I am thinking of Italy – did well when they were able to give clear directives on the health front to all Regions to look after the elderly and loneliness in the first place.

Secondly, prevention means adapting our infrastructures to climate change, both energy infrastructure and those dealing with social life. But prevention means prioritizing the need for every investment to be directed towards preventing the occurrence of phenomena that impact the life of every citizen.

You see, Mr President and colleagues who spoke before me, climate change adaptation does not mean that man is an unwelcome presence in the environmental system. Climate adaptation means that States – each government – must know how to adopt policies and make use of the investments that are available.

Then our debate on this issue too will become a seriously sensible debate: abandoning any ideological approach, focusing – and I very much appreciate the work the Commissioner is doing – on pragmatic and practical issues, starting from rules that must be shared.

3-0059-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, je voulais tout d’abord m’adresser à vous: merci pour l’engagement que vous avez dans cette politique de protection civile et la défense d’un monde qui se mobilise en ce moment.

Dans mon pays, plus de 15 000 hectares sont partis en fumée: c’est trois fois plus que l’an dernier à la même période. Je voulais remercier l’ensemble des députés qui sont engagés également dans l’intergroupe de protection civile. Ces éléments-là font l’actualité, mais vous êtes toujours là, également, à nos côtés, pour défendre cette politique aux côtés de Hadja Lahbib.

Le climat accélère, mais notre réponse, elle, reste trop lente. Nous ne pouvons pas davantage choisir entre atténuation et adaptation. Il faut combiner les deux politiques, c’est certain. Les feux de forêt ne sont plus seulement une conséquence du dérèglement climatique: ils en deviennent un accélérateur, parce que, lorsqu’une forêt brûle, elle rejette du carbone, et en plus elle ne peut plus en absorber.

Les fumées tuent, la canicule aussi. En 2003, il y a plus de vingt ans, nous disions: «Plus jamais cela!» Pour autant, depuis quarante ans ou presque sapeur-pompier, je suis sûr qu’à l’automne la plupart des décideurs politiques auront oublié l’émotion que suscite finalement cette situation.

La préparation ne peut plus être une politique d’urgence. Ce doit être un élément porté chaque jour, une politique d’anticipation portée par chaque citoyen, chaque entreprise, chacun d’entre nous.

Monsieur le Président, laissez-moi encore quelques secondes. Je viens d’apprendre, il y a quelques minutes, le décès d’un jeune sapeur-pompier volontaire, en France, qui luttait contre un feu. Nous ne sommes que début juillet. L’été sera compliqué…

(Le Président retire la parole à l’orateur)
3-0059-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I wanted first of all to address you: thank you for your commitment to this civil protection policy and the defense of a world that is mobilizing at the moment.

In my country, more than 15,000 hectares have gone up in smoke: that is three times more than last year over the same period. I wanted to thank all the Members who are also involved in the civil protection intergroup. These elements are making the news, but you are still there, alongside us, to defend this policy alongside Hadja Lahbib.

The climate is accelerating, but our response remains too slow. We can no longer choose between mitigation and adaptation. We must combine both policies, that is for sure. Forest fires are no longer just a consequence of climate change: they are becoming an accelerator of it, because when a forest burns, it releases carbon, and furthermore it can no longer absorb it.

Smoke kills, and so does the heatwave. In 2003, more than twenty years ago, we said: "Never again!" However, having been a firefighter for almost forty years, I am sure that by autumn most policymakers will have forgotten the emotion ultimately sparked by this situation.

Preparedness can no longer be an emergency policy. It must be an element supported every day, an anticipation policy carried out by every citizen, every business, each and every one of us.

Mr President, allow me a few more seconds. I have just learned, a few minutes ago, of the death of a young volunteer firefighter in France, who was fighting a fire. We are only at the beginning of July. The summer will be complicated...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

3-0060-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, at least 1 300 people died in a heatwave. I want us to be serious about it. Imagine, just for a moment, that 1 300 people had been killed in a terrorist attack. All of Europe would be mourning: the heads of states, the governments would have crisis meetings. We would be in a situation where we understand how dramatic that is, and we would offer our deepest condolences. We would take it much more seriously than we do now.

In this House, we need to finally understand that the climate crisis is severe – for thousands of lives, for real people. Just standing here, with cynical words, a next speech, is not enough. This is a consequence of political decisions taken by governments, taken by leaders, that are killing people in Europe. People are downplaying, blocking and delaying climate action also now – and I think we should make them account for what they are doing. They are responsible.

So here in this House I have a proposal to make: let us name the next heatwaves after the people actually fuelling them, causing them. So why don't we just say the next heatwave is called 'Friedrich' or 'Katherina' or 'Donald' or, I don't know, 'Vladimir'.

3-0061-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, deadly heatwaves, thunderstorms, flooding and rampant wildfires – this is the world that the wealthy and the powerful have created. These are the consequences of our fossil fuel‑based economies. This is human‑made climate change. And we must be honest – we are not prepared for this. Our buildings and our cities are not designed for this. Our agriculture, our nature cannot stand this. And we are not all affected in the same way – those who are already struggling are hit the hardest. They also lack the resources to change the systems or to change their own circumstances.

So while people are dying from the heat, what is the right wing doing? They also did not bother to show up for this debate. They are calling for the EU's most effective climate‑policy tool, the Emissions Trading System, to be weakened. Under pressure from polluting industries and from far‑right groups, they have been watering down Europe's climate policy throughout this whole mandate.

The most important response, the most important preparedness, is to stand against the weakening of the EU's climate policy. We will stand against the weakening of the EU's climate policy because we know we must cut our dependencies on fossil fuels. We must tax the oil and gas companies and use the money to invest in climate‑friendly choices and adaptations that are accessible to everyone, not only for the rich and the wealthy.

3-0062-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, en Europe, moins d’un foyer sur cinq est équipé d’un climatiseur. Aux États-Unis et au Japon, neuf foyers sur dix en possèdent. Et pourtant, avec l’argent du contribuable, nous sommes tellement riches que nous climatisons le monde entier. L’Agence française de développement prête 20 millions d’euros pour rénover la climatisation d’une banque en Thaïlande, elle verse 7 millions pour équiper des bâtiments administratifs à Djibouti, elle installe des climatiseurs à technologie Inverter dans les dispensaires du Sénégal. Quant à l’Europe, elle offre 11 climatiseurs à un service de pédiatrie du Monténégro, elle prête 40 millions d’euros pour climatiser un hôpital neuf de 250 lits en Turquie, elle cofinance la climatisation des hôpitaux tunisiens de Gafsa et de Sidi Bouzid.

Vous financez le confort thermique à l’autre bout du monde pendant que vous expliquez aux Européens qu’ils doivent souffrir en silence et sans clim parce que ça pollue. Alors, assez de vos leçons de morale! Assez de vos gabegies! Ce n’est pas votre argent, c’est celui des Européens.
3-0062-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, in Europe, less than one home in five is equipped with an air conditioner. In the United States and Japan, nine homes out of ten have one. And yet, with taxpayers' money, we are so rich that we are air-conditioning the entire world. The French Development Agency is lending 20 million euros to renovate the air conditioning of a bank in Thailand, it is paying 7 million to equip administrative buildings in Djibouti, it is installing Inverter technology air conditioners in dispensaries in Senegal. As for Europe, it is offering 11 air conditioners to a pediatric department in Montenegro, it is lending 40 million euros to air-condition a new 250-bed hospital in Turkey, it is co-financing the air conditioning of Tunisian hospitals in Gafsa and Sidi Bouzid.

You are financing thermal comfort at the other end of the world while telling Europeans that they must suffer in silence and without air conditioning because it pollutes. So, enough of your moral lessons! Enough of your waste! This is not your money, it is the Europeans' money.

3-0063-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, first of all, I would like to thank you all for your constructive and positive contribution to this debate so far. What I've heard is really encouraging. I think that we are all on the same page that we need to work without ideology. And what I've heard so far nearly goes far beyond ideology.

Because indeed, as you rightly say, Ms García Pérez, this is the lethal reality of climate change that we are facing today. And we cannot deny this reality. That's why also I count on your support for the negotiation of the next MFF. We propose, on behalf of the Commission, a very ambitious budget, to have a EU CPM here – a comprehensive manner to respond to the climate change and to the risks we are facing today.

You've raised the importance of helping the people who live in rural areas. Yes, people and local communities play a major role in wildfire risk prevention and management. The share of wildfire ignition caused by human activity in the EU by far exceeds those from natural causes and could be as high as 96 % – 96 % caused by human activity.

Complementing the preparedness union strategy, the Commission today proposes to promote and disseminate good practices in wildfire risk assessment and awareness and community involvement, for example through the EU CPM Knowledge Network, develop a toolkit for supporting resilience-building and promote volunteering and exchange opportunities in the field of preparedness.

We are working also with Member States on guidelines to increase awareness about risks and threats, with particular attention to ensuring that information is accessible, inclusive and adapted to the needs of groups at risk.

I totally agree that EU CPM, our mechanism of civil protection, is European solidarity at its best, and we need to develop it further. That is why we presented one year ago our new preparedness strategy. We will present also, as requested by Mr Knotek, a climate adaptation plan that will be presented by Commissioner Hoekstra in autumn.

Yes, I totally agree that the first responders are always Member States. They are the ones who need to spend the money and the budget we allocate on the right funds. That is why also we need to adapt our cities with the RFF, for instance, or the solidarity funds, because we must protect our citizens and particularly those living also in urban areas by making our cities, buildings and public spaces more resilient.

Finally, I will respond to Mr Allione.

Si nous avons aujourd’hui le cœur lourd en raison du nombre de morts qui ne cesse d’augmenter – je regardais hier encore dans le journal tous ces citoyens qui refusent de quitter leur village dans le sud de la France parce qu’ils y sont attachés, parce qu’ils y sont nés, parce qu’ils veulent y voir grandir leurs enfants et aussi parce qu’ils veulent contribuer, même avec parfois des bouteilles d’eau simplement, à réduire l’ampleur des feux –, nous ne sommes pas à un moment où il faut pleurer, où il faut présenter nos condoléances. Même si nous avons le cœur lourd, nous devons absolument agir!

Et nous ne cessons d’agir, vous le savez: nous avons activé le mécanisme déjà de nombreuses fois depuis le début de la saison, qui a commencé fin avril. Jamais la «saison des feux», comme on l’appelle malheureusement maintenant, n’a commencé aussi tôt. Et oui, quand il s’agit de reconnaître le statut des volontaires et des pompiers, nous y travaillons, même si cela ressort plutôt de la compétence de la commissaire Mînzatu.

Nous avons aujourd’hui, pour la première fois, des échanges de jeunes sapeurs-pompiers, de jeunes volontaires qui ont lieu à Varsovie. Ce n’est jamais arrivé avant. Nous voulons aussi contribuer à créer de la prise de conscience, à avoir une nouvelle génération, qui est plus à même de répondre à ces dangers et à ce réchauffement climatique.

3-0065-0000.sourceText:
Thank you very much, Commissioner. We have more than 20 catch-the-eyes, I want to inform you. This is because it's a really important debate, and I understand it.

I only kindly ask you to respect the time that we have, because then we will be able to take as many Members as possible intervening in this important debate.

3-0066-0000.sourceText:
�� Senhor Presidente, a União Europeia já conta este ano com mais de 118 000 hectares ardidos até ao início de julho, acima da média dos últimos 20 anos.

Portugal sabe que estes números não são abstrações. Sabe o que significa ver aldeias cercadas pelas chamas, sabe o que significa retirar populações à pressa, o que significa perder casas, empresas, explorações agrícolas, floresta, solo fértil e memória coletiva.

Pela primeira vez em Portugal, a participação das Forças Armadas na prevenção e combate direto aos incêndios é um sinal de compromisso e prontidão. Mostra que Portugal mobiliza todos os instrumentos do Estado quando as populações estão em risco.

Mas se um Estado-Membro precisa de mobilizar todos os seus meios nacionais tão cedo no verão, então a União Europeia tem de responder com outra escala. É justo reconhecer que a União Europeia avançou. Mas sejamos claros, já não basta. A Europa tem de deixar de chegar quando o país já está exausto, tem de chegar antes.

Por isso, desafio a Comissão Europeia a ir mais longe. Precisamos de transformar o RescEU numa verdadeira força permanente europeia de combate a incêndios, com meios aéreos próprios, com brigadas multinacionais e com pré-posicionamento automático nas regiões de maior risco.

Desafio também a Comissão a mudar a lógica do financiamento europeu. A prevenção tem de ser uma prioridade central do próximo orçamento europeu: gestão de combustível, cadastro, caminhos florestais, pontos de água, apoio ao mundo rural e tecnologia de deteção precoce.

E precisamos de justiça mais firme: a resposta penal não pode ser simbólica.

Temos verões cada vez mais longos, mais secos e mais extremos. A escala da ameaça mudou, a resposta europeia tem de mudar também.

(A oradora recusa uma pergunta «cartão azul» de João Oliveira)
3-0066-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the European Union has already recorded more than 118,000 hectares burned by the beginning of July this year, above the average of the last 20 years.

Portugal knows that these numbers are not abstractions. It knows what it means to see villages surrounded by flames, it knows what it means to evacuate populations in a hurry, what it means to lose homes, businesses, farms, forests, fertile soil and collective memory.

For the first time in Portugal, the participation of the Armed Forces in the prevention and direct fight against fires is a sign of commitment and readiness. It shows that Portugal mobilizes all state instruments when populations are at risk.

But if a Member State needs to mobilize all its national resources so early in the summer, then the European Union must respond on a different scale. It is fair to recognize that the European Union has progressed. But let us be clear, it is no longer enough. Europe must stop arriving when the country is already exhausted, it must arrive sooner.

Therefore, I challenge the European Commission to go further. We need to transform RescEU into a true permanent European firefighting force, with its own aerial assets, multinational brigades and automatic pre-positioning in the highest-risk regions.

I also challenge the Commission to change the logic of European funding. Prevention must be a central priority of the next European budget: fuel management, land registry, forest roads, water points, support for the rural world and early detection technology.

And we need firmer justice: the penal response cannot be symbolic.

We have increasingly longer, drier and more extreme summers. The scale of the threat has changed, the European response must change too.

(The speaker declines a "blue card" question from João Oliveira)

3-0067-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, tijdens de laatste hittegolf werd het voetbaltoernooi van mijn zoontje afgelast. Een enorme teleurstelling voor mijn zoon, maar het was simpelweg te warm om nog veilig te kunnen spelen. En met een knuffel kom je dan al heel ver om die teleurstelling weg te nemen. Maar dat is natuurlijk klein leed, want op andere plekken in Europa gingen tijdens diezelfde hittegolf mensenlevens verloren en bosbranden verwoestten complete gebieden.

En toch blijven rechtse partijen in dit huis, in het Parlement stemmen tegen verduurzaming, tegen vergroening, en klimaatmaatregelen vertragen en fossiele belangen beschermen. Ik vraag me echt af: wanneer houdt het op? Bij tienduizend doden, bij honderdduizend doden? Wanneer stoppen we met die cognitieve dissonantie? Wanneer erkennen klimaatontkenners en partijen die hen napraten dat dit een probleem is van vandaag en niet pas van morgen? We weten wat er moet gebeuren. We moeten stoppen met fossiele subsidies. We moeten die energietransitie versnellen. Ik vraag maar één ding: bescherm onze mensen tegen hitte.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
3-0067-0000.englishText:
Mr President, during the last heatwave my son's football tournament was cancelled. A huge disappointment for my son, but it was simply too warm to still be able to play safely. And a cuddle will get you a very long way to take away that disappointment. But of course that is minor suffering, because in other places in Europe human lives were lost during that same heatwave and wildfires devastated entire areas.

And yet right-wing parties in this house, in Parliament continue to vote against sustainability, against greening, and delay climate measures and protect fossil interests. I really wonder: when will it stop? At ten thousand deaths, at a hundred thousand deaths? When do we stop this cognitive dissonance? When will climate deniers and parties that echo them acknowledge that this is a problem of today and not just of tomorrow? We know what needs to happen. We must stop fossil subsidies. We must accelerate that energy transition. I am asking for only one thing: protect our people against heat.

(The speaker agrees to answer a "blue card" question)

3-0068-0000.sourceText: Taip, gerbiamas pranešėjau. Jūs, socialdemokratai, labai kovojate su klimato kaita, su CO2, kad būtų nulinis CO2 išmetimas. Ir čia Europa tikrai padarė didelę pažangą. Pramonė, faktiškai, galima sakyti, stagnuoja, CO2 mažiau išmetama, bet Europa labiausiai kenčia nuo karščių. Ką jūs ne taip darote?
3-0068-0000.englishText: Yes, esteemed speaker. You, Social Democrats, are fighting very hard against climate change, against CO2, so that there would be zero CO2 emissions. And here Europe has indeed made great progress. Industry is, in fact, one might say, stagnating, less CO2 is emitted, but Europe suffers the most from heatwaves. What are you doing wrong?

3-0069-0000.sourceText: Maybe he should try to answer that question himself. I mean, it's very clear we are trying our best from day one to show more ambition, to take also our historical responsibility. And this is a consequence of that. You know, scientists are very clear: whatever we can do to lower global warming, the more lives we can save. This is something that we have been telling you for quite a while. So what can we do now? We should do a bit more, and we should convince the rest of the world to do more.

3-0070-0000.sourceText:
Tisztelt Elnök Úr! Rendkívüli aszállyal nézünk szembe. A Copernicus aszálymegfigyelő adatai szerint júniusban tovább romlott a helyzet, ami azt is jelenti, hogy riasztási szintű aszály alakult ki többek között Németországban, Franciaországban, de Magyarországon is. Az én hazámban áprilisban a szokásos csapadékmennyiségnek csak a tizede hullott, 4 mm. 2021. óta akkora csapadékhiány halmozódott fel, mint a teljes évnyi csapadékmennyiség. Ennyinek felel meg. Jelentős beruházásokra van szükség a vízvisszatartás és az öntözött területek növelése érdekében, de ehhez uniós forrásokra is szükség van. Ehhez képest az Európai Bizottság 20%-kal megvágná az agrárkasszát a hétéves költségvetésben.

Sokan kérjük arra az Európai Bizottságot, hogy változtasson ezen, biztosítson külön forrásokat, ne csak a vízvisszatartásra, létesítményfejlesztésre, hanem az öntözésfejlesztésre is. Utóbbi ugyanis nagyon kis hangsúlyt kap a Bizottság terveiben. Ha nem lesz elég víz, akkor nem lesz élelmiszerbiztonság sem, pláne nem megfizethető áron.

(A felszólaló hajlandó válaszolni egy kékkártyás kérdésre)
3-0070-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! We are facing an extraordinary drought. According to Copernicus drought monitoring data, the situation deteriorated further in June, which also means that an alert-level drought has developed in Germany, France, and Hungary, among others. In my homeland, only a tenth of the usual amount of precipitation fell in April, namely 4 mm. Since 2021, a precipitation deficit equivalent to an entire year's worth of precipitation has accumulated. It corresponds to this. Significant investments are needed to increase water retention and irrigated areas, but EU funds are also needed for this. In contrast, the European Commission would cut the agricultural fund by 20% in the seven-year budget.

Many of us are asking the European Commission to change this, to provide separate funds not only for water retention and facility development, but also for irrigation development. The latter receives very little emphasis in the Commission's plans. If there is not enough water, there will be no food security either, let alone at an affordable price.

(The speaker agrees to take a blue card question)

3-0071-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleague, over the past four years, more than 200 000 people have died from heat in Europe. This week, temperatures are exceeding 30 °C in cities across the Continent. And work continues on construction sites and in fields regardless. I agree on your point on water, definitely. But so far, the far right, together with many right-wing parties, has said 'no' to the binding rules on really tackling the climate crisis and really protecting workers from heat at their workplaces.

So please, tell us directly, how many deaths would it take to convince you and your colleagues in your parties that this isn't a hypothetical situation or problem, but something that is happening right now, killing people all over the European Union?

3-0072-0000.sourceText: Köszönöm a kérdését. Azt hiszem, hogy a célban egyetértünk: abban, hogy a klímaváltozás következményei ellen fel kell lépni, de az, hogy hogyan kezeljük ezt, abban már eltérő megközelítéseink vannak. Önök, és mondhatom azt, hogy a baloldali nagykoalíció egy tervgazdasági megközelítéssel dolgoznak, ami azt jelenti, hogy olyan terveket tesznek kötelezővé, amelyekről nagyon hamar kiderül, hogy nem teljesülnek, és mindeközben nincsenek tekintettel arra, hogy milyen következményei vannak ezeknek a terveknek. Gondoljanak csak az autóiparra! Beletolták az európai autóipart kötelező tervekbe, kötelező átállásba, következésképp tönkremennek. A Volkswagen ennek is következményeként jelentette be, hogy százezer embertől válik meg, százezer munkahely szűnik meg, ez a következménye az Önök politikájának.
3-0072-0000.englishText: Thank you for your question. I believe we agree on the goal: that we must act against the consequences of climate change, but how we handle this, we already have different approaches. You, and I can say that the left-wing grand coalition, work with a planned economy approach, which means that you make plans mandatory that very soon turn out not to be fulfilled, and meanwhile you do not care about what consequences these plans have. Just think of the automotive industry! You pushed the European automotive industry into mandatory plans, a mandatory transition, consequently they are going bankrupt. Partly as a consequence of this, Volkswagen announced that it is parting with a hundred thousand people, a hundred thousand jobs are disappearing, this is the consequence of your policy.

3-0073-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, în ultimele săptămâni, Europa a ars și s-a inundat în același timp. Franța, Spania și Italia au înregistrat temperaturi de peste 38 de grade. România a fost lovită de furtuni violente, inundații și distrugeri. Răspunsul Uniunii Europene rămâne însă prea des unul birocratic. Vorbim despre obiective pentru anul 2050, în timp ce oamenii au nevoie de soluții astăzi.

Pactul verde a rămas un exercițiu birocratic construit pe reguli multe și costuri mari pentru cetățeni și industrie - contrazis de știință. Un raport recent arată că reducerea aerosolilor proveniți din arderea cărbunelui a contribuit la creșterea încălzirii globale cu 1 grad Celsius în orașele europene. Asta în condițiile în care Uniunea Europeană a împovărat industria europeană, a crescut costul vieții, a diminuat competitivitatea economiei noastre.

Cetățenii Europei nu mai au nevoie de promisiuni pentru 2050. Și încă un lucru: încercarea de a introduce „cu ligheanul lumină în casa fără ferestre” nu e știință - este prostie în stare pură.
3-0073-0000.englishText:
Mr President, in recent weeks, Europe has burned and flooded at the same time. France, Spain and Italy recorded temperatures of over 38 degrees. Romania has been hit by violent storms, floods and destruction.

The European Union's response remains, however, too often a bureaucratic one. We are talking about targets for the year 2050, while people need solutions today.

The Green Deal has remained a bureaucratic exercise built on many rules and high costs for citizens and industry - contradicted by science. A recent report shows that the reduction of aerosols from coal burning has contributed to an increase in global warming by 1 degree Celsius in European cities. This is under conditions where the European Union has burdened European industry, increased the cost of living, and diminished the competitiveness of our economy.

The citizens of Europe no longer need promises for 2050. And one more thing: trying to introduce "light with a washbasin into the windowless house" is not science - it is pure stupidity.

3-0074-0000.sourceText:
Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem. Ako je možné, že v roku 2026 sú v Európe krajiny, kde nemocnice nemajú klimatizáciu, kde je počas horúčav 42 stupňov na izbe? Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré ani nerátajú, nerátajú úmrtia kvôli horúčavám? Čiže ani nevieme, koľko ľudí vlastne zomrelo. Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré majú ministrov, ktorí sa zrazu zobudili do toho, že existuje zmena klímy, a nepočúvali o tom posledných 30 rokov? A potom, potom budeme počúvať o tom, že za všetko zlé môže Brusel. Ten zlý magický Brusel. A pritom v mnohých členských krajinách stále stovkami miliónov, miliardami, dotujeme fosílnu ideológiu, dotujeme fosílnu loby. Namiesto toho, aby sme presne tieto peniaze, ale aj európske peniaze, použili na pomoc poľnohospodárom, na pomoc mestám udržať si zeleň, na modernizáciu nemocníc tak, aby pacienti neležali pri horúčavách na izbách a sestričky neodpadávali pri operáciách. Ďakujem.

(Rečník súhlasil, že odpovie na otázku položenú zdvihnutím modrej karty)
3-0074-0000.englishText:
Vážený pán predsedajúci, ďakujem. Ako je možné, že v roku 2026 sú v Európe krajiny, kde nemocnice nemajú klimatizáciu, kde je počas horúčav 42 stupňov na izbe? Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré ani nerátajú, nerátajú úmrtia kvôli horúčavám? Čiže ani nevieme, koľko ľudí vlastne zomrelo. Ako je možné, že sú v Európe krajiny, ktoré majú ministrov, ktorí sa zrazu zobudili do toho, že existuje zmena klímy, a nepočúvali o tom posledných 30 rokov? A potom, potom budeme počúvať o tom, že za všetko zlé môže Brusel. Ten zlý magický Brusel. A pritom v mnohých členských krajinách stále stovkami miliónov, miliardami, dotujeme fosílnu ideológiu, dotujeme fosílnu loby. Namiesto toho, aby sme presne tieto peniaze, ale aj európske peniaze, použili na pomoc poľnohospodárom, na pomoc mestám udržať si zeleň, na modernizáciu nemocníc tak, aby pacienti neležali pri horúčavách na izbách a sestričky neodpadávali pri operáciách. Ďakujem.

(Rečník súhlasil, že odpovie na otázku položenú zdvihnutím modrej karty)

3-0075-0000.sourceText:
Esteemed colleague, with the heatwave, more than ever we need a cooling strategy, and in that cooling strategy also an action plan for geothermal energy, in order to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels.

Now, the Commission has been promising that to be delivered in May, then in June, then it was postponed. Now it's July. So I would like to ask about your views about that cooling strategy, and particularly on the role of geothermal.

3-0076-0000.sourceText:
Indeed, we are walking on the very heat, but also cold – let's be honest, from here you can make cold – that's physics – that we need. Geothermal is the very one we have been overlooking and understating.

So I expect the Commission to come up now, in the electrification strategy, with a very concrete, dedicated action on next-generation geothermal, so we can use it both for electricity, as well as heating, and right now, cooling.

3-0077-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, señor presidente en ejercicio del Consejo, (la oradora se expresa en una lengua no oficial), así reaccionaba Núria, una pagesa catalana al ver cómo las llamas de los incendios que estos días afectan a Cataluña convertían el territorio en cenizas. Eventos climáticos extremos como las olas de calor o los incendios de sexta generación, que ya forman parte de los veranos en el sur de Europa, son cada vez más frecuentes en el centro y en el norte del continente.

(La oradora se expresa en una lengua no oficial), decía Núria, y hemos dejado de escucharla. El ritmo del sistema bajo el que vivimos es incompatible con la sostenibilidad del mundo en el cual residimos. Frente a un mundo complejo, rápido y expansivo, la solución pasa por potenciar las formas de vida arraigadas al territorio y en armonía con el entorno.

Ni la tierra es plana ni el callo solar funciona. O apostamos por la ciencia, la evidencia y la gestión regional y local del territorio o el negacionismo climático conseguirá que Europa se convierta en un cenicero gigante.

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0077-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, Mr President-in-Office of the Council, (the speaker speaks in an unofficial language), this is how Núria, a Catalan peasant woman, reacted when she saw how the flames of the fires affecting Catalonia these days were turning the land into ashes. Extreme weather events such as heat waves or sixth-generation fires, which are already part of summers in southern Europe, are increasingly frequent in the center and north of the continent.

(The speaker speaks in an unofficial language), Núria said, and we have stopped listening to her. The rhythm of the system under which we live is incompatible with the sustainability of the world in which we reside. Faced with a complex, rapid and expansive world, the solution involves promoting ways of life rooted in the territory and in harmony with the environment.

Neither is the earth flat nor does solar callousing work. Either we bet on science, evidence and regional and local management of the territory, or climate denialism will make Europe turn into a giant ashtray.

(The speaker agrees to answer a question raised under the blue card procedure)

3-0078-0000.sourceText: Señor presidente, este año se calculan ya 20 000 muertes en Europa, la mitad de ellas de personas mayores, y seguimos sin hacer nada. La falta de inversiones para adaptar sus viviendas no está siendo una prioridad para esta comisión. Muchas residencias de mayores tampoco cumplen con la adaptación climática. En Europa los mayores sufren un edadismo que les hace vivir peor y morir antes. Pregúntense, señorías, porque todos llegaremos a mayores, ¿por qué dejamos de ser sujetos con derechos a partir de cierta edad y pasamos a convertirnos en objetos que hay que esconder o apartar y cuya vida ya no vale nada? ¿Es esto lo que queremos? Yo, sinceramente, no.
3-0078-0000.englishText: Mr President, this year an estimated 20,000 deaths are already expected in Europe, half of them among elderly people, and we are still doing nothing. The lack of investment to adapt their homes is not being a priority for this Commission. Many nursing homes also fail to meet climate adaptation standards. In Europe, the elderly suffer from ageism that makes them live worse and die sooner. Ask yourselves, honourable members, because we will all grow old, why do we stop being subjects with rights from a certain age and become objects that must be hidden or set aside, and whose lives are no longer worth anything? Is this what we want? I, honestly, do not.

3-0079-0000.sourceText: Creo que es verdad que estamos hablando a grandes rasgos, pero, cuando vemos la cifra de miles de muertos que también han expuesto nuestros compañeros, dentro de estas cifras hay una mayoría que son los mayores de edad. Creo que tenemos que prestar más atención a estos grupos vulnerables —la gente mayor y los menores—. Hemos visto que en Alemania no hay ni un hospital que esté climatizado, no hay residencias climatizadas, tampoco hay escuelas bien climatizadas en toda Europa. Tenemos que adaptarnos urgentemente a esta situación, porque el cambio climático creo que nos pone dos objetivos por delante: la descarbonización —de la que hemos hablado—, el Pacto Verde, pero también la adaptación, que ya hoy es una realidad de esta subida de las temperaturas.
3-0079-0000.englishText: I think it is true that we are speaking in broad terms, but, when we see the figure of thousands of deaths that our colleagues have also presented, within these figures there is a majority who are older adults. I think we need to pay more attention to these vulnerable groups—the elderly and minors. We have seen that in Germany there is not a single hospital that is air-conditioned, there are no air-conditioned care homes, nor are there well-air-conditioned schools throughout Europe. We urgently need to adapt to this situation, because climate change, I think, places two objectives before us: decarbonisation—which we have spoken about—, the Green Deal, but also adaptation, which is already a reality today of this rise in temperatures.

3-0080-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η κλιματική κρίση είναι εδώ, κι ας μην την αναγνωρίζουν οι συντηρητικοί μιμητές του Τραμπ, κι ας την υποτιμά ακόμα και η κυρία von der Leyen. Ο καύσωνας σκοτώνει, οι πυρκαγιές καταστρέφουν, οι χώρες του ευρωπαϊκού Νότου δοκιμάζονται. Στην πρώτη γραμμή βρίσκεται η Κύπρος. Ακραίες θερμοκρασίες, παρατεταμένη ξηρασία, καμένα δάση, χαμένες περιουσίες, ανθρώπινες ζωές σε κίνδυνο.

Δεν αρκεί να μετράμε τις καταστροφές. Χρειαζόμαστε περισσότερη πρόληψη, όχι με κριτήριο το κόστος. Περισσότερη ανθεκτικότητα. Περισσότερη ευρωπαϊκή αλληλεγγύη. Η Κύπρος, λόγω της στρατηγικής γεωγραφικής της θέσης, μπορεί και πρέπει να γίνει πρότυπο ευρωπαϊκό περιφερειακό κέντρο δασοπυρόσβεσης και πολιτικής προστασίας για την Ανατολική Μεσόγειο, με μόνιμα εναέρια μέσα, με εξειδικευμένο προσωπικό, με επαρκή ευρωπαϊκή χρηματοδότηση. Η κλιματική κρίση δεν γνωρίζει σύνορα ούτε η ευρωπαϊκή αλληλεγγύη πρέπει να προσφέρεται με το σταγονόμετρο.
3-0080-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the climate crisis is here, even if Donald Trump's conservative imitators do not recognize it, and even if Mrs von der Leyen underestimates it. The heatwave kills, fires destroy, the countries of the European South are tested. On the front line is Cyprus. Extreme temperatures, prolonged drought, burnt forests, lost properties, human lives in danger.

It is not enough to count the disasters. We need more prevention, not based on cost. More resilience. More European solidarity. Cyprus, due to its strategic geographical position, can and must become a model European regional firefighting and civil protection hub for the Eastern Mediterranean, with permanent aerial assets, specialized personnel, with adequate European funding. The climate crisis knows no borders, nor should European solidarity be offered drop by drop.

3-0081-0000.sourceText:
�� Vážený pán predsedajúci. Tie vlny horúčav sú skutočne niekedy naozaj neznesiteľné, ale teda hovoríte, že musíme znižovať emisie, že musíme obmedzovať dopravu a obmedzovať priemysel, aby sme zastavili to otepľovanie. A ja mám na vás, kolegovia, jednu možno trošku konšpiračnú, ale – podľa mňa – úplne legitímnu otázku. Čo ak sa to otepľovanie napriek tomu drastickému znižovaniu emisií jednoducho nezastaví? V roku 1990 sme mali nejakú úroveň emisií, teraz sa tá úroveň emisií znížila údajne o 40 % oproti roku 1990. Teplo je napriek tomu stále. Kde máte garanciu, že keď znížime tie emisie o 90 %, že to otepľovanie jednoducho nebude? Čo keď bude jediným výsledkom vašej zelenej politiky, vášho Green Dealu, to, že si zničíme naše hospodárstvo, náš priemysel a aj tak bude v Európe teplo? Podľa mňa treba viac peňazí investovať práve na tú adaptáciu, investovať ich do klimatizácií, do vodozádržných opatrení, na boj proti suchám alebo do budovania viac zelených miest, aby tam nebol len samý žeravý betón. Jednoducho pripravovať sa na to, že to teplo v Európe bude.

(Rečník odmietol otázku, ktorú zdvihnutím modrej karty položil Martin Hojsík)
3-0081-0000.englishText:
Mr. Chairman. Those heat waves are really sometimes truly unbearable, but you say that we must reduce emissions, that we must restrict transport and restrict industry to stop that warming. And I have one, perhaps a bit conspiratorial, but - in my opinion - completely legitimate question for you, colleagues. What if that warming simply does not stop despite that drastic reduction in emissions? In 1990 we had a certain level of emissions, now that emission level has allegedly decreased by 40% compared to 1990. It is still hot despite that. Where do you have the guarantee that when we reduce those emissions by 90%, that warming simply will not happen? What if the only result of your green policy, your Green Deal, will be that we destroy our economy, our industry and it will still be hot in Europe? In my opinion, more money should be invested precisely in that adaptation, investing it in air conditioning, in water retention measures, in the fight against droughts or in building greener cities so that there is not just glowing concrete everywhere. Simply preparing for the fact that there will be heat in Europe.

(The speaker declined a question asked by Martin Hojsík via the raising of a blue card)

3-0082-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κάθε καλοκαίρι ίδια συζήτηση, ίδια λάθη. Η φύση δεν μας αιφνιδίασε. Η επιστήμη προειδοποιεί εδώ και δεκαετίες. Εσείς όμως κάθε φορά που έπρεπε να διαλέξετε ανάμεσα στο περιβάλλον και το κέρδος, διαλέγατε το κέρδος. Δώσατε γη και ύδωρ —δάση, ακτές, φυσικούς πόρους—, στο όνομα μιας δήθεν ανάπτυξης. Σήμερα τον λογαριασμό δεν τον πληρώνουν όσοι κέρδισαν· τον πληρώνουν οι λαοί.

Δεν υπάρχουν πλέον φυσικές καταστροφές χωρίς πολιτικές ευθύνες. Η κλιματική αλλαγή δεν είναι άλλοθι της πολιτικής αδράνειας. Και όχι, δεν μπορούμε να μιλάμε για ετοιμότητα, όταν απέναντι σε μόνιμους κινδύνους εξακολουθείτε να στέλνετε εποχικούς εργαζόμενους. Δεν μπορούμε να μιλάμε για προστασία των πολιτών, όταν ζητάμε από οικοδόμους, αγρότες, διανομείς, εργαζόμενους στην ύπαιθρο και διασώστες να εργάζονται κάτω από ακραίες θερμοκρασίες και χωρίς επαρκή προστασία.

Σας ζητώ να χρηματοδοτήσει η Ευρώπη την πρόληψη, τη διαχείριση των δασών, τις αντιπυρικές ζώνες, την προστασία των οικισμών και την προστασία των ανθρώπων που βρίσκονται στην πρώτη γραμμή.
3-0082-0000.englishText:
Mr President, every summer the same discussion, the same mistakes. Nature did not catch us by surprise. Science has been warning us for decades. Yet every time you had to choose between the environment and profit, you chose profit. You gave land and water —forests, coasts, natural resources— in the name of a so-called development. Today, the bill is not being paid by those who profited; it is being paid by the peoples.

There are no longer natural disasters without political responsibilities. Climate change is not an alibi for political inertia. And no, we cannot talk about preparedness when, in the face of permanent dangers, you continue to send seasonal workers. We cannot talk about protecting citizens when we ask builders, farmers, delivery workers, rural workers, and rescuers to work under extreme temperatures and without adequate protection.

I ask you that Europe funds prevention, forest management, firebreaks, the protection of settlements, and the protection of the people on the front line.

3-0083-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: SOPHIE WILMÈS

Vice-President

3-0084-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin! Europa brennt mal wieder, und das ist längst keine Ausnahme mehr; es ist zur neuen Realität geworden, und das hat sehr viel mit Klimaveränderung zu tun. Allein in diesem Jahr wurden bereits 1000 Waldbrände registriert, fast doppelt so viele wie im Durchschnitt der vergangenen Jahrzehnte. 2025 war das zerstörerischste Waldbrandjahr in der Geschichte der EU – mehr als 1 Mio. Hektar wurden verwüstet. Frankreich und Portugal haben den Katastrophenschutzmechanismus erst vor wenigen Tagen erneut aktivieren müssen.

Wir reden nicht über ein Zukunftsszenario, wir reden über die traurige Gegenwart. Die Kommission hat bereits über 800 Feuerwehrkräfte aus 14 Ländern in den Hochrisikogebieten Südeuropas vorpositioniert; das ist richtig, das ist notwendig, aber es wird leider nicht reichen, denn wir haben es längst nicht mehr mit einzelnen Extremereignissen zu tun.

Wir arbeiten gerade auch mit Hochdruck daran, den sogenannten Europäischen Katastrophenschutzmechanismus weiterzuentwickeln, wir brauchen aber weitere Investitionen in Prävention, moderne Frühwarnsysteme, klimaresistente Wälder und den Schutz unserer Einsatzkräfte. Unser Leitgedanke muss sein, Krisen antizipieren statt improvisieren, vorbereiten statt hinterherlaufen, handeln, bevor eine Lage eskaliert.

Ich möchte diese Rede hier auch nutzen, um diejenigen in den Fokus unserer Aufmerksamkeit zu stellen, die das verdienen: Wer löscht den Brand, wenn es brennt? Es sind natürlich die Feuerwehrmänner und -frauen. In Europa gibt es ungefähr 2 Mio., 2,5 Mio. freiwillige Feuerwehrleute – die müssen wir in den Fokus stellen. Die müssen wir nicht nur schützen, wir müssen sogar diese Freiwilligkeit fördern. Dazu gehört auch, dass wir unsere Systeme der sozialen Sicherheit an diese Freiwilligkeit anpassen. Europa brennt, und wir müssen dem helfen, der den Brand löscht.
3-0084-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner! Europe is burning once again, and this is long no longer an exception; it has become the new reality, and that has a great deal to do with climate change. This year alone, 1,000 wildfires have already been registered, almost twice as many as the average of past decades. 2025 was the most destructive wildfire year in the history of the EU - more than 1 million hectares were devastated. France and Portugal had to reactivate the Civil Protection Mechanism just a few days ago.

We are not talking about a future scenario, we are talking about the sad present. The Commission has already pre-positioned over 800 firefighters from 14 countries in the high-risk areas of southern Europe; that is right, that is necessary, but unfortunately it will not be enough, because we are long no longer dealing with isolated extreme events.

We are currently also working at full speed to further develop the so-called European Civil Protection Mechanism, but we need further investments in prevention, modern early warning systems, climate-resilient forests and the protection of our emergency personnel. Our guiding principle must be to anticipate crises instead of improvising, to prepare instead of lagging behind, to act before a situation escalates.

I would also like to use this speech here to put those in the focus of our attention who deserve it: Who puts out the fire when it burns? It is, of course, the male and female firefighters. In Europe there are approximately 2 million, 2.5 million volunteer firefighters - we must put them in the focus. We must not only protect them, we must even promote this volunteer work. This also includes that we adapt our social security systems to this volunteer work. Europe is burning, and we must help those who put out the fire.

3-0085-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, in Europa siamo già alla terza ondata di super caldo e siamo solo all'inizio di luglio, quindi i dati sul cambiamento climatico sono indiscutibili e chi oggi si esercita nel negazionismo è semplicemente pazzo.

Quindi, devono stare fuori dalla politica quelli che negano il cambiamento climatico, perché il nostro dovere è rispondere ai bisogni dei cittadini. E vedo, comunque, che i banchi vuoti dell'estrema destra vanno in questa direzione.

Il punto, oggi, è quello delle nuove diseguaglianze che si stanno creando: diseguaglianze nell'accesso al raffreddamento, diseguaglianze nelle fasce di età, diseguaglianze anche sul piano dei migranti – stanno aumentando i migranti climatici – quindi, c'è un forte nesso tra giustizia ambientale e giustizia sociale.

Serve un approccio di ecologia integrale – quello che già Papa Francesco indicava – dove si danno risposte integrate soprattutto a chi è più vulnerabile.

L'Europa ha fatto molto: prenda in mano il timone e soprattutto si porti dietro tutti, e non solo alcuni.
3-0085-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, in Europe we are already experiencing the third super-heatwave and it is only the beginning of July, so the data on climate change are indisputable and anyone who engages in denialism today is simply crazy.

Therefore, those who deny climate change must stay out of politics, because our duty is to respond to the needs of citizens. And I see, anyway, that the empty benches of the far right go in this direction.

The point today is that of the new inequalities that are being created: inequalities in access to cooling, generational inequalities, inequalities also regarding migrants - climate migrants are increasing - therefore, there is a strong link between environmental justice and social justice.

An integral ecology approach is needed - the one that Pope Francis already indicated - where integrated responses are given above all to the most vulnerable.

Europe has done a lot: it should take the helm and above all bring everyone along, and not just some.

3-0086-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, ce week-end, un incendie d’une virulence rare est parti du village de ma famille, Lédenon, dans le Gard. Il a dévasté 500 hectares de garrigue en quelques heures. Des familles ont été confinées, des habitants évacués. D’autres incendies ravagent en ce moment la France et d’autres pays en Europe.

Ces feux arrivent avec un mois d’avance, ils sont plus intenses, plus incontrôlables du fait de la canicule et de la sécheresse des sols. Nous savons que tout cela n’est qu’un début; les scientifiques le répètent depuis des décennies. Pourtant, dans cet hémicycle, certains font toujours le choix d’affaiblir ce qui peut nous protéger en détricotant le pacte vert.

Je pose la question au groupe de Jordan Bardella: allez-vous installer la clim contre les incendies dans le champ des agriculteurs? Vous avez choisi de désarmer l’Union européenne face au changement climatique en votant mois après mois contre la restauration des forêts, contre les énergies renouvelables, contre l’obligation de transparence climatique des entreprises. Vous avez choisi l’inaction alors que les canicules et les incendies ont fait 200 000 morts en Europe sur les quatre dernières années.

Soyons clairs: seule une politique de lutte contre le réchauffement climatique pourra nous sauver. Sortir des énergies fossiles, adapter le logement, nos villes, protéger les forêts, renforcer la sécurité civile: nous avons tous les atouts. La maison brûle, ne regardons pas ailleurs!
3-0086-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, this weekend, a fire of rare virulence started in my family's village, Lédenon, in the Gard department. It devastated 500 hectares of scrubland in a few hours. Families were confined, residents evacuated. Other fires are currently ravaging France and other countries in Europe.

These fires are arriving a month early, they are more intense, more uncontrollable due to the heatwave and dry soils. We know that all this is only a beginning; scientists have been repeating it for decades. Yet, in this hemicycle, some still choose to weaken what can protect us by unpicking the Green Deal.

I put the question to Jordan Bardella's group: are you going to install air conditioning against fires in farmers' fields? You chose to disarm the European Union in the face of climate change by voting month after month against forest restoration, against renewable energies, against the obligation of corporate climate transparency. You chose inaction while heatwaves and fires caused 200,000 deaths in Europe over the last four years.

Let's be clear: only a policy to fight against global warming can save us. Phase out fossil fuels, adapt housing, our cities, protect forests, strengthen civil protection: we have all the assets. The house is burning, let's not look elsewhere!

3-0087-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, οι καύσωνες και οι πυρκαγιές δεν είναι απειλές του μέλλοντος αλλά η νέα σκληρή πραγματικότητα. Οι αριθμοί μιλούν από μόνοι τους: Το 2025 αποτέλεσε τη χειρότερη περίοδο δασικών πυρκαγιών, αφού πάνω από 1.000.000 εκτάρια καταστράφηκαν στην Ευρώπη, ενώ ο Ιούνιος του 2026 ήταν ο θερμότερος που έχει καταγραφεί ποτέ σε αρκετές χώρες της Ευρώπης. Πρόκειται για μια πραγματικότητα την οποία η Ελλάδα αλλά και γενικότερα η Μεσόγειος βιώνουν με αυξανόμενη ένταση και η οποία κάνει τη λήψη μέτρων για τη βελτίωση της ανθεκτικότητας των πόλεων απολύτως αναγκαία.

Πρέπει όμως να αναπροσαρμόσουμε το μοντέλο αντιμετώπισης των φυσικών καταστροφών, με έμφαση στην πρόληψη και την έγκαιρη προειδοποίηση αλλά και με δραστική αύξηση των ευρωπαϊκών μέσων. Η Ένωση Ετοιμότητας θα πρέπει να πάρει σάρκα και οστά —με καλύτερο συντονισμό μεταξύ ευρωπαϊκού και εθνικού επιπέδου, ενίσχυση του Ευρωπαϊκού Ταμείου Αλληλεγγύης και του μηχανισμού rescEU, περαιτέρω ανάπτυξη του Ευρωπαϊκού Συστήματος Πληροφοριών για τις δασικές πυρκαγιές, δημιουργία ευρωπαϊκής πλατφόρμας έγκαιρης προειδοποίησης με αξιοποίηση της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης και, φυσικά, ενισχυμένη χρηματοδότηση στο πλαίσιο του επόμενου επταετούς προϋπολογισμού της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης, ώστε τα κράτη μέλη να είναι επαρκώς εξοπλισμένα.

Η κλιματική κρίση απαιτεί συντονισμένη δράση, αυξημένα μέσα και αλλαγή του τρόπου που ενεργούσαμε στο παρελθόν, και αυτή η αλλαγή πρέπει να γίνει τώρα.
3-0087-0000.englishText:
Madam President, heatwaves and wildfires are not threats of the future but the new harsh reality. The numbers speak for themselves: 2025 was the worst wildfire season, with over 1,000,000 hectares destroyed in Europe, while June 2026 was the hottest ever recorded in several European countries. This is a reality that Greece and the Mediterranean in general are experiencing with increasing intensity, making the adoption of measures to improve the resilience of cities absolutely necessary.

However, we must readjust our disaster management model, with an emphasis on prevention and early warning, as well as a drastic increase in European resources. The Preparedness Union must materialize—with better coordination between the European and national levels, strengthening of the European Solidarity Fund and the rescEU mechanism, further development of the European Forest Fire Information System, creation of a European early warning platform utilizing artificial intelligence, and, of course, enhanced funding under the next multiannual financial framework of the European Union so that member states are adequately equipped.

The climate crisis requires coordinated action, increased resources, and a change in the way we have operated in the past, and this change must happen now.

3-0088-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, cada verano escuchamos en este hemiciclo la misma excusa: que los incendios son inevitables, que todo es culpa del cambio climático y que debemos resignarnos.

Y mientras unos utilizan cada incendio para hacer su propaganda climática, otros sabemos cómo se evita el fuego. Los incendios en verano se apagan en invierno, señorías, con pastoreo, con cortafuegos, con desbroces, con una gestión forestal inteligente, con esa España rural que ustedes han expulsado con su amado y querido y alabado Pacto Verde Europeo; con esa misma España rural es como se apagan los incendios.

Qué informes utilizamos, preguntaban los socialistas. Señora García Pérez, pregunte a los ganaderos, a los que han impedido pastorear; pregunte a los agricultores, a los silvicultores y a todos los que han sido expulsados del campo por décadas de políticas del bipartidismo y de su Pacto Verde Europeo que ha dado la espalda al mundo rural. Esos son nuestros informes: el mundo real, ese que ustedes solamente pisan cuando hay cámaras.

El clima cambia, señorías, efectivamente, pero el cambio climático no limpia los montes, no abre cortafuegos, no desbroza, no retrasa las ayudas y no explica por qué España concentra el 40 % de los incendios de toda la superficie de la Unión Europea cuando Portugal comparte el mismo clima y no...

(la presidenta retira la palabra a la oradora)

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0088-0000.englishText:
Madam President, every summer we hear the same excuse in this hemicycle: that fires are inevitable, that it is all the fault of climate change and that we must resign ourselves.

And while some use every fire to make their climate propaganda, others know how fire is prevented. Summer fires are put out in winter, honorable members, with grazing, with firebreaks, with clearing, with intelligent forest management, with that rural Spain that you have expelled with your beloved, cherished and praised European Green Deal; with that same rural Spain is how fires are put out.

What reports do we use, the Socialists asked. Mrs. García Pérez, ask the livestock farmers, those who have been prevented from grazing; ask the farmers, the foresters and all those who have been driven from the countryside by decades of policies of bipartisanship and your European Green Deal that has turned its back on the rural world. Those are our reports: the real world, the one that you only step on when there are cameras.

The climate changes, honorable members, indeed, but climate change does not clean the forests, does not open firebreaks, does not clear brush, does not delay aid and does not explain why Spain concentrates 40% of the fires of the entire surface of the European Union when Portugal shares the same climate and does not...

(the President withdraws the floor from the speaker)

(The speaker agrees to take a question raised under the "blue card" procedure)

3-0089-0000.sourceText: ��blauen Karte“. – Ja, vielen Dank! Ich fände noch mal spannend zu hören, weil Sie ja wieder Klimaideologie als Begriff benutzt haben – könnten Sie uns vielleicht noch mal erklären, was Ihre Definition von „ideologisch“ ist? Denn ich habe das Gefühl, dass Ihre Besessenheit davon, Autokraten dieser Welt eine Importgarantie für fossile Energien zu geben, eine ganz schön ideologische Herangehensweise ist, anstatt EU‑Bürgerinnen und ‑bürgern in Spanien und überall anders tatsächlich die Chance zu geben, auch günstige erneuerbare Energien zu beziehen. Ist das nicht eher die Ideologie? Vielleicht könnten Sie noch mal unsere Definition klären.
3-0089-0000.englishText: Blue Card. - Yes, thank you very much! I would find it exciting to hear once again, because you used the term climate ideology again - could you perhaps explain to us once more what your definition of "ideological" is? Because I have the feeling that your obsession with giving autocrats of this world an import guarantee for fossil fuels is quite an ideological approach, instead of actually giving EU citizens in Spain and everywhere else the chance to also obtain cheap renewable energy. Isn't that more of the ideology? Perhaps you could clarify our definition again.

3-0090-0000.sourceText:
Vamos a ver... lo primero, estamos hablando aquí de incendios, no de energías renovables, pero ¿qué concibo yo como ideología? Su ideología, su fanatismo climático, es simplemente hacer un uso político e ideológico de un hecho fáctico que es el cambio climático, que aquí nadie niega que el clima es cambiante. El clima lleva cambiando desde los orígenes del planeta Tierra.

Ustedes utilizan ese hecho fáctico de que el clima es cambiante para establecer una ideología y establecer sus propios intereses ideológicos, su fanatismo climático, para inventarse cuestiones como esta: que los incendios son culpa del cambio climático, cuando ha quedado más que demostrado que los incendios son culpa de su nefasta gestión y como son incapaces de asumir responsabilidades, ustedes se escudan en su fanatismo climático...

(la presidenta retira la palabra a la oradora)
3-0090-0000.englishText:
Let's see... first of all, we are talking here about fires, not about renewable energies, but what do I conceive as ideology? Your ideology, your climate fanaticism, is simply making political and ideological use of a factual event which is climate change, which nobody here denies that the climate is changing. The climate has been changing since the origins planet Earth.

You use that factual event that the climate is changing to establish an ideology and establish your own ideological interests, your climate fanaticism, to invent issues like this: that fires are the fault of climate change, when it has been more than demonstrated that fires are the fault of your disastrous management and since you are incapable of assuming responsibilities, you hide behind your climate fanaticism...

(the president withdraws the floor from the speaker)

3-0091-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, nous vivons l’été le plus frais du reste de notre vie. La canicule, ce n’est plus une anomalie, c’est notre nouvelle normalité, et cette canicule tue: 200 000 personnes en Europe en quatre ans!

Sue Ellen Demestre lance un cri d’alarme au nom des gens du voyage: «Nous cherchons un refuge climatique. Nous ne pouvons plus respirer!» Sarah, sans-abri, mère de quatre enfants, raconte qu’en été tous les abris sont fermés: «On dort dans les parcs, parfois sur le béton. Il n’y a pas d’eau.» Et pendant que nous débattons ici, ouvriers, agricultrices, éboueurs continuent de travailler sous 40 °C, sans protection européenne.

Parce que oui, la canicule ne touche pas tout le monde de la même façon. La Commission le sait; elle la connaît, cette injustice, elle qui a allumé la climatisation pour les commissaires dans les étages supérieurs et l’a éteinte pour les fonctionnaires dans les étages inférieurs. Elle a aussi brillé par son absence de réaction: pas un communiqué, pas un plan d’action, pas un tweet lorsque la haute chaleur a touché notre continent. Cette inaction doit cesser!

Les canicules ne tombent pas du ciel.
