Elles portent le nom des multinationales des fossiles, et notre plan d’action doit être clair: reprendre en main les firmes qui ont provoqué le dérèglement climatique, adopter une grande loi pour protéger les travailleurs exposés aux chaleurs extrêmes, dégager les moyens urgents pour adapter nos hôpitaux, nos écoles et les logements aux grandes chaleurs. N’attendons plus!

(L’oratrice refuse des questions carton bleu de Jaak Madison et de Kateřina Konečná)
3-0091-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, we are experiencing the coolest summer of the rest of our lives. Heatwaves are no longer an anomaly, they are our new normal, and these heatwaves are killing: 200,000 people in Europe in four years!

Sue Ellen Demestre is sounding the alarm on behalf of travelers: "We are looking for a climate refuge. We can no longer breathe!" Sarah, a homeless mother of four, recounts that in summer all shelters are closed: "We sleep in parks, sometimes on concrete. There is no water." And while we debate here, workers, female farmers, garbage collectors continue to work in 40 °C, without European protection.

Because yes, the heatwave does not affect everyone in the same way. The Commission knows this; it is aware of this injustice, having turned on the air conditioning for the commissioners on the upper floors and turned it off for the civil servants on the lower floors. It has also shone by its lack of reaction: not a press release, not an action plan, not a tweet when the high heat hit our continent. This inaction must stop!

Heatwaves do not fall from the sky. They bear the name of fossil fuel multinationals, and our action plan must be clear: take back control of the firms that caused climate disruption, adopt a major law to protect workers exposed to extreme heat, release urgent resources to adapt our hospitals, schools, and housing to the high heat. Let us wait no longer!

(The speaker refuses blue-card questions from Jaak Madison and Kateřina Konečná)

3-0092-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, κυρία Επίτροπε, προέρχομαι από μία χώρα όπου ο καύσωνας το καλοκαίρι είναι σχεδόν καθημερινό φαινόμενο. Στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση πέρυσι είχαμε ρεκόρ πυρκαγιών με πάνω από 10 εκατομμύρια στρέμματα καμένης γης. Για την Κύπρο, την πατρίδα μου, τα δεδομένα του Ευρωπαϊκού Συστήματος Πληροφόρησης για τις Δασικές Πυρκαγιές καταγράφουν μια ακραία κορύφωση των καμένων εκτάσεων. Χαιρετίζω λοιπόν την απόφαση-σταθμό, καθώς θα υπάρχει ένας αριθμός-ρεκόρ για την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση: 777 πυροσβέστες, 22 αεροσκάφη και 5 ελικόπτερα σε διάφορα σημεία της ευρωπαϊκής επικράτειας, ώστε να συνδράμουν ανά πάσα στιγμή εκεί όπου χρειάζεται.

Θέλω όμως να μάθω αν υπάρχει προγραμματισμός για το πού θα πάνε και πότε —αν μπορείτε να μας πείτε. Ήμουν και παραμένω ένας εξ αυτών που υποστήριξαν σθεναρά την απόλυτη ανάγκη μόνιμης και ενισχυμένης παρουσίας του rescEU στην Κύπρο, καθώς η γεωγραφική απομόνωσή της την καθιστούσε ευάλωτη. Νομίζω πως είμαστε τώρα σε μια σωστή κατεύθυνση και επιβάλλεται η συνεχής ενίσχυση. Οποιεσδήποτε καθυστερήσεις είναι επικίνδυνες, με ανυπολόγιστες συνέπειες για το φυσικό περιβάλλον και την ανθρώπινη ζωή.
3-0092-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, I come from a country where the summer heatwave is an almost daily phenomenon. In the European Union last year we had a record of fires with over 10 million stremmas of burnt land. For Cyprus, my homeland, the data from the European Forest Fire Information System record an extreme peak in burnt areas. I therefore welcome the milestone decision, as there will be a record number for the European Union: 777 firefighters, 22 aircraft and 5 helicopters in various parts of the European territory, to assist at any time where needed.

However, I want to know if there is planning for where they will go and when—if you can tell us. I was and remain one of those who strongly supported the absolute need for a permanent and enhanced presence of rescEU in Cyprus, as its geographical isolation made it vulnerable. I think we are now on the right track and continuous reinforcement is imperative. Any delays are dangerous, with incalculable consequences for the natural environment and human life.

3-0093-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, justice sociale et justice climatique: même combat. Aujourd’hui déjà et demain plus encore, ce sont les plus vulnérables, au nord comme au sud de la planète, qui paient le prix du dérèglement climatique. En Europe, on estime que le décompte morbide sera chaque été de 80 000 morts. Rien qu’en Belgique, pour la canicule de ce mois de juin, on déplore plus de 1 200 décès supplémentaires liés aux fortes chaleurs, et à nouveau les plus fragiles sont touchés: les personnes âgées, les malades chroniques ou les bébés. Les travailleurs aussi sont en première ligne.

Mais, pendant ce temps, notre gouvernement, par la voix de notre ministre de la défense, nous invite à ne pas dramatiser et à profiter d’une bonne bière au bord de la piscine. Monsieur Francken, je vous invite à vous mettre dans la peau des 130 millions de travailleurs exposés à des températures infernales qui mettent leur santé et leur vie en danger. C’est pourquoi il est urgent d’adopter une directive qui protège les travailleurs et les travailleuses afin de prévenir les risques pour leur santé, pas pour prendre acte ou pour subir.
3-0093-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, social justice and climate justice: same struggle. Today already and tomorrow even more so, it is the most vulnerable, in the north as in the south of the planet, who pay the price of climate disruption. In Europe, it is estimated that the morbid toll will be 80,000 deaths each summer. In Belgium alone, for the heatwave of this month of June, we deplore more than 1,200 additional deaths related to high temperatures, and once again the most fragile are hit: the elderly, the chronically ill or babies. Workers are also on the front line.

But, meanwhile, our government, through the voice of our Minister of Defense, invites us not to dramatize and to enjoy a good beer by the pool. Mr. Francken, I invite you to put yourself in the shoes of the 130 million workers exposed to infernal temperatures that put their health and lives in danger. This is why it is urgent to adopt a directive that protects workers in order to prevent risks to their health, not to take note or to suffer.

3-0094-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidente, lejos de remitir la incidencia de los incendios en Europa, como todos desearíamos, cada año se inician antes y son más virulentos.

La Unión es consciente del problema y trata de coordinar mejor los medios efectivos que hay contra los incendios, pero tenemos una causa pendiente: la prevención, no lo hacemos bien. Hemos avanzado algo, como, por ejemplo, con la nueva aprobación de las nuevas técnicas de edición genómica para hacer más resiliente el mundo vegetal o el reconocimiento de anteayer, por parte de la Comisión Europea, de la ganadería extensiva del ovino y del caprino y su importante papel medioambiental y en la lucha contra incendios. Pero aún quedan decisiones políticas y presupuestarias necesarias que evidencien, de manera incontestable, la apuesta por el entorno poblacional del mundo rural y su papel.

Hay que modificar legislación como la Red Natura 2000, reglamentos como el Reglamento de Restauración de la Naturaleza, la Nueva Estrategia de la UE en favor de los Bosques para 2030, reglamentos como los relacionados con la biodiversidad o los hábitats para volver a permitir, sin polémicas, que la población rural europea vuelva a practicar medidas eficaces para prevenir los desastres naturales que son los incendios. ¿Y cómo? Permitiéndoles volver a prácticas que durante siglos y siglos han funcionado, como las talas, los clareos, las limpiezas, las veredas, los cortafuegos.

No sé a qué estamos esperando, pero, mientras discutimos si son galgos o podencos, Europa sigue ardiendo.

(La oradora acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0094-0000.englishText:
Madam President, far from diminishing, the incidence of fires in Europe, as we would all wish, starts earlier every year and is more virulent.

The Union is aware of the problem and tries to better coordinate the effective means available against fires, but we have a pending cause: prevention, we are not doing it well. We have made some progress, for example, with the recent approval of new genomic editing techniques to make the plant world more resilient or the recognition the day before yesterday by the European Commission of extensive sheep and goat farming and its important environmental role and in the fight against fires. But there are still necessary political and budgetary decisions that incontestably show the commitment to the populated environment of the rural world and its role.

We must modify legislation such as the Natura 2000 network, regulations such as the Nature Restoration Regulation, the New EU Forest Strategy for 2030, regulations related to biodiversity or habitats to allow once again, without controversy, the European rural population to practice effective measures to prevent natural disasters which are fires. And how? By allowing them to return to practices that for centuries and centuries have worked, such as logging, thinning, cleaning, trails, firebreaks.

I do not know what we are waiting for, but while we argue over trifles, Europe continues to burn.

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

3-0095-0000.sourceText: ��blauwe kaart”-vraag. – Ik heb al een aantal tussenkomsten gehoord van, laten we zeggen, beschaafd rechts, centrumrechts. En ik hoor telkens maar pleidooien voor preventie en voor investeringen en weet ik veel. Nu, wat ik vaststel, is dat overal in Europa, waar het overgrote deel rechtse of centrumrechtse regeringen zijn, er overal net wordt bespaard op preventie, dat er overal wordt bespaard op hulpdiensten en dergelijke. Dus ik zou willen vragen: is dat wel consequent wat u komt vertellen en hoe ziet u dat?
3-0095-0000.englishText: "Blue card" question. – I have already heard a number of interventions from, let us say, civilized right, center-right. And all I hear are pleas for prevention and for investments and goodness knows what. Now, what I observe is that everywhere in Europe, where the vast majority are right-wing or center-right governments, cuts are being made precisely on prevention everywhere, cuts are being made everywhere on emergency services and the like. So I would like to ask: is what you are coming to tell us consistent at all and how do you see that?

3-0096-0000.sourceText:
La visión es muy clara, caballero. Y gracias por su pregunta.

Mire, tenemos que ser conscientes de que hay una prevención muy importante, que es la práctica que siempre se ha llevado a cabo en el mundo rural.

Los que mejor conocen el mundo rural son aquellos que por herencia, por tradición, por familia, por conocimientos, lo hacen bien desde hace siglos y, durante yo diría que más de una década, hemos empezado a prohibir sistemáticamente un montón de medidas por las que ellos apostaban. Han desaparecido los cortafuegos, por eso ahora no podemos limitar el alcance del fuego. No les dejamos, cuando entran en Red Natura 2000, utilizar los recursos naturales como lo han hecho siempre. No limpiamos. Hemos acabado con la ganadería extensiva del ovino y del caprino, con lo que representa para la lucha contra incendios.

Oiga, es tan sencillo como aplicar lo que sabemos —el conocimiento— y no prohibirlo.
3-0096-0000.englishText:
The vision is very clear, sir. And thank you for your question.

Look, we must be aware that there is a very important prevention, which is the practice that has always been carried out in the rural world.

Those who know the rural world best are those who, by inheritance, tradition, family, and knowledge, have been doing it well for centuries and, for I would say more than a decade, we have started to systematically ban a lot of measures that they bet on. Firebreaks have disappeared, which is why we now cannot limit the extent of the fire. We do not let them, when they enter the Natura 2000 Network, use natural resources as they have always done. We do not clean. We have put an end to extensive sheep and goat farming, with all that it represents for the fight against fires.

Listen, it is as simple as applying what we know—knowledge—and not banning it.

3-0097-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin! Jedes Jahr sterben in Europa mehr als 175 000 Menschen an den Folgen extremer Hitze. Die Temperaturen in Europa steigen doppelt so schnell wie im globalen Durchschnitt. Doch anstatt dies als den Notfall zu behandeln, der es ist, baut die EU Klimaschutzmaßnahmen ab. Während die reichsten 1 % so viel CO2 ausstoßen wie die ärmsten zwei Drittel der Bevölkerung zusammen, sind es die Arbeiterinnen, Rentnerinnen und einkommensschwachen Familien, die am meisten leiden.

Klimaschutz bedeutet: Besteuerung von extremen Vermögen und Emissionen, Abbau von Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe, Investitionen in öffentliche Dienstleistungen und die größten Umweltverschmutzer zur Kasse zu bitten. Doch während Europa brennt, stecken Konservative und extrem Rechte gemeinsam unter der Decke: Sie schwächen den Green Deal, und die EU steckt weiterhin Milliarden in Subventionen für fossile Brennstoffe.

Menschen statt Verschmutzer, Leben statt Gewinne aus fossilen Brennstoffen schützen!

(Der Redner ist damit einverstanden, auf eine Frage nach dem Verfahren der „blauen Karte“ zu antworten.)
3-0097-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Every year, more than 175,000 people in Europe die as a result of extreme heat. Temperatures in Europe are rising twice as fast as the global average. Yet instead of treating this as the emergency that it is, the EU is dismantling climate protection measures. While the richest 1% emit as much CO2 as the poorest two-thirds of the population combined, it is workers, pensioners, and low-income families who suffer the most.

Climate protection means: taxation of extreme wealth and emissions, phasing out fossil fuel subsidies, investment in public services, and making the biggest polluters pay. But while Europe burns, conservatives and the far-right are in bed together: they are weakening the Green Deal, and the EU continues to pour billions into fossil fuel subsidies.

Protect people instead of polluters, lives instead of fossil fuel profits!

(The speaker agreed to respond to a question under the "blue card" procedure.)

3-0098-0000.sourceText: Jaa. Kuna räägite saksa keeles, ma räägin eesti keeles. Teie kõne oli ääretult entusiastlik ja ja positiivne, seega kõnepidamine oli väga hea. Kuid kui te räägite fossiilkütustest ja et Euroopa põlemises on süüdi fossiilkütused, meil pole kliimakokkulepet, rohepööret, kõike seda, siis lihtsalt väikene küsimus, et minu teada kliima on alati muutunud. Alati läbi ajaloo. Aastal 1685 oli Thamesi jõgi nii jäätunud, et seal hobused jooksid. Mis teie arvate, miks muutus kliima umbes kakssada aastat tagasi, kui ta nüüd muutub ainult sellepärast, et meil on bensiiniautod? Et kui varem muutus kliima tänu päikesele ja kogu loodusele, siis nüüd ta muutub hoopis sellepärast, et meil on olemas teaduslik areng ja võimalik majandust arendada ka loodusressurssidele. Mis juhtus vahepeal? Miks varem kliima muutus?
3-0098-0000.englishText: Yes. Since you are speaking in German, I will speak in Estonian. Your speech was extremely enthusiastic and positive, so the speechmaking was very good. But when you talk about fossil fuels and that fossil fuels are to blame for Europe burning, that we don't have a climate agreement, a green transition, all of that, then just a little question: to my knowledge, the climate has always changed. Always throughout history. In the year 1685, the River Thames was so frozen that horses ran on it. What do you think, why did the climate change about two hundred years ago, if now it only changes because we have petrol cars? So if previously the climate changed thanks to the sun and all of nature, now it changes precisely because we have scientific development and it is possible to develop the economy also on natural resources. What happened in between? Why did the climate change before?

3-0099-0000.sourceText:
��blauen Karte“. – Ja, es gab Klimawandel auch vor dem menschengemachten Klimawandel. Den menschengemachten Klimawandel zu ignorieren, der wissenschaftlich eindeutig festgestellt ist, das ist klimaterroristische Ideologie, die Sie zusammen verfolgen, unter der Arbeiterinnen, Rentnerinnen und ärmere Familien in dieser EU leiden.

Ich fordere Sie auf, endlich Verantwortung dafür zu übernehmen – für Ihre Politik – und den Leuten ehrlich zu sagen, was auf sie zukommt. Das tun Sie nicht; Sie belügen die Menschen.
3-0099-0000.englishText:
Blue Card". - Yes, climate change also existed before human-made climate change. Ignoring human-made climate change, which has been scientifically clearly established, is climate-terrorist ideology that you are pursuing together, and from which female workers, female pensioners, and poorer families in this EU are suffering.

I call on you to finally take responsibility for this - for your politics - and to honestly tell people what is coming their way. You are not doing that; you are lying to the people.

3-0100-0000.sourceText: Jaa, kui te räägite, et keegi peab võtma vastutuse, siis miks te arvate, et Euroopa peab võtma vastutuse? Kui te räägite kliimamuutustest ja kliimasoojemisest, siis ainult Euroopas on vaid märkimisväärselt vähe tõusnud kliimamuutused. Samas ülejäänud maailmas, Aafrikas, Aasias ei ole seda juhtunud. Miks peab Euroopa inimene teie poliitika tõttu hakkama rohkem kinni maksma rohelepet, kõrgemat kütuse hinda, kõrgemat toasooja hinda, et teha mingit ideoloogilist projekti, nagu tegid kommunistid? Noh, te olete ka ju natukene kommunist. Et miks meie peame kinni maksma Euroopa inimestena teie ideoloogia, kui me teame, et tegelikult inimmõju kliimamuutustele on marginaalne, väga väikene või olematu? Miks te tahate, et Euroopa [cut off]
3-0100-0000.englishText: Yes, when you talk about someone having to take responsibility, then why do you think that Europe has to take responsibility? When you talk about climate change and global warming, it is only in Europe that climate change has increased significantly. At the same time, in the rest of the world, in Africa, in Asia, this has not happened. Why should the European person, because of your policy, have to pay more for the Green Deal, higher fuel prices, higher heating prices, in order to do some ideological project, like the communists did? Well, you are also a bit of a communist after all. So why do we, as Europeans, have to pay for your ideology when we know that actually the human impact on climate change is marginal, very small, or non-existent? Why do you want Europe [cut off]

3-0101-0000.sourceText:
Erstens: Es sind 57 Konzerne, die 80 % aller weltweiten Emissionen produzieren. Es sind nicht die Menschen, die es zahlen sollten, es sind diese Konzerne, die zahlen sollten, endlich ihrer Verantwortung gerecht werden sollten. Und ja, das sind auch viele europäische Konzerne.

Ich bin sehr dafür, dass es nicht die Menschen sind, die am meisten darunter leiden – was sie heutzutage schon tun. 175 000 Tote durch extreme Hitze in Europa, und Konzerne wie Exxon sagen für das erste Vierteljahr bereits, dass sie 5 Milliarden mehr Profit gemacht haben. Wo bleibt da eigentlich Ihre Initiative? Wo ist da der Aufschrei zu sagen: Stoppt diese Profite!
3-0101-0000.englishText:
Firstly, it is 57 corporations that produce 80% of all global emissions. It is not the people who should pay for it, it is these corporations that should pay, that should finally live up to their responsibility. And yes, these are also many European corporations.

I am very much in favor of it not being the people who suffer the most from this – which they are already doing nowadays. 175,000 deaths from extreme heat in Europe, and corporations like Exxon are already saying for the first quarter that they have made 5 billion more in profit. Where is your initiative in all this? Where is the outcry to say: Stop these profits!

3-0102-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en los últimos días hemos vivido récords de temperatura en toda Europa. Y mucho me temo que este va a ser el verano más fresco de los próximos años. Las olas de calor han dejado miles de víctimas y han multiplicado los incendios. El estrés térmico amenaza a más de 130 millones de trabajadores y la superficie quemada ya supera las 130 000 hectáreas. En nuestra tierra, en Castellón, en Soneja, pero también repetitivamente en León, en Cataluña, de forma simultánea, están luchando contra el fuego. Damos todo nuestro apoyo.

Nuestro nuevo mecanismo de protección civil debe reforzar las capacidades de la Unión para responder. Estamos en ello. Pero, sobre todo, tiene que fomentar una cultura de la preparación, de la planificación, de la prevención, con la participación de actores locales y rurales. Tenemos que entender su dimensión, su frecuencia y su virulencia en emergencia climática. No podremos hacerlo si no desmantelamos las leyes que protegen y monitorean nuestros bosques como aquí se está intentando. Y no lo haremos si no entendemos sus causas: el cambio climático, la despoblación, si no tenemos en cuenta a los actores locales y rurales.

Señorías, este no es un debate sobre más aire acondicionado. Hay que climatizar, sí, pero sobre todo hay que prevenir. Hay que anticiparse y evitar más incendios y, también, más muertes por el calor.
3-0102-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in recent days we have experienced record temperatures across Europe. And I very much fear that this will be the coolest summer of the coming years. Heatwaves have left thousands of victims and multiplied fires. Thermal stress threatens more than 130 million workers and the burnt area already exceeds 130,000 hectares. In our land, in Castellón, in Soneja, but also repeatedly in León, in Catalonia, simultaneously, they are fighting the fire. We give all our support.

Our new civil protection mechanism must strengthen the Union's capacities to respond. We are working on it. But, above all, it has to foster a culture of preparedness, planning, prevention, with the participation of local and rural actors. We have to understand its dimension, frequency, and virulence in a climate emergency. We will not be able to do this if we do not dismantle the laws that protect and monitor our forests, as is being attempted here. And we will not do it if we do not understand its causes: climate change, depopulation, if we do not take into account local and rural actors.

Ladies and gentlemen, this is not a debate about more air conditioning. We need to air-condition, yes, but above all we need to prevent. We must anticipate and avoid more fires and also more deaths from the heat.

3-0103-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, komission jäsen, meillä on vain yksi planeetta. Tällä hetkellä se palaa monin paikoin, ja sään ääri-ilmiöt yleistyvät. Ilmastonmuutos on täällä. Me näemme sen omin silmin joka päivä, ja tuhannet ihmiset Euroopassa ovat menettäneet henkensä helteen vuoksi. Se on järkyttävää.

Suomessa lapsemme ja lastenlapsemme eivät sinilevän vuoksi voi enää uida meressä samalla tavoin kuin ennen. Myrskyt ja rajut ukkosilmat seuraavat toisiaan. Arktisella alueella asuvat saamelaiset kärsivät ilmastonmuutoksesta erityisen paljon.

On vastuutonta, että vielä tänäkin päivänä on päättäjiä, jotka kieltävät ilmastonmuutoksen. Euroopan kansalaisilla on oikeus odottaa meiltä toimia. Meidän on luovuttava fossiilisista polttoaineista, öljystä ja kivihiilestä. Meidän on rakennettava EU:n varautumisunioni, ja on aika toteuttaa presidentti Niinistön raportti EU:n kokonaisvaltaisen varautumisen vahvistamisesta.

(Puhuja suostui vastaamaan sinisen kortin kysymykseen)
3-0103-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, we only have one planet. At present, it is burning in many places, and extreme weather events are becoming more common. Climate change is here. We see it with our own eyes every day, and thousands of people in Europe have lost their lives due to the heat. It is shocking.

In Finland, because of blue-green algae, our children and grandchildren can no longer swim in the sea in the same way as before. Storms and violent thunderstorms follow one another. The Sami people living in the Arctic region suffer particularly badly from climate change.

It is irresponsible that even today there are decision-makers who deny climate change. European citizens have the right to expect action from us. We must abandon fossil fuels, oil and coal. We must build an EU preparedness union, and it is time to implement President Niinistö's report on strengthening the EU's comprehensive preparedness.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

3-0104-0000.sourceText: Ta otázka je vlastně na vás, kolegové ze skupin socialistů, Zelených i Renew. Bavíte se o tom, že máme opustit fosilní paliva. Bavíte se o tom, že nám Evropu a svět oteplují fosilní paliva. Proč se nebavíte o válce? Kolik emisí způsobují vaše války, které začínáte? Vy podporujete nákupy zbraní, které zabíjí lidi a ničí klima. A o tom nikdo z vás neřekl ani slovo. Pojďme to tedy vzít komplexně. Pojďme se podívat na to, jak vaše válečné štvaní, které vy podporujete a do kterého investujete peníze, ničí tuto planetu.
3-0104-0000.englishText: That question is actually for you, colleagues from the groups of Socialists, Greens, and Renew. You are talking about leaving fossil fuels behind. You are talking about how fossil fuels are warming Europe and the world for us. Why are you not talking about war? How many emissions are caused by your wars that you start? You support purchases of weapons that kill people and destroy the climate. And not a single one of you said a word about that. So let us take it comprehensively. Let us look at how your war-mongering, which you support and into which you invest money, destroys this planet.
3-0104-0000.factCheck: The claim that no members of the Socialists, Greens, or Renew groups have addressed military emissions is false; MEPs from these groups have repeatedly raised the issue, such as proposing amendments to European Parliament resolutions to close the military emissions gap and advocating for mandatory reporting of military carbon footprints.

3-0105-0000.sourceText:
Det verkar som att parlamentarikern har missat någonting elementärt. Det är Ryssland och Putin som har startat ett krig mot Ukraina, och det är tragiskt. Det kriget pågår varje dag, och vi ska se till att vi gör allt för att stödja Ukraina, för att vi i Europa inte ska köpa rysk gas och olja.

Vi kan på vårt eget sätt stödja Ukraina genom våra egna åtgärder i våra länder, och det är vår uppgift att se till att Ukraina också en dag kan bli medlem i Europeiska unionen.
3-0105-0000.englishText:
It seems that the parliamentarian has missed something elementary. It is Russia and Putin that have started a war against Ukraine, and that is tragic. That war is ongoing every day, and we must make sure that we do everything to support Ukraine, so that we in Europe do not buy Russian gas and oil.

We can in our own way support Ukraine through our own actions in our countries, and it is our task to ensure that Ukraine can also one day become a member of the European Union.

3-0106-0000.sourceText: Tady přece vůbec nejde o Ukrajinu. Vy jste nebyli schopni odhlasovat, že nesouhlasíte s tím, jak agresivně postupuje Donald Trump v Íránu. A tam se také používají zbraně. Tam se také ničí klima. Vy jste nebyli schopni odhlasovat, že nesouhlasíte s genocidou v Palestině. Také se tam používají zbraně. Prostě dokud nepřistoupíte na to, že mírová politika je ta environmentálně nejčistější politika, a bude to svádět jenom na jednu část ekonomiky nebo sektoru, tak je to „papalášství“ a jenom si na něco hrajete.
3-0106-0000.englishText: This is not about Ukraine at all. You were not able to vote that you disagree with how aggressively Donald Trump is acting in Iran. And weapons are used there too. The climate is also being destroyed there. You were not able to vote that you disagree with the genocide in Palestine. Weapons are used there too. Simply until you agree that peace policy is the most environmentally clean policy, and you will blame only one part of the economy or sector, it is hypocrisy and you are just pretending something.

3-0107-0000.sourceText:
Det är förstås på det sättet att det skulle vara väldigt bra om vi skulle ha fred i världen. Men det betyder inte att vi kan stänga våra ögon för den miljökatastrof som håller på att hända i världen nu, den klimatkatastrof som vi har.

Vi måste jobba på många plan varje dag. Vi måste bekämpa klimatförändringen. Vi måste göra oss av med fossila bränslen. Vi ska satsa på den gröna omställningen, och vi ska jobba för en värld där människor respekteras – demokrati, mänskliga rättigheter – och att varje land har rätt till sin suveränitet.
3-0107-0000.englishText:
It is of course the case that it would be very good if we had peace in the world. But that does not mean that we can close our eyes to the environmental catastrophe that is happening in the world now, the climate catastrophe that we have.

We must work on many levels every day. We must combat climate change. We must get rid of fossil fuels. We will invest in the green transition, and we will work for a world where people are respected – democracy, human rights – and that every country has the right to its sovereignty.

3-0108-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, face aux vagues de chaleur, la climatisation n’est pas un luxe, c’est un enjeu de santé publique. Depuis 2017, près de 40 000 Français sont morts des conséquences de la chaleur. Pourtant, seuls 24 % des logements sont climatisés, contre plus de 50 % en Italie. Lorsque les températures s’affolent, il faut pouvoir protéger efficacement les écoles, les hôpitaux et les maisons de retraite.

À Nice, nous avons choisi un grand plan d’action, un plan d’action de climatisation de notre ville. S’adapter au changement climatique, ce n’est pas renoncer à le combattre. S’adapter, c’est investir dans le nucléaire pour produire une électricité décarbonée. S’adapter, c’est rendre nos bâtiments vivables été comme hiver. C’est avant tout protéger la vie des plus fragiles.

La véritable écologie, ce n’est pas celle qui culpabilise, c’est celle qui protège. La véritable écologie ne choisit jamais entre la planète et les personnes, elle protège les deux.
3-0108-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, in the face of heatwaves, air conditioning is not a luxury, it is a public health issue. Since 2017, nearly 40,000 French people have died from the consequences of heat. Yet, only 24% of homes are air-conditioned, compared to over 50% in Italy. When temperatures go wild, schools, hospitals, and retirement homes must be effectively protected.

In Nice, we have chosen a major action plan, an air-conditioning action plan for our city. Adapting to climate change does not mean giving up on fighting it. Adapting means investing in nuclear power to produce decarbonised electricity. Adapting means making our buildings livable both summer and winter. Above all, it means protecting the lives of the most vulnerable.

True ecology is not the one that makes people feel guilty, it is the one that protects. True ecology never chooses between the planet and people, it protects both.

3-0109-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, «as ondas de calor extremo são uma emergência de saúde pública», disse ontem o diretor regional da OMS Europa.

Nós já o sabíamos. As temperaturas elevadas têm um impacto direto no aumento da morbilidade e também da mortalidade. O excesso de mortalidade devido ao calor foi de mais de 7 000 mortos, apenas no mês de junho, em três países da Europa.

Mas, para além dos meios de combate a incêndios que a União Europeia tem disponíveis para apoiar todos os países, nós precisamos de fazer mais. O recuo nas políticas de redução do aquecimento global, de desregulação ambiental, tem um custo pesado. Mede-se em doenças evitáveis, mede-se em mortes evitáveis, e as medidas de adaptação e mitigação climática são a chave de longo prazo.

Para muitos neste hemiciclo, basta olhar para ele, os incêndios são uma coisa que acontece porque as ganadarias foram terminadas, as doenças transmitidas por vetores acontecem porque vêm nuns aviões, de uns sítios estranhos, que trazem uns mosquitos a bordo. E as alterações climáticas são ideologia.

Enquanto não nos entendermos sobre os factos, não vamos não correr atrás do prejuízo.
3-0109-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, "extreme heatwaves are a public health emergency," said the WHO Regional Director for Europe yesterday.

We already knew that. High temperatures have a direct impact on increasing morbidity and also mortality. Excess mortality due to heat was over 7,000 deaths, just in the month of June, in three European countries.

But, beyond the firefighting resources that the European Union has available to support all countries, we need to do more. The rollback of global warming reduction policies, of environmental deregulation, comes at a heavy cost. It is measured in preventable illnesses, it is measured in preventable deaths, and climate adaptation and mitigation measures are the long-term key.

For many in this hemicycle, you only have to look at it, fires are something that happens because cattle farming was ended, vector-borne diseases happen because they come on planes, from strange places, carrying mosquitoes on board. And climate change is ideology.

Until we agree on the facts, we will not catch up with our losses.

3-0110-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, six jours de canicule en juin en France, 2 025 morts. Et pendant que certains discutent encore, d’autres agissent. À Madrid, le métro est climatisé. À Barcelone, des refuges climatiques sont accessibles en quelques minutes à pied. En Grèce, les employeurs doivent prévoir des espaces rafraîchis pour leurs salariés. Ces pays ont compris une chose simple: protéger la population face à la chaleur, ce n’est pas un luxe, c’est une politique publique.

En France, nous sommes en retard. Trop d’écoles, d’EHPAD, trop d’hôpitaux, trop de logements restent inadaptés, et pourtant la chaleur tue. Elle frappe les enfants, les personnes âgées, les malades, les travailleurs. Face à cela, nous proposons un «Plan Clim’»: le droit à la fraîcheur pour tous. Rafraîchir des bâtiments publics prioritaires et aider les familles à adapter leur logement, développer l’isolation et les pompes à chaleur réversibles et, aussi, produire ces équipements chez nous. Chaque euro investi doit protéger les Français, relancer notre industrie et créer des emplois européens non délocalisables.

Voilà notre ligne. Ni déni climatique ni écologie punitive: une écologie de protection qui s’adapte et, surtout – surtout! –, qui sauve des vies.
3-0110-0000.englishText:
Madam President, six days of heatwave in June in France, 2,025 deaths. And while some are still discussing, others are acting. In Madrid, the metro is air-conditioned. In Barcelona, climate shelters are accessible within a few minutes on foot. In Greece, employers must provide cooled spaces for their employees. These countries have understood a simple thing: protecting the population against the heat is not a luxury, it is a public policy.

In France, we are lagging behind. Too many schools, EHPADs [residential care homes for the elderly], too many hospitals, too many homes remain unsuitable, and yet the heat kills. It strikes children, the elderly, the sick, workers. Faced with this, we are proposing a 'Climate Plan': the right to coolness for everyone. Cooling priority public buildings and helping families adapt their housing, developing insulation and reversible heat pumps, and also producing this equipment at home. Every euro invested must protect the French people, revive our industry and create non-relocatable European jobs.

This is our line. Neither climate denial nor punitive ecology: a protection ecology that adapts and, above all—above all!—saves lives.

3-0111-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Caros Colegas, há uma relação inevitável entre alterações climáticas, ondas de calor e incêndios. Esta circunstância é cada vez menos conjuntural e mais estrutural, o que explica a permanência desta mesma sequência.

A questão que se coloca é: o que fazer?

Há dois níveis de ação muito relevantes. Primeiro, a mitigação: continuar a apostar na redução das causas, combater as alterações climáticas; mas o segundo é o nível da adaptação. Não podemos ser inocentes ao ponto de pensarmos que a mitigação vai acontecer num ápice e temos de nos preparar para essa circunstância.

O que fazer? Preparar as comunidades mais expostas, reforçar a resiliência dos territórios, modernizar e capacitar as autoridades de proteção civil. Investigar ou investir cada vez mais em investigação contra os fogos.

Mas também é preciso reforçar a atuação de nível europeu, nomeadamente o Mecanismo de Proteção Civil da União Europeia e o RescEU, assim como a partilha de meios e a cooperação operacional.

Só com um nível europeu ativo e preparado podemos ser bem‑sucedidos no combate ao flagelo dos fogos.

(O orador aceita responder a várias perguntas «cartão azul»)
3-0111-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, Dear Colleagues, there is an inevitable relationship between climate change, heatwaves and fires. This circumstance is increasingly less cyclical and more structural, which explains the permanence of this very sequence. 

The question that arises is: what to do? 

There are two very relevant levels of action. First, mitigation: continuing to invest in reducing causes, combating climate change; but the second is the level of adaptation. We cannot be naive to the point of thinking that mitigation will happen in a flash and we have to prepare ourselves for this circumstance. 

What to do? Prepare the most exposed communities, reinforce the resilience of territories, modernize and empower civil protection authorities. Investigate or invest increasingly in research against fires. 

But it is also necessary to strengthen European-level action, namely the European Union Civil Protection Mechanism and RescEU, as well as the sharing of resources and operational cooperation. 

Only with an active and prepared European level can we be successful in combating the scourge of fires. 

(The speaker agrees to answer several blue card questions)

3-0112-0000.sourceText:
Nós estamos a discutir o mecanismo de proteção civil na Europa e tenho defendido que precisamos de incluir num mecanismo de solidariedade a recuperação precoce.

Em Portugal, estamos a ter fogos em florestas onde ainda está deitada a madeira das tempestades e temos populações ainda sem eletricidade e mesmo dificuldades em comunicações.

Os grupos aqui do Parlamento Europeu têm tido um consenso sobre a necessidade da recuperação precoce, exceto o seu grupo, o PPE. E, por isso, pergunto-lhe, quando defende aqui mais solidariedade europeia, se não acha que devíamos fazer tudo e assegurar esta recuperação precoce para limparmos o território e repormos eletricidade e comunicações com solidariedade e rapidamente?
3-0112-0000.englishText:
We are discussing the civil protection mechanism in Europe and I have argued that we need to include early recovery in a solidarity mechanism.

In Portugal, we are having fires in forests where the timber from the storms is still lying around and we still have populations without electricity and even difficulties with communications.

The groups here in the European Parliament have had a consensus on the need for early recovery, except for your group, the EPP. And so I ask you, when you defend more European solidarity here, don't you think we should do everything and ensure this early recovery to clear the territory and restore electricity and communications with solidarity and quickly?

3-0113-0000.sourceText:
Reitero que a aposta na mitigação é crucial, mas isso não significa que não nos devamos preparar para as circunstâncias que são inevitáveis.

Infelizmente, as alterações climáticas são uma realidade e a sua afetação ao nível dos incêndios, particularmente dos incêndios florestais, é também uma realidade. E, para isso, a adaptação e a preparação das comunidades são fulcrais.

O que o meu grupo político defende, e a Comissão Europeia tem-no feito, é apostar em fundos como o preparedness, que ajudam as comunidades a ficarem mais resilientes, mais bem preparadas para melhor vencerem estas circunstâncias.
3-0113-0000.englishText:
I reiterate that the commitment to mitigation is crucial, but that does not mean we should not prepare for circumstances that are inevitable.

Unfortunately, climate change is a reality and its impact in terms of fires, particularly forest fires, is also a reality. And for this, the adaptation and preparation of communities are central.

What my political group advocates, and the European Commission has been doing, is to invest in funds like preparedness, which help communities become more resilient, better prepared to better overcome these circumstances.

3-0114-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Deputado, não vou aqui nacionalizar a questão, como no passado fez, aliás, o PSD com eurodeputados do PS, vou mesmo europeizá-la. Falou do mecanismo de proteção civil e estamos juntos, não apenas nessa ação, nessa ativação e naquilo em que há ajuda aos Estados-Membros, mas é que aqui nesta casa, em 2023, foi aprovada legislação europeia contra a desflorestação.

No último ano, essa legislação aqui voltou para ser ratificada ou para ser adiada. Ao contrário deste grupo que votou a favor da ratificação, o seu grupo votou a favor do adiamento.

Portanto, a pergunta que lhe deixo é: em vez de um mecanismo de proteção civil, não era melhor ter um mecanismo de proteção dos deputados, que seja a favor da prevenção, e evitar aquilo que hoje acontece em Portugal?
3-0114-0000.englishText:
Mr Member of the European Parliament, I am not going to nationalise the issue here, as the PSD did in the past with PS MEPs, I am actually going to Europeanise it. You spoke about the civil protection mechanism and we are together, not only in that action, in that activation and in what concerns aid to Member States, but it is just that here in this House, in 2023, European legislation against deforestation was approved.

In the last year, that legislation came back here to be ratified or to be postponed. Unlike this group, which voted in favour of ratification, your group voted in favour of postponement.

Therefore, the question I leave you with is: instead of a civil protection mechanism, wouldn't it be better to have a mechanism to protect MEPs, one that is in favour of prevention, and avoid what is happening in Portugal today?

3-0115-0000.sourceText:
O grupo político, a que orgulhosamente pertenço, tem tido uma posição muito consistente nessa como noutras matérias. O que nós não podemos defender é um regime de desflorestação que não seja compatível com outras dimensões que importa acautelar.

Tenho defendido, em muitas circunstâncias, que o conceito de sustentabilidade pressupõe não só avaliar os impactos ambientais das medidas económicas, mas também os impactos económicos das medidas ambientais.

Foi disso que falámos quando tratámos de um tema como aquele que aqui sugere e, portanto, consistência, sentido de responsabilidade e, acima de tudo, uma dimensão de sustentabilidade que seja mais adequada às circunstâncias em que nós vivemos.
3-0115-0000.englishText:
The political group to which I proudly belong has had a very consistent position on this as on other matters. What we cannot defend is a regime of deforestation that is not compatible with other dimensions that need to be safeguarded.

I have argued, on many occasions, that the concept of sustainability presupposes not only assessing the environmental impacts of economic measures, but also the economic impacts of environmental measures.

That was what we talked about when we dealt with a topic like the one suggested here and, therefore, consistency, a sense of responsibility and, above all, a dimension of sustainability that is more appropriate to the circumstances in which we live.

3-0116-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, je voudrais dire aux députés d’extrême droite de cet hémicycle qu’ils portent une très lourde part de responsabilité dans la situation actuelle. Vous avez voté contre tous les textes – tous les textes! – qui nous permettent de réduire les pires effets du dérèglement climatique. Vous avez voté contre le principe même qu’il y ait une politique climatique européenne pour réduire les émissions, et donc pour réduire le choc climatique. Vous avez donc une part de responsabilité très claire dans le fait qu’il y ait, par exemple, en France, 12 millions de personnes – 12 millions de personnes! – dont les maisons sont en train de se fissurer, de se craquer et de perdre toute leur valeur à cause de l’impact du dérèglement climatique.

Vous portez une lourde responsabilité dans le fait que des milliers d’agriculteurs sont en train de perdre toutes leurs récoltes, dans le sud de la France, à cause de la multiplication des feux de forêt, à cause du changement climatique. Assumez, au moins! Assumez au moins cette responsabilité! Dites-le devant l’ensemble des Français et des Européens! Et s’il vous plaît, arrêtez, arrêtez cette politique climatosceptique, qui est insupportable aujourd’hui en Europe!

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0116-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I would like to tell the far-right deputies of this hemicycle that they bear a very heavy share of responsibility for the current situation. You have voted against all the texts – all the texts! – that allow us to reduce the worst effects of climate change. You voted against the very principle of having a European climate policy to reduce emissions, and therefore to reduce the climate shock. You therefore bear a very clear share of responsibility for the fact that there are, for example, in France, 12 million people – 12 million people! – whose houses are cracking, breaking apart, and losing all their value due to the impact of climate change.

You bear a heavy responsibility for the fact that thousands of farmers are losing all their harvests, in the south of France, due to the multiplication of forest fires, due to climate change. Take responsibility, at least! Take at least this responsibility! Say it in front of all French and European people! And please, stop, stop this climate-skeptic policy, which is unbearable today in Europe!

(The speaker accepts a blue-card question)

3-0117-0000.sourceText: ��blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank, Herr Kollege, dass Sie die Zwischenfrage zulassen. Sie haben gerade gesagt, dass die Verantwortung dafür, dass es zu Umweltkatastrophen und Waldbränden gekommen ist, bei der Rechten liegt. Ich habe mal die Frage: Welches Gesetz kennen Sie ganz konkret, wo Sie glauben, dass es nicht zustande gekommen ist wegen einer Abstimmung der Rechten? Ich würde nämlich behaupten, es sind alle Gesetze zustande gekommen, und am Ende ist doch dann die Feststellung, dass Ihre Gesetze einfach wirkungslos sind.
3-0117-0000.englishText: Blue Card. - Thank you, dear colleague, for allowing the point of order. You just said that the responsibility for environmental disasters and forest fires lies with the right. I have a question: Which specific law do you know that you believe failed to be passed because of a vote by the right? I would argue that all laws were passed, and in the end the conclusion is simply that your laws are ineffective.

3-0118-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur, votre groupe politique et l'ensemble des groupes politiques d'extrême droite ont voté contre la loi sur la restauration de la nature, qui permet justement d'avoir des zones humides qui permettent de limiter les impacts du changement climatique sur le stress hydrique ou sur les feux de forêt. Vous avez voté contre le principe même qu'il y ait une loi climat européenne qui respecte l'accord de Paris. Vous avez voté absolument contre tous les textes sur l'industrie, sur l'automobile, sur tout, sur l'agriculture, qui permettraient de limiter les conséquences absolument dramatiques pour les Européens du changement climatique.

Assumez, ayez au moins l'honneur d'assumer cette responsabilité!
3-0118-0000.englishText:
Sir, your political group and all the far-right political groups voted against the nature restoration law, which precisely makes it possible to have wetlands that help limit the impacts of climate change on water stress or forest fires. You voted against the very principle of having a European climate law that respects the Paris Agreement. You voted absolutely against all texts on industry, on the automobile, on everything, on agriculture, which would make it possible to limit the absolutely dramatic consequences of climate change for Europeans.

Take responsibility, have at least the honor of taking this responsibility!

3-0119-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Viele von uns haben in ihrer Heimat in den letzten Jahren die Erfahrung gemacht, dass wir mit Extremwetterereignissen zurechtkommen müssen. Auch in meiner Heimat Sachsen erleben wir diese Entwicklung unmittelbar: Der Großbrand in der Gohrischheide im vergangenen Jahr war der größte Waldbrand Deutschlands. Deshalb geht an dieser Stelle auch ein großer Dank an die vielen tausend Einsatzkräfte, Feuerwehrleute, Katastrophenhelfer, die uns in diesen Situationen zur Seite stehen und helfen.

Aber gerade deshalb ist es richtig, dass Europa seine Katastrophenvorsorge und den preparedness-Gedanken weiter stärkt. Mit dem Europäischen Katastrophenschutzmechanismus, gemeinsamen Löschflugzeugen und Satellitendaten aus dem Copernicus‑Programm schafft die Europäische Union einen echten Mehrwert. Europa hilft, Gefahren früher zu erkennen und im Ernstfall schneller gemeinsam zu handeln.

Mindestens genauso wichtig ist aber die Vorsorge. Wir brauchen widerstandsfähigere Wälder, neue Konzepte der Wasserversorgung, moderne Frühwarnsysteme und Investitionen in den Bevölkerungsschutz. Europa kann hier unterstützen, die Verantwortung beginnt aber vor Ort mit einer preparedness-Strategie, die Menschen schützt, Infrastruktur sichert und unsere Regionen widerstandsfähiger macht – und genau darauf werden wir auch in den Verhandlungen über einen neuen EU‑Haushalt als Hohes Haus achten müssen.
3-0119-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues! In recent years, many of us have had the experience in our home countries of having to cope with extreme weather events. In my home region of Saxony, too, we are experiencing this development firsthand: the major forest fire in the Gohrischheide last year was Germany's largest forest fire. Therefore, a big thank you goes out at this point to the many thousands of emergency workers, firefighters, and disaster relief personnel who stand by our side and help us in these situations.

Precisely for this reason, however, it is right for Europe to further strengthen its disaster preparedness and the idea of preparedness. With the Union Civil Protection Mechanism, joint firefighting aircraft, and satellite data from the Copernicus program, the European Union creates genuine added value. Europe helps to identify dangers earlier and to act together more quickly in an emergency.

At least as important, however, is prevention. We need more resilient forests, new water supply concepts, modern early warning systems, and investments in civil protection. Europe can provide support here, but responsibility begins locally with a preparedness strategy that protects people, secures infrastructure, and makes our regions more resilient – and that is precisely what we will also have to pay attention to in the negotiations on a new EU budget as this august House.

3-0120-0000.sourceText:
Fru talman! Då var det dags igen – ny värmebölja här i Strasbourg. Den förra vi hade för två veckor sedan ungefär är faktiskt en av de värsta som vi någonsin haft i flera av EU:s länder.

Men EU och medlemsländerna kan göra mycket för att klimatkrisen i alla fall ska bli mindre katastrofal. I dag har vi från Gröna gruppen skickat ett brev till er i kommissionen med våra krav för att skydda oss i Europa från följderna av extremväder.

Vi måste satsa mer på naturbaserade lösningar, se till att klimatresiliens finns med i all lagstiftning, ta fullt ansvar för hela klimatanpassningsarbetet i alla samhällssektorer, sätta tydliga mål för de 36 största utpekade riskerna, och sist men absolut inte minst skydda de arbetare som riskerar att drabbas av den extrema värmen.

Kort sagt, vi behöver en väldigt stark klimatanpassningslag för EU.
3-0120-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Then it was time again – a new heatwave here in Strasbourg. The previous one we had about two weeks ago is actually one of the worst we have ever had in several of the EU's countries.

But the EU and the member states can do a lot to make the climate crisis at least less catastrophic. Today, we from the Greens group have sent a letter to you in the Commission with our demands to protect us in Europe from the consequences of extreme weather.

We must invest more in nature-based solutions, ensure that climate resilience is included in all legislation, take full responsibility for all climate adaptation work in all sectors of society, set clear targets for the 36 largest identified risks, and last but definitely not least, protect the workers who risk being affected by the extreme heat.

In short, we need a very strong climate adaptation law for the EU.

3-0121-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, de hittegolf van eind juni was niet de eerste die we tegenkwamen en zal ook niet de laatste zijn. Net daarom moet onze focus liggen op klimaatadaptatie. Maak huizen, kantoren, ziekenhuizen, rusthuizen, scholen en crèches beter bestand tegen die extreme hitte. En daarom moeten we in de eerste plaats stoppen met het demoniseren van airco's. Een airco is geen symbool van klimaatonverschilligheid. Integendeel, het is een noodzakelijk hulpmiddel om ouderen, zieken, jonge kinderen en zorgverleners te beschermen wanneer de temperaturen hoog oplopen. Airco's redden levens. Ze zijn dus levensnoodzakelijk.

Wat we zeker niet moeten doen, is het voorbeeld van de Commissie volgen, want tijdens de hittegolf in juni moesten medewerkers op de lagere verdiepingen van het commissiegebouw namelijk zonder airco werken, terwijl de kantoren van de commissievoorzitter en de andere commissarissen op de bovenste verdiepingen wel gekoeld werden. Orwell zou zeggen: “All floors are equal, but some floors are more equal than others.” Zoiets heet hypocrisie en vat het beleid van de Commissie heel goed samen.
3-0121-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the heatwave at the end of June was not the first we have encountered and will not be the last. Precisely for that reason, our focus must be on climate adaptation. Make houses, offices, hospitals, nursing homes, schools, and daycare centers more resilient to that extreme heat. And that is why we must, first of all, stop demonizing air conditioning. Air conditioning is not a symbol of climate indifference. On the contrary, it is a necessary tool to protect the elderly, the sick, young children, and caregivers when temperatures soar. Air conditioning saves lives. They are therefore vital.

What we certainly should not do is follow the example of the Commission, because during the heatwave in June, employees on the lower floors of the Commission building actually had to work without air conditioning, while the offices of the Commission President and the other Commissioners on the upper floors were indeed cooled. Orwell would say: “All floors are equal, but some floors are more equal than others.” That sort of thing is called hypocrisy and sums up the Commission's policy very well.

3-0122-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrte Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Klimaapokalypse abgesagt – so hat sich die AfD im Mai noch gefreut. Ich würde sagen, das ist gealtert wie frische Milch in der Hitzewelle. Keine zwei Monate später, und wir haben europaweit Temperaturen von über 40 Grad, Waldbrände, Stromausfälle, Hitzetote, Plünderungen. Und die Wissenschaft ist sich einig: Diese extreme Hitzewelle wäre ohne den menschengemachten Klimawandel, ohne die Klimakrise undenkbar, und die Europäische Union trifft es unmittelbar.

Was fällt Ihnen am rechten Rand dazu ein? Klimaanlagen. Wow! Haben Sie schon mal in dieser Hitzewelle auf einer Baustelle gearbeitet? Pakete verteilt? Kranke gepflegt? Nein, haben Sie nicht, Sie sitzen hier im klimatisierten Plenarsaal.

Wir brauchen Investitionen in unsere Krankenhäuser, in Pflegeeinrichtungen, in Produktionshallen – ja, aber wir brauchen auch Katastrophenschutz; wir brauchen mehr erneuerbare Energien; wir brauchen eine resiliente Infrastruktur. Und gleichzeitig – und ich weiß, an zwei Dinge gleichzeitig zu denken, fällt Ihnen schwer –, wir haben es in der Hand, dafür zu sorgen, dass dieser Hitzesommer eine Ausnahme bleibt und nicht der Anfang der Klimakrise ist. Der Green Deal muss konsequent weiterverfolgt werden, Emissionen müssen runter. Anpassung alleine wird uns nicht retten. Wann begreifen Sie das endlich?
3-0122-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! Climate apocalypse cancelled – that is how the AfD was still rejoicing in May. I would say that has aged like fresh milk in a heatwave. Not two months later, and we have temperatures of over 40 degrees across Europe, wildfires, power outages, heat-related deaths, looting. And science is in agreement: this extreme heatwave would be unthinkable without human-made climate change, without the climate crisis, and it affects the European Union directly.

What comes to mind on the far right? Air conditioning. Wow! Have you ever worked on a construction site during this heatwave? Delivered packages? Nursed the sick? No, you haven't, you are sitting here in the air-conditioned chamber.

We need investments in our hospitals, in care facilities, in production halls – yes, but we also need civil protection; we need more renewable energies; we need resilient infrastructure. And at the same time – and I know thinking about two things at once is hard for you – we have it in our hands to ensure that this hot summer remains an exception and not the beginning of the climate crisis. The Green Deal must be pursued consistently, emissions must come down. Adaptation alone will not save us. When will you finally grasp that?

3-0123-0000.sourceText:
President, Commissioner, Colleagues, I will address you in Portuguese.

Mais de 1 300 europeus perderam a vida, acima do que é habitual, entre 21 e 29 de junho, devido à onda de calor. Estima-se que se perdem cerca de 44 000 vidas por ano devido às altas temperaturas na Europa.

A prevenção de incêndios e a resiliência climática são uma das agendas mais importantes deste mandato e quero focar-me numa medida de adaptação climática em particular: ar condicionado acessível a todos os europeus de norte a sul. Não é um luxo, é uma necessidade.

Apenas uma em cada cinco casas na UE tem ar condicionado. Nos Estados Unidos e no Japão, nações que enfrentam verões semelhantes aos nossos, são nove em cada dez. Em vários países europeus, instalar um aparelho de ar condicionado em casa pode exigir licenças, aprovações municipais e consentimento da maioria do condomínio.

Uma União que considera urgente a adaptação às alterações climáticas não pode considerar tecnologias como o ar condicionado um luxo dispensável porque gasta muita energia. Deve e tem de tratá-la já como uma medida de adaptação climática.

(A oradora aceita responder a uma pergunta «cartão azul»)
3-0123-0000.englishText:
President, Commissioner, Colleagues, I will address you in Portuguese.

More than 1,300 Europeans lost their lives, above the usual number, between June 21 and 29, due to the heatwave. It is estimated that around 44,000 lives are lost every year due to high temperatures in Europe.

Fire prevention and climate resilience are among the most important agendas of this term, and I want to focus on a particular climate adaptation measure: affordable air conditioning for all Europeans from north to south. It is not a luxury, it is a necessity.

Only one in five homes in the EU has air conditioning. In the United States and Japan, nations facing summers similar to ours, it is nine out of ten. In several European countries, installing an air conditioning unit at home can require permits, municipal approvals, and the consent of the majority of the condominium.

A Union that considers adaptation to climate change urgent cannot consider technologies like air conditioning a dispensable luxury because it consumes a lot of energy. It must and has to treat it now as a climate adaptation measure.

(The speaker agrees to take a "blue card" question)

3-0124-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Deputada Ana Vasconcelos, falou-nos de ar condicionado a propósito da mitigação do calor, mas queria fazer-lhe uma pergunta sobre gestão de recursos hídricos e acesso a fundos europeus para a melhoria das redes de água e de abastecimento de água e de saneamento que, em muitas circunstâncias, se veem limitadas na possibilidade de utilização de fundos europeus para terem melhor eficiência na gestão dos recursos hídricos, questões tão absolutamente essenciais para fazer face às situações de seca e de calor excessivo que temos.

A Senhora Deputada acha que devemos continuar a lidar com este tipo de restrições no acesso aos fundos europeus, por parte das entidades públicas que têm essa responsabilidade da gestão da água e saneamento?
3-0124-0000.englishText:
Madam Deputy Ana Vasconcelos, you spoke to us about air conditioning regarding the mitigation of heat, but I wanted to ask you a question about water resource management and access to European funds for the improvement of water networks, water supply and sanitation, which in many circumstances see their possibility of using European funds limited in order to have better efficiency in the management of water resources, issues so absolutely essential to cope with the situations of drought and excessive heat that we have.

Does the Deputy think we should continue to deal with these kinds of restrictions in access to European funds by public entities that have this responsibility for water and sanitation management?

3-0125-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Deputado, o Sul da Europa, Portugal incluído, tem sido dos maiores beneficiários de fundos europeus para gerir os recursos hídricos. Aliás, é graças à má gestão desses fundos que não temos tido um bom desempenho na gestão desses recursos e na disponibilidade de água aos nossos cidadãos.

Portanto, sim, devemos gerir melhor os nossos recursos, os recursos europeus e os recursos nacionais, para disponibilização de água de qualidade e para evitar perdas de água por causa de infraestruturas mal mantidas.
3-0125-0000.englishText:
Mr Member of the European Parliament, Southern Europe, including Portugal, has been among the largest beneficiaries of European funds to manage water resources. In fact, it is thanks to the mismanagement of these funds that we have not had a good performance in managing these resources and in the availability of water to our citizens.

Therefore, yes, we must better manage our resources, European resources and national resources, for the provision of quality water and to avoid water losses due to poorly maintained infrastructure.

3-0126-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, nella più recente ondata di calore abbiamo contato in Europa più di 1 300 vittime, chi per malori causati dal lavoro in condizioni insostenibili, chi per fragilità pregresse o malori improvvisi, che hanno intasato i nostri pronto soccorso, chi per essersi tuffato in bacini o corsi d'acqua pericolosi.

Le città che hanno preso sul serio questa questione – guarda caso nessuna guidata da negazionisti di estrema destra – stanno salvando vite, creando rifugi climatici, potenziando il verde urbano, rimuovendo l'asfalto, desigillando il suolo, si salvano vite, soprattutto quelle dei più fragili e dei più soli.

E pensiamo anche ai detenuti, a chi non ha una casa o che ne ha una che è un frigo d'inverno e un forno d'estate. Ed è qui che le strategie per combattere la crisi climatica, la crisi sociale e i loro effetti si saldano. Investire sull'abitare sostenibile taglia emissioni, crea coesione sociale, crea lavoro stabile, potenzia le filiere industriali europee, come quella delle pompe di calore, salva vite e la loro dignità.

Abbiamo gli strumenti, ci vuole il coraggio della politica.
3-0126-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, during the most recent heatwave we counted more than 1 300 victims in Europe, some due to illnesses caused by working in unsustainable conditions, some due to pre-existing vulnerabilities or sudden illnesses that clogged our emergency rooms, some for having dived into dangerous basins or watercourses.

The cities that have taken this issue seriously - coincidentally none led by far-right deniers - are saving lives, creating climate refuges, enhancing urban greenery, removing asphalt, unsealing the soil, lives are being saved, especially those of the most fragile and the most lonely.

And let us also think of prisoners, of those who do not have a home or who have one that is a fridge in winter and an oven in summer. And this is where strategies to combat the climate crisis, the social crisis and their effects come together. Investing in sustainable housing cuts emissions, creates social cohesion, creates stable jobs, boosts European industrial supply chains, such as that of heat pumps, saves lives and their dignity.

We have the tools, it takes political courage.

3-0127-0000.sourceText:
�� Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, Gaston Bachelard escreveu que o fogo é a maior ambiguidade da experiência humana. Desde que o primeiro homem contemplou uma chama, percebemos porquê.

O fogo aquece e destrói; ilumina e consome; brilha no Paraíso e queima no Inferno. Mas, acima de tudo, o fogo foi sempre o símbolo da prova.

Em todas as culturas, a prova de fogo representa o teste decisivo, aquele que revela o verdadeiro valor. Foi assim que, durante séculos, se aferiu a autenticidade do ouro. Só o ouro verdadeiro resiste ao fogo.

O ouro e o bombeiro partilham a mesma verdade essencial: não é o fogo que faz o ouro. Nem o bombeiro. O fogo apenas revela aquilo de que um e o outro são feitos. Sempre que entram nas chamas para proteger os outros, as casas dos outros, as vidas dos outros, os bombeiros portugueses passam, uma vez mais, pela prova de fogo. É aí, face a face com as chamas, que se prova que aqueles homens e mulheres são autenticamente feitos de ouro.

Portugal está a ferro e fogo. O Mecanismo de Proteção Civil da União Europeia pode ajudar, mas só os bombeiros portugueses podem impedir que ardam 900 anos de existência.

(O orador recusa uma pergunta «cartão azul» de Marta Temido)
3-0127-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, Gaston Bachelard wrote that fire is the greatest ambiguity of human experience. Ever since the first man gazed at a flame, we have understood why.

Fire warms and destroys; it illuminates and consumes; it shines in Paradise and burns in Hell. But above all, fire has always been the symbol of the trial.

In all cultures, the trial by fire represents the decisive test, the one that reveals true value. This is how, for centuries, the authenticity of gold was measured. Only true gold resists fire.

Gold and the firefighter share the same essential truth: it is not the fire that makes the gold. Nor the firefighter. Fire merely reveals what each is made of. Whenever they step into the flames to protect others, the homes of others, the lives of others, Portuguese firefighters go through the trial by fire once again. It is there, face to face with the flames, that it is proven that those men and women are authentically made of gold.

Portugal is in iron and fire. The European Union Civil Protection Mechanism can help, but only Portuguese firefighters can prevent 900 years of existence from burning.

(The speaker refuses a "blue card" question from Marta Temido)

3-0128-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, quest'estate ancora milioni di europei vivono giornate soffocanti. Anziani che non riescono a uscire di casa, bambini che devono rinunciare ai giochi nei parchi, famiglie evacuate per gli incendi, vigili del fuoco che rischiano la vita.

Questa non è più un'emergenza, è una realtà.

L'Europa deve continuare a combattere il cambiamento climatico con la mitigazione, basandosi più su incentivi che sulla penalizzazione, ma deve – accanto alla riduzione delle emissioni – pensare a una grande strategia di adattamento.

Dobbiamo continuare a prevenire i cambiamenti climatici, ma accanto a questo dobbiamo proteggere le persone dagli effetti dei cambiamenti climatici.

I tre miliardi di alberi previsti entro il 2030 sono un segnale importante. L'Europa deve rafforzare la propria strategia di riforestazione: un miliardo di alberi in più nelle città per abbassare le temperature da 2 fino a 8 °C in meno, più foreste dove il fuoco ha distrutto interi territori, più verde nelle aree minacciate dalla desertificazione.

Adattarsi al cambiamento climatico non significa arrendersi, significa difendere la salute, difendere la sicurezza, difendere il futuro dei nostri figli. È una responsabilità che oggi l'Europa deve assumersi.
3-0128-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, this summer millions of Europeans are still living through suffocating days. Elderly people who cannot leave their homes, children who have to give up playing in parks, families evacuated due to fires, firefighters risking their lives.

This is no longer an emergency, it is a reality.

Europe must continue to combat climate change through mitigation, relying more on incentives than on penalties, but it must – alongside the reduction of emissions – think about a major adaptation strategy.

We must continue to prevent climate change, but alongside this we must protect people from the effects of climate change.

The three billion trees planned by 2030 are an important signal. Europe must strengthen its reforestation strategy: one billion more trees in cities to lower temperatures by 2 to 8 °C, more forests where fire has destroyed entire territories, more greenery in areas threatened by desertification.

Adapting to climate change does not mean surrendering, it means defending health, defending security, defending the future of our children. It is a responsibility that Europe must assume today.

3-0130-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, el año pasado el sur de Europa sufrió una temporada de incendios sin precedentes marcada por los llamados incendios de sexta generación. Los datos de este año tampoco son buenos, más bien lo contrario.

Yo celebro que la Unión Europea esté reaccionando. La Comisión presentó el pasado mes de marzo la primera Comunicación sobre la gestión integrada de los incendios forestales y también ha aumentado el despliegue de medios. Es un paso en la buena dirección y las demás administraciones públicas debían seguir esta línea.

En este sentido, yo quiero celebrar la importancia que la Xunta de Galicia está dando en estos años a la prevención y a la extinción de los incendios. Está reforzando todavía más, en este año 2026, un dispositivo que es una auténtico referente no solo a nivel nacional, sino internacional. Para este año 2026, la Xunta ha mejorado los sistemas a todos los niveles —prevención, vigilancia, extinción—, se han aumentado los medios materiales y humanos disponibles y se ha aprobado el mayor presupuesto de la historia: más de 213 millones de euros, un 18 % más que el año pasado.
3-0130-0000.englishText:
Madam President, last year southern Europe suffered an unprecedented fire season marked by so-called sixth-generation fires. This year's data is not looking good either, quite the contrary.

I welcome the fact that the European Union is reacting. Last March, the Commission presented the first Communication on the integrated management of wildfires and has also increased the deployment of resources. This is a step in the right direction, and other public administrations should follow this line.

In this regard, I want to praise the importance that the Xunta de Galicia has been giving in recent years to wildfire prevention and extinction. In this year 2026, it is further strengthening a system that is a true benchmark not only at the national level, but also internationally. For this year 2026, the Xunta has improved systems at all levels —prevention, surveillance, extinction—, material and human resources available have been increased, and the largest budget in history has been approved: more than 213 million euros, 18% more than last year.

3-0131-0000.sourceText: Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, de la intensidad de este debate y de la controversia suscitada es evidente que la Unión Europea es la región del mundo más afectada por el calentamiento global y tiene un balance trágico en mortalidad este mismo verano, pero rebajar los estándares en la ambición europea en la agenda digital y en la agenda migratoria sin duda ninguna es dañino y, a mi juicio, suicida. Pero nada es más injusto que rebajar los estándares en la transición verde justa, y eso no puede pasar, bajo ningún concepto, por rebajar la partida financiera necesaria en el marco financiero plurianual para que la Unión Europea pueda mantener su ambición en la incorporación de energías renovables, en el combate a la carbonización de la economía europea que ha coadyuvado al calentamiento global. Es imprescindible que haya recursos para proteger a la ciudadanía y, especialmente, a la clase trabajadora que no puede soportar este calor.
3-0131-0000.englishText: Madam President, Madam Commissioner, from the intensity of this debate and the controversy it has sparked, it is clear that the European Union is the region of the world most affected by global warming and has a tragic mortality toll this very summer, but lowering standards in European ambition regarding the digital agenda and the migration agenda is undoubtedly harmful and, in my view, suicidal. But nothing is more unjust than lowering standards in the fair green transition, and that cannot happen, under any circumstances, by reducing the necessary financial allocation within the multiannual financial framework so that the European Union can maintain its ambition in the incorporation of renewable energies and in combating the carbonization of the European economy that has contributed to global warming. It is essential that there are resources to protect citizens and, especially, the working class who cannot bear this heat.

3-0132-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, for years, decades even, we have been warning about the impact of climate change. Yet here we are. Every summer is hotter, every wildfire season more devastating, and our response is still too slow. Why? Because of those who repeatedly choose to ignore the facts. Unfortunately, some of them are today here in this plenary.

Heatwaves and wildfires are no longer exceptional events. They are Europe's reality. Families lose their homes, workers face unbearable conditions and firefighters risk their lives.

Europe must do more, because no Member States should be left to face these disasters alone. There is no credible strategy against heatwaves and wildfires if at the same time we weaken climate policies or dismantle the Green Deal. Every delay and every vote against climate action has consequences that are measured in lives lost and communities destroyed.

3-0133-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, seuraa EU-uutisia: helleaallot koettelivat Brysseliä ja muuta Eurooppaa, ja komission rakennuksesta sammutettiin osittain ilmastointi. Nyt vaaditaan hiki hatussa EU:n hellestrategioita ja EU:n tason vastauksia. Mutta mitä yhteistä on Suomen hellepäivällä ja Espanjan yli 40 asteen lämpöaallolla? Eipä juuri mitään, ja siksi ratkaisujenkin on oltava erilaisia.

Pelastuspalvelut, terveydenhuolto, rakentaminen ja varautuminen kuuluvat jäsenmaille. Ne tuntevat omat olosuhteensa paremmin kuin yksikään Brysselissä hikoileva virkamies. Mutta kun lämpömittari nousee, näyttää Brysselissä nousevan valtakuume. Jos puhutaan ilmastotoimista, me kyllä voimme käydä keskustelua Kiinasta ja muista riistolaisista, mutta kun puhutaan varautumisratkaisuista tähän hetkeen, niin ratkaisujen on pysyttävä kansallisissa käsissä.
3-0133-0000.englishText:
Mr President, here is EU news: heatwaves hit Brussels and the rest of Europe, and the air conditioning in the Commission building was partially turned off. Now, sweating profusely, people are demanding EU heatwave strategies and EU-level responses. But what do a hot day in Finland and a heatwave of over 40 degrees in Spain have in common? Practically nothing, and that is why the solutions must be different, too.

Rescue services, healthcare, construction, and preparedness belong to the member states. They know their own conditions better than any bureaucrat sweating in Brussels. But when the thermometer rises, it seems that a fever for power rises in Brussels, too. When it comes to climate action, we can certainly discuss China and other exploiters, but when it comes to preparedness solutions for the present moment, the solutions must remain in national hands.

3-0134-0000.sourceText: Madam President, the five biggest fossil fuel companies – TotalEnergies, BP, Chevron, ExxonMobil and Shell – together generate roughly EUR 8 trillion in revenue every year. According to the Commission's own estimate, making Europe heatwave proof would cost EUR 70 billion a year – just 7 % of these companies' revenue. These same companies have spent decades profiting from the very emissions now killing people all over the world and in Europe. So my question to the Commission is: will the Commission make the companies causing the climate crisis pay the bill for making schools, hospitals and care homes safe in hot weather?

3-0135-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, écoutez, cela a été dit, mais 1 222 personnes sont mortes, en Belgique, à cause de la chaleur. Si cela avait été une attaque militaire, comment est-ce que vous auriez réagi ici? S’il y avait eu 1 200 personnes mortes en Belgique à cause d’une attaque militaire? Cela aurait été l’état d’urgence. Vous auriez mobilisé toutes les troupes, toutes les forces, tous les fonds pour réagir à cela. Et ici, aujourd’hui, qu’est-ce que j’entends de la Commission? «Ne vous inquiétez pas, dans quelques mois, on viendra avec un nouveau plan d’action.»

Mais entre-temps, les fonds pour la militarisation, pour la guerre, s’élèvent à des centaines de milliards pour les avions de chasse. Où sont les centaines de milliards pour nos maisons de repos? Pour les hôpitaux? On doit mettre maintenant des couvertures de survie en Europe – des couvertures de survie! – sur les fenêtres de nos hôpitaux pour que les patients ne crèvent pas de chaleur!
