Les travailleurs qui doivent travailler à 40 degrés. Où est le plan d’urgence? Comment est-ce qu’on va les sauver?

Et là, l’extrême droite qui nie même l’évidence, c’est une honte! Mais la coalition au gouvernement, la coalition au pouvoir ici, a aussi des questions et des responsabilités auxquelles elle doit répondre.
3-0135-0000.englishText:
Madam President, listen, it has been said, but 1,222 people died in Belgium because of the heat. If it had been a military attack, how would you have reacted here? If there had been 1,200 people dead in Belgium because of a military attack? That would have been a state of emergency. You would have mobilized all the troops, all the forces, all the funds to react to that. And here, today, what do I hear from the Commission? "Don't worry, in a few months we will come up with a new action plan."

But in the meantime, the funds for militarization, for war, amount to hundreds of billions for fighter jets. Where are the hundreds of billions for our nursing homes? For the hospitals? We now have to put emergency blankets in Europe – emergency blankets! – on the windows of our hospitals so that patients don't die of the heat! Workers who have to work at 40 degrees. Where is the emergency plan? How are we going to save them?

And there, the far right even denying the obvious, it's a disgrace! But the government coalition, the ruling coalition here, also has questions and responsibilities to which it must respond.

3-0136-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, čestitam povjerenice za povećanje Fonda za EU Rescue mehanizam za 11 milijardi eura.

Kao izvjestiteljica za mišljenje Odbora za razvoj mislim da je to ključno. Godine 2019. ova kuća uopće nije imala interes da išta učinimo na tom pogledu, ali mi još uvijek ne ulažemo ono što je osnovno, a to su vatrogasci. Nitko ne pomaže vatrogascima da nabave opremu, protekli tjedan u Mostaru, znači, mi koristimo ovu opremu i za prekogranično gašenje požara i u Bosni i Hercegovini. Očajan, vatrogasac je došao i rekao: „Mi ne možemo dalje. Mi ne možemo više, mi nemamo opremu”. Znači, požari dolaze i u Hrvatsku, iz Bosne i Hercegovine, 11 milijardi, ovdje se raspravlja, mi za prevenciju još ništa ne radimo.

Ništa ne koristimo, a 1956. u Mostaru je bilo 46 stupnjeva zabilježeno, vrućine je bilo i bit će, ali našeg nerada još uvijek ovdje postoji.
3-0136-0000.englishText:
Madam President, congratulations Commissioner on the increase of the EU Rescue mechanism Fund by 11 billion euros.

As the rapporteur for the opinion of the Committee on Development, I think this is crucial. In 2019, this house had no interest at all in us doing anything in that regard, but we are still not investing in what is fundamental, and that is firefighters. No one is helping firefighters to procure equipment; last week in Mostar, meaning, we use this equipment for cross-border firefighting in Bosnia and Herzegovina as well. Desperate, a firefighter came and said: „We can't go on. We can't do any more, we don't have equipment”. Meaning, fires are also coming to Croatia, from Bosnia and Herzegovina, 11 billion, we are discussing here, we are still doing nothing for prevention.

We are using nothing, and in 1956 in Mostar 46 degrees was recorded, there was heat and there will be, but our inaction still exists here.

3-0137-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, proteger a las personas frente a las olas de calor implica también proteger a los trabajadores y trabajadoras; porque la preparación frente a las olas de calor empieza por no obligar a nadie a elegir entre su salario y su salud.

Por eso, resulta incomprensible que el Partido Popular en España proponga precisamente recortar prestaciones a quienes están de baja, como si los médicos no tuvieran criterio o como si, por ejemplo, sufrir un golpe de calor no fuera lo suficientemente grave. ¿Esa es su receta para proteger a las personas trabajadoras cuando las temperaturas extremas ya están poniendo en riesgo su salud? Porque el cambio climático no entiende de ideologías, pero sí de consecuencias.

Un trabajo de calidad tiene que ser un trabajo seguro, saludable y adaptado a la realidad del siglo XXI. Y eso, en 2026, pasa por proteger a quienes trabajan frente al calor extremo, por establecer normas mínimas comunes de prevención y protección, y pasa por garantizar los ingresos cuando no sea seguro trabajar. Esa es la diferencia entre quienes entienden la adaptación como un recorte y quienes la entendemos como una ampliación de derechos.
3-0137-0000.englishText:
Madam President, protecting people from heatwaves also means protecting workers; because preparation for heatwaves starts with not forcing anyone to choose between their salary and their health.

That is why it is incomprehensible that the Partido Popular in Spain proposes precisely to cut benefits for those on sick leave, as if doctors had no criteria or as if, for example, suffering a heatstroke were not serious enough. Is that your recipe for protecting workers when extreme temperatures are already putting their health at risk? Because climate change does not understand ideologies, but it does understand consequences.

Quality work must be safe, healthy, and adapted to the reality of the 21st century. And that, in 2026, involves protecting those who work against extreme heat, establishing common minimum standards of prevention and protection, and guaranteeing income when it is not safe to work. That is the difference between those who understand adaptation as a cut and those who understand it as an expansion of rights.

3-0138-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, the data is clear: the next climate refugees will be us. It will be families in Spain, Portugal or Italy forced to leave towns their grandparents built because the climate is just too hot. In Andalusia right now, experts are using crop planting methods once reserved for the Sahara, because that's what Europe's soil is turning into.

Yet some still prefer just distracting citizens. Today we again listened to some of your climate lies that, in the end, only serve and protect the wealthy – those who are building climatised luxury bunkers because they know what's coming. As do you. You're just fooling your own voters.

We need a European plan to work with nature to update our infrastructure before our own citizens are forced to flee it. Let's stop pretending the danger is somewhere out at the gates. The danger is right here in our own ranks.

3-0139-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, kolegice i kolege, požari su i sigurnosni i gospodarski i klimatski izazov.

Dolazim iz Hrvatske, iz zemlje koja je bila razarana požarima proteklih godina i dobro znamo što znači štititi živote, domove i prirodu. Zahvaljujući snažnom sustavu civilne zaštite, profesionalnim i dobrovoljnim vatrogascima te protupožarnoj zračnoj floti, pokazali smo da dobra organizacija ipak spašava živote i imovinu. To je ono što zovemo prevencija.

Sada tu razinu spremnosti moramo podići na europsku razinu. Potrebni su i veći zajednički kapaciteti kroz RescuEU, brža prekogranična pomoć i više ulaganja u prevenciju i upravljanje šumama i moderni sustavi ranog upozoravanja. Ulaganje u otpornost nije samo klimatska politika. To je politika sigurnosti europskih građana i zato moramo razgovarati o tome prije nego što dođe sljedeća sezona, jer opet ćemo reći, došli su požari, došlo je toplo vrijeme.

Ne, o tome moramo razmišljati danas.
3-0139-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, wildfires are a security, economic, and climate challenge.

I come from Croatia, a country that has been devastated by fires in recent years, and we know very well what it means to protect lives, homes, and nature. Thanks to a strong civil protection system, professional and volunteer firefighters, and an aerial firefighting fleet, we have shown that good organization ultimately saves lives and property. That is what we call prevention.

Now we must raise that level of preparedness to the European level. We need greater joint capacities through RescuEU, faster cross-border assistance, increased investment in prevention, forest management, and modern early warning systems. Investing in resilience is not just climate policy. It is a security policy for European citizens, and that is why we must discuss this before the next season arrives, because otherwise we will say again: the fires are here, the warm weather has come.

No, we must think about that today.

3-0140-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária Lahbib, a prevenção e o combate aos incêndios exigem a valorização do mundo rural, exigem o investimento nos serviços públicos e nas estruturas de proteção civil.

Quando se defende a competitividade, esmagam-se as pequenas empresas e os pequenos produtores. Quando se defende a militarização, desviando os recursos da PAC e de outros fundos europeus que deviam apoiar os setores produtivos, arruína-se a agricultura familiar, e tudo isto contribui para a desertificação do mundo rural, transformando o território num barril de pólvora.

Quando se impõem limitações orçamentais ao investimento dos Estados nos serviços públicos, condiciona-se a capacidade de ação dos serviços de saúde, condiciona-se a resposta da proteção civil.

Tudo isso é absolutamente essencial ser revertido. Precisamos de melhor planeamento, precisamos de melhor abordagem às questões da prevenção dos incêndios.

Mas nada disto se consegue fazer se não houver da parte dos Estados a capacidade e os meios para fazerem face às suas responsabilidades, incluindo nestas áreas que sublinhei.
3-0140-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner Lahbib, the prevention and fight against fires require the valorization of the rural world, they require investment in public services and civil protection structures.

When competitiveness is defended, small businesses and small producers are crushed. When militarization is defended, diverting resources from the CAP and other European funds that should support productive sectors, family farming is ruined, and all this contributes to the desertification of the rural world, turning the territory into a powder keg.

When budgetary limitations are imposed on State investment in public services, the capacity for action of health services is conditioned, the response of civil protection is conditioned.

All of this is absolutely essential to be reversed. We need better planning, we need a better approach to fire prevention issues.

But none of this can be done if there is not on the part of the States the capacity and the means to face their responsibilities, including in these areas that I highlighted.

3-0141-0000.sourceText: Sinjura President, imma aħna verament ippreparati? Għadna qed nitkellmu fuq il-heatwaves bħallikieku huma l-problema ta' għada. Imma mhumiex. In-nies qegħdin ibatu biex jorqdu, it-tfal ma jistgħux imorru l-iskola bħas-soltu, ħaddiema qed jaħdmu f'temperaturi perikolużi u b'hekk din hija emerġenza soċjali. In-nies m'għandhomx bżonn iktar dibattiti għandhom bżonn protezzjoni u azzjoni llum. Ninsolaw lid-djar tagħna, nipproteġu l-iskejjel u l-isptarijiet, aktar spazji bid-dell fil-bliet tagħna u dan l-istess Parlament, sena ilu, sejjaħ għall-aċċess għall-ilma tax-xorb fl-ispazji pubbliċi. Dawn huma miżuri prattiċi illi jsalvaw il-ħajjiet u eluf ta' persuni diġà tilfu ħajjithom. Għażiża Kummissjoni, daqshekk strateġiji, in-nies iridu azzjoni tanġibbli. Qed nistenna qafas għar-reżiljenza klimatika illi jaħdem, mhux għaxar snin oħra, mhux is-sajf li ġej, imma issa.
3-0141-0000.englishText: Madam President, but are we truly prepared? We are still talking about heatwaves as if they are tomorrow's problem. But they are not. People are struggling to sleep, children cannot go to school as usual, workers are working in dangerous temperatures and thus this is a social emergency. People do not need more debates, they need protection and action today. Let us insulate our homes, protect schools and hospitals, more shaded spaces in our cities and this very Parliament, a year ago, called for access to drinking water in public spaces. These are practical measures that save lives and thousands of people have already lost their lives. Dear Commission, enough with strategies, people want tangible action. I am waiting for a climate resilience framework that works, not in ten years' time, not next summer, but now.

3-0142-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, χιλιάδες νεκροί από το κύμα καύσωνα στην Ευρώπη. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση και οι κυβερνήσεις, αφού αφαίμαξαν δισ. ευρώ από τους λαούς για να ταΐσουν τα αρπακτικά των πράσινων ομίλων με την επίκληση αλλαγών στο κλίμα, τώρα εμφανίζονται προκλητικά αιφνιδιασμένες και απροετοίμαστες. Την ίδια ώρα, προϋπολογίζουν ήδη εκατοντάδες δισ. πολεμικής προετοιμασίας, καταπνίγοντας και τις πιο στοιχειώδεις ανάγκες που αφορούν βεβαίως τους λαούς, όπως στις υποδομές.

Στην εποχή της τεχνητής νοημοσύνης, οι λαοί και οι εργαζόμενοι στους χώρους δουλειάς λιώνουν στα απάνθρωπα ωράρια και τις υψηλές θερμοκρασίες. Θρηνούν απώλειες και καταστροφές από φυσικά φαινόμενα για τα οποία πάντα προβάλλεται ως άλλοθι η κλιματική αλλαγή, ενώ δασικές υπηρεσίες και πυρόσβεση —όπως στην Ελλάδα— είναι γυμνές από υποδομές και προσωπικό. Ισχυριζόσασταν ότι η καπιταλιστική αγορά και ο ανταγωνισμός θα έλυναν ακρίβεια, ενεργειακή φτώχεια, χαμηλούς μισθούς —και τελικά ο λαός ζει σε αδιανόητες στερήσεις για τον 21ο αιώνα. Από παντού φωνάζει η ανάγκη του νέου κόσμου του σοσιαλισμού, ανατρέποντας το σάπιο, ξεπερασμένο καπιταλιστικό σύστημα του πολέμου, των κερδών και της εκμετάλλευσης.
3-0142-0000.englishText:
Madam President, thousands of dead from the heatwave in Europe. The European Union and governments, after bleeding billions of euros from the peoples to feed the predators of green conglomerates under the guise of climate change, now appear provocatively surprised and unprepared. At the same time, they are already budgeting hundreds of billions for military preparation, suffocating even the most elementary needs concerning the peoples, such as in infrastructure.

In the era of artificial intelligence, peoples and workers in workplaces melt in inhuman working hours and high temperatures. They mourn losses and destruction from natural phenomena for which climate change is always put forward as an alibi, while forestry services and firefighting—as in Greece—are stripped of infrastructure and personnel. You claimed that the capitalist market and competition would solve high prices, energy poverty, low wages—and ultimately the people live in unimaginable deprivation for the 21st century. From everywhere shouts the need for the new world of socialism, overthrowing the rotten, outdated capitalist system of war, profits, and exploitation.

3-0143-0000.sourceText: Señora presidenta, señorías, Europa necesita un presupuesto a la altura de la emergencia climática. Acaba de empezar el verano y España ya está en llamas. Y frente a los Gobiernos autonómicos que pactan con los negacionistas del cambio climático y recortan los recursos destinados a afrontar esta crisis, estamos los socialistas, que defendemos invertir donde realmente importa: en prevención, en servicios de emergencia, en adaptación y en una solidaridad europea efectiva, especialmente en las zonas rurales y despobladas donde nuestros agricultores, nuestras familias, nuestros vecinos —como los míos de Leciñena y Robres— arriesgan sus vidas cuando intentan acotar las llamas con sus propios medios. Demos prioridad a la agenda de la adaptación y la prevención climática. Actuemos ahora. Salvemos vidas y salvemos también el patrimonio europeo.
3-0143-0000.englishText: Madam President, honourable members, Europe needs a budget commensurate with the climate emergency. Summer has just begun and Spain is already in flames. And facing regional governments that make pacts with climate change deniers and cut resources allocated to address this crisis, there are we Socialists, who defend investing where it really matters: in prevention, in emergency services, in adaptation and in effective European solidarity, especially in rural and depopulated areas where our farmers, our families, our neighbours — like mine from Leciñena and Robres — risk their lives when they try to contain the flames with their own means. Let us give priority to the climate adaptation and prevention agenda. Let us act now. Let us save lives and also save European heritage.

3-0145-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, I will be very brief in one minute. I just want to correct some information. First of all, thank you for this very hot debate. The EU must be an added value, some of you said – and that is exactly the spirit of the preparedness strategy that we presented last year. I would like to add that it is not a strategy that started last year: the rescEU capacities and the ERCC, the Emergency Response Coordination Centre, have existed since 2000. So we didn't start it last year from scratch.

Our rescue capacities must be a permanent reserve, some of you said. It is a permanent reserve. It is not during the summer that we activate. This is a reserve that we can activate when Member States are overwhelmed and, through rescEU and the European Civil Protection Pool, we have 22 firefighting aircraft, 5 helicopters and 22 certified ground firefighting teams available across 10 countries.

So I would like to thank you for this strong debate, and I hope to have such commitment in the autumn, when the temperature goes down and we need your support for the next efforts.

3-0146-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, thank you, and I want to thank the honourable Members and indeed the Commissioner as well. This has been a timely debate on a very, very important topic.

I should say as well that it is important to remember those who have died and those who have suffered because of the unprecedented heat wave that we have just experienced in Europe. And it is a reminder of the urgent need to tackle the causes and consequences of the climate crisis. The presidency will support continuing work in this regard, alongside risk management and preparedness to extreme events.

I should acknowledge that many Members from southern Europe spoke during the debate, and we must acknowledge the suffering and deaths there. But there was not just Members from southern Europe; we see that this has been an issue in other Member States of the European Union, and it is an example of where best I think the European Union can show solidarity and action.

The Council has been acting on two main fronts countering the effect of climate change. One is to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions, which we know from the science lead to negative impacts of climate change. The second is to adapt to climate change.

Regarding the mitigation of emissions, I would like to stress that the EU has one of the most ambitious and necessary climate policies in the world. Our task for the following months and years is to ensure that the implementation of the climate measures supports and enhances the competitiveness of the European economy and indeed not just contributes to climate resilience, but contributes to economic resilience as well.

With the increasing economic costs of extreme weather events such as wildfires, heatwaves and floods, it's increasingly clear that the cost of inaction against climate change exceeds the cost of timely climate measures. On the front of adaptation to climate change, the recent analysis by the European Environment Agency has acknowledged uneven progress in national adaptation policies and identified gaps between the plans and implementation across European countries.

Indeed, to address these challenges, the Council looks forward to a proposal for a European Union framework for climate resilience, which the Commission is expected to propose in the fall.

3-0147-5000.sourceText:
τώς – Κάθε καλοκαίρι η Ευρώπη δοκιμάζεται όλο και περισσότερο από ακραίους καύσωνες και καταστροφικές δασικές πυρκαγιές. Από την Ελλάδα μέχρι την Πορτογαλία και από την Ισπανία μέχρι τη Γαλλία, οι πολίτες μας περιμένουν από την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση να είναι καλύτερα προετοιμασμένη.

Η αλληλεγγύη μέσω του rescEU είναι πολύτιμη, αλλά από μόνη της δεν αρκεί. Χρειαζόμαστε μια πιο φιλόδοξη ευρωπαϊκή προσέγγιση που θα ενισχύει την πρόληψη και την ετοιμότητα.

Γι’ αυτό καλώ την Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή να δημιουργήσει έναν ευρωπαϊκό μηχανισμό κοινών προμηθειών για την πολιτική προστασία, στα πρότυπα των κοινών προμηθειών που αναπτύσσουμε στον τομέα της άμυνας.

Με κοινές ευρωπαϊκές παραγγελίες, τα κράτη μέλη θα μπορούν να προμηθεύονται πυροσβεστικά οχήματα, αεροσκάφη, εξοπλισμό για τους πυροσβέστες και σύγχρονα μέσα αντιμετώπισης φυσικών καταστροφών με χαμηλότερο κόστος, ταχύτερα και με μεγαλύτερη διαλειτουργικότητα.

Οι φυσικές καταστροφές δεν γνωρίζουν σύνορα. Η απάντησή μας δεν μπορεί να περιορίζεται στα εθνικά σύνορα. Μια ισχυρότερη Ευρώπη στην πολιτική προστασία σημαίνει ισχυρότερη επιχειρησιακή ικανότητα για τις Εθνικές Αρχές και μεγαλύτερη ασφάλεια για τους πολίτες και τις περιουσίες τους.
3-0147-5000.englishText:
tós – Every summer Europe is tested more and more by extreme heatwaves and devastating forest fires. From Greece to Portugal and from Spain to France, our citizens expect the European Union to be better prepared.

Solidarity through rescEU is invaluable, but on its own it is not enough. We need a more ambitious European approach that will strengthen prevention and preparedness.

That is why I call on the European Commission to create a European mechanism for joint procurement for civil protection, along the lines of the joint procurement we are developing in the field of defence.

With joint European orders, member states will be able to procure fire engines, aircraft, firefighter equipment and modern means of dealing with natural disasters at a lower cost, faster and with greater interoperability.

Natural disasters know no borders. Our response cannot be limited to national borders. A stronger Europe in civil protection means a stronger operational capacity for National Authorities and greater security for citizens and their property.

3-0147-7500.sourceText:
Európa-szerte rekordmelegek tombolnak, hőhullámok pusztítanak, és több mint 1300 ember vesztette életét a hőség miatt az elmúlt hetekben. Magyarországon is emberek ezrei szenvedtek az extrém hőségtől. Az Európai Bizottság mégis egy új végrehajtási határozattal szigorítja egyes klímagázok kvótáit a következő évekre, ezzel tovább drágítva a hűtőberendezéseket és a légkondicionálókat.

Ahelyett, hogy segítené az embereket az alkalmazkodásban – például megfizethetőbb légkondicionáló berendezésekkel –, a Bizottság olyan döntéseket hoz, amelyek emberek egészségét és biztonságát sodorják veszélybe elvont zöld ideológiai célok érdekében.

Ez nem klímavédelem, hanem zöld fundamentalizmus. A környezet védelme nem történhet az emberek biztonságának és egészségének rovására. Ésszerű, megfizethető alkalmazkodási megoldásokra van szükség, amelyek egyszerre szolgálják a környezet és az emberek védelmét.
3-0147-7500.englishText:
Record highs are raging across Europe, heatwaves are devastating, and more than 1,300 people have lost their lives due to the heat in recent weeks. In Hungary, too, thousands of people have suffered from the extreme heat. Yet the European Commission is tightening the quotas of certain climate gases for the coming years with a new implementing decision, thereby further increasing the cost of cooling equipment and air conditioners.

Instead of helping people to adapt—for example, with more affordable air conditioning equipment—the Commission makes decisions that endanger people's health and safety for abstract green ideological goals.

This is not climate protection, but green fundamentalism. Environmental protection cannot happen at the expense of people's safety and health. Rational, affordable adaptation solutions are needed that serve both the protection of the environment and the people.

3-0147-8125.sourceText:
Los incendios y las olas de calor se han convertido en dos de las amenazas más destructivas y letales a las que se enfrenta Europa. Agravadas de manera directa por la emergencia climática, las olas de calor son cada vez más frecuentes, intensas y prolongadas, lo que provoca miles de muertes y crea las condiciones perfectas para que los incendios forestales se propaguen con una virulencia sin precedentes. Nuestra solidaridad está con las víctimas y con los afectados por estos fenómenos.

Prepararse ante estas amenazas implica anticipar, conocer y prevenir los riesgos, comprender las alertas tempranas y saber cómo actuar antes de una emergencia y durante esta. Las autoridades regionales y locales desempeñan un papel insustituible en este ámbito, pues son las que mejor conocen el territorio, la vegetación, las condiciones climáticas locales y las necesidades específicas de sus comunidades. Del mismo modo, la activación de sistemas de alerta temprana y la educación ciudadana sobre evacuación y autoprotección son competencias que solo pueden ejercerse de manera efectiva desde la proximidad. Cada euro invertido en prevención ahorra hasta seis en respuesta y recuperación.

Desde el Gobierno de España y la Unión, se seguirán reforzando los medios, incluido RescEU, en aplicación de los nuevos planes de preparación ante incendios.
3-0147-8125.englishText:
Fires and heatwaves have become two of the most destructive and lethal threats facing Europe. Directly aggravated by the climate emergency, heatwaves are increasingly frequent, intense and prolonged, causing thousands of deaths and creating the perfect conditions for wildfires to spread with unprecedented virulence. Our solidarity is with the victims and those affected by these phenomena.

Preparing for these threats involves anticipating, knowing and preventing risks, understanding early warnings and knowing how to act before and during an emergency. Regional and local authorities play an irreplaceable role in this area, as they are the ones who best know the territory, the vegetation, local climatic conditions and the specific needs of their communities. Likewise, the activation of early warning systems and citizen education on evacuation and self-protection are responsibilities that can only be effectively exercised from proximity. Every euro invested in prevention saves up to six in response and recovery.

From the Government of Spain and the Union, resources will continue to be reinforced, including RescEU, in application of the new fire preparedness plans.

3-0147-8750.sourceText:
Danes v Sloveniji zaradi ekstremne vročine velja velika požarna ogroženost. V Franciji in Grčiji se medtem že spopadajo z obsežnimi gozdnimi požari – na skrajnem jugu Francije je moralo domove zapustiti okoli 10.000 ljudi, medtem ko požar zahodno od Aten sili prebivalce, da ostanejo v zaprtih prostorih. To ni izjema, ampak nova evropska realnost.

Evropa je to pomlad podrla temperaturne rekorde. Samo junijski vročinski val je v Evropi zahteval že več kot 1.300 smrtnih žrtev. To je grozljiva statistika.

Znanost nam je to napovedala. Zdaj je čas za ukrepanje, ne za popuščanje podnebnim ambicijam.

Slovenija to razume, predvsem zaradi največjega požara iż leta 2022 ter zgodovinskih poplav iż leta 2023. V zadnjih petih letih smo temeljito reformirali sistem zaščite in reševanja. Z novo opremo, infrastrukturo in izobraženim kadrom. Toda enak temeljit preobrat potrebuje celotna Evropska unija. Brez evropske solidarnosti takrat nam v Sloveniji ne bi uspelo, in brez nje danes ne bo uspelo nikomur.

Zato pozivamo: za spopadanje z vročinskimi valovi potrebujemo celovito ukrepanje – od podnebno prilagojene gradnje in prenove stavb, okrepitve evropskega mehanizma civilne zaščite in RescEU do zavezujoče zaščite delavcev pred vročino ter predvsem odločnega zmanjšanja emisij, da omejimo nadaljnjo rast temperatur.

Solidarnost deluje. Zdaj jo moramo okrepiti.
3-0147-8750.englishText:
Today, Slovenia is under a high fire risk due to extreme heat. Meanwhile, France and Greece are already battling extensive forest fires—in the far south of France, around 10,000 people had to leave their homes, while a fire west of Athens is forcing residents to stay indoors. This is not an exception, but a new European reality.

Europe broke temperature records this spring. The June heatwave alone has already claimed more than 1,300 lives in Europe. This is a horrifying statistic.

Science predicted this for us. Now is the time for action, not for backing down on climate ambitions.

Slovenia understands this, primarily because of the largest fire in 2022 and the historic floods in 2023. Over the past five years, we have thoroughly reformed the protection and rescue system. With new equipment, infrastructure, and trained personnel. However, the entire European Union needs the same thorough overhaul. Without European solidarity back then, we in Slovenia would not have succeeded, and without it, no one will succeed today.

Therefore, we call: to combat heatwaves, we need comprehensive action—from climate-adapted construction and building renovation, the strengthening of the European Civil Protection Mechanism and RescEU, to binding protection of workers against heat and, above all, a decisive reduction in emissions to limit further temperature increases.

Solidarity works. Now we must strengthen it.

3-0147-9375.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, WHO:n arvioiden mukaan yli 200 000 ihmistä on kuollut Euroopassa viimeisen neljän vuoden aikana lämmöstä johtuvista syistä. Kesäkuun helleaalto oli ennätyksellisen raju. Vain yhden viikon aikana tuhansia ihmisiä menehtyi Euroopassa. Käynnissä oleva El Niño -ilmiö nostaa hetkellisesti maapallon keskilämpötilaa pahentaen tilannetta entisestään, ja vuodesta 2026 odotetaankin ennätyksellisen kuumaa. Voimme pitää kesän ennätyshelteitä esimakuna tulevaan.

Ilmastonmuutos kiihtyy, minkä seurauksena helleaallot ja maastopalot yleistyvät ja voimistuvat. Meidän on tehtävä kaikkemme, jotta välttäisimme ilmastonmuutoksen pahimmat seuraukset. On täysin eri asia, lämpeneekö maapallo kaksi astetta vai neljä. Paras ja kestävin vaihtoehto helleaaltoihin ja maastopaloihin varautumisessa on ilmastonmuutoksen hillitseminen. Mitä vähemmän meillä on helleaaltoja ja maastopaloja tulevaisuudessa, sitä harvemmin niihin tarvitsee reagoida. Siksi myös ilmasto- ja ympäristöpolitiikkamme kunnianhimon tasoa tulisi nostaa vastaamaan tieteellisiä tosiasioita. Nykyiset toimemme eivät yksiselitteisesti riitä.
3-0147-9375.englishText:
Mr President, according to WHO estimates, over 200,000 people have died in Europe over the past four years due to heat-related causes. The June heatwave was record-breaking in severity. In just one week, thousands of people died in Europe. The ongoing El Niño phenomenon is temporarily raising the average global temperature, worsening the situation further, and 2026 is expected to be a record-hot year. We can view this summer's record heatwaves as a foretaste of the future.

Climate change is accelerating, as a result of which heatwaves and wildfires are becoming more common and intense. We must do everything we can to avoid the worst consequences of climate change. It makes all the difference whether the planet warms by two degrees or four. The best and most sustainable option for preparing for heatwaves and wildfires is to mitigate climate change. The fewer heatwaves and wildfires we have in the future, the less frequently we will need to react to them. Therefore, the level of ambition in our climate and environmental policy should also be raised to match scientific facts. Our current actions are unequivocally insufficient.

Directly aggravated by the climate emergency, heatwaves are increasingly frequent, intense, and prolonged, causing thousands of deaths and creating the perfect conditions for wildfires to spread with unprecedented virulence. Our solidarity is with the victims and those affected by these phenomena.

Preparing for these threats involves anticipating, knowing, and preventing risks, understanding early warnings, and knowing how to act before and during an emergency. Regional and local authorities play an irreplaceable role in this area, as they best know the territory, vegetation, local climatic conditions, and the specific needs of their communities. Likewise, the activation of early warning systems and citizen education on evacuation and self-protection are competencies that can only be effectively exercised from proximity. Every euro invested in prevention saves up to six in response and recovery.

From the Government of Spain and the Union, resources will continue to be reinforced, including RescEU, in application of the new fire preparedness plans.

3-0147-9648.sourceText:
Los incendios y las olas de calor se han convertido en dos de las amenazas más destructivas y letales a las que se enfrenta Europa. Agravadas de manera directa por la emergencia climática, las olas de calor son cada vez más frecuentes, intensas y prolongadas, lo que provoca miles de muertes y crea las condiciones perfectas para que los incendios forestales se propaguen con una virulencia sin precedentes. Nuestra solidaridad está con las víctimas y con los afectados por estos fenómenos.

Prepararse ante estas amenazas implica anticipar, conocer y prevenir los riesgos, comprender las alertas tempranas y saber cómo actuar antes de una emergencia y durante esta. Las autoridades regionales y locales desempeñan un papel insustituible en este ámbito, pues son las que mejor conocen el territorio, la vegetación, las condiciones climáticas locales y las necesidades específicas de sus comunidades. Del mismo modo, la activación de sistemas de alerta temprana y la educación ciudadana sobre evacuación y autoprotección son competencias que solo pueden ejercerse de manera efectiva desde la proximidad. Cada euro invertido en prevención ahorra hasta seis en respuesta y recuperación.

Desde el Gobierno de España y la Unión, se seguirán reforzando los medios, incluido RescEU, en aplicación de los nuevos planes de preparación ante incendios.

3-0147-9687.sourceText:
Cada verano se repiten las mismas imágenes: columnas de humo, carreteras cortadas, vecinos pendientes del viento y bomberos al límite. Pero los incendios no empiezan cuando aparecen las llamas; empiezan mucho antes, cuando se abandona el monte, se cierran caminos, se acumula maleza y desaparecen el pastoreo y la actividad rural.

Asturias, mi región, lo sabe bien. El pasado verano ardieron más de 6 000 hectáreas. No perdimos solo vegetación: perdimos paisaje, explotaciones, memoria y futuro para nuestros pueblos.

Europa ha reforzado sus medios de emergencia, su coordinación y su capacidad de respuesta. Esa solidaridad es imprescindible, pero no podemos limitarnos a actuar cuando todo está ardiendo. La Unión debe seguir apoyando la vigilancia, la gestión forestal, los caminos, los puntos de agua y la cooperación entre administraciones.

Pero Europa no puede sustituir la responsabilidad de los Estados miembros, quienes deben convertir los fondos europeos en actuaciones concretas sobre el terreno. Y España no ha aprovechado suficientemente estos recursos.

La prevención quizá no ofrezca grandes fotografías, pero salva viviendas, empleos, hectáreas y vidas. Los recursos existen; lo que falta es voluntad política y capacidad de gestión para actuar durante el invierno y la primavera, antes de volver a lamentar en verano lo que no se hizo a tiempo.
3-0147-9687.englishText:
Every summer the same images are repeated: columns of smoke, blocked roads, residents watching the wind and firefighters pushed to the limit. But fires do not start when the flames appear; they start much earlier, when the countryside is abandoned, paths are closed, undergrowth accumulates and grazing and rural activity disappear.

Asturias, my region, knows this well. Last summer more than 6,000 hectares burned. We did not only lose vegetation: we lost landscape, farms, memory and a future for our villages.

Europe has reinforced its emergency resources, coordination and response capacity. That solidarity is essential, but we cannot limit ourselves to acting when everything is burning. The Union must continue supporting surveillance, forest management, paths, water points and cooperation between administrations.

But Europe cannot replace the responsibility of Member States, which must turn European funds into concrete actions on the ground. And Spain has not made sufficient use of these resources.

Prevention may not offer great photographs, but it saves homes, jobs, hectares and lives. The resources exist; what is lacking is political will and management capacity to act during winter and spring, before regretting in summer what was not done in time.

3-0158-0000.sourceText: The first vote is on the objection pursuant to Rule 114(3): Trajectory to decrease the contribution of high indirect land-use change-risk biofuels, bioliquids and biomass fuels to renewable energy targets (see minutes, item 10.1).

3-0160-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, I would like to encourage honourable Members to support the Commission Delegated Act on indirect land-use change and to vote against the tabled objection.

In the latest review, it was found that both palm oil and soy beans qualify as feedstock with a high risk of indirect land-use change and therefore the Commission was obliged to revise the delegated act accordingly. This Delegated Act is supported by robust scientific analysis and latest available data and is legally required by the legislative framework agreed by the co-legislators.

Updating the scientific data to determine which feedstocks are classified as high risk is also needed for the EU to comply with the findings in two WTO dispute settlement cases, and the WTO. Should the Delegated Act be blocked, then the EU risks being subject to substantial sanctions, which could target our agricultural exporters.

It is important to underline that the categorisation of soy beans as high-ILUC risk feedstock does not represent a ban. Member States are still free to promote and support biofuels, including from soy beans, as they consider most appropriate. Only the amount of fuels that is counted towards the targets in the Renewable Energy Directive is gradually reduced until 2030.

I would also like to stress that only a small share of biodiesel consumed in the EU is produced from soybeans and the vast majority of it is grown in third countries. Therefore, although some operators in the EU may need to adapt, the economic impact of classifying soya as high ILUC on EU producers and crushing industry should remain limited because the EU livestock sector continues to rely on soyabean and there are alternative outlets for soya oil, including food, feed and industrial uses. Strong global demand and high soyabean oil prices, together with possible lower EU imports and export opportunities, should further help limit negative effects on suppliers and the soya industry.

Independently from that, work is currently ongoing on ways to review the low ILUC-risk certification procedure, so that producers of soy beans that receive such certification will be exempted from the categorisation of a feedstock as high-ILUC risk, and we will further assess in setting-up the renewable energy framework for the decade ahead how we can further support domestic biofuel production as well as the farming sector.

3-0176-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, stiamo procedendo a un voto che rappresenta un allineamento tecnico per la partecipazione del Marocco a PRIMA, Partenariato per la ricerca e l'innovazione nell'area del Mediterraneo, con focus su acqua, agricoltura e sicurezza alimentare.

Questo voto ne garantirà la continuità fino al 2031, senza implicazioni di bilancio.

Io ne approfitto anche per ringraziare i colleghi della commissione ITRE, che hanno votato il provvedimento in commissione quasi all'unanimità.

Ciò premesso, però, vorrei ampliare la riflessione al tema dell'agricoltura, visto che non possiamo guardare a un accordo con il Marocco senza estendere la nostra visione a un quadro più ampio delle relazioni, in particolar modo sul fronte agricolo.

Solo negli ultimi due mesi del 2025 il Marocco ha coperto oltre il 70 % delle importazioni extra‑UE per quanto riguarda il pomodoro, un flusso che negli ultimi vent'anni è quadruplicato.

Per cui, questa relazione vorrebbe anche aprire una riflessione sul tema che la Commissione dovrebbe monitorare l'attuazione di queste tipologie di accordi, anche quelli riferiti alla ricerca e all'innovazione, con particolare attenzione alle importazioni agricole, affinché siano rispettati i principi di reciprocità e concorrenza leale.
3-0176-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, we are proceeding with a vote that represents a technical alignment for Morocco's participation in PRIMA, the Partnership for Research and Innovation in the Mediterranean Area, with a focus on water, agriculture, and food security.

This vote will guarantee its continuity until 2031, with no budgetary implications.

I also take this opportunity to thank my colleagues on the ITRE Committee, who voted for the measure in committee almost unanimously.

That being said, however, I would like to broaden the reflection to the topic of agriculture, given that we cannot look at an agreement with Morocco without extending our vision to a broader framework of relations, particularly on the agricultural front.

In the last two months of 2025 alone, Morocco covered over 70% of extra-EU imports regarding tomatoes, a flow that has quadrupled over the last twenty years.

Therefore, this report would also like to open a reflection on the issue that the Commission should monitor the implementation of these types of agreements, even those referring to research and innovation, with particular attention to agricultural imports, so that the principles of reciprocity and fair competition are respected.

3-0180-0000.sourceText: Panie Przewodniczący! Proponujemy poprawkę w następującym brzmieniu (przeczytam ją w tej chwili): „Parlament Europejski upomina się o pamięć 100 tys. bestialsko pomordowanych w rzezi wołyńskiej Polaków i Żydów; zdecydowanie nie akceptuje kultu bandytów z Ukraińskiej Powstańczej Armii i Stefana Bandery, którzy odpowiadają za ludobójstwo i współpracę z Hitlerem; wzywa władze Ukrainy do natychmiastowego zaprzestania ich państwowego upamiętniania oraz gloryfikacji; kultywowanie pamięci o ludobójcach jest sprzeczne z moralnością i wartościami europejskimi; dlatego wzywamy władze Ukrainy do jednoznacznego odrzucenia gloryfikacji osób odpowiedzialnych za ludobójstwo; podkreśla, że ideologia banderowska jest lustrzanym odbiciem ideologii nazistowskiej i – tak jak nazizm – banderyzm musi zostać uznany za ideologię zakazaną w Unii Europejskiej”.
3-0180-0000.englishText: Mr President! We propose an amendment in the following wording (I will read it right now): "The European Parliament demands memory for the 100,000 brutally murdered Poles and Jews in the Volhynian slaughter; firmly rejects the cult of bandits from the Ukrainian Insurgent Army and Stepan Bandera, who are responsible for genocide and cooperation with Hitler; calls on the Ukrainian authorities to immediately cease their state commemoration and glorification; cultivating the memory of genocide perpetrators is contrary to morality and European values; therefore, we call on the Ukrainian authorities to unequivocally reject the glorification of persons responsible for genocide; emphasizes that Banderite ideology is a mirror image of Nazi ideology and - like Nazism - Banderism must be recognized as a banned ideology in the European Union."

3-0183-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, la perspective de l’adhésion de l’Ukraine à l’Union européenne constituerait une menace majeure pour l’agriculture de nos nations. Nos agriculteurs en subissent déjà les conséquences depuis 2022. La libéralisation des importations agricoles ukrainiennes, que seul le groupe des Patriotes a combattu dès le départ, a entraîné l’arrivée massive de sucre, de céréales et de volailles sur le marché européen, au détriment du revenu de nos producteurs.

Pourtant, la Commission veut aller plus loin. Dans sa nouvelle stratégie sur les protéines végétales présentée hier, elle confirme son renoncement à l’ambition de voir l’agriculture européenne satisfaire nos besoins en protéines végétales, pour aggraver les importations depuis l’Ukraine.

Je propose donc l’amendement suivant pour créer un nouveau paragraphe 32: «souligne que la Commission, dans sa dernière stratégie en matière de protéines, propose de s’appuyer sur la capacité de production agricole de l’Ukraine pour remédier à la pénurie de protéines végétales dans l’Union, au lieu de privilégier le développement de la production européenne».
3-0183-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the prospect of Ukraine's accession to the European Union would constitute a major threat to our nations' agriculture. Our farmers have already been suffering the consequences since 2022. The liberalization of Ukrainian agricultural imports, which only the Patriots group fought against from the very start, has led to the massive influx of sugar, cereals, and poultry onto the European market, to the detriment of our producers' incomes.

Yet the Commission wants to go further. In its new vegetable protein strategy presented yesterday, it confirms its abandonment of the ambition to see European agriculture satisfy our needs for vegetable protein, in order to worsen imports from Ukraine.

I therefore propose the following amendment to create a new paragraph 32: "stresses that the Commission, in its latest protein strategy, proposes to rely on Ukraine's agricultural production capacity to remedy the shortage of vegetable protein in the Union, instead of favoring the development of European production".

3-0186-0000.sourceText:

3-0189-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, I would like to draw your attention to some of the chants that were uttered here from that side of the Chamber, when somebody dared to stand in opposition to one of the oral amendments. People – colleagues – were called Nazis just because they dared to have a different position on something, which is very sensitive, but we do not share the style of calling each other Nazis. Some of the real Nazis...

(Protests)

Some of the real Nazis who are present in this Chamber are never called as such during the sessions here. I have never heard anyone call each other that. I would like to ask you to identify and to sanction those who are attacking their colleagues just for their opinion here, who dare to oppose that amendment.

3-0200-0000.englishText:
