3-0221-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, μπορεί η επίσημη κατάπαυση του πυρός στη Γάζα να συμφωνήθηκε τον περασμένο Οκτώβριο, όμως στην πραγματικότητα ο πόλεμος συνεχίζεται ακόμη και σήμερα. Τα χτυπήματα δεν σταμάτησαν ποτέ. Η ανθρωπιστική πρόσβαση συνεχίζει να γίνεται μετ' εμποδίων και η πλειοψηφία των κατοίκων της παραμένει εκτοπισμένη. Την ίδια στιγμή, η κατάσταση στη Δυτική Όχθη επιδεινώνεται. Το 2026 η βία των εποίκων έφτασε σε πρωτοφανή επίπεδα. Νέοι παράνομοι εποικισμοί, καταστροφές και κατασχέσεις σε περιουσίες χριστιανών και Αράβων, ακόμα και εντός του διαδρόμου Ε1.

Όλα αυτά τα μέτρα εδραιώνουν μια de facto προσάρτηση με μόνο στόχο να μπλοκάρουν κάθε βιώσιμη προοπτική για τη λύση των δύο κρατών. Για τον λόγο αυτό, ζητήσαμε ως ομάδα των Σοσιαλιστών και Δημοκρατών τη σημερινή επίκαιρη συζήτηση στην Ολομέλεια, αφού ήταν ο μόνος τρόπος να το θέσουμε ξανά, γιατί η Ευρώπη δεν μπορεί να παραμένει άλλο θεατής στις παραβιάσεις του διεθνούς και ανθρωπιστικού δικαίου. Δεν μπορούμε να θέλουμε να εμφανιζόμαστε ως οι υπερασπιστές της διεθνούς έννομης τάξης και την ίδια στιγμή το Συμβούλιο Υπουργών Εξωτερικών να μην μπορεί να αναγνωρίσει την πραγματικότητα, ότι δηλαδή παραβιάζεται το άρθρο 2 της Συμφωνίας Σύνδεσης, και να λάβει τις απαραίτητες στοχευμένες κυρώσεις κατά των εποίκων αλλά και κατά των ακροδεξιών υπουργών της κυβέρνησης Νετανιάχου. Δεν μπορούμε από τη μια να υπερασπιζόμαστε τα Ηνωμένα Έθνη και από την άλλη να συμμετέχει η Επιτροπή, έστω και ως παρατηρητής, στο Συμβούλιο Ειρήνης του προέδρου Τραμπ.

Σας το είπαμε, κυρία Επίτροπε: Ήταν λάθος σας που πήγατε, τόσο δικό σας όσο και της Προέδρου της Επιτροπής, που σας το ζήτησε. Δεν είχατε καμία εξουσιοδότηση για να συμμετάσχετε. Όπως επίσης ήταν πολύ λανθασμένη και η πρόσφατη επίσκεψή σας στο Ισραήλ. Δεν είχε τη σαφήνεια ούτε την απαραίτητη αυστηρότητα απέναντι στην κυβέρνηση Νετανιάχου και έγινε σε μια πολύ λάθος στιγμή, όταν η ισραηλινή κυβέρνηση επιτέθηκε στην Ύπατη Εκπρόσωπο. Μόνο και μόνο γι' αυτό, η επίσκεψη έπρεπε να έχει ακυρωθεί. Όταν ο θεσμικός μας εκπρόσωπος δέχεται επιθέσεις, η σιωπή δεν είναι ουδετερότητα, είναι υποχώρηση.

Κυρία Επίτροπε, το ζήτημα της ανασυγκρότησης της Γάζας και η διασφάλιση των προϋποθέσεων για ένα βιώσιμο παλαιστινιακό κράτος είναι πολύ σοβαρό ζήτημα, για να το αφήσουμε σε έναν ιδιωτικό μηχανισμό εκτός του διεθνούς πλαισίου. Ζητούμε έναν μηχανισμό ανασυγκρότησης της Γάζας με κεντρικό ρόλο των Ηνωμένων Εθνών, συμπεριλαμβανομένης της UNRWA, όπου τον κύριο λόγο θα τον έχουν οι Παλαιστίνιοι. Μόνο έτσι θα είναι επιτυχής. Η Ευρώπη πρέπει να είναι όχι μόνο παρούσα αλλά η κινητήριος δύναμη. Δεν αρκεί πια να είμαστε απλώς ο μεγαλύτερος χορηγός ανθρωπιστικής βοήθειας στην περιοχή. Θα πρέπει να έχουμε και την αντίστοιχη επιρροή και συμμετοχή. Δεν θα αποφασίζει κάποιος άλλος και εμείς απλώς θα πληρώνουμε.

Για τον λόγο αυτό, επαναλαμβάνω το αίτημά μας για μια φιλόδοξη, ολοκληρωμένη και συνεκτική στρατηγική για τη Μέση Ανατολή, που θα αντιστοιχεί στο μέγεθος της πρόκλησης, χωρίς διπλά μέτρα και σταθμά, με σαφή φωνή και με πολιτική βούληση. Μας το υποσχέθηκε η Πρόεδρος πριν από δύο χρόνια και ακόμα δεν έχει ξεκινήσει καν η προεργασία.
3-0221-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the official ceasefire in Gaza may have been agreed last October, but in reality the war is still continuing today. The strikes never stopped. Humanitarian access continues to face obstacles and the majority of its inhabitants remain displaced. At the same time, the situation in the West Bank is worsening. In 2026, settler violence reached unprecedented levels. New illegal settlements, destructions and seizures of property belonging to Christians and Arabs, even within the E1 corridor.

All these measures consolidate a de facto annexation with the sole aim of blocking any viable prospect for the two-state solution. For this reason, as the Socialists and Democrats group, we requested today's timely debate in plenary, as it was the only way to raise it again, because Europe cannot remain a spectator any longer to violations of international and humanitarian law. We cannot want to appear as the defenders of the international legal order while at the same time the Council of Foreign Ministers is unable to recognise reality—namely that Article 2 of the Association Agreement is being violated—and to adopt the necessary targeted sanctions against settlers and against far-right ministers of Netanyahu's government. We cannot defend the United Nations on the one hand and on the other have the Commission participate, even as an observer, in President Trump's Peace Council.

We told you, Commissioner: It was a mistake for you to go, both yours and the Commission President's who asked you to. You had no mandate to participate. Likewise, your recent visit to Israel was also very misguided. It lacked clarity and the necessary firmness towards the Netanyahu government and took place at a very wrong moment, when the Israeli government attacked the High Representative. For that reason alone, the visit should have been cancelled. When our institutional representative is attacked, silence is not neutrality, it is retreat.

Commissioner, the issue of Gaza's reconstruction and securing the conditions for a viable Palestinian state is too serious an issue to be left to a private mechanism outside the international framework. We call for a Gaza reconstruction mechanism with a central role for the United Nations, including UNRWA, where Palestinians will have the primary say. Only in this way will it be successful. Europe must not only be present, but be the driving force. It is no longer enough to simply be the largest donor of humanitarian aid in the region. We must also have the corresponding influence and participation. Someone else will not decide while we simply pay.

For this reason, I reiterate our request for an ambitious, comprehensive and coherent strategy for the Middle East that corresponds to the scale of the challenge, without double standards, with a clear voice and with political will. The President promised it to us two years ago and preliminary work has not even started yet.

3-0222-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, MEP Maniatis, honourable and distinguished Members, Commissioner Šuica, thank you for organising this debate on a topic that unfortunately is a recurring one for both Parliament and the Council.

Let me stress that the Irish Presidency will do its utmost to support efforts on all European Union work strands concerning the Middle East. Concerning Gaza, the European Council continues to express concerns about the lack of progress in the implementation of the ceasefire and other provisions of UN Security Council Resolution 2803. It called on all actors to fully implement the resolution, including the permanent disarmament of the terrorist Hamas group and other non-state armed groups, and the full withdrawal of Israeli soldiers from the Gaza Strip.

We remain gravely concerned over the persistent and devastating humanitarian crisis in Gaza. Israel must allow immediate, unimpeded access and sustained distribution of humanitarian assistance at scale into and throughout Gaza. When it comes to providing support for the reconstruction and development of Gaza in line with international law, the role of international and regional stakeholders is crucial. This is why the European Union is engaging with all partners to contribute to recovery and reconstruction efforts.

Next week, on 13 July, the European Union will host the next ministerial meeting of the Palestine Donor Group in Brussels, co-chaired by the Commission and the Palestinian Authority. The European Union will also continue to support the Palestinian Authority in implementing its reform programme so that it can securely and effectively take back control of Gaza and be fully involved in its reconstruction.

Israel must also do its part to ensure the proper functioning of the Palestinian Authority. This includes the release of withheld tax revenues so that it can deliver essential services to the population. In terms of accountability, the European Union has consistently urged the Government of Israel to abide by its obligations under international law and to protect the Palestinian population of the occupied territories.

Independent and impartial investigations and prosecution of crimes are essential to achieve justice. In May 2025, the Foreign Affairs Council agreed to a review of Israel's compliance with its human rights obligations under Article 2 of the EU‑Israel Association Agreement. It is clear from the finalised review that Israel is in breach of its human rights obligations.

Faced with continuing and growing settler violence against Palestinian civilians, which the EU strongly condemns, on 28 May the Council adopted additional restrictive measures against extremist Israeli settlers and organisations which support them under the EU global human rights sanctions regime. When the Foreign Affairs Council returns to the matter next week, ministers expect to have a discussion of options for measures related to illegal settlements, presented by the Commission.

3-0223-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for the opportunity to discuss this crucial issue. The persistent crisis in Gaza and in Palestine more broadly obliged us to act. During my recent visit to Ramallah, I met Palestinian Vice-President al-Sheikh and Prime Minister Mustafa. The Palestinian Authority finances were under pressure, which affected the banking sector and access to finance of the private sector.

I see some positive further steps from the Israeli side. As you know, the corresponding banking arrangements have lately been extended every two weeks. This morning, we were informed that these arrangements have been extended until the end of 2026, which is another positive sign.

Basic services such as healthcare are challenged. Rising settler violence is straining all this further. During my visit to Israel, I underlined that our partnership requires a continued open and frank dialogue. Both President Herzog and Foreign Minister Sa'ar agreed and reiterated the importance of EU-Israeli relations. We need to engage with all parties. It is important that they engage with all European interlocutors as well.

Supporting a reformed Palestinian Authority and continuing to engage with Israel are not mutually exclusive. Without a buy-in from both sides, we will not be able to deliver on our objectives; early recovery in Gaza and the financial stability of a reformed Palestinian Authority. As I spoke to Israeli Foreign Minister Sa'ar, I told him the European Union remains strong in our support of a viable Palestinian state. There can be no just and lasting peace without it. I insisted on our collective interest in avoiding backsliding on the implementation of the Gaza peace plan, in line with the implementation of UN Secretary resolution 2803.

Early recovery in Gaza must start now, together with much more humanitarian assistance to meet the basic needs of civilians. We achieved an important step – Minister Sa'ar is open – or was open, has been open – for the European Union and its partners to initiate two critical early recovery interventions, one on solid waste management and another on water and sanitation.

This paves the way for the Palestinian donor group next week, on Monday 13 July, which I will co-chair with Prime Minister Mustafa. We are planning to bring together more than 65 delegations. We will be informed about the reform progress of the Palestinian Authority. We will also launch the Team Gaza initiative – the European Union, together with like-minded partners for early recovery in Gaza.

It is true – the situation is dire, but we are achieving real, concrete results with our diplomatic work.

3-0224-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, thank you very much, Mr Maniatis, I understand that you are pressed by the leadership of the socialist group – the Spanish leadership – to talk about this now. But what I don't understand – because, you know, there are some problems in Spain and the government, and this classic debate appears always out of the blue when there are problems in Spain – but what I can't understand is that in your speech, you did not mention Hamas, Hezbollah, Iran, Türkiye. Again, double standards. I would love to talk about the reconstruction of Gaza, please. This is what I want to talk about! But now, all the interventions will be about who is against and who is in favour, you know, instead of talking about Gaza's reconstruction. Sorry for that. This is a spoiled debate, already from the start.

I wish for accountability for everybody, for terrorists and for the massacred also. And also democracies, because they have courts of law. They have judges. I am sure there will be also investigations and prosecutions. And we will be a European state, the example of the Commissioner, she just spoke, she was there. She talked with everybody. That is the European way of doing things: talking and listening to everybody, not only to one side. Please, everybody.

Let's try for once – for once – not to be seen to be taking one or the other side. Accountability is for everybody. That's what Europe has to do. And these kind of debates – again, where some of you will speak about one side, the others will speak about the other – are not going to solve any of the problems of the region. I think that we have to take seriously, for once in this Parliament, these kind of debates and that we really have these European solutions, these pragmatic solutions. Thank you very much for that, Commissioner. I think it was very welcome, your visit and the results. Let's hope that all of us will make a little effort not to be biased for once, and to talk about the real reconstruction of Gaza and the humanitarian help that this European Union has to provide. I am on board. I am on board. Thank you very much.

3-0225-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, Hamás, Hezbolá, etcétera. Lo mencionamos, pero vamos al tema de hoy, que es la responsabilidad de Israel.

Comisaria Šuica, usted me dijo en algunas ocasiones: ¿habrá dinero para la reconstrucción? Hay distintas partidas de las que sacar dinero. Yo creo que crear un mecanismo para Gaza da visibilidad externa a nuestro compromiso. Por tanto, le ruego que reexamine la posibilidad de, en vez de tomar dinero de varias partidas, crear este mecanismo que nuestro Grupo le está pidiendo.

Vamos a acabar con los dobles estándares. Estamos hablando todo el día de la responsabilidad de Rusia en la reconstrucción de Ucrania. ¿Por qué es tan difícil hablar de la responsabilidad de Israel en la reconstrucción de Gaza? ¿No es la misma violación del Derecho internacional a la que hemos asistido? Por tanto, hay que exigirle a Israel lo mismo que le exigimos a Rusia.

Comisaria, yo no la culpo a usted. A usted la han enviado a la Junta de Paz. La señora Von der Leyen la ha enviado a saludar a ministros genocidas. Yo entiendo que ustedes son un equipo. Por favor, comisaria, cuando tenga que saludar a esos ministros, muestre alguna incomodidad por estar en ese papel.
3-0225-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Hamas, Hezbollah, and so on. We mention it, but let us move on to today's topic, which is Israel's responsibility.

Commissioner Šuica, you told me on a few occasions: will there be money for reconstruction? There are different budget lines to draw money from. I believe that creating a mechanism for Gaza gives external visibility to our commitment. Therefore, I beg you to re-examine the possibility of, instead of taking money from various budget lines, creating this mechanism that our Group is asking you for.

Let us put an end to double standards. We are talking all day about Russia's responsibility in the reconstruction of Ukraine. Why is it so difficult to talk about Israel's responsibility in the reconstruction of Gaza? Is it not the same violation of international law that we have witnessed? Therefore, Israel must be demanded the same things that we demand of Russia.

Commissioner, I do not blame you. You have been sent to the Peace Board. Ms Von der Leyen has sent you to greet genocidal ministers. I understand that you are a team. Please, Commissioner, when you have to greet those ministers, show some discomfort at being in that role.

3-0226-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, meine sehr geehrten Damen und Herren! Halten wir fest, dass Israel die einzige Demokratie im Nahen Osten ist. Halten wir ferner fest – auch wenn Sie lachen –, dass Israel umgeben ist von einer halben Milliarde Muslimen, wo sehr viel an Bedrohung gegeben ist. Halten wir ferner fest, dass an diesem 7. Oktober 2023 der brutalste Anschlag überhaupt stattgefunden hat auf Israel, mit über 1 200 Toten, wo Zivilisten missbraucht wurden als lebende Schilde. Ich weiß schon, dass Sie gern lachen, das ist aber Faktum. Halten wir ferner fest, dass wir wissen, dass die Europäische Union über UNRWA Mittel in den Gazastreifen gepumpt hat und dass diese Gelder aber in den Terrorküchen der Hamas gelandet sind. Das ist der falsche Weg.

Leute wie der israelische Außenminister Gideon Sa'ar und auch die Amerikaner haben recht: Diese Terrororganisationen sind endlich zu entwaffnen. Es hat eine Demilitarisierung dieser Region stattzufinden, und erst dann, und nachdem sichergestellt wird, dass Israel sein Recht auf Existenz und Verteidigung behält, kann man über entsprechende Hilfen reden.
3-0226-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen! Let us note that Israel is the only democracy in the Middle East. Let us also note – even if you laugh – that Israel is surrounded by half a billion Muslims, where there is a great deal of threat. Let us also note that on this 7th of October 2023, the most brutal attack ever took place against Israel, with over 1,200 dead, where civilians were used as human shields. I know that you like to laugh, but that is a fact. Let us also note that we know the European Union has pumped funds into the Gaza Strip via UNRWA and that these funds ended up in Hamas's terror kitchens. That is the wrong path.

People like Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar and also the Americans are right: these terrorist organizations must finally be disarmed. A demilitarization of this region must take place, and only then, and after it is ensured that Israel retains its right to existence and defense, can one talk about corresponding aid.

3-0227-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, oggi la comunità internazionale è chiamata ad affrontare due sfide inseparabili.

La prima è garantire un'assistenza umanitaria immediata alla popolazione civile, la seconda è fare in modo che il 7 ottobre resti confinato alla storia e non torni mai più a segnare il futuro del Medio Oriente.

La prima impone di assicurare un accesso umanitario pieno, sicuro e senza ostacoli, affinché gli aiuti raggiungano rapidamente chi ne ha bisogno, senza essere intercettati o strumentalizzati da organizzazioni terroristiche.

La seconda richiede una visione politica di lungo periodo. La ricostruzione di Gaza dovrà accompagnarsi allo smantellamento delle reti terroristiche e ogni forma di estremismo che ha alimentato l'odio e la violenza.

L'Europa deve guidare questo processo mobilitando gli strumenti già disponibili per ricostruire ospedali, scuole e infrastrutture essenziali e creare le condizioni per una crescita economica e duratura, perché dalla stabilità di Gaza passa anche la stabilità del Mediterraneo, e dalla stabilità del Mediterraneo passa una parte decisiva della sicurezza e della prosperità dell'Europa.
3-0227-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, today the international community is called upon to face two inseparable challenges.

The first is to guarantee immediate humanitarian assistance to the civilian population, the second is to ensure that October 7 remains confined to history and never again marks the future of the Middle East.

The first requires ensuring full, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, so that aid quickly reaches those who need it, without being intercepted or exploited by terrorist organisations.

The second requires a long-term political vision. The reconstruction of Gaza must be accompanied by the dismantling of terrorist networks and every form of extremism that has fueled hatred and violence.

Europe must lead this process by mobilizing the tools already available to rebuild hospitals, schools and essential infrastructure and create the conditions for lasting economic growth, because the stability of the Mediterranean also passes through the stability of Gaza, and a decisive part of Europe's security and prosperity passes through the stability of the Mediterranean.

3-0228-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, the world spends more on weapons in one single day than it spends on tackling sexual violence as a weapon of war in an entire year. For the first time, the UN has listed Israeli forces among the parties suspected of conflict‑related sexual violence. At the same time, the UN has recorded, colleagues, the highest number of grave violations against children ever verified. More than 2 700 Palestinian children have been killed.

When we ask for justice, we are told this conflict is a difficult issue. Yes, for many Member States, it is. But that cannot be an excuse for silence. Europe must defend international law every time, everywhere. I repeat my goal for a ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements. Europe, it is time to act.

3-0229-0000.sourceText:
Hr. formand! Temaet for debatten i dag er genopbygning af Gaza, og jeg siger det til oplysning for højrefløjen, som gerne vil diskutere alt muligt andet. Men endnu vigtigere: respekten for menneskeliv og menneskeværd skal genoprettes.

Mere end 70 000 mennesker bekræftes døde. Intet her i verden – heller ikke Hamas' forfærdelige terrorangreb – berettiger drab på mange uskyldige mennesker og fastholdelse af mere end 2 millioner mennesker i en katastrofal situation.

Mange tusinder ligger gemt – men ikke glemt – under ruinerne. De oplever nu at leve i kaos, affald, forurenet vand og skadedyr. EU og EU's medlemslande ved godt, hvad der sker. Vi ved godt, hvad der sker, ikke alene her, men også på Vestbredden. Selv uden adgang til internationale journalister ved vi, hvad der sker.

Vi taler om frihed, om fred. Vi taler om respekt og retfærdighed. Men vi handler stadig med ulovlige bosættelser. Vi har stadig en associeringsaftale, der endda har menneskerettigheder skrevet ind som forudsætning.

Vores handlingslammelse er en moralsk skamplet.
3-0229-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! The theme of the debate today is the reconstruction of Gaza, and I say this for the information of the right wing, which would rather discuss all sorts of other things. But even more importantly: respect for human life and human dignity must be restored.

More than 70,000 people are confirmed dead. Nothing in this world—not even Hamas's horrific terror attack—justifies the killing of many innocent people and the keeping of more than 2 million people in a catastrophic situation.

Many thousands lie hidden—but not forgotten—under the rubble. They are now experiencing living in chaos, garbage, polluted water, and pests. The EU and the EU member states know well what is happening. We know well what is happening, not only here, but also in the West Bank. Even without access to international journalists, we know what is happening.

We talk about freedom, about peace. We talk about respect and justice. But we still trade with illegal settlements. We still have an association agreement that even has human rights written in as a precondition.

Our paralysis is a moral stain.

3-0230-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, the people of Gaza have now suffered more than 1 000 days of genocide, 1 000 days of mass murder, starvation and an international community that's too cowardly to hold Israel accountable. The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestine Territory has found that Israel continues to commit genocide and deliberately targets Palestinian children in Gaza and the West Bank.

This is the rogue State that, according to the European Commission, is a close ally – this rogue State! We stand here and we talk about reconstruction and pretend that the genocide is over, when it continues. We need sanctions, a two-way arms embargo, suspension of the association agreement, a ban on trade with the illegal settlements and full, unequivocal support for UNWRA.

Before we even talk about reconstruction in Gaza, how about we talk about the fact that Israel has destroyed at least EUR 150 million of EU-funded infrastructure, and has not paid back a single cent? When is the Commission going to recover our taxpayers' money? When are they going to release the documents that relate to the destruction of EU-funded infrastructure in Gaza? Because the public has a right to know how much Israel is costing them.

Finally, the EU must urgently act to secure the immediate release of Doctor Hussam Abu Safiya, who has been arbitrarily detained by Israel since December 2024. He has been beaten, he has been tortured, he is at risk of death – free Doctor Hussam Abu Safiya!

3-0231-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, Europe has been engaged for decades in providing humanitarian aid and basic social services to the people of Gaza. Recent initiatives by Commissioner Šuica, including the convening of donor conferences, demonstrate Europe's continued strong commitment, even at a time when equally devastating humanitarian catastrophes in Sudan, Yemen and Afghanistan demand our attention.

But reconstruction cannot simply mean rebuilding buildings. It must mean building a future in which Hamas can never again use civilian infrastructure as a base for terror, store weapons in schools or hospitals, or divert international assistance for its own extremist Islamist purposes. The reality is that Hamas has never respected and never will respect international law. On the contrary, its ideology is built on a cult of death and martyrdom in which individual human lives are meaningless, and the highest civilian death toll is cynically exploited to preserve its grip on power.

For us Europeans and for our partner Israel, international law matters because we have committed ourselves to it. But it is also clear that international law alone does not always provide solutions when dealing with terrorist organisations or violent and oppressive regimes. This is why we must urgently advance the implementation of the political process laid down in UN Security Council Resolution 2803.

Hamas announcing its withdrawal from Gaza's civil administration opens a critical window. The apolitical, technocratic National Committee for the Administration of Gaza can assume its responsibilities. The EU police training mission can help restore public order and improve security for civilians. And the CMCC is fully operational to coordinate stabilisation and relief efforts.

3-0232-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, while Israel continues with oppression and occupation, generations of Palestinians are paying the price. Yet every time until now, our European Union has failed to act properly.

Too many in this House, especially in the centre-right and the far-right side, chose to see nothing, hear nothing and say nothing. And you play the fourth monkey, through crossing your arms and thinking that you are not doing any evil. Let me be clear: inaction is action, and that choice has consequences. You even attack vital organisations such as UNRWA with baseless allegations, making yourself Netanyahu's and Hamas's useful idiots.

The EU does not suffer from a lack of solutions; the EU suffers from a lack of political courage. What more should Israel do for enough to be enough? Should it commit the genocide? Let me remind you: it has already done that. Can we start acting now and suspend the EU-Israel Association Agreement?

Commissioner, with all due respect, I don't know what steps you mean the Israeli Government has taken. The only steps I have seen until now are steps into other countries.

3-0233-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señorías, el título de este debate, para empezar, es tramposo: juzga la responsabilidad de Israel y omite la del culpable. Todo debate serio exige partir de la verdad y aquí algunos grupos se han instalado en la mentira deliberada.

Tres hechos se obvian una y otra vez. Primero, si hablamos de reconstruir Gaza es porque Hamás decidió destruirla. El 7 de octubre de 2023, una organización terrorista asesinó a más de 1 200 personas, el mayor asesinato de judíos desde el Holocausto. Y quien omite esta responsabilidad no busca la paz, sino una coartada.

Segundo, la Comisión Europea y algunos Estados miembros —con el Gobierno corrupto socialista español a la cabeza— siguen financiando al UNRWA, cuyos empleados estuvieron implicados en la masacre.

Tercero, el artículo 51 de la Carta de las Naciones Unidas reconoce a todo Estado el derecho inmanente a la legítima defensa. A todo Estado, también a Israel.

Por eso, exigimos la suspensión inmediata de toda financiación al UNRWA y que no se desembolse ni un solo euro...

(el presidente retira la palabra al orador)
3-0233-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, honourable members, the title of this debate, to begin with, is deceitful: it judges Israel's responsibility and omits that of the culprit. Any serious debate requires starting from the truth and here some groups have installed themselves in deliberate lies.

Three facts are ignored over and over again. First, if we talk about rebuilding Gaza, it is because Hamas decided to destroy it. On October 7, 2023, a terrorist organization murdered more than 1,200 people, the largest murder of Jews since the Holocaust. And whoever omits this responsibility is not looking for peace, but an alibi.

Second, the European Commission and some Member States —headed by the corrupt Spanish socialist Government— continue to finance UNRWA, whose employees were involved in the massacre.

Third, Article 51 of the United Nations Charter recognizes the inherent right of every State to self-defense. To every State, including Israel.

For this reason, we demand the immediate suspension of all funding to UNRWA and that not a single euro be disbursed...

(the president withdraws the floor from the speaker)

3-0234-0000.sourceText: Voorzitter, als het ergens moeilijk is om perspectief te zien, dan is het wel in Gaza. Twee miljoen Palestijnen leven onder erbarmelijke omstandigheden, in een volstrekt uitzichtloze situatie. Allemaal de schuld van Israël, zeggen velen, maar dat is natuurlijk niet zo. Zeker, Israël moet zich maximaal inspannen om de humanitaire hulp bij de getroffen bevolking te krijgen. Maar we kunnen Israël toch onmogelijk verwijten dat ze probeert Hamas onder controle te krijgen? Dat brengt ons bij de kern van het probleem: de weigering van Hamas om de wapens neer te leggen. Hoe kan de EU dan helpen bij de wederopbouw? Ik zou willen zeggen: laten we ons daarbij concentreren op Hamasvrije gebieden. Zorg er in ieder geval voor dat er geen euro in handen komt van Hamas, want zolang deze terroristische organisatie er nog de lakens uitdeelt, blijft de situatie zoals die nu is volstrekt uitzichtloos.
3-0234-0000.englishText: Mr President, if it is difficult to see perspective anywhere, it is certainly in Gaza. Two million Palestinians live in appalling conditions, in a completely hopeless situation. It is all Israel's fault, many say, but of course that is not true. Certainly, Israel must make maximum efforts to get humanitarian aid to the affected population. But how can we possibly blame Israel for trying to get Hamas under control? That brings us to the core of the problem: Hamas's refusal to lay down its arms. How can the EU then help with reconstruction? I would say: let us concentrate on Hamas-free areas. In any case, make sure that not a single euro gets into the hands of Hamas, because as long as this terrorist organisation is still in charge, the situation as it is now will remain completely hopeless.

3-0235-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, I was asking myself what kind of a charade is this? Rebuilding Gaza, really? For 1 000 days, the Palestinians in Gaza have been enduring unimaginable suffering, and they have not even elected the despicable terrorist organisation Hamas, still, they are paying the price for this narrative that is broadcasted in Europe – somehow it is still connected.

1 000 days of killings, even during the so-called ceasefire! Nothing seems to get a grip on us as Europeans. We are still unable to take any concrete action. Why haven't we suspended the agreement with Israel? Why haven't we forbidden imports from illegal settlements? Why haven't we acted? We still just speak these big words while 73 000 Palestinians have been killed, children have lost their limbs in thousands and many of them have been operated on without anaesthesia. Somewhere there has to be a heart – even in you, even in you! Somewhere there has to be a heart.

3-0236-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, grand statements do not resolve complex crises. It has been nine months since Trump declared a ceasefire for Gaza. Since then, more than 1 000 Palestinians have been killed and more than 60 % of Gaza is controlled by the Israeli military – with Netanyahu pushing for 70 % – and families forced to flee again and again.

An illegitimate so-called 'peace board' is to govern Gaza, without any role for Palestinians. Rafah never fully reopened, aid deliveries still severely restricted: this is not peace. This is war disguised as peace – and Netanyahu wants to keep it this way.

So where is Europe? How much longer will we hide behind constructive dialogue, when all it has delivered is nothing? The Commission put measures on the table almost a year ago: partial suspension of the Association Agreement, sanctions, trade measures. Let's finally take these steps and stop treating the status quo as a solution. Because it's not!

3-0237-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, una pregunta: ¿Donald Trump tiene el teléfono de ustedes? ¿Les llama como llama al presidente de la FIFA? No sé, cuéntenos cómo son esas conversaciones. ¿Donald Trump les llama para que apoyen el genocidio, para que apoyen la ocupación ilegal de Cisjordania? ¿Les llama cuando van a quemar niños vivos o simplemente les llama para que estén calladitos y paguen sus guerras mientras bombardea a medio mundo?

Porque eso es lo que ve la gente, comisaria, que hay un grupo pequeño de hombres muy peligrosos que están destruyendo el mundo por negocios y a los que nadie les pone límite. Y hay un problema porque, ahora mismo, cogerle el teléfono a Trump es convertirle en el dueño de Europa y a ustedes en cómplices de sus crímenes.

Hagan algo ya: paren el genocidio, rompan relaciones con el Estado terrorista de Israel. Es su obligación. Dejen de cogerle el teléfono a Donald Trump. ¡Cuélguenle el teléfono!
3-0237-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, a question: does Donald Trump have your phone number? Does he call you like he calls the president of FIFA? I don't know, tell us what those conversations are like. Does Donald Trump call you to support genocide, to support the illegal occupation of the West Bank? Does he call you when children are going to be burned alive or simply calls you to keep quiet and pay for his wars while he bombs half the world?

Because that is what people see, Commissioner, that there is a small group of very dangerous men who are destroying the world for business and whom no one is stopping. And there is a problem because, right now, answering Trump's phone calls is turning him into the owner of Europe and you into accomplices to his crimes.

3-0238-0000.sourceText:

Please note that I don't speak about Israel or about the Jews. It is not about a country, and it is not at all about race. It is about a genocidal regime. The EU should denounce Netanyahu and his ministers as war criminals, which they are, now, or bear the mark of Cain of utter hypocrisy.

3-0239-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, my dear colleagues, reconstruction is an important step towards providing the people of Gaza with the prospect of returning to a semblance of normal life. Hopefully, it is soon possible.

Reconstruction must go far beyond rebuilding roads, hospitals and schools. It must restore hope and the foundation of a lasting peace.

The European Union is already the largest humanitarian donor to the Palestinians – it has to be mentioned. However, its construction also needs accountability. Therefore, I think the terror organisation of Hamas cannot play any role in the future of Gaza. The European Union must still support its two-state solution, enabling Palestine and Israel to coexist.

3-0240-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, yesterday, Hamas announced that it had dissolved its own government and had agreed to give up its role into the hands of the Palestinian Authority. It's the beginning of a big change yet doubts and fear in this moment are bigger than satisfaction in the Middle East.

The fear is that Hamas is going to apply the Hezbollah model: separation between administration and military wing. The suspicion is sustained by the fact that it has said nothing about the future of the military wing. On the other hand, the Board of Peace is a lost case – it has proved to be an ineffective, slow institution.

So I think these things can work in this moment. It is a very critical moment – new protagonists, new power, new country. Europe, especially, should act very fast and insert itself into this process. So it's time for Europe to step up, but very fast, Commissioner, with an independent, fully diplomatic initiative. We have the contacts, the people and the money to get it.

3-0241-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear leftists, when you talk about accountability, perhaps you should first look at yourselves. Let me be absolutely clear: Europe must never spend a single euro rebuilding what Hamas will simply use for the next war. We have already once paid for tunnels, rocket infrastructure and a terrorist regime.

So if you want accountability under international law, start with the organisation that started the war and massacred civilians. Before you say another word about reconstruction, make sure first that the Islamist terrorists are wiped out for good.

3-0242-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, dans la reconstruction de Gaza culminent tous les problèmes que nous pouvons nous imaginer: le nombre de victimes, qui se comptent par dizaines de milliers, l’atténuation de la catastrophe humanitaire qui sévit toujours. La question de la responsabilité de la présente situation n’est pas seulement celle du gouvernement de Netanyahou, mais aussi celle du Hamas et de sa tutelle iranienne, sans vouloir passer sous silence ceux qui ne veulent en aucun cas accepter la solution à deux États,

L’Union européenne, quant à elle, reste divisée sur l’opportunité de mettre en œuvre le peu de moyens dont elle dispose pour peser sur le cours des choses – c’est du déjà-vu. Nous souffrons d’un manque d’autorité, et on est respectés ni par les uns ni par les autres. Tant que nous nous payons le luxe de la division, nous resterons un observateur impuissant de la situation au Moyen-Orient. Et la seule chose qu’on nous demandera, c’est de payer: «Player or payer. That’s the question.»

'Player or payer?' That's the question.
3-0242-0000.englishText:
Mr President, in the reconstruction of Gaza culminate all the problems we can imagine: the number of victims, which number in the tens of thousands, the mitigation of the humanitarian catastrophe that is still raging. The question of responsibility for the present situation is not only that of Netanyahu's government, but also that of Hamas and its Iranian guardianship, without wishing to remain silent about those who in no way want to accept the two-state solution,

The European Union, for its part, remains divided on the advisability of implementing the few means at its disposal to influence the course of events – this has been seen before. We suffer from a lack of authority, and we are respected by neither side. As long as we afford ourselves the luxury of division, we will remain a powerless observer of the situation in the Middle East. And the only thing we will be asked to do is pay: "Player or payer. That’s the question."

'Player or payer?' That's the question.

3-0244-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, a few months ago, I stood in the occupied West Bank, and around me was the rubble of what was once a community centre. The family next door were next – their house was next to go. And right there, there was still a children's playground with a shiny blue EU plaque. I wonder how many of those plaques are buried under the destruction of the genocide in Gaza.

Israel has destroyed more than EUR 150 million of EU-funded infrastructure there and in the West Bank, and the reconstruction of Gaza might cost up to EUR 70 billion in the next decade. When will we demand that Israel pay for the destruction that they caused? Yes, we must act swiftly to ensure humanitarian aid and reconstruct Gaza – we need to do this together with Palestinians and by recognising the irreplaceable role of UNWRA. But without accountability, we risk rebuilding today what Israel will destroy again tomorrow.

It's time for accountability – on Monday, finally, stop trade with illegal settlements, suspend the association agreement, introduce proper sanctions and support the ICC, because words will not rebuild Gaza, only actions will.

3-0245-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, dopo oltre 1 000 giorni di pulizia etnica, 75 000 morti accertati, milioni di sfollati, questo Parlamento ancora non condanna il genocidio israeliano.

E, per pulirvi la coscienza, ci proponete un dibattito sul ruolo dell'Unione europea nella ricostruzione di Gaza. Però, io dico, ma con quale coraggio, onestamente?

Ci sono migliaia di esseri umani che restano intrappolati in un campo di morte a cielo aperto, uccisi dalla fame, dalle malattie oppure dalle bombe democratiche di Tel Aviv.

L'Unione europea, in realtà, oggi è lo zerbino di Trump e di Netanyahu: da Tajani con il cappellino MAGA, a Meloni e von der Leyen, al "Board of Peace", fate a gara a inginocchiarvi dinanzi agli Stati Uniti, incapaci perfino di difendere i giudici della Corte penale internazionale o la relatrice Francesca Albanese.

Per salvare la dignità dell'Unione c'è una sola via: sospendere l'accordo di associazione con Israele e sanzionare il governo Netanyahu. Il resto è solo vergognosa ipocrisia.
3-0245-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, after over 1,000 days of ethnic cleansing, 75,000 confirmed deaths, millions of displaced people, this Parliament still does not condemn the Israeli genocide.

And, to clear your conscience, you propose a debate on the role of the European Union in the reconstruction of Gaza. But, I say, with what courage, honestly?

There are thousands of human beings who remain trapped in an open-air death camp, killed by hunger, disease or the democratic bombs of Tel Aviv.

The European Union, in reality, today is the doormat of Trump and Netanyahu: from Tajani with the MAGA hat, to Meloni and von der Leyen, to the "Board of Peace", you race to kneel before the United States, incapable even of defending the judges of the International Criminal Court or the rapporteur Francesca Albanese.

To save the dignity of the Union there is only one way: suspend the association agreement with Israel and sanction the Netanyahu government. The rest is just shameful hypocrisy.

3-0246-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, γενοκτονία με πάνω από 73.000 νεκρούς Παλαιστινίους, ισοπέδωση Γάζας, σχέδιο διαμελισμού και γενικευμένος εποικισμός στη Δυτική Όχθη με ιστορικό υψηλό δολοφονίας παιδιών: ατιμώρητα κατά συρροή εγκλήματα του κράτους κατακτητή Ισραήλ, με επίθεση επιπλέον στο Ιράν και εισβολή στον Λίβανο και τη Συρία.

Παράλληλα, επιβραβεύετε με προκλητική ασυλία επισκέψεις σαν της Επιτροπής στο Ισραήλ, στρατιωτικές και εμπορικές συμφωνίες από τις συνένοχες Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες, Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, ΝΑΤΟ και την ελληνική κυβέρνηση. Το αμερικανικό σχέδιο δήθεν ειρήνης, όπως και το αντίστοιχο ΝΑΤΟϊκό σχέδιο «Πύλη της Ανατολικής Μεσογείου», που μεθοδεύτηκε στη σύναξη στην Άγκυρα, προωθούν τους ενεργειακούς εμπορικούς διαύλους ευρωατλαντικών συμφερόντων στον ανταγωνισμό με Κίνα και Ρωσία.

Παρ' όλα αυτά, οι εξελίξεις απέδειξαν ότι ο ιμπεριαλισμός δεν είναι άτρωτος. Δεν είστε παντοδύναμοι, γιατί ούτε τον παλαιστινιακό λαό ούτε αυτόν του Ιράν βάλατε στο χέρι. Με τη διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη και την αυτοτελή του πάλη, ο παλαιστινιακός λαός έχει τη δύναμη να επιβάλει το δίκιο του για ανεξάρτητο παλαιστινιακό κράτος με πρωτεύουσα την Ανατολική Ιερουσαλήμ στα σύνορα του '67.
3-0246-0000.englishText:
Mr President, genocide with over 73,000 dead Palestinians, the flattening of Gaza, a partition plan and generalised colonisation in the West Bank with a historic high in the murder of children: unpunished serial crimes of the occupying state of Israel, with an additional attack on Iran and an invasion of Lebanon and Syria.

At the same time, you reward with provocative immunity visits like that of the Commission to Israel, military and commercial agreements from the complicit United States, European Union, NATO and the Greek government. The supposed American peace plan, as well as the corresponding NATO "Eastern Mediterranean Gate" plan, orchestrated at the gathering in Ankara, promote the energy and trade routes of Euro-Atlantic interests in the competition with China and Russia.

Nevertheless, developments have proven that imperialism is not invincible. You are not all-powerful, because you have neither brought the Palestinian people nor the people of Iran to their knees. Through internationalist solidarity and their independent struggle, the Palestinian people have the power to enforce their right to an independent Palestinian state with East Jerusalem as its capital on the '67 borders.

3-0247-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, the Commission estimates that rebuilding Gaza will cost USD 71 billion. For decades, the EU has funded schools, hospitals, water networks, community centres in Palestine – many of them now destroyed. We must ask ourselves why the European Union has become remarkably consistent in financing the foundations of Palestinian life, while displaying far less determination in holding accountable those who systematically dismantle them.

The EU has a moral responsibility to help rebuild Gaza, but it must also go hand in hand with accountability. UNRWA – the only organisation with the capacity to respond at this scale on the ground – has become a scapegoat, while the real questions go unanswered.

What has the so-called Board of Peace delivered? Without a two-state solution, we'll find ourselves funding the reconstruction of Gaza again and again. Europe must help build not only infrastructure, but also the conditions for a just and lasting peace.

3-0248-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, once again, this Parliament is debating on Gaza while the humanitarian catastrophe continues to deepen. Despite the so-called peace agreement, civilians continue to suffer, humanitarian access remains severely restricted and there is still no credible political horizon.

At the same time, the West Bank faces unprecedented settler violence and de facto annexation. Lebanon continues to suffer repeated violations of its sovereignty and territorial integrity, and the recent conflict with Iran has once again demonstrated how volatile the regional security environment remains.

And what is the European strategy? We don't have a holistic approach on militias, disarmament, Hamas, Hezbollah, territorial integrity, borders being part of a peace agreement, being on the table to negotiate. We need a comprehensive Middle East strategy that matches all these challenges. Our credibility depends on how we apply international law and humanitarian law.

The foundation of a credible European foreign policy, particularly on the Middle East and Europe, has often failed. We need to act (inaudible) reconstruction in Gaza. And it's not about the Israeli population; we need them on board, but we need to stop the impunity of the killing of the Netanyahu government. Let us act once and for all.

3-0249-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, colleagues, some of you are talking about the reconstruction of Gaza as if the need arose from a natural disaster. Gaza was destroyed, and that destruction has a name: 'genocide'. Now, one thing is to pay the bills, but what about accountability for those responsible? 3-0250-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, chers collègues, Madame la Commissaire, le ministre des affaires étrangères israélien insulte Kaja Kallas, la cheffe de la diplomatie européenne, et quatre jours plus tard vous courez à Tel-Aviv lui serrer la main, sans doute avec l’approbation d’Ursula von der Leyen. Quels sont désormais les critères, quels sont vos critères pour qualifier un partenaire clé ou…

(Le Président retire la parole à l’orateur)
3-0250-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, Madam Commissioner, the Israeli Foreign Minister insults Kaja Kallas, the head of European diplomacy, and four days later you run to Tel Aviv to shake his hand, no doubt with Ursula von der Leyen's approval. The signal sent is disastrous, and your contempt for European credibility is total. To make the absurdity absolute, you add that Israel is a key partner.

Ms Šuica, Israel is blocking the humanitarian aid and medicines that you are sending to Gaza, Israel is razing infrastructure funded by the European Union while ignoring your requests for reimbursement, Israel is pursuing an assumed apartheid policy, war crimes in Lebanon and a genocide in Gaza, despite your calls for peace.

Ms Šuica, I need to understand: when were our treaties amended to authorize you to free yourself and free European foreign policy from international law and the values of the European Union? What are the criteria now, what are your criteria for qualifying a key partner or...

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone)

3-0251-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señorías, reconstruir Gaza no es solamente dedicar recursos para volver a hacerla habitable —que también—, sino cómo hacemos para que los palestinos y las palestinas sean los únicos dueños y gobernantes de ese territorio. Cómo hacemos, cómo actúa y presiona Europa para que Gaza no se convierta en un resort de lujo para millonarios sin empatía ni vergüenza.

Gaza no es tierra de nadie, es parte de la nación palestina y, por lo tanto, solo corresponde a palestinos y palestinas decidir, comenzando por los términos de la reconstrucción y acabando con el ejercicio del derecho a decidir, con el derecho de autodeterminación del pueblo de Palestina.

Cualquier otro que se arrogue esa competencia en sustitución del pueblo palestino siempre contará con nuestro rechazo y nuestra denuncia. Y esa debiera ser también la actitud de la Unión en defensa de la legalidad internacional.

A fecha de hoy, Palestina sigue siendo objeto de un genocidio planificado que ha costado más de 70 000 vidas. Situarse del lado correcto de la historia exige suspender inmediatamente el Acuerdo de Asociación UE-Israel y dar cobertura política a la Corte Penal Internacional, particularmente en lo referente a las órdenes de detención contra los perpetradores del genocidio palestino.
3-0251-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable members, rebuilding Gaza is not just a matter of dedicating resources to make it habitable again — though it is that too —, but of ensuring that Palestinian men and women are the sole owners and rulers of that territory. How we do it, how Europe acts and exerts pressure so that Gaza does not become a luxury resort for millionaires without empathy or shame.

Gaza is no man's land, it is part of the Palestinian nation and, therefore, it is up to Palestinians alone to decide, starting with the terms of the reconstruction and ending with the exercise of the right to decide, with the right to self-determination of the people of Palestine.

Anyone else who arrogates that competence to themselves to the detriment of the Palestinian people will always face our rejection and denunciation. And that should also be the Union's attitude in defence of international legality.

To date, Palestine remains the target of a planned genocide that has cost more than 70,000 lives. Standing on the right side of history requires the immediate suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement and providing political cover to the International Criminal Court, particularly regarding the arrest warrants against the perpetrators of the Palestinian genocide.

3-0252-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Irgendwie haben alle Vorredner so ein bisschen recht, aber das wird den Menschen in Gaza tatsächlich nicht helfen. Der Aufbau – und da sind wir uns, glaube ich, alle klar – wird nur im Rahmen einer für alle Beteiligten politischen, grundsätzlichen Befriedung des Konfliktes möglich sein. Der EU fällt dabei die Rolle des zentralen finanziellen und diplomatischen Unterstützers zu, während Israel nach dem Völkerrecht als Besatzungsmacht primär für die Versorgung und den Wiederaufbau ziviler Infrastruktur verantwortlich wäre. In der Realität passiert genau das Gegenteil – und Frieden liegt in der Ferne.

Unterdessen muss die EU weiterhin in Zusammenarbeit mit allen Akteuren versuchen, humanitäre Hilfe nach Gaza zu bringen, und versuchen, die Verletzten des Gazakrieges zu retten. Wir sollten überlegen, ob wir die Mittel für die Grenzmission Rafah schnell in die Krankenhäuser von West Bank und Jordanien umleiten, um praktische Hilfe leisten zu können.

Letzte Woche war ich Zeuge der Evakuierung von Verletzten und Angehörigen über Jordanien nach Spanien und die Türkei. Danke Spanien, danke Jordanien, danke der Türkei!

Seien wir die EU, die für die Schwachen, die Entrechteten, die Betrogenen und die leidenden Verletzten die Völkerfamilie ist, die sich kümmert!
3-0252-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! Somehow all previous speakers are a little bit right, but that will not actually help the people in Gaza. Reconstruction—and I think we are all clear on that—will only be possible within the framework of a political, fundamental pacification of the conflict for all involved. The EU has the role of the central financial and diplomatic supporter, while Israel, under international law as an occupying power, would be primarily responsible for the provision and reconstruction of civilian infrastructure. In reality, the exact opposite is happening—and peace is far away.

Meanwhile, the EU must continue to try, in cooperation with all actors, to bring humanitarian aid to Gaza and try to save the wounded of the Gaza war. We should consider whether we should quickly redirect the funds for the Rafah Border Mission to the hospitals of the West Bank and Jordan in order to provide practical help.

Last week I witnessed the evacuation of the wounded and their relatives via Jordan to Spain and Turkey. Thank you Spain, thank you Jordan, thank you Turkey!

Let us be the EU that is the family of nations that cares for the weak, the disenfranchised, the cheated, and the suffering wounded!

3-0253-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! EU är den största givaren till den palestinska myndigheten, och inför nästa veckas möte i den palestinska givargruppen måste det vara glasklart att ekonomiskt stöd förutsätter konkreta reformer. Utan resultat finns inga förutsättningar för en varaktig fred.

Först måste Hamas avväpnas och genomgripande avradikalisering genomföras i Gaza. Skolundervisningen måste reformeras så att antisemitism, glorifiering av terrorism och martyrskap inte traderas till nästa generation.

I fjol betalade PA ut motsvarande 156 miljoner US-dollar i ersättningar och förmåner till terrorister och deras familjer inom ramen för pay to slay. Också detta måste omedelbart upphöra.

Om dessa förhållanden inte förändras förblir tvåstatslösningen en illusion. Kommissionen måste vara glasklar: Uteblivna reformer kommer att få kännbara ekonomiska konsekvenser. Europeiska skattebetalares pengar ska aldrig användas för att finansiera eller belöna terrorism.
3-0253-0000.englishText:
Mr President! The EU is the largest donor to the Palestinian Authority, and ahead of next week's meeting of the Palestinian donor group, it must be crystal clear that financial support requires concrete reforms. Without results, there are no conditions for a lasting peace.

First, Hamas must be disarmed and comprehensive deradicalization carried out in Gaza. School education must be reformed so that antisemitism, glorification of terrorism, and martyrdom are not passed on to the next generation.

Last year, the PA paid the equivalent of 156 million US dollars in compensation and benefits to terrorists and their families within the framework of pay to slay. This, too, must cease immediately.

If these conditions do not change, the two-state solution will remain an illusion. The Commission must be crystal clear: missing reforms will have tangible economic consequences. European taxpayers' money must never be used to finance or reward terrorism.

3-0254-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, à Gaza, le cessez-le-feu n’existe que sur le papier. Les frappes continuent. Elles tuent 125 Palestiniens chaque mois. L’armée israélienne ne s’est pas retirée; elle contrôle 60 % de la bande de Gaza.

Alors, dans ce Parlement, il faut que notre groupe insiste à chaque plénière pour que nous puissions juste débattre de ce qu’il se passe en Palestine. Toute discussion est systématiquement verrouillée par les groupes de droite et d’extrême droite. Pourquoi? Comment être à ce point aveugle à la souffrance humaine et à l’injustice?

Mais nous, nous tergiversons depuis des années, sans suspension de l’accord d’association avec Israël. Cette inaction complice est celle des droites européennes, que l’histoire jugera. Il y a des élections dans quelques mois en Palestine et en Israël. Une nouvelle génération peut arriver au pouvoir pour enfin travailler à la justice, à l’égalité des droits et à la paix. Il faut agir maintenant.
3-0254-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, in Gaza, the ceasefire only exists on paper. The strikes continue. They kill 125 Palestinians every month. The Israeli army has not withdrawn; it controls 60% of the Gaza Strip.

So, in this Parliament, our group has to insist at every plenary session just so that we can debate what is happening in Palestine. Every discussion is systematically blocked by the right-wing and far-right groups. Why? How can one be so blind to human suffering and injustice?

It has been said: it took the Israeli government a few hours to break off relations with the High Representative of the European Union, Kaja Kallas, because she denounced the apartheid regime in the West Bank. 3-0255-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, international law is the foundation of peace and security. When we weaken it, we all become less secure. That is why, first, Europe should be sceptical of the so-called Board of Peace. Lasting peace depends on strong institutions and clear rules that provide legitimacy, predictability and accountability. Europe should never accept their replacement by alternative and personalised structures that lack a sound foundation in international law.

Second, the same principles must guide our approach to Gaza. We should support Israel's right to self-defence. At the same time, all violations of international humanitarian law must be investigated and those responsible held accountable. The independence of the International Criminal Court should be respected. Advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice have to be respected as well.

Third, the reconstruction of Gaza cannot succeed while Hamas remains an armed force. It has no role in Gaza's future. The real test is not declarations, but genuine disarmament.

3-0256-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, volete sapere come possiamo opporci e garantire la ricostruzione di Gaza, la pace?

Le Nazioni Unite ce l'hanno detto: Israele ha deliberatamente ucciso bambini, Israele sta compiendo un genocidio.

Israele sta illegalmente occupando Gaza e la Cisgiordania. Nel frattempo, i palestinesi a Gaza continuano a morire tra i topi, senza acqua, tra le rovine, sotto le bombe, tra i corpi dei loro cari.

Basta! Dobbiamo interrompere i rapporti con Israele.

Ma di che ricostruzione state parlando? Di quella di Trump che vuole farci un resort o di Netanyahu che vuole annetterla a Israele? O del progettino coloniale del Board of Peace a cui l'Europa ha vergognosamente partecipato?

(Il Presidente toglie la parola all'oratrice)
3-0256-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, do you want to know how we can oppose and ensure the reconstruction of Gaza, peace?

We must oppose the occupation. We must oppose genocide. Responsibility must be assigned before speaking of reconstruction.

The United Nations have told us: Israel has deliberately killed children, Israel is committing genocide.

And where are these criminals now? They are in Gaza. They decide what goes in and what goes out, who goes in and who goes out. They are in the West Bank, where they make deals with settlers to steal Palestinian land, capture them and brutally kill them.

Israel is illegally occupying Gaza and the West Bank. Meanwhile, Palestinians in Gaza continue to die among rats, without water, in the ruins, under the bombs, among the bodies of their loved ones.

And what are we doing? We continue to do business with war criminals, with a genocidal government, we continue to treat them as allies.

Enough! We must cut ties with Israel.

But what reconstruction are you talking about? Trump's, who wants to build a resort there, or Netanyahu's, who wants to annex it to Israel? Or the colonial project of the Board of Peace in which Europe has shamefully participated?

(The President cuts off the speaker's microphone)

3-0257-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Kommissionär! FN larmar om att Israel medvetet attackerar och dödar palestinska barn. Detta är barn som sover, barn som leker, barn som flyr, barn som är måltavlor. Kan ni se era barn i ögonen och säga att ni har gjort allt i er makt för att stoppa folkmordet? Kan ni det?

Människor som demonstrerar på gator och torg har betydligt mer civilkurage än den ryggradslösa politiska elit som fortsätter att gång på gång skydda krigsbrottslingen Netanyahu. Världen ser denna medbrottslighet. Ni visste allt och ni gjorde ingenting.

Stoppa handelsavtalet med Israel och ställ mördarna inför rätta.
3-0257-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! Commissioner! The UN is sounding the alarm that Israel is deliberately attacking and killing Palestinian children. These are children who are sleeping, children who are playing, children who are fleeing, children who are targets. Can you look your children in the eye and say that you have done everything in your power to stop the genocide? Can you?

People demonstrating in the streets and squares have significantly more civil courage than the spineless political elite that continues time and time again to protect the war criminal Netanyahu. The world sees this complicity. You knew everything and you did nothing.

Stop the trade agreement with Israel and bring the murderers to justice.

3-0258-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, this crisis must not be forgotten. Hamas is still around in Gaza. It is not yet gone. People are still under pressure. This terrorist organisation even was not ashamed to put children on the line, to put women on the line, to put their own civil society, the civil population, at risk. And they are still around.

So I can only one more time advocate for deweaponising the terrorist organisation, demilitarising Gaza, creating proper education towards a proper civil society without hatred, antisemitism, Islamism, creating a precondition for economic self-capability so that one day it will not be necessary anymore that the whole world pours money into the region.

And when development aid is given, not one single cent must be misused for hatred, for Islamism, for antisemitism, because that means pouring hatred into even children's hearts, which leads again to such an outrageous violence such as in 7 October.

3-0259-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, hoe kan deze Commissie zichzelf nog in de ogen kijken. Hoe doen onze regeringsleiders dat eigenlijk? Terwijl Gaza levend wordt begraven en de Westelijke Jordaanoever wordt opgeslokt, nederzetting per nederzetting. En dat in real time voor onze ogen. En laten we ook stoppen met te zeggen dat dit een ingewikkeld verhaal is. Dat is het niet. Het geweld is onwettig, de bezetting is onwettig, de nederzettingen zijn illegaal.

De Verenigde Naties zeggen ons dat, het Internationaal Gerechtshof heeft het gezegd en ook vanuit de Europese Unie moet dat luid en duidelijk blijven klinken. En toch gebeurt er niets. En dat heeft een naam: medeplichtigheid. Schors dat associatieverdrag volledig, verbiedt de handel in producten uit illegale nederzettingen en breidt die sancties uit. Deze Commissie wilde ooit een geopolitieke Commissie zijn. Europa wil een belangrijke rol spelen op het geopolitieke toneel. Wel, doe dan iets. Woorden volstaan niet. Free Palestine. Nu.
3-0259-0000.englishText:
Mr President, how can this Commission still look itself in the eye. How do our heads of government actually do that? While Gaza is being buried alive and the West Bank is being swallowed up, settlement by settlement. And that in real time before our eyes. And let us also stop saying that this is a complicated story. It is not. The violence is unlawful, the occupation is unlawful, the settlements are illegal.

The United Nations tell us that, the International Court of Justice has said so and that must also continue to resound loudly and clearly from the European Union. And yet nothing happens. And that has a name: complicity. Completely suspend that association agreement, ban trade in products from illegal settlements and expand those sanctions. This Commission once wanted to be a geopolitical Commission. Europe wants to play an important role on the geopolitical stage. Well, then do something. Words are not enough. Free Palestine. Now.

3-0260-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, humanitarian aid has been weaponised and politicised, 90 % of Gaza destroyed, 60 % of Gaza occupied, continual encroachments into the West Bank, aggressive actions by settlers being facilitated by the Netanyahu government and the Israeli Defence Forces. Fundamental breaches of international law, refusal to accept decisions of the International Criminal Court. At the same time, we are here in the House today debating the EU's role and reconstruction of the Gaza Strip and accountability of Israel under international law.

But maybe it's time that we started looking for accountability among ourselves, because we have consistently turned a blind eye to Israel in all its actions with regard to Palestine. No acceptance of the two-state solution, no acceptance of the Palestinians' right to self-determination.

Israel acts with impunity because we have granted it immunity. We simply will never sanction any action that Israel does. So the accountability should start here in this House, in the European Union, and particularly among the Council.

3-0261-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, le tengo que confesar algo. Tras Gaza, tras mil días de genocidio, yo soy otra persona. Nadie puede convivir con tanto horror sin cambiar su forma de estar en el mundo, de verse a sí mismo y a la humanidad.

Hoy debatimos sobre Israel, pero en realidad debatimos sobre nosotros. Sucedió y puede volver a suceder. Nos lo advirtió Primo Levi después de Auschwitz. ¿Y nosotros qué le dijimos? No, nunca más... lo prometimos. Mentimos. Está volviendo a suceder. Y ustedes se hacen fotos con los responsables.

¿Somos mejores que aquellos que miraron a otro lado cuando deportaban a judíos como Primo Levi? Somos peores, porque ahora no podemos decir que no sabíamos, ni tan siquiera que no participábamos. Cuando nos preguntamos por quién doblan las campanas, doblan por nosotros.

¿Qué será de nosotros después de Gaza, señora comisaria? Los lugares más oscuros del infierno nos esperan: a la derecha —que hoy no está aquí— por su participación en el genocidio, por deshumanizarse, y a nosotros por no impedirlo.
3-0261-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I have to confess something to you. After Gaza, after a thousand days of genocide, I am a different person. No one can live with so much horror without changing their way of being in the world, of seeing themselves and humanity.

Today we are debating Israel, but in reality we are debating ourselves. It happened and it can happen again. Primo Levi warned us after Auschwitz. And what did we tell him? No, never again... we promised. We lied. It is happening again. And you take pictures with those responsible.

Are we better than those who looked the other way when Jews like Primo Levi were being deported? We are worse, because now we cannot say that we did not know, nor even that we did not participate. When we ask who the bell tolls for, it tolls for us.

What will become of us after Gaza, Madam Commissioner? The darkest places in hell await us: the right —which is not here today— for its participation in genocide, for dehumanising itself, and us for not preventing it.

3-0262-0000.sourceText:
SĒDI VADA: ROBERTS ZĪLE

Priekšsēdētāja vietnieks

3-0263-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária Šuica, enquanto discutimos a reconstrução de Gaza, a destruição no terreno continua.

O cessar-fogo é uma mentira. Israel continua a assassinar palestinianos, a impedir a entrada da ajuda humanitária de que necessitam, a atacar acampamentos de palestinianos desalojados, a destruir infraestruturas civis, algumas delas construídas com financiamento da União Europeia.

Enquanto aqui discutimos a responsabilização de Israel pelas violações do direito internacional, a União Europeia mantém a sua plena cumplicidade com o genocídio. A Senhora Comissária foi a Israel para reafirmar que as relações políticas, económicas e até de cooperação militar com Israel se mantêm a todo o vapor: a prova mais evidente da cumplicidade da União Europeia com o genocídio está aqui.

Nem o relatório da Comissão de Inquérito das Nações Unidas, que denuncia o genocídio e os crimes cometidos por Israel contra as crianças, faz a União Europeia corar de vergonha e reverter o caminho.

Mas esse tem de ser o sentido: garantir o respeito pelos direitos do povo palestiniano, pôr fim ao genocídio.
3-0263-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner Šuica, as we discuss the reconstruction of Gaza, the destruction on the ground continues.

The ceasefire is a lie. Israel continues to murder Palestinians, to prevent the entry of the humanitarian aid they need, to attack camps of displaced Palestinians, to destroy civil infrastructure, some of it built with European Union funding.

While we discuss here holding Israel accountable for violations of international law, the European Union maintains its full complicity in the genocide. The Commissioner went to Israel to reaffirm that political, economic and even military cooperation relations with Israel continue at full steam: the most obvious proof of the European Union's complicity in the genocide is right here.

Not even the report by the United Nations Commission of Inquiry, which denounces the genocide and crimes committed by Israel against children, makes the European Union blush with shame and reverse its path.

But that must be the direction: to guarantee respect for the rights of the Palestinian people, to put an end to the genocide.

3-0264-0000.sourceText:
Sur President, kollegi, tlabt li nitkellem f'dan id-dibattitu f'isem iż-żgħażagħ li niltaqa' magħhom Malta. Iż-żgħażagħ jgħiduli "Xbajna bid-double standards, xbajna bl-ipokrezija Ewropea." Jiena irrid il-prosperità tal-poplu Palestinjan daqskemm irrid is-sigurtà tal-Iżraeliti f'darhom. Però l-akbar kontribut li rridu nagħmlu għat-tnejn li huma, huwa li ninsistu fuq il-legalità. Għalhekk ma nistgħux nibqgħu nappoġġjaw ftehim tal-kummerċ kif għandna bħalissa mal-Iżrael. Qisu xejn mhu xejn.

Il-President von der Leyen f'din l-istess plenarja hawnhekk, wegħditna sospensjoni ta' dan il-ftehim. X'ġara sadanittant? Weħilna f'deadlock bejn il-gvernijiet. Emmnuni ħbieb tiegħi, jiena nistħi nispjega din is-sitwazzjoni lit-tifel tiegħi ta' erbatax-il sena. Nistħi ngħid li l-Ewropa hija kompletament impotenti. Għandna kriżi ta' kredibbiltà li noħorġu minnha billi jkollna rikostruzzjoni accountable li la sservi lill-Ħamas u lanqas biex jerġgħu jitkissru l-binjiet... 

(Il-President irtira l-kelma lill-kelliem)
3-0264-0000.englishText:
Mr President, colleagues, I asked to speak in this debate on behalf of the young people I meet in Malta. Young people tell me, "We are sick of double standards, we are sick of European hypocrisy." I want the prosperity of the Palestinian people just as much as I want the security of the Israelis in their home. But the biggest contribution we want to make to both is to insist on legality. That is why we can no longer continue to support a trade agreement as we currently have with Israel. As if nothing is the matter.

President von der Leyen in this same plenary here, promised us a suspension of this agreement. What happened in the meantime? We got stuck in a deadlock between governments. Believe me, my friends, I am ashamed to explain this situation to my fourteen-year-old son. I am ashamed to say that Europe is completely impotent. We have a credibility crisis which we will get out of by having accountable reconstruction that neither serves Hamas nor serves to rebuild buildings to be destroyed again...

(The President withdrew the floor from the speaker)

3-0265-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, the situation in Gaza is dire. But we must also draw attention to the situation of the West Bank, where Israeli forces are actively cooperating with the violent settlers, ignoring court decisions and international law, and facilitating attacks on innocent Palestinian families. From the beginning of the war, settlers and the IDF have killed at least 1 160 Palestinians in the West Bank, including 242 children – children, colleagues, while simply living on their own land.

This is why I strongly condemn any tolerance and support for Israeli violations, including dangerous threats by the new Slovenian Government and President of the Government Janez Janša, member of the EPP, to move the Slovenian embassy to Jerusalem. This not only shows the one-eighty overnight shift in Slovenian foreign policy but also deviates from the official EU position.

Colleagues, the EU will retake a test of principles on Monday. To pass, we must suspend the EU‑Israel Association Agreement.

3-0266-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, before I came to this Parliament, I was a schoolteacher in Germany. And back in my home country, we make sure children deeply study the darkest chapter of our past so they never, ever question the horrors of what happened.

But we only succeed as educators if we get students to think beyond the specifics of one era. Because that's exactly what people do to avoid accountability: they hide behind the specifics of the moment to justify looking away at today's crimes.

But history is not a museum piece; it's a life lesson in human dignity. And the hardest part is recognising suffering when it wears a different face in a different era. True reconstruction begins with the courage to apply international law equally. If we don't ask for accountability now from the perpetrator of this genocide, we have failed the most fundamental lesson of our recent history.

3-0267-0000.sourceText: Voorzitter, we praten over de wederopbouw van Gaza alsof er een natuurramp heeft plaatsgehad. Maar de realiteit is anders: als onderdeel van een genocidale campagne heeft Israël 85 % van Gaza met de grond gelijk gemaakt. Er is op papier een staakt‑het‑vuren, dus zou wederopbouw mogelijk moeten zijn en zou humanitaire hulp mogelijk moeten zijn. Maar dat verhult de werkelijkheid. Ook zijn sinds dat staakt‑het‑vuren meer dan duizend Palestijnen gedood en duizenden gewonden gevallen. En de hulp die wel binnenkomt is onvoldoende en aan banden gelegd met absurde beperkingen. Protheses worden tegengehouden als militaire middelen. Deze week nog werden hulpverleners blootgesteld aan luchtaanvallen. Onder zulke omstandigheden is het onmogelijk om te spreken over wederopbouw en een fatsoenlijk gesprek daarover te hebben. Het beleid van de Israëlische regering is niet veranderd. Zolang Europa dit blindelings laat gebeuren, is trots praten over de Europese inzet voor wederopbouw en humanitaire hulp niets meer dan een schaamlap. Het Palestijnse volk verdient wederopbouw en humanitaire hulp. Daarom moet het Associatieverdrag tussen de EU en Israël worden opgeschort.
3-0267-0000.englishText: Mr President, we are talking about the reconstruction of Gaza as if a natural disaster has taken place. But the reality is different: as part of a genocidal campaign, Israel has razed 85% of Gaza to the ground. There is a ceasefire on paper, so reconstruction should be possible and humanitarian aid should be possible. But that obscures reality. Also, since that ceasefire, more than a thousand Palestinians have been killed and thousands injured. And the aid that does get in is insufficient and restricted by absurd limitations. Prosthetics are being withheld as military equipment. Just this week, aid workers were exposed to airstrikes. Under such circumstances, it is impossible to speak about reconstruction and have a decent conversation about it. The policy of the Israeli government has not changed. As long as Europe blindly lets this happen, proudly talking about the European commitment to reconstruction and humanitarian aid is nothing more than a fig leaf. The Palestinian people deserve reconstruction and humanitarian aid. Therefore, the Association Agreement between the EU and Israel must be suspended.

3-0268-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, sono stato con altri parlamentari nella Cisgiordania, nei territori occupati.

Abbiamo visto, appena arrivati nella città di Hebron, una curva dove ci è stato indicato che c'erano ancora delle macchie di sangue di alcuni palestinesi uccisi qualche giorno prima e abbiamo chiesto: "Ma perché non vi rivolgete alla giustizia?" "No, perché noi non abbiamo la giustizia normale. Noi abbiamo la giustizia militare, e la prima cosa che farebbero sarebbe venire a distruggere la nostra casa."

Ho visto un bambino che non aveva l'incubatrice: nato sottopeso, era in una scatola di scarpe con del cotone; una sposa che piangeva perché, dietro di lei, la sua casa era distrutta per motivi di sicurezza.

Non possiamo continuare in questo modo. Ho visto trattare esattamente quel popolo come sono stati trattati gli ebrei durante la Seconda guerra mondiale.

Dobbiamo sanzionare Israele, interrompere ogni contatto con Israele, perché Israele ascolta, in questo momento, con il suo governo, solo la forza.
