3-0268-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, I have been with other parliamentarians in the West Bank, in the occupied territories.

As soon as we arrived in the city of Hebron, we saw a curve where we were told there were still bloodstains of some Palestinians killed a few days earlier, and we asked: "Why don't you turn to justice?" "No, because we do not have normal justice. We have military justice, and the first thing they would do would be to come and destroy our house."

I saw a baby who did not have an incubator: born underweight, he was in a shoebox with cotton; a bride who was crying because, behind her, her house was destroyed for security reasons.

We cannot continue in this way. I saw that people treated exactly as the Jews were treated during the Second World War.

We must sanction Israel, break off all contact with Israel, because Israel listens, at this moment, with its government, only to force.

3-0269-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, o Tribunal Internacional de Justiça foi claro: Israel tem obrigações. Tem de garantir o essencial à sobrevivência da população de Gaza. Tem de deixar entrar ajudas, sem exceções. Mais, o Tribunal rejeitou com factos as desculpas usadas para bloquear essas mesmas ajudas.

Uma decisão do Tribunal que não é cumprida não é só uma decisão ignorada. É o direito internacional posto em causa e quem viola o direito internacional tem de responder por isso perante a justiça e perante a História.

Não pode haver impunidade. Não pode haver regras para uns, exceções para outros. A História julgará não só aqueles que violaram direitos humanos, como aqueles que assistiram e nada disseram.

Basta de palavras sem consequências! É tempo de suspender o Acordo de Associação União Europeia-Israel!
3-0269-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the International Court of Justice was clear: Israel has obligations. It must guarantee the essentials for the survival of the population of Gaza. It must let aid in, without exceptions. Furthermore, the Court rejected with facts the excuses used to block that very aid.

A Court decision that is not complied with is not just an ignored decision. It is international law called into question, and those who violate international law must answer for it before justice and before History.

There can be no impunity. There can be no rules for some, exceptions for others. History will judge not only those who violated human rights, but those who stood by and said nothing.

Enough words without consequences! It is time to suspend the European Union-Israel Association Agreement!

3-0270-0000.sourceText:
(inicio de la intervención fuera de micrófono)...no puede mirar hacia otro lado mientras denuncia lo que pasa en Gaza. Mientras pedimos que se aplique el Derecho internacional en Ucrania, pero no lo aplicamos con la misma firmeza en Palestina, el mundo entiende una cosa terrible: que en Europa no todas las vidas valen lo mismo.

Este doble estándar está destruyendo nuestra credibilidad y nuestra dignidad. Gaza ha pasado de ser una cárcel al aire libre —como decía Borrell— a un cementerio al aire libre. Y cuando dentro de unos años mi hijo me pregunte qué hizo Europa para frenar el genocidio en Gaza yo quiero decirle que no miramos hacia otro lado. Por eso, Europa debe actuar ya, debe pedir el alto el fuego inmediato, el fin de la ocupación, pero hoy les pedimos a los ministros de Asuntos Exteriores una medida urgente: que se suspenda el Acuerdo de Asociación UE‑Israel.

Porque cuando Europa calla ante Gaza no solo pierde su credibilidad, sino también su alma.
3-0270-0000.englishText:
cannot look the other way while denouncing what is happening in Gaza. While we call for international law to be applied in Ukraine, but we do not apply it with the same firmness in Palestine, the world understands a terrible thing: that in Europe not all lives are worth the same.

This double standard is destroying our credibility and our dignity. Gaza has gone from being an open-air prison —as Borrell said— to an open-air cemetery. And when in a few years my son asks me what Europe did to stop the genocide in Gaza I want to tell him that we did not look the other way. Therefore, Europe must act now, it must call for an immediate ceasefire, the end of the occupation, but today we ask the Ministers for Foreign Affairs for an urgent measure: that the EU-Israel Association Agreement be suspended.

Because when Europe remains silent in the face of Gaza, it not only loses its credibility, but also its soul.

3-0271-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, Minister, you just saw a lucky mother with her excellent child. But unfortunately in Gaza the hospitals are destroyed. Hospitals are not battlefields; yet in Gaza, the basic principle of humanity has been broken for too long, colleagues.

Since the October ceasefire, the strikes have not stopped and humanitarian access remains conditional and obstructed, colleagues. I am speaking with you, the representatives from the Council, colleagues, now.

Children are dying not only from bombs, but from the collapse of hospitals and the healthcare system. Now you see the contrast between those two examples.

And of course, you know, this is not a side issue to the political debate. A ceasefire that still allows a hospital to run out of oxygen is not peace, it's a crime. And we need to stop it immediately. And it's up to us now to send a clear message to the Council: please act.

3-0272-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, dear colleagues, stability in the Middle East is of utmost importance. For European security and stability but, most importantly, of course, for the people who have been suffering too much and for too long. The only viable way to long-term stability is the two-state solution. What does this mean, a two-state solution? It means two fully democratic states holding regular and free elections, meaning no space for religious extremists on all sides. No Hamas nor Orthodox extremists, which also includes the settlers in the West Bank.

With the newest reports coming now from Gaza, a clear European position for a two-state solution is essential. We cannot leave rebuilding to the United States under Donald Trump. We need to stand on the side of human rights, of international law and the people hoping for peace and prosperity in this region.

3-0273-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, 73 000 Palestinians have been killed. Among them, 21 000 kids; 10 000 kids have suffered life-changing injuries; 60 000 kids have lost one or both of their parents. Hundreds of journalists have been killed. Hundreds of thousands of homes have been completely damaged or totally destroyed. So when this genocide is being perpetrated, settler violence still continues to this very day. Land is stolen. Families are beaten. Children are being terrorised.

Now, let's be honest: no horror will ever justify another. But what if these were Ukrainian kids or Ukrainian families? What if this genocide was being perpetrated by the Iranian regime? This Chamber would not be empty as it is today. It would roar. It would call it for what it is.

So please spare us the empty speeches, especially from the right side of this House, because there is no reconstruction without justice. There is no reconstruction without a Palestinian state. Israel has every right to exist, but so does Palestine. And recognising the right of the Palestinian people is no punishment against Israel; it is the rightful recognition of the Palestinian people. So end the EU-Israel Association Agreement now.

3-0274-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, a Gaza il genocidio non è mai finito.

Le parole del patriarca di Gerusalemme, Pizzaballa, sono come pietre: mancano acqua, cibo, medicinali, i topi mordono i bambini, mentre le persone muoiono.

Hamas sembra aprire al trasferimento dell'amministrazione civile, ma non al disarmo. E intanto si parla del dispiegamento di un contingente marocchino.

Il piano di Trump avanza nel vuoto lasciato dall'Europa, ma la ricostruzione di Gaza deve essere sotto l'egida delle Nazioni Unite e delle sue agenzie, come l'UNRWA.

Per questo serve dare messaggi netti ora, di fronte alla deriva del governo israeliano. Mi rivolgo al governo italiano in primis, a Giorgia Meloni: abbia il coraggio, per una volta, e tolga il veto sulla sospensione dell'accordo di associazione UE‑Israele, riconosca, come Italia, lo Stato di Palestina. È necessario che almeno la parte commerciale degli accordi sia sospesa, come abbiamo chiesto in questo Parlamento.

L'Europa rompa con il doppio standard e faccia ciò che serve per restituire dignità e libertà ai palestinesi.

Stop al genocidio, stop al terrorismo, stop alla violenza. Lavoriamo insieme per ricostruzione e pace.
3-0274-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, the genocide in Gaza has never ended.

The words of the Patriarch of Jerusalem, Pizzaballa, are like stones: water, food and medicine are lacking, rats are biting children, while people die.

Hamas appears to be open to the transfer of civil administration, but not to disarmament. And in the meantime, there is talk of deploying a Moroccan contingent.

Trump's plan is advancing in the vacuum left by Europe, but the reconstruction of Gaza must be under the aegis of the United Nations and its agencies, such as UNRWA.

This is why we need to send clear messages now, in the face of the drift of the Israeli government. I appeal first and foremost to the Italian government, to Giorgia Meloni: have the courage, for once, and lift the veto on the suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement, and recognise the State of Palestine as Italy. It is necessary that at least the commercial part of the agreements be suspended, as we have asked in this Parliament.

Europe must break with the double standard and do what is necessary to restore dignity and freedom to the Palestinians.

Stop the genocide, stop terrorism, stop violence. Let us work together for reconstruction and peace.

3-0275-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Minister Byrne, I have a simple question: what do we mean when we say 'respect for human rights'? It is the foundation of our European project and a legal obligation under Article 2 of the EU-Israel Association Agreement. It doesn't mean the killing of tens of thousands of Palestinian children, reducing the city of Gaza to rubble, turning what's left into an open-air prison the world is forbidden to enter.

The list of Israel's crimes is endless, but I can name one action we need to take: ending the EU-Israel Association Agreement. Why does the agreement remain? It's worth billions to the Israeli economy. Yet we comfort ourselves by saying we will lead in rebuilding Gaza. But you cannot rebuild a hospital with one hand, while rewarding the war criminals that flattened us with the other.

Ending this agreement is not radical. It is the minimum required by our own law and our own values. The Irish Presidency of the EU must lead. End the EU-Israel Association Agreement once and for all!

3-0276-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members who are left in this room, I was listening carefully to each of you, and I heard each word which you said during this meeting.

Our speaking slots are not enough to elaborate on this very difficult topic. One-minute speeches are not enough to discuss this topic. I have to say that I am here representing High Representative/Vice-President Kaja Kallas. So I will quote her first: 'The European Union and Israel have a lot that binds us together. I value our dialogue and engagement, respectfully and constructively. Dialogue is the foundation of diplomacy, especially when differences arise.' This is what our HR/VP said. So I'm building on this and leaning on this.

All of us know that the situation is dire. The topic is very serious, as I said. Listening to you, I felt like I was a rival in a Foreign Affairs Council. As long as we are divided, we will stay powerless. All of you turn to the Commission, turn to me. I don't want to blame anyone. This is not a black-and-white story; this is not a blame game. But the ball is with the Council. The Member who was speaking last, Mr Ó Ríordáin, really said the right thing. He was the only one who turned towards the Council. I am also looking towards the Council, and I think that during the Irish Presidency, I wish they would be capable of reaching consensus.

Unfortunately, the association agreement and its suspension is at the table as of last September, you remember. During the State of the Union speech, it was put on the table. Unfortunately, I was present at each and every Foreign Affairs Council – the Member States are divided. Not to blame anyone, but just to say there is a problem. We can speak for decades like this. We can blame each other. We can post our video clips blaming someone. But I say we won't reach a solution if we attack each other. This is not the way how it works. So I really hope that under the Irish Presidency, we will be capable of reaching the unanimity on this.

Someone said time to suspend the association agreement. Yes, time is to spend the association agreement, but it's on the table. And, as I told you, turning towards us and toward me was not the right address. We are trying to find a solution all the time. We are having a dialogue. In parallel, we are really financing the Palestinian Authority. Without us, all of you know that the Palestinian Authority would not have survived. Those people there – teachers, nurses, doctors – we have this package programme, which is EUR 1.6 billion. So without us, they would have collapsed.

3-0277-0000.sourceText: In our new procedure, we have to ask also Commissioners to stick to time. Please conclude.

3-0278-0000.sourceText:
I have replied to all of you. I especially want to thank Mr Sánchez Amor, because I need your support for this. In the next MFF, we want to have extra money on top of our budget. The Team Gaza initiative is being launched and we would like to have this in our budget. It is very important, but we cannot do it without you. You are the ones who decide on the budget in the end. So we are trying to bring together a coalition of all Member States, a coalition of the willing, and this is what we are doing.

But, as I said, each and every conflict ended at the negotiation table. We need conditions, we need circumstances for this. And, first of all, we need accession to Gaza. Unfortunately, this NCAG committee which was established sits in Cairo. At the moment they haven't acceded Gaza. This is what I was trying to do during my visit in Israel. As I told you in my introductory speech, they released now these banking sector issues, and they also approved the two projects for waste and water management, which I think is a good sign.

So we need diplomacy and we are doing what we can.

I hope that during this Palestine donor group, which will be held on Monday, there will be much more to say. So I want to thank you for all this and we need to be together. We need to be unified. This not a blame game. We have to help people on the ground.

3-0279-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, thank you very much, and I want to thank all of the speakers who made their voices heard so strongly in this debate. I have noted that I think almost 50 Members have spoken in this debate and it shows the very strong views here in the European Parliament. The Council certainly takes note of everything that was said and I particularly mention, as the Commissioner did, Aodhán Ó Ríordáin, but also Mr Andriukaitis as well, for directly addressing the Council.

Diverging views have been expressed on what the EU can and should do to help the people in Gaza, and to hold Israel and Hamas accountable. But I can say this: we are united in one common goal, and that is lasting peace and security in the Middle East.

In our priorities as the Irish Presidency, which our Taoiseach presented yesterday, we have committed to promoting active engagement in support of such lasting peace and security regarding the conflicts in the Middle East, and in particular the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians. This reaffirms, and must reaffirm, the EU's commitment to a two-state solution, where both Israelis and Palestinians can live in peace and security.

We must work towards ending the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the deteriorating situation in the West Bank. Next week, as I said already, the Council is looking forward to the options that the Commission will present for the meeting of the Foreign Affairs Council on 13 July in light, particularly, of the further deteriorating situation regarding the illegal settlements. I have no doubt that the Council and the members of the Council will certainly hear the views that have been expressed here in the European Parliament.

3-0282-0000.sourceText:
Nākamais darba kārtības punkts ir debates par Komisijas paziņojumu par narkotiku tirdzniecību Eiropas ūdeņos – mūsu robežu aizsardzība un tiesībaizsardzības amatpersonu atbalstīšana (2026/2797(RSP)).

Vēlos atgādināt runātājiem, ka, ņemot vērā pašlaik spēkā esošos testa režīma pasākumus un noteikto debašu beigu laiku, būs stingri jāievēro uzstāšanās laiks, tai skaitā visiem runātājiem, ne tikai deputātiem.
3-0282-0000.englishText:
The next item on the order of business is the debate on the Commission statement on drug trafficking in European waters - protecting our borders and supporting law enforcement officials (2026/2797(RSP)).
I would like to remind speakers that, given the test regime measures currently in place and the scheduled end time of the debate, speaking time will be strictly enforced for all speakers, not just Members.

3-0283-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, on 8 May, two Spanish Guardia Civil agents were killed after their boats collided while chasing suspected drug traffickers in the Atlantic. I feel deeply for the two officers, their relatives and their colleagues. This tragic event reminds us of the risks that law enforcement officers face to keep narcotics off our streets. They deserve our full support.

Honourable Members, we recently presented the annual European Drugs Report. It paints an alarming picture. Cocaine is more available than ever before. Between 2013 and 2023, cocaine seizures in Europe increased sixfold. At the same time, we are seeing a sharp rise in synthetic drugs, which are often even more dangerous and harder to detect.

Drug trafficking is not an isolated crime. It fuels money laundering, corruption, human trafficking, violence and other forms of serious organised crime. Behind this market are highly sophisticated criminal networks. They use advanced technologies, including for their communications, international logistics chains and enormous financial resources. At the same time, they exploit social vulnerabilities, social inclusion, lack of opportunities, mental health challenges and other societal pressures that create an environment in which drug use and addiction can flourish. That is why we take a comprehensive approach: the new EU drugs strategy combines public health preservation and treatment with a strong security and law enforcement response, because we need to reduce both supply and demand.

On the law enforcement side, we presented a European action plan against drug trafficking at the end of last year. Its objective is to target criminal networks along the entire supply chain, from production countries and transit routes to European markets. A key focus is the security of our ports. A large share of the cocaine entering Europe comes through them. That is why we are strengthening the European Ports Alliance, improving controls and tackling the infiltration of ports by organised crime. The alliance shows what can be achieved when public authorities and private operators work hand in hand, and you can see the results in the media: four tonnes of cocaine seized at Rotterdam in March, eight tonnes concealed in cocoa beans in Wilhelmshaven in May, and over 100 tonnes of cocaine and ketamine hidden in timber from Chile.

We are also stepping up cooperation with partner countries, particularly in Latin America. Drug trafficking is a global business and our response must be global as well. Europol has recently concluded new partnerships with Brazil and Ecuador to strengthen the fight against drug trafficking and organised crime. The Commission has recently proposed a new mandate for Europol; it will strengthen the agency as Europe's information hub, operational hub and technology hub, enabling it to better support Member States in tackling increasingly sophisticated criminal networks. And early next year, we will propose modernised rules on organised crime.

I encourage you to give priority to all these files in the coming months, so that we will be able to see their impact on the ground soon. I look forward to the discussions that will follow.

3-0284-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, o narcotráfico marítimo no Atlântico está a evoluir rapidamente e pressiona cada vez mais as fronteiras da União Europeia. Falamos de redes mais organizadas, mais agressivas, mais sofisticadas, com impacto direto na nossa segurança interna e na nossa capacidade de resposta.

As operações recentes em Espanha e em Portugal, nas quais lamentamos a morte de agentes da Guardia Civil e da GNR, mostram que esta é uma ameaça estruturada e cada vez mais impune. Só em 2025 deixámos escapar cerca de 192 embarcações e 700 toneladas de cocaína no Atlântico. As redes adaptam-se: mudam de rota, usam a África Ocidental como ponto de transbordo, recorrem a embarcações de alta velocidade e a narcossubmarinos para redistribuir a droga por diferentes rotas. No mar, continuam a ter vantagem pela mobilidade, pelo alcance e pela rapidez de fuga.

A Comissão Europeia não pode limitar-se a acompanhar o fenómeno. Tem de liderar uma resposta operacional, legislativa e tecnológica à altura da ameaça.

Precisamos de mais financiamento, sim, mas precisamos sobretudo de mais capacidade, mais vigilância aérea, mais partilha de informação e de inteligência, mais instrumentos operacionais.

Precisamos também de rever com seriedade as regras de intervenção no mar, com uma abordagem clara sobre o uso proporcional da força em operações marítimas de alto risco. A Comissão deve ainda avançar com legislação europeia sobre a posse, a modificação e a operação de embarcações de alta potência utilizadas pelo crime organizado. Deve apoiar tecnologias capazes de neutralizar motores à distância e deve reforçar a cooperação com os Estados-Membros e com os países da África Ocidental, onde muitas destas rotas se consolidam.

Senhor Comissário, não podemos pedir às nossas forças de segurança que enfrentem organizações que não conhecem fronteiras com meios limitados, com regras desajustadas, com financiamento pensado para os desafios do século passado. Não podemos exigir eficácia sem lhes dar capacidade.

Esta é uma questão de segurança, de soberania e de Estado de direito.
3-0284-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, maritime drug trafficking in the Atlantic is evolving rapidly and increasingly pressures the borders of the European Union. We are talking about networks that are more organized, more aggressive, more sophisticated, with a direct impact on our internal security and our response capacity.

Recent operations in Spain and Portugal, in which we mourn the deaths of officers from the Guardia Civil and the GNR, show that this is a structured threat that is operating with increasing impunity. In 2025 alone, we let approximately 192 vessels and 700 tons of cocaine slip away in the Atlantic. The networks adapt: they change routes, use West Africa as a transshipment point, resort to high-speed boats and narco-submarines to redistribute the drugs through different routes. At sea, they continue to have the advantage due to mobility, range, and speed of escape.

The European Commission cannot limit itself to monitoring the phenomenon. It must lead an operational, legislative, and technological response worthy of the threat.

We need more funding, yes, but above all we need more capacity, more aerial surveillance, more information and intelligence sharing, and more operational instruments.

We also need to seriously review the rules of engagement at sea, with a clear approach to the proportional use of force in high-risk maritime operations. The Commission must also advance European legislation on the possession, modification, and operation of high-power vessels used by organized crime. It must support technologies capable of neutralizing engines remotely and must strengthen cooperation with Member States and West African countries, where many of these routes are consolidated.

Mr. Commissioner, we cannot ask our security forces to face organizations that know no borders with limited means, with mismatched rules, with funding designed for the challenges of the last century. We cannot demand effectiveness without giving them capacity.

This is a matter of security, sovereignty, and the rule of law.

3-0285-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, llevamos dos años de legislatura del Parlamento Europeo y es raro el pleno —si es que hay alguno— que se libre de un punto en el que las fuerzas que hacen oposición al Gobierno de España no lo aprovechen instrumentalmente para criticarlo.

Resulta deplorable en un asunto tan sensible que debería concitar tanto nuestra unidad como es la lucha contra el narcotráfico en nuestras fronteras exteriores y el apoyo a las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad, que es exactamente lo que hace el Gobierno de España.

El ministro del Interior ha incrementado en 17 000 los policías y los guardias civiles —4 000 de ellos en Andalucía— durante el mandato del Gobierno progresista que preside Pedro Sánchez. Se han invertido 2 000 millones EUR en infraestructuras de comisarías y, por tanto, centros de seguridad en la zona del Campo de Gibraltar.

Evidentemente, este asunto tiene dimensión europea y, por tanto, lo que importa es la Estrategia de la UE sobre Drogas y el plan de acción de la UE contra el narcotráfico, con coordinación europea y en colaboración con Eurojust y con Europol.

Tal y como sugiere la Agencia de la Unión Europea sobre Drogas —situada en Lisboa—, tiene que haber una partida europea para recursos europeos y, por supuesto, la protección de víctimas. Debemos ponernos del lado de las víctimas sin hacernos jamás la foto con los narcotraficantes.
3-0285-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, we are two years into the European Parliament's legislative term, and it is rare for a plenary session —if indeed there is any— to pass without a point where the forces in opposition to the Government of Spain take instrumental advantage of it to criticize it.

It is deplorable on such a sensitive issue that should command our utmost unity, such as the fight against drug trafficking at our external borders and the support for law enforcement and security forces, which is precisely what the Government of Spain does.

The Minister of the Interior has increased the number of police officers and civil guards by 17,000 —4,000 of them in Andalusia— during the term of the progressive government presided over by Pedro Sánchez. Two billion euros have been invested in police station infrastructure and, therefore, security centers in the Campo de Gibraltar area.

Obviously, this issue has a European dimension and, therefore, what matters is the EU Drugs Strategy and the EU action plan against drug trafficking, with European coordination and in collaboration with Eurojust and Europol.

As suggested by the European Union Drugs Agency —located in Lisbon—, there must be a European budget line for European resources and, of course, the protection of victims. We must stand on the side of the victims without ever having our photo taken with drug traffickers.

3-0286-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, el narcotráfico no es solo un enemigo terrible para la salud de los individuos y sociedades, hoy el narcotráfico es, además, un arma de guerra híbrida y un poder político colosal.

El crimen organizado ha entrado en la política. Hace décadas, los carteles de la droga se aliaron con la izquierda iberoamericana. Hoy, ese narcosocialismo del Foro de São Paulo ya está en Europa y entró por España. El Gobierno de Sánchez liquidó a las mejores unidades de policía antidrogas y las otras, sin medios, son impotentes. De ahí los muertos por las ventajas de los narcos que ha provocado el propio Gobierno español.

España es hoy el paraíso de los narcos gracias al Gobierno amigo. Primero, porque están abiertas todas las costas y, después, porque campan a sus anchas y porque invierten y blanquean su dinero en España.

La única forma de frenar el narcotráfico es acabar con los Gobiernos que trabajan para él; es decir, acabar con el socialismo —con el narcosocialismo— es la clave para acabar con esta plaga.
3-0286-0000.englishText:
Mr President, drug trafficking is not only a terrible enemy for the health of individuals and societies, today drug trafficking is also a hybrid warfare weapon and a colossal political power.

Organized crime has entered politics. Decades ago, drug cartels allied with the Ibero-American left. Today, that narco-socialism of the São Paulo Forum is already in Europe and entered through Spain. Sánchez's government liquidated the best anti-drug police units and the others, without resources, are powerless. Hence the deaths due to the advantages of the drug traffickers that the Spanish Government itself has caused.

Spain is today the paradise of drug traffickers thanks to the friendly government. First, because all the coasts are open, and then because they roam freely and because they invest and launder their money in Spain.

The only way to stop drug trafficking is to end the governments that work for it; that is, to end socialism—narco-socialism—is the key to ending this plague.

3-0287-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, per troppo tempo le istituzioni hanno trattato il narcotraffico, lo spaccio e il consumo di droga come un male endemico, ormai non più estirpabile, quasi invincibile, a volte da arginare, se non, nelle peggiori delle ipotesi, addirittura da ignorare o favorire.

Se vogliamo, invece, essere responsabili come persone impegnate in politica, dobbiamo dimostrare di avere un cuore aperto alla coscienza e al bene comune. Dobbiamo crederci, crederci fermamente, dobbiamo credere nel fatto che queste reti criminali possono essere sconfitte e possono essere sconfitti coloro che guadagnano sulla pelle dei più giovani e sulla morte delle persone.

E se è così, allora abbiamo il compito, il dovere, di dare gli strumenti adeguati alle nostre forze dell'ordine e di investire maggiori risorse. Dobbiamo imporre ai porti maggiori e costanti controlli, difendere i confini e usare il pugno di ferro.

Questo è l'unico modo per vincere contro i trafficanti di morte. Non possiamo infatti lasciare soli coloro che combattono, da soli, in prima linea.
3-0287-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, for too long the institutions have treated drug trafficking, drug dealing and drug consumption as an endemic evil, no longer eradicable, almost invincible, sometimes to be contained, if not, in the worst cases, even ignored or encouraged.

If, on the other hand, we want to be responsible as people engaged in politics, we must show that we have a heart open to conscience and the common good. We must believe it, firmly believe it, we must believe in the fact that these criminal networks can be defeated and those who profit from the skin of the youngest and the death of people can be defeated.

And if this is the case, then we have the task, the duty, to give the appropriate tools to our law enforcement agencies and to invest more resources. We must impose greater and constant controls on ports, defend borders and use an iron fist.

This is the only way to win against the traffickers of death. In fact, we cannot leave alone those who fight, alone, on the front line.

3-0288-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, the convicted and wanted drug lord Jos Leijdekkers remains free because Sierra Leone refuses to extradite him. One month ago, I called on the European Commission to increase pressure on Sierra Leone after the largest seizure of cocaine in the Canary Islands. The Netherlands has already made repeated requests through all available diplomatic and legal channels. Yet Sierra Leone continues to refuse cooperation. In fact, it appears to be shielding Jos Leijdekkers and even facilitating drug trafficking. This must stop now.

Drug-related organised crime undermines our security, trust in the rule of law and ultimately threatens our democracy. All European countries should therefore take this seriously and stand united in the fight against organised crime. The European Union must come forward with a concrete and comprehensive package of measures, including suspension of EU development cooperation with countries that refuse to cooperate in the extradition of convicted criminals. I ask the Commissioner: what is the current state of this confrontation and when can we expect...

(The President cut off the speaker)

3-0289-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, l'Europa attrae e consuma enormi quantità di sostanze stupefacenti in un mercato di droghe miliardario.

L'Europa è diventata luogo di incontro tra narcotraffico colombiano, narcomafie europee e italiane e organizzazioni criminali belghe, olandesi, francesi e altre.

Questo criminale mercato si alimenta anche di produzione di droga in paesi dell'Asia – dal Laos al Myanmar, dall'Afghanistan al Pakistan – con il recente allarme dell'ONU sulla provenienza di droghe sintetiche da est.

Una rete di complicità rende possibile eludere i controlli di polizia nei maggiori porti europei. Non basta accertare l'identità di quanti attraversano il Mediterraneo e l'Atlantico, è urgente intervenire e intercettare all'origine gli accordi criminali tra cartelli nello smercio verso l'Europa.

Urge, in sede di loro prevista riforma, signor Commissario, rafforzare Europol ed Eurojust nella loro lotta alla criminalità organizzata, per offrire una risposta europea forte. C'è inoltre bisogno di maggiore coordinamento per contrastare il riciclaggio dei profitti del narcotraffico tramite sistemi bancari e finanziari europei.

Considerando gli effetti che questo riciclaggio di denaro ha nella vita...

(Il Presidente toglie la parola all'oratore)
3-0289-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, Europe attracts and consumes enormous quantities of narcotics in a multi-billion-dollar drug market.

Europe has become a meeting place for Colombian drug trafficking, European and Italian drug mafias, and Belgian, Dutch, French and other criminal organisations.

This criminal market is also fuelled by drug production in Asian countries – from Laos to Myanmar, from Afghanistan to Pakistan – with the recent UN alarm over the origin of synthetic drugs from the East.

A network of complicity makes it possible to evade police checks in major European ports. It is not enough to ascertain the identity of those crossing the Mediterranean and the Atlantic; it is urgent to intervene and intercept at the source the criminal agreements between cartels in the distribution towards Europe.

It is urgent, during their planned reform, Mr Commissioner, to strengthen Europol and Eurojust in their fight against organised crime, in order to offer a strong European response. There is also a need for greater coordination to counter the laundering of drug trafficking profits through European banking and financial systems.

Considering the effects that this money laundering has on life...

(The President cuts off the speaker)

3-0290-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident! Europa steht vor einer Explosion der Drogenkriminalität, und wir erleben eine Rekordverfügbarkeit illegaler Drogen. Die EU hat die USA inzwischen als größten Kokainmarkt überholt, und bei Eurojust sind die Fallzahlen in nur fünf Jahren – nur fünf Jahren – um 60 % gestiegen; Drogen im Wert von 20 Mrd. EUR wurden festgestellt. Mehr als die Hälfte der gefährlichsten kriminellen Netzwerke Europas sind im Drogenschmuggel tätig, zwei Drittel setzen Gewalt ein, über 70 % nutzen Korruption, um Behörden und Hafenpersonal zu beeinflussen.

Das ist keine Randerscheinung mehr; das ist ein sicherheitspolitisches Totalversagen. Selbst Europol stellt fest: Die Netzwerke, die Drogen nach Europa schmuggeln, sind häufig dieselben kriminellen Strukturen, die auch illegale Migration und Menschenhandel organisieren. Die Kartelle haben längst verstanden: Europas offene Grenzen und politische Kuschelkurse sind ihr Geschäftsmodell.

Unsere Häfen dürfen nicht länger Einfallstore für Drogenkartelle sein, und unsere Grenzen dürfen nicht länger Geschäftsmodelle für Schleuser sein. Die Lösung ist so simpel und heißt: Außengrenzen sichern, Schleusernetzwerke zerschlagen und illegale Migration stoppen.
3-0290-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Europe is facing an explosion in drug crime, and we are experiencing record availability of illegal drugs. The EU has now overtaken the USA as the largest cocaine market, and case numbers at Eurojust have risen by 60% in just five years - just five years; drugs worth EUR 20 billion have been seized. More than half of Europe's most dangerous criminal networks are involved in drug smuggling, two-thirds use violence, and over 70% use corruption to influence authorities and port personnel.

This is no longer a marginal phenomenon; this is a total security policy failure. Even Europol states: The networks smuggling drugs into Europe are frequently the same criminal structures that also organise illegal migration and human trafficking. The cartels have long since understood: Europe's open borders and cozy political approaches are their business model.

Our ports must no longer be gateways for drug cartels, and our borders must no longer be business models for smugglers. The solution is so simple and is called: secure external borders, smash smuggling networks, and stop illegal migration.

3-0291-0000.sourceText:
�� Señor presidente, señorías, el narcotráfico mata: mata a quienes consumen, mata el futuro de los jóvenes, mata el Estado de Derecho y mata a los agentes que lo combaten.

Los guardias civiles asesinados en Huelva y Barbate arrollados por narcolanchas no son una tragedia aislada, son la consecuencia de años de impunidad, de falta de recursos de un Gobierno como el de Sánchez, que desprotege a las fuerzas de seguridad, que liquida OCON-Sur —la unidad clave en la lucha contra el narco—.

Europol lo ha advertido: los narcotraficantes ya no solo introducen la droga desde fuera de la Unión Europea, sino que están infiltrados en Europa. Operan desde nuestros puertos, blanquean capitales con empresas pantalla y usan armas de guerra y tecnología punta para corromper, intimidar y matar.

Europa, comisario, acierta con la Alianza Europea de Puertos, persiguiendo el dinero y cortando el oxígeno financiero de las bandas, pero el nuevo marco estratégico solo funcionará si protegemos a quienes nos protegen, tipificamos el eurodelito a cada ataque a cada policía, reconocemos la profesión de riesgo de nuestros policías.

El narcotráfico es la mayor amenaza para la seguridad de Europa y debemos estrechar la cooperación entre Europol, Eurojust, Frontex, Aduanas y las policías nacionales. Debemos exigir a cada Estado más compromiso, más agentes, más medios, más seguridad jurídica y una legislación más dura, porque solo así derrotaremos el narcotráfico. Pero no con Gobiernos que abandonen a sus policías, sino con una Europa que les reconozca, les respalde y les proteja.

(La oradora se niega a que Petras Gražulis le formule una pregunta con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0291-0000.englishText:
Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, drug trafficking kills: it kills those who consume it, it kills the future of young people, it kills the rule of law and it kills the officers who fight it.

The civil guards murdered in Huelva and Barbate, run down by drug boats, are not an isolated tragedy; they are the consequence of years of impunity and a lack of resources from a Government like that of Sánchez, which leaves the security forces unprotected, which liquidates OCON-Sur — the key unit in the fight against drug trafficking.

Europol has warned: drug traffickers no longer only smuggle drugs from outside the European Union, but are infiltrated within Europe. They operate from our ports, launder capital with shell companies and use weapons of war and cutting-edge technology to corrupt, intimidate and kill.

Europe, Commissioner, is right with the European Ports Alliance, pursuing the money and cutting off the financial oxygen of the gangs, but the new strategic framework will only work if we protect those who protect us, classify any attack on any police officer as a eurocrime, and recognise the profession of our police officers as high-risk.

Drug trafficking is the greatest threat to Europe's security and we must strengthen cooperation between Europol, Eurojust, Frontex, Customs and national police forces. We must demand from each State more commitment, more officers, more resources, more legal certainty and tougher legislation, because only in this way will we defeat drug trafficking. But not with Governments that abandon their police officers, but with a Europe that recognises them, supports them and protects them.

(The speaker refuses to take a question from Petras Gražulis under the "blue card" procedure)

3-0292-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le narcotrafic est une menace majeure pour nos sociétés. Il alimente les violences, corrompt nos économies et fragilise l’état de droit. Face à des organisations criminelles qui opèrent à l’échelle mondiale, notre réponse doit être européenne.

Mais ne nous trompons pas de combat. Le narcotrafic ne se combattra pas en entretenant la confusion entre migration et criminalité organisée. Les réseaux qui acheminent la drogue vers les ports européens n’ont rien à voir avec celles et ceux qui fuient les conflits et les persécutions. Penser qu’une politique migratoire toujours plus restrictive répondra à nos défis sécuritaires est une impasse politique et une erreur stratégique. La lutte contre le narcotrafic exige autre chose, notamment davantage de coopération entre les États membres et une action déterminée contre le blanchiment d’argent.

Soyons fermes contre les trafiquants. Soyons lucides sur les réponses à apporter. Refusons les raccourcis qui affaiblissent à la fois notre sécurité et nos valeurs.
3-0292-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, drug trafficking is a major threat to our societies. It fuels violence, corrupts our economies and undermines the rule of law. Faced with criminal organisations operating on a global scale, our response must be European.

But let us not be mistaken in our fight. Drug trafficking will not be combated by blurring the lines between migration and organised crime. The networks that channel drugs into European ports have nothing to do with those who are fleeing conflict and persecution. Believing that an ever more restrictive migration policy will address our security challenges is a political dead end and a strategic mistake. The fight against drug trafficking requires something else, notably greater cooperation between member states and decisive action against money laundering.

Let us be firm against traffickers. Let us be clear-headed about the responses to be provided. Let us reject shortcuts that weaken both our security and our values.

3-0293-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Mesdames et Messieurs, chers collègues, face au narcotrafic, il ne faut plus des mots mais des actes, car, derrière chaque cargaison interceptée, il y a désormais du sang versé dans nos villes européennes.

L’Union européenne semble enfin prendre conscience de l’ampleur de la menace. Nous avons applaudi des deux mains un accord important avec l’Équateur – dont j’ai été le rapporteur –, pays devenu un point stratégique dans le trafic de cocaïne vers l’Europe. Nous avons également tout fait pour renforcer l’agence de police européenne Europol, afin de mieux coordonner la lutte contre les réseaux criminels transnationaux.

Autant de vraies avancées contre des narcomafias qui désormais kidnappent, corrompent, intimident et, bien souvent, tuent en plein jour. Je pense au jeune Mehdi Kessaci, au père de famille et chauffeur Uber Nessim Ramdane, à Marseille, ou encore à l’étudiante Socayna Jean, victimes des balles, des kalashnikovs, des narcotrafiquants, et tous morts à Marseille, devenue capitale française du narcotrafic. Derrière Marseille, d’autres villes suivront si rien n’est fait: Anvers, Hambourg, Rotterdam. De par mon métier de policier, j’ai vu l’organisation de ces groupes et leur force de frappe sans foi ni loi. Notre faiblesse depuis des décennies est leur principal carburant.

Pour tous ceux qui l’ont payé de leur vie: reprenons le contrôle de nos frontières maritimes, protégeons nos ports stratégiques et donnons des moyens réels à nos douaniers, policiers, gendarmes, magistrats et services de renseignement!

(L'orateur accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0293-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Ladies and Gentlemen, dear colleagues, in the face of drug trafficking, we no longer need words but actions, because behind every intercepted shipment, there is now blood spilled in our European cities.

The European Union finally seems to be waking up to the scale of the threat. We enthusiastically applauded an important agreement with Ecuador—of which I was the rapporteur—a country that has become a strategic hub in the cocaine trade destined for Europe. We have also done everything possible to strengthen the European police agency, Europol, in order to better coordinate the fight against transnational criminal networks.

These are all real steps forward against drug mafias that now kidnap, corrupt, intimidate, and very often kill in broad daylight. I am thinking of young Mehdi Kessaci, family man and Uber driver Nessim Ramdane in Marseille, or student Socayna Jean, victims of bullets and Kalashnikovs from drug traffickers, all of whom died in Marseille, which has become the French capital of drug trafficking. Following Marseille, other cities will follow if nothing is done: Antwerp, Hamburg, Rotterdam. From my profession as a police officer, I have seen the organization of these groups and their ruthless striking power. Our weakness for decades has been their main fuel.

For all those who paid with their lives: let us regain control of our maritime borders, protect our strategic ports, and give real resources to our customs officers, police, gendarmes, magistrates, and intelligence services!

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

3-0294-0000.sourceText: Aš manau, kad mes visi sutiksime, kad čia nėra nei ideologijų, nei kairės, nei dešinės. Visi matome didžiulę problemą, kad tas narkotikų biznis ar nusikaltėliai klesti tiesiog Europoje. Ir viena tendencija – ar jūs nemanote, kad čia persipina jėgos struktūros su nusikalstamu pasauliu, tie, kurie turi kontroliuoti? Pavyzdžiui, Lietuvoje sulaikyta dvylika pareigūnų ir savivaldybės darbuotojai, kurie dalyvavo kontrabandoje. Ar tai yra tik Lietuvos problema? Ar čia yra visuotinė problema?
3-0294-0000.englishText: I think we will all agree that there are no ideologies here, neither left nor right. We all see the huge problem that this drug business or criminals are simply thriving in Europe. And one trend - do you not think that power structures are intertwining with the criminal world, those who are supposed to control them? For example, twelve officials and municipal employees were detained in Lithuania who participated in smuggling. Is this only Lithuania's problem? Or is this a universal problem?

3-0295-0000.sourceText:
Écoutez, cher collègue, la corruption est un combat que nous devons tous mener, mais la majorité de nos policiers, gendarmes, agents pénitentiaires, services de renseignement et militaires font un travail exceptionnel.

Je veux le redire ici: le problème, ce n’est pas majoritairement la corruption dans nos démocraties, ce sont des voyous qu’on a laissés que trop faire et qui ont bénéficié d’un laxisme judiciaire, d’un laxisme politique, d’une lâcheté… Et en France, l’extrême gauche et la gauche sont membres des partis qui défendent des voyous, des criminels, plutôt que nos policiers, nos gendarmes.

Donc, il faut changer de logiciel et il faut une vraie révolution, avec une volonté transpartisane de lutter contre ce narcotrafic, qui peut mettre à bas nos démocraties.
3-0295-0000.englishText:
Listen, dear colleague, corruption is a fight we must all wage, but the majority of our police officers, gendarmes, prison guards, intelligence services, and military personnel do an exceptional job.

I want to say it again here: the problem is not mostly corruption in our democracies, it is thugs that we have let off far too much and who have benefited from judicial laxity, political laxity, cowardice... And in France, the far left and the left are members of parties that defend thugs, criminals, rather than our police officers, our gendarmes.

Therefore, we need to change our mindset and we need a real revolution, with a cross-party willingness to fight against this drug trafficking, which can bring down our democracies.

3-0296-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Mam przekonanie, że Unia Europejska przez długi czas nie doceniała problemu ochrony granic, pozostawiając państwa na zewnętrznych granicach Unii bez dostatecznego wsparcia. Aby sprawić, że granice Unii będą bezpieczne, należy spełnić kilka warunków. Kraje graniczne muszą uzyskać znaczące wsparcie finansowe związane z zadaniami ochrony morskiej i lądowej granicy zewnętrznej. Służby krajowe muszą zostać wzmocnione i mieć stosowne narzędzia techniczne – także te, które były tu, w Parlamencie Europejskim, poddawane powszechnej krytyce. Frontex musi wszechstronnie wspierać służby krajowe, a nie prowadzić postępowania wobec funkcjonariuszy. Dość z polityczną poprawnością – państwa muszą zliberalizować przepisy dotyczące używania środków przymusu bezpośredniego, a funkcjonariuszom zapewnić bezpieczeństwo prawne.

Nie sposób nie wiązać przestępczości narkotykowej z grupami przestępczymi rekrutującymi się z obywateli państw trzecich, nielegalnych imigrantów i oszustów azylowych. Aplikujący o pobyt w Unii muszą mieć świadomość, że nieprzestrzeganie prawa wiąże się z szybką karą i skuteczną readmisją. Skuteczna ochrona granic jest pierwszym krokiem przywrócenia porządku i bezpieczeństwa w wielu miastach europejskich.
3-0296-0000.englishText:
Mr. President! I am convinced that the European Union has for a long time underestimated the problem of border protection, leaving states at the Union's external borders without sufficient support. To make the Union's borders secure, several conditions must be met. Border countries must receive significant financial support related to the tasks of maritime and land external border protection. National services must be strengthened and provided with appropriate technical tools – including those that were universally criticized here in the European Parliament. Frontex must comprehensively support national services rather than initiate proceedings against officers. Enough with political correctness – states must liberalize regulations regarding the use of direct coercive measures and ensure legal security for officers.

It is impossible not to link drug crime with criminal groups recruited from third-country nationals, illegal immigrants, and asylum fraudsters. Applicants for residence in the Union must be aware that non-compliance with the law entails swift punishment and effective readmission. Effective border protection is the first step to restoring order and security in many European cities.

3-0297-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, iedere dag weer gaan onze mensen van de politie en de douane de strijd aan tegen internationale drugsbendes. Door kleine ruimtes kruipend op zoek naar drugs, verstopt op de meest onwaarschijnlijke plekken, geïntimideerd door georganiseerde criminelen die ze proberen te corrumperen. Het gevecht tegen deze onterechte criminaliteit dwingt ons allemaal harder en slimmer te gaan lopen. Een paar heilige huisjes zullen omver moeten: minder nationaal denken, meer Europees.

Ten eerste, meer middelen, meer bevoegdheden en meer mogelijkheden voor Europol, onze unieke Europese politie, met meer operationele aanwezigheid in het veld en meer investeringen in innovaties zoals artificiële intelligentie en drones. Ten tweede, een ambitieuze Europese anti-corruptiestrategie. Zonder corruptie is er geen drugshandel. Ten derde, durven blijven investeren in preventie in onze wijken om te voorkomen dat kwetsbare kinderen gerekruteerd worden door drugscriminelen. Narcos is meer dan een Netflixtitel en cosmetische oplossingen krijgen van mij een duimpje omlaag.

(De spreker stemt ermee in om te antwoorden op een “blauwe kaart”-vraag)
3-0297-0000.englishText:
Mr President, every single day our police and customs officers fight a battle against international drug gangs. Crawling through small spaces looking for drugs hidden in the most unlikely places, intimidated by organised criminals trying to corrupt them. The fight against this unjustified criminality forces all of us to run harder and smarter. A few sacred cows will have to be overthrown: less national thinking, more European.

First, more resources, more powers and more opportunities for Europol, our unique European police force, with more operational presence in the field and more investment in innovations such as artificial intelligence and drones. Second, an ambitious European anti-corruption strategy. Without corruption there is no drug trade. Third, daring to continue investing in prevention in our neighbourhoods to prevent vulnerable children from being recruited by drug criminals. Narcos is more than a Netflix title and cosmetic solutions get a thumbs down from me.

(The speaker agrees to answer a "blue card" question)

3-0298-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Deputada García Hermida-Van Der Walle, ouvimos neste debate um deputado da extrema-direita espanhola, Hermann Tertsch, fazer uma diferença entre o tráfico de droga, que é mau se vier de alguns países, mas que já pode não ser tão mau se vier de outros.

A mim parece-me que isto é um aproveitamento político verdadeiramente indecente do tráfico de droga e é particularmente difícil de compreender como é que é possível fazer este tipo de aproveitamento quando estão em causa, por exemplo, as vidas de profissionais das forças e serviços de segurança, como aqueles que foram, infelizmente, assassinados em operações de combate à droga.

O que lhe pergunto é se não acha que este é um aproveitamento que não devia ser feito?
3-0298-0000.englishText:
Madam Deputy García Hermida-Van Der Walle, we heard in this debate a deputy of the Spanish far-right, Hermann Tertsch, make a distinction between drug trafficking, which is bad if it comes from some countries, but may not be as bad if it comes from others.

It seems to me that this is a truly indecent political exploitation of drug trafficking and it is particularly difficult to understand how it is possible to make this type of exploitation when the lives of security forces and services professionals are at stake, such as those who were, unfortunately, murdered in anti-drug operations.

What I ask you is whether you do not think that this is an exploitation that should not be done?

3-0299-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, thank you colleague Oliveira, yes – debates get hijacked all the time in this House by those who want to put every single fault on a single country or a single group of people. To me, it is really important to understand that drug trafficking is from all times.

Colleague Tertsch will remember that, in Spain, the country that I come from originally, we had huge problems with drug gangs in Galicia and they were all home-grown. They were not coming from outside the European Union – they were Spanish home-grown. In the Netherlands we see criminals that are international, but also home-grown, and in other countries we see the same. So it's really important that we take this as the problem that it is and not try to make it into a different problem which citizens are not particularly interested in.

3-0300-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, how many women have to be raped and murdered before you all start doing anything? How many children have to die at the hands of vile criminals and murderers before you realise what is happening outside? How many seniors have to become victims of those criminals in Europe before you start thinking about the future of Europe and the safety of Europeans? We just need to secure our external borders right now, immediately – we need to protect our borders at all costs.

People just deserve this safety, and we need to start with mass deportations right now. Every illegal immigrant from Europe has to be deported – even every legal immigrant who does not respect our way of life and our laws and committed a crime has to be deported. As soon as you do this, you will realise how the narco-trafficking problem, which we are discussing right now, just disappears. As soon as you do this, you will see how the numbers of rapes, violent attacks and murders just drops down.

If you are not ready to fight for Europe, then we need to replace you, defeat you in the elections and save Europe for our children.

3-0301-0000.sourceText: Thank you, colleague, but words like 'mass deportations' are not approved here. We will do it according to the Rules. The European Union is not doing mass deportations.

3-0302-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signor Commissario, onorevoli colleghi, la recente perdita di due agenti della Guardia civile spagnola per lo speronamento da parte di una barca di narcotrafficanti è l'ennesima dimostrazione di quanto il traffico di stupefacenti costituisca una seria minaccia per le nostre società.

Come mamma di due appartenenti alle forze dell'ordine voglio esprimere la mia solidarietà alle loro famiglie.

Enormi profitti per le organizzazioni criminali, perdita di vite umane, corruzione, riciclaggio, violenza dilagante, minori reclutati, insicurezza ed enormi costi sanitari e sociali: tutto questo è ed è sempre stato il traffico di droga.

E l'impatto sull'Europa – mercato di consumo, hub di transito e luogo di produzione – è davvero enorme. Dobbiamo quindi proseguire con decisione nell'attuazione della strategia ProtectEU e soprattutto nel piano d'azione per individuare e contrastare le rotte di traffico marittime, terrestri e aeree, rafforzare la cooperazione tra Frontex, Europol, l'MAOC-N e le forze di polizia nazionali, migliorare lo scambio di informazioni tra autorità doganali di contrasto e giudiziarie e rafforzare la cooperazione con i paesi terzi di origine degli stupefacenti.

Per questo occorre dotare di risorse e di mezzi le nostre forze di polizia, ma occorre anche investire in prevenzione e recupero per contrastare non solo l'offerta, ma anche la domanda di stupefacenti.

È questa, contro la droga, una battaglia non facile, è vero, ma che l'Unione europea intera non può permettersi di perdere.
3-0302-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, honourable members, the recent loss of two members of the Spanish Guardia Civil after being rammed by a drug traffickers' boat is yet another demonstration of how drug trafficking constitutes a serious threat to our societies.

As the mother of two members of law enforcement, I want to express my solidarity with their families.

Enormous profits for criminal organisations, loss of human life, corruption, money laundering, rampant violence, recruited minors, insecurity and huge health and social costs: all of this is and has always been drug trafficking.

And the impact on Europe – a consumer market, transit hub and production place – is truly enormous. We must therefore resolutely continue with the implementation of the ProtectEU strategy and, above all, the action plan to identify and counter maritime, land and air trafficking routes, strengthen cooperation between Frontex, Europol, MAOC-N and national police forces, improve information exchange between customs law enforcement and judicial authorities, and strengthen cooperation with third countries of origin of narcotics.

For this reason, it is necessary to provide our police forces with resources and means, but it is also necessary to invest in prevention and recovery to combat not only the supply, but also the demand for drugs.

This is not an easy battle against drugs, it is true, but one that the entire European Union cannot afford to lose.

3-0303-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Europe's ports have become a gateway for organised crime. Record amounts of cocaine are entering the European Union, fuelling violence, corruption and criminal networks. Our law enforcement officers, custom authorities and coastguards deserve all our support. They need better tools, modern technology and stronger cooperation across Europe, not more bureaucracy.

But if we are talking about corruption, we also need to talk about protecting the workers in the ports, because we all know how much money the organised crime has, and sometimes the port workers, without protection, have to make the choice between their lives or being corrupted. So it goes hand in hand. If we talk about our law enforcement authorities, they have to have better tools, but we also need to protect the workers in the ports.

The fight against drug trafficking starts at our borders. We need stronger port security, closer cooperation between Member States and Europol, and the relentless effort to dismantle criminal networks and seize their assets. The safety of our citizens depends on it.

3-0304-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señor comisario, hoy no voy a hablar de lo peligrosas que son las mafias del Estrecho. Eso ya lo sabemos todos: sabemos que tienen más dinero, sabemos que, sorprendentemente, tienen más medios y sabemos que son cada vez más violentas.

Lo que no entiendo es por qué seguimos tratando a quien nos defiende como si el problema no fuera sangrante. En la frontera del sur de España, los guardias civiles mueren, señorías, mueren y no tienen reconocida la tan peleada profesión de riesgo. Todavía seguimos sin considerar eurodelito las agresiones a las fuerzas y cuerpos de seguridad europeos que se juegan la vida, cada día, frente a criminales con armas de guerra, sin seguridad física y sin seguridad jurídica.

Y todavía hay Gobiernos en los que se toman decisiones incomprensibles, como el de España, al desmantelar la unidad OCON‑Sur, una unidad que había logrado miles de detenciones y algunos de los mayores golpes al narcotráfico en el Campo de Gibraltar.

Este es el mensaje que reciben las mafias. Ellas se organizan, ellas se arman, avanzan y nosotros desmantelamos herramientas que funcionan. Señorías, despierten: la violencia extrema se combate con medios, con contundencia y con autoridad.
3-0304-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, today I am not going to talk about how dangerous the mafias of the Strait are. We all already know that: we know they have more money, we know that, surprisingly, they have more resources and we know that they are increasingly violent.

What I do not understand is why we continue to treat those who defend us as if the problem were not bleeding. At the southern border of Spain, civil guards are dying, ladies and gentlemen, they are dying and they do not have the hard-fought profession of risk recognized. We still continue not to consider as a European crime the attacks on European security forces who risk their lives every day against criminals with weapons of war, without physical security and without legal certainty.

And there are still Governments in which incomprehensible decisions are made, such as that of Spain, by dismantling the OCON-Sur unit, a unit that had achieved thousands of arrests and some of the biggest blows against drug trafficking in the Campo de Gibraltar.

This is the message that the mafias receive. They organize, they arm themselves, they advance and we dismantle tools that work. Ladies and gentlemen, wake up: extreme violence is combated with resources, with forcefulness and with authority.

3-0305-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, κύριε Επίτροπε, σήμερα βρισκόμαστε εδώ όχι μόνο για να συζητήσουμε αλλά κυρίως για να εκφράσουμε την ευγνωμοσύνη και τον σεβασμό μας στους αφανείς ήρωες, στις γυναίκες και στους άνδρες του Πολεμικού Ναυτικού, των εθνικών ακτοφυλακών, των σωμάτων ασφαλείας, της Frontex και όλων των ευρωπαϊκών υπηρεσιών που αγωνίζονται για την καταπολέμηση της μάστιγας των ναρκωτικών· σε όλους εκείνους που με αυταπάρνηση και υψηλό αίσθημα καθήκοντος φυλάσσουν τα εθνικά και ευρωπαϊκά μας σύνορα.

Η απειλή των ναρκωτικών μπορεί πολλές φορές να μοιάζει μακρινή και αθέατη, στην πραγματικότητα όμως είναι διαρκής, οργανωμένη και αδυσώπητη. Γνωρίζουμε καλά το βαρύ αποτύπωμα στις γειτονιές, στους δρόμους και στις πόλεις μας. Γνωρίζουμε όμως εξίσου καλά ότι η καταπολέμηση των ναρκωτικών απαιτεί συνεχή επαγρύπνηση, άριστο συντονισμό και διεθνή συνεργασία. Γι' αυτό οφείλουμε από αυτή την αίθουσα να ενισχύουμε διαρκώς το έργο όσων επιχειρούν καθημερινά στις θάλασσες και στα λιμάνια της Ευρώπης, στην πρώτη γραμμή της μάχης απέναντι στο οργανωμένο έγκλημα. Κάθε φορτίο ναρκωτικών που αναχαιτίζεται δεν θα φτάσει ποτέ στις κοινωνίες μας. Και κάθε εγκληματικό δίκτυο που εξαρθρώνεται είναι μια νίκη για την ασφάλεια, την ανθρώπινη αξιοπρέπεια και τη συνοχή των κοινωνιών της Ευρώπης.
3-0305-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, today we are here not only to discuss but above all to express our gratitude and respect to the unsung heroes, the women and men of the Navy, national coastguards, law enforcement agencies, Frontex and all European services fighting to combat the scourge of drugs; to all those who, with self-denial and a high sense of duty, guard our national and European borders.

The threat of drugs may often seem distant and unseen, but in reality it is continuous, organized and relentless. We know well the heavy footprint in our neighborhoods, streets and cities. But we know equally well that the fight against drugs requires constant vigilance, excellent coordination and international cooperation. That is why from this chamber we must constantly strengthen the work of those operating daily in Europe's seas and ports, at the forefront of the battle against organized crime. Every drug shipment intercepted will never reach our societies. And every criminal network dismantled is a victory for the security, human dignity and cohesion of Europe's societies.

3-0307-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, si le narcotrafic prospère, c’est parce que – disons-le – nos frontières sont devenues des passoires et que l’Union européenne continue de multiplier les obstacles à ceux qui sont chargés de les protéger. Nos policiers, nos douaniers et nos magistrats ont besoin d’une coopération renforcée, pas d’une bureaucratie supplémentaire. Il faut faciliter la collecte et l’échange des données entre les autorités nationales, Europol, Frontex et Eurojust. Les cartels, eux, n’attendent pas les autorisations de Bruxelles pour partager leurs informations.

Pourtant, le Contrôleur européen de la protection des données a suspendu la coopération entre Europol et Frontex. C’est une décision totalement déconnectée de la réalité du terrain. À force de privilégier les contraintes administratives sur l’efficacité opérationnelle, ce sont les criminels qui en sortent gagnants.

Nous devons également clarifier le rôle de la future Agence européenne des douanes. Il n’est pas question de créer une nouvelle couche institutionnelle qui viendrait brouiller les missions d’Europol et de Frontex.

Enfin, donnons à l’Alliance des ports européens les moyens d’échanger librement leurs renseignements avec les autorités de police et de justice. Face à des mafias toujours plus puissantes, notre réponse doit être simple: plus de coopération, plus de renseignement, plus d’efficacité et moins d’idéologie.
3-0307-0000.englishText:
Madam President, if drug trafficking is thriving, it is because – let us be frank – our borders have become like sieves and the European Union continues to multiply the obstacles facing those responsible for protecting them. Our police officers, customs officers and magistrates need enhanced cooperation, not additional bureaucracy. We must facilitate the collection and exchange of data between national authorities, Europol, Frontex and Eurojust. The cartels do not wait for authorization from Brussels to share their information.

Yet the European Data Protection Supervisor has suspended cooperation between Europol and Frontex. This is a decision completely disconnected from the reality on the ground. By constantly prioritizing administrative constraints over operational efficiency, it is the criminals who emerge victorious.

We must also clarify the role of the future European Customs Agency. There is no question of creating a new institutional layer that would blur the missions of Europol and Frontex.

Finally, let us give the European Ports Alliance the means to freely exchange intelligence with police and judicial authorities. Faced with increasingly powerful mafias, our response must be simple: more cooperation, more intelligence, more efficiency and less ideology.

3-0308-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, un vas pleacă încărcat cu 10 tone de cocaină dintr-o țară sud-americană către Europa; fiul de 16 ani al unui doctor din Bruxelles - sau din Paris, sau din Berlin, sau din Roma, sau din București - încearcă primul său gram la o petrecere. Este un copil bun, cu rezultate extraordinare la școală, bine educat de părinți și cu un viitor luminos în față - sau cel puțin așa trebuia să-i fie viitorul până la acel prim gram. Știe că nu este bun, dar prietenii râd de el că nu are curaj să încerce și își spune că este puternic și că va fi o singură dată, apoi se va opri.

În timp ce băiatul trage prima sa linie de „zăpadă” sau „pudra morții”, alt vas încărcat ajunge într-un port european și reușește să descarce marfa. Zecile de tone înseamnă sute de mii, chiar milioane de victime, de dependenți, de tineri care își anulează viitorul, de copii buni precum al meu sau ai voștri.

Și fix în timp ce se întâmplă toate astea, în Parlamentul European, unii colegi de-ai noștri votează să nu întărească structurile de forță competente în combaterea traficului de droguri. Adică fix acele structuri care ar fi putut opri cele două vase venite de pe mare și ne-ar fi putut salva copiii.
3-0308-0000.englishText:
Madam President, a ship leaves loaded with 10 tons of cocaine from a South American country towards Europe; the 16-year-old son of a doctor from Brussels - or from Paris, or from Berlin, or from Rome, or from Bucharest - tries his first gram at a party. He is a good child, with extraordinary school results, well-educated by his parents and with a bright future ahead of him - or at least his future was supposed to be like that until that first gram. He knows it is no good, but his friends laugh at him for not having the courage to try and he tells himself that he is strong and that it will be just once, then he will stop.

While the boy snorts his first line of "snow" or "powder of death", another loaded ship arrives in a European port and manages to unload the cargo. The tens of tons mean hundreds of thousands, even millions of victims, of addicts, of young people whose future is cancelled, of good children like mine or yours.

And right while all this is happening, in the European Parliament, some of our colleagues vote not to strengthen the competent law enforcement structures in combating drug trafficking. Meaning precisely those structures that could have stopped the two ships coming from the sea and could have saved our children.

3-0309-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, les cartels entrent en Europe par nos failles. La ligne portée en France par Bruno Retailleau doit trouver son prolongement européen. Le narcotrafic n’est plus l’écume de faits divers dispersés, c’est une puissance criminelle, maritime, financière, territoriale. Elle défie nos États, elle jauge nos frontières, elle appelle des moyens d’exception.

Cette puissance transforme nos scrupules en couloir de circulation. Quand il faut empêcher un trafiquant identifié de revenir sur son point de deal, une partie de la gauche trouve l’État trop ferme. Quand les habitants réclament de l’air, elle rouvre le débat sur la dépénalisation. C’est une étrange boussole: moins de contraintes pour les dealers, plus d’abandon pour nos populations.

Lorsque la drogue entre par la mer, c’est l’Europe qui prend l’eau, emportée par une vague qui gagne nos campagnes, qui finit par recruter, par abîmer et par tuer nos enfants. Alors, passons aux actes! Faisons de nos ports des zones de riposte douanière, avec coordination inter-services, commandements clairs, contrôles ciblés vingt-quatre heures sur vingt-quatre, protection des agents menacés. Faisons payer les cartels pour la sécurité: chaque euro doit équiper les services répressifs. Il ne suffit plus d’écoper, il faut définitivement reprendre le gouvernail!

(L'oratrice accepte une question carton bleu)
3-0309-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Mr Commissioner, cartels are entering Europe through our vulnerabilities. The line pursued in France by Bruno Retailleau must find its European extension. Drug trafficking is no longer just a scattering of isolated news items; it is a maritime, financial, and territorial criminal power. It challenges our states, tests our borders, and calls for exceptional resources.

This power turns our scruples into a transit corridor. When it is necessary to prevent an identified trafficker from returning to their dealing spot, part of the left finds the state too firm. When residents demand some breathing room, it reopens the debate on decriminalisation. This is a strange compass: fewer constraints for dealers, more abandonment for our populations.

When drugs enter by sea, it is Europe that is springing leaks, swept away by a wave that reaches our countryside, ends up recruiting, harming, and killing our children. So let us take action! Let us turn our ports into zones of customs retaliation, with inter-agency coordination, clear commands, targeted twenty-four-hour controls, and the protection of threatened agents. Let us make the cartels pay for security: every euro must equip law enforcement services. It is no longer enough to bail out water; we must permanently take back the helm!

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

3-0310-0000.sourceText:
Céline Imart, vous parlez de Bruno Retailleau et du narcotrafic en France: hier, la présomption de légitime défense a été adoptée à l’Assemblée nationale. On va enfin croire nos policiers avant les voyous.

Mais, pendant un an, Monsieur Retailleau était à Beauvau: réforme de la police judiciaire, recrutement des OPJ, paiement des heures supplémentaires, simplification de la procédure pénale, mais aussi peines planchers, peines minimales pour lutter contre les récidivistes et les délinquants qui s’en prennent à l’uniforme de la République.

Vous ne l’avez pas fait pendant un an: du courage, Céline Imart, rejoignez Marine Le Pen et Jordan Bardella! Le redressement, c’est maintenant! Ce que vous n’avez pas pu ou voulu faire, faites-le à nos côtés! Le pronostic vital de notre pays est engagé.
3-0310-0000.englishText:
Céline Imart, you are talking about Bruno Retailleau and drug trafficking in France: yesterday, the presumption of self-defense was adopted in the National Assembly. We are finally going to believe our police officers before the thugs.

But, for a year, Mr. Retailleau was at Beauvau: reform of the judicial police, recruitment of judicial police officers, payment of overtime, simplification of criminal procedure, but also mandatory minimum sentences, minimum sentences to fight against recidivists and delinquents who attack the uniform of the Republic.

You did not do it for a year: have courage, Céline Imart, join Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella! Recovery is now! What you could not or did not want to do, do it by our side! The vital prognosis of our country is engaged.

3-0311-0000.sourceText:
Merci, Monsieur Valet, pour votre très aimable invitation. Je tiens à vous rappeler que Bruno Retailleau n’était pas ministre de la justice, mais ministre de l’intérieur. Donc, il a agi sur les compétences qu’il avait à l’intérieur de son portefeuille, qui malheureusement ne concernent pas notamment la justice pour les mineurs.

Mais il a agi sur ce qui, dans son portefeuille, pouvait être fait, c’est-à-dire avoir une loi d’urgence narcotrafic, qui va aller taper les trafiquants au portefeuille, qui va mobiliser les forces de l’ordre et les rendre plus efficaces sur ces points de deal.

Je crois que nous avons des convictions assez similaires sur ce sujet, et en tout cas le combat continue à l’échelle française, mais aussi à l’échelle européenne, parce que ce combat-là, il est vital pour nos enfants.
3-0311-0000.englishText:
Thank you, Mr. Valet, for your very kind invitation. I would like to remind you that Bruno Retailleau was not Minister of Justice, but Minister of the Interior. Therefore, he acted within the powers he had within his portfolio, which unfortunately do not notably concern juvenile justice.

But he acted on what could be done within his portfolio, that is to say, having an emergency anti-narcotics law, which will hit traffickers in the pocketbook, which will mobilize law enforcement and make them more effective on these drug dealing spots.

I believe we have quite similar convictions on this subject, and in any case the fight continues on a French scale, but also on a European scale, because this fight is vital for our children.

3-0312-0000.sourceText:
Fru formand! Kære kollegaer. Jeg har været politibetjent i 19 år, og jeg ved, hvad narkotika i virkeligheden er. Det er at banke på en dør klokken to om natten. En far og en mor åbner, og deres ansigter krakelerer, når de forstår, hvorfor. Deres barn er død af en overdosis. Det glemmer man aldrig.

Imens så strømmer kokainen ind gennem Europas havne og grænser. Og hvad gør EU? De skriver strategier, mens narkobagmændene tjener milliarder. Strategier alene stopper ikke forbryderne. Det gør betjentene, tolderne og effektiv kontrol. Så løsningen, det er ikke mere EU. Løsningen er permanent grænse- og havnekontrol, stærke nationale politistyrker og hårdere straffe. Giv landene magten tilbage og politiet de redskaber, der skal til for at stoppe forbryderne.

Mine gamle kollegaer knokler hver evig eneste dag, så svigt dem ikke. Det skylder vi både dem og vores unge mennesker.

(Taleren accepterede at besvare et blåt kort-spørgsmål)
3-0312-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Dear colleagues. I have been a police officer for 19 years, and I know what drugs really are. It is knocking on a door at two o'clock in the night. A father and a mother open, and their faces crack when they understand why. Their child has died of an overdose. You never forget that.
