Meanwhile, cocaine is streaming in through Europe's ports and borders. And what does the EU do? They write strategies while the drug masterminds earn billions. Strategies alone do not stop the criminals. Police officers, customs officers and effective control do. So the solution is not more EU. The solution is permanent border and port control, strong national police forces and tougher punishments. Give countries back the power and the police the tools needed to stop the criminals.

My old colleagues are working their fingers to the bone every single day, so do not fail them. We owe that to both them and our young people.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

3-0313-0000.sourceText: Next year, the 'Prüm Regulation' will enter into force for automated data exchange of DNA profiles, fingerprints and number plates of vehicles of criminals. Your country, Denmark, cannot participate in this system and will not be able to exchange data of criminals with other countries. How do you think Denmark can stay a safe country without this key instrument if it keeps the opt‑out on justice and home affairs?

3-0314-0000.sourceText:
Jeg er rigtig stolt af, at vi i Danmark har vores retsforbehold, for jeg har selv arbejdet med international og grænseoverskridende kriminalitet igennem 10 år. Og vores retsforbehold i Danmark beskytter både politiet og vores lovgivning. Det beskytter således, at vi faktisk kan implementere nye efterforskningsmetoder uden at skulle spørge EU om lov. Og det gør, at man kan tilpasse efterforskningsmetoderne inden for det land, man nu kommer fra.

Så jeg er stolt af, at vi i Danmark har et retsforbehold, som beskytter os på lige præcis det her område. Og til det skal jeg også sige, at i og med at jeg selv har arbejdet inden for det her område, så har vi en lang række parallelaftaler i Danmark. Og Danmark er måske en af dem, der er mest førende og bedst til at opklare international organiseret kriminalitet. Så derfor har vi parallelaftaler, som gør, at vi kan få alle de samme oplysninger, som man sidder og forhandler om i den nye aftale.
3-0314-0000.englishText:
I am really proud that we in Denmark have our justice opt-out, because I have myself worked with international and cross-border crime for 10 years. And our justice opt-out in Denmark protects both the police and our legislation. It thus protects the fact that we can actually implement new investigation methods without having to ask the EU for permission. And it means that one can adapt the investigation methods within the country one happens to come from.

So I am proud that we in Denmark have a justice opt-out that protects us in this exact area. And to that I must also say that seeing as I have myself worked within this area, we have a large number of parallel agreements in Denmark. And Denmark is perhaps one of those that is most leading and best at solving international organized crime. So therefore we have parallel agreements that mean we can get all the same information that is being negotiated in the new agreement.

3-0315-0000.sourceText: Thank you so much for your answer and I really appreciate your service as a police officer, also having worked in a border region. But the whole point here is automated data. When a criminal is crossing from, say, Germany into Denmark, if you cannot have access to automated data exchange, then it is impossible for you to know what that person has done and why it might pose a risk to your country. So wouldn't you want to solve that by being part of the Prüm Regulation and other parts of the justice system of the European Union?

3-0316-0000.sourceText: Tak for spørgsmålet. Det kan man løse, og det løser man allerede i dag, fordi man har, med de her parallelaftaler, fuldstændig adgang til alle de her oplysninger. Det er blevet nummerpladeregistrering, vi har samarbejdet med Europol, vi har selv et kontor dernede, vi kan få DNA-svar osv. Så jeg ved, at det her er muligt i Danmark, og jeg har selv gjort det utallige gange, og oplysningerne er kun et opkald væk. Og jeg kan supplere med, at Danmark sidste år har sendt 40 000 SIENA-anmodninger, som også er et samarbejde, man har. Så vores parallelaftaler gælder faktisk ikke kun Europa, men også uden for, og det gør, at vi står langt stærkere i efterforskning af kriminalitet i Danmark.
3-0316-0000.englishText: Thank you for the question. That can be solved, and it is already being solved today, because with these parallel agreements, you have complete access to all this information. It has become license plate registration, we have cooperated with Europol, we have an office down there ourselves, we can get DNA answers, etc. So I know that this is possible in Denmark, and I have done it countless times myself, and the information is only a phone call away. And I can add that last year Denmark sent 40,000 SIENA requests, which is also a cooperation one has. So our parallel agreements actually apply not only to Europe, but also outside, and this means that we are in a much stronger position in the investigation of crime in Denmark.

3-0317-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Nie da się mówić o przestępczości zorganizowanej, która trudni się handlem narkotykami, bez tematu nielegalnej imigracji. Tak się składa, że akurat koalicja rządząca w Unii Europejskiej jest odpowiedzialna za wpuszczenie nielegalnych imigrantów. Więc jeżeli chcecie zwalczyć drogę dotyczącą narkotyków, to musicie też zająć się nielegalną imigracją. Temat, który dotyczy konsekwencji chociażby za pomoc związaną z nielegalnymi imigrantami pod przykrywką organizacji pozarządowych, leży i nie jest dalej procedowany, dlatego, że lewica to blokuje.

Może warto zwrócić uwagę na to, jakim doświadczeniem może podzielić się Polska. Tak się składa, że miałem przyjemność być w rządzie, który zatrzymał nielegalną migrację, który doprowadził do tego, że odsyłano nielegalnych migrantów.

Ale co się dzieje? Zaraz na drugi dzień przyjmujecie rozwiązania, które są związane z paktem migracyjnym. Chcecie, aby ci migranci, z których wielu trudni się działalnością przestępczą – wzrost przestępczości na różnym tle, w tym seksualnym, jest gigantyczny – zostali przerzuceni do innych krajów? Więc prosta odpowiedź jest taka: zero nielegalnych migrantów i zamkniemy również temat związany ze skalą problemu z narkotykami.
3-0317-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is impossible to talk about organized crime involved in drug trafficking without addressing the issue of illegal immigration. As it happens, the ruling coalition in the European Union is responsible for letting in illegal immigrants. So if you want to combat the drug route, you also have to deal with illegal immigration. The issue concerning the consequences of, for example, aiding illegal immigrants under the guise of non-governmental organizations is stalled and is no longer being processed because the left is blocking it.

Perhaps it is worth paying attention to the experience that Poland can share. As it happens, I had the pleasure of being in a government that stopped illegal migration, that led to the deportation of illegal migrants.

But what happens? The very next day you adopt solutions related to the migration pact. Do you want these migrants—many of whom engage in criminal activity; the increase in crime on various grounds, including sexual, is gigantic—to be relocated to other countries? So the simple answer is this: zero illegal migrants, and we will also close the issue related to the scale of the drug problem.

3-0318-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, igual les parezco un poco dura, pero voy a decir algo.

La droga que mañana van a ofrecer a cualquiera de nuestros hijos, la cocaína en cualquier capital europea, probablemente venga de España, todo un país europeo.

España es la principal puerta del sur de Europa, y es una puerta que está completamente abierta. Es la puerta por la que se está colando buena parte de la droga que está envenenando nuestro continente.

Tranquilos, porque esta frontera tiene guardianes, guardias civiles valientes que cada noche salen a plantarle cara al narco con más vocación que recursos. Pero quiero decirle algo, comisario: les estamos mandando a la guerra sin armas. Mientras enfrente tienen semisumergibles y armamento bélico, detrás tienen un Estado cada vez más débil y un Gobierno enfermo de corrupción.

Ha muerto gente en Barbate, han muerto en Huelva y van a seguir muriendo. Porque los criminales los matan, sí. Pero por falta también de nuestra voluntad política. Así que, comisario, por favor, más recursos para Europa y para Frontex, más inteligencia compartida, penas más duras contra los criminales.

No esperemos al próximo funeral para reconocer el peligro. Son una profesión de riesgo.
3-0318-0000.englishText:
Mr President, I may seem a little harsh to you, but I am going to say something.

The drugs that tomorrow will be offered to any of our children, the cocaine in any European capital, will probably come from Spain, a whole European country.

Spain is the main gateway to southern Europe, and it is a gateway that is completely open. It is the gateway through which a large part of the drugs poisoning our continent are slipping.

Rest assured, because this border has guardians, brave civil guards who every night go out to stand up to drug trafficking with more vocation than resources. But I want to tell you something, Commissioner: we are sending them to war without weapons. While opposite them they have semi-submersibles and military weaponry, behind them they have an increasingly weaker State and a Government sick with corruption.

People have died in Barbate, they have died in Huelva and they are going to keep dying. Because criminals kill them, yes. But also due to a lack of our political will. So, Commissioner, please, more resources for Europe and for Frontex, more shared intelligence, harsher sentences against criminals.

Let us not wait for the next funeral to recognise the danger. Theirs is a high-risk profession.

3-0319-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Tylko w 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad półtora miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. Belgijska Antwerpia jest dla gangów narkotykowych bramą przemytu do Europy – przypadkiem, tuż pod nosem eurokratów, tych nauczycieli praworządności.

W latach 2018–2023 liczba pacjentów rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów związanych z kokainą wzrosła o 31%. Liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu uzależnienia od cracku wzrosła o 35%. Taka skala przemytu narkotyków to dzieło Komisji Europejskiej. To polityka otwartych granic. W czasie, gdy Europejczycy boją się gangów narkotykowych w swoich miastach, kartele narkotykowe traktują europejskie wybrzeża i porty jak swoje magazyny. Służby ochrony granic potrzebują realnego wsparcia, twardego prawa i wolnej ręki w działaniu, a nie ataku lewicowej agendy ze strony Komisji Europejskiej.

Powiem szczerze: brak waszej skuteczności w zwalczaniu przemytu narkotyków do Europy nasuwa pytanie, czy wy czasami nie współpracujecie z przemytnikami i nie czerpiecie jakichś korzyści finansowych z handlu narkotykami w Europie. Tak dla kolegi pytam.
3-0319-0000.englishText:
Madam President! In 2024 alone, European Union member states reported over one and a half million drug-related crimes. Belgian Antwerp is the gateway for drug gangs smuggling into Europe – coincidentally, right under the nose of Eurocrats, those teachers of the rule of law.

Between 2018 and 2023, the number of patients starting treatment for cocaine-related problems increased by 31%. The number of people starting treatment for crack addiction increased by 35%. Such a scale of drug smuggling is the work of the European Commission. This is an open-border policy. At a time when Europeans are afraid of drug gangs in their cities, drug cartels treat European coasts and ports like their warehouses. Border protection services need real support, tough laws, and a free hand in action, not an attack by the leftist agenda from the European Commission.

I will be honest: your lack of effectiveness in combating drug smuggling into Europe raises the question of whether you sometimes cooperate with smugglers and derive some financial benefits from the drug trade in Europe. I'm asking for a friend, so to speak.

3-0321-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário, a nova estratégia de combate às drogas da União Europeia não pode repetir dois erros: esquecer a emergência do combate às drogas sintéticas, ignorar que as suas fronteiras ocidentais começam no coração do Atlântico com os Açores e com a Madeira.

É pelo Atlântico que têm passado rotas cada vez mais exploradas por redes internacionais de tráfico de droga, com barcos, drones e até narcossubmarinos. É por isso que é urgente reforçar a vigilância marítima, a tecnologia, a partilha de informação, a cooperação para as agências europeias, mas também o reconhecimento da importância das nossas forças de segurança que tanto têm feito com tão pouco.

Precisamos também de reconhecer que as fronteiras externas da União Europeia começam pelos Açores e pela Madeira, e os Açores e a Madeira têm um papel fundamental na segurança da União Europeia. E é também por isso que precisamos de ter uma nova estratégia para o Atlântico, que enquadre as novas tensões geopolíticas, mas também o combate ao tráfico de droga e a segurança da União Europeia.
3-0321-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, the European Union's new drug strategy cannot repeat two mistakes: forgetting the emergency of fighting synthetic drugs, and ignoring that its western borders begin in the heart of the Atlantic with the Azores and Madeira.

It is through the Atlantic that routes increasingly exploited by international drug trafficking networks have been passing, with boats, drones and even narco-submarines. That is why it is urgent to reinforce maritime surveillance, technology, information sharing, and cooperation for European agencies, as well as the recognition of the importance of our security forces who have done so much with so little.

We also need to recognize that the European Union's external borders begin with the Azores and Madeira, and the Azores and Madeira play a fundamental role in the security of the European Union. And that is also why we need a new strategy for the Atlantic, which frames new geopolitical tensions, but also the fight against drug trafficking and the security of the European Union.

3-0322-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, i nostri confini sono un colabrodo e voi lo sapete.

Oggi parliamo di narcotraffico nel Mediterraneo, ma la droga è il sintomo: la malattia è che noi non difendiamo i nostri confini, perché ogni anno dai nostri porti arrivano tonnellate di droga – soprattutto dal Nord Africa – che stanno uccidendo migliaia di giovani europei.

Quella stessa rotta, che negli ultimi 15 anni ha portato clandestinamente, via mare, un milione e mezzo di immigrati in Italia e tre milioni in Europa, è stata sfruttata anche per trafficare droga e armi e alimentare profitti miliardari per le mafie.

Mentre voi predicavate porti aperti e mentre von der Leyen e le sinistre europee trasformavano Frontex in un bersaglio ideologico, scafisti e organizzazioni criminali facevano affari d'oro.

Difendere i confini non è uno slogan, è l'unico strumento serio e concreto per bloccare il narcotraffico.
3-0322-0000.englishText: Madam President, honourable colleagues, our borders are like a sieve and you know it. Today we are talking about drug trafficking in the Mediterranean, but drugs are the symptom: the disease is that we do not defend our borders, because every year tons of drugs arrive from our ports – especially from North Africa – which are killing thousands of young Europeans. That same route, which over the last 15 years has clandestinely brought a million and a half immigrants by sea to Italy and three million to Europe, has also been exploited to traffic drugs and weapons and fuel billionaire profits for the mafias. While you preached open ports and while von der Leyen and the European left turned Frontex into an ideological target, smugglers and criminal organisations made a fortune. Defending borders is not a slogan, it is the only serious and concrete tool to block drug trafficking.

3-0323-0000.sourceText: Madam President, let us be brutally blunt: Europe is losing control of its security. Open‑border policies fuel chaos, turning narco‑trafficking into a real threat for all of us. The core issue is a catastrophic failure of integration. Multigenerational migrant neighbourhoods are forming parallel societies that reject European values. In Sweden, second generation migrants dominate gangs behind record bombings. In France, suburb drug wars drive hundreds of narco‑homicides. Criminal groups exploit this isolation. They turn youth into foot soldiers and use minors as legal shields for drugs and killings. We can no longer deny the link between uncontrolled migration, failed integration and tribal gang violence. The age of naive multiculturalism must be over.

3-0324-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhor Comissário Costas Kadis, é preciso atuar em duas dimensões: por um lado, combater a toxicodependência, fazendo desaparecer o negócio lucrativo do narcotráfico; por outro lado, combater o tráfico de droga e as redes criminosas que nele florescem.

Em ambas as dimensões, o papel dos Estados é determinante. Para vencer este combate, precisamos de políticas eficazes de combate à toxicodependência, serviços públicos de saúde e inserção social robustos, de investimento público no tratamento e reabilitação dos consumidores.

Precisamos também de medidas de política criminal adequadas e de investimento nas forças e serviços de segurança nacionais, incluindo nas alfândegas, melhorando as condições de trabalho dos seus profissionais e reforçando a sua capacidade operacional.

Ao mesmo tempo, precisamos de nos libertar das imposições da UE sobre os orçamentos nacionais que condicionam o investimento público, que é essencial para todos estes objetivos.

E não podemos permitir que o combate ao narcotráfico seja o pretexto para a militarização, para justificar medidas de vigilância indiscriminada sobre os cidadãos, ou para propagandear suspeitas e preconceitos de natureza racista e xenófoba, como infelizmente acabámos de ouvir nas últimas intervenções feitas pela extrema‑direita.
3-0324-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner Costas Kadis, action needs to be taken in two dimensions: on the one hand, combating drug addiction by making the lucrative drug trafficking business disappear; on the other hand, combating drug trafficking and the criminal networks that flourish within it.

In both dimensions, the role of States is decisive. To win this fight, we need effective policies to combat drug addiction, robust public health and social integration services, and public investment in the treatment and rehabilitation of consumers.

We also need appropriate criminal policy measures and investment in national security forces and services, including customs, improving the working conditions of their professionals and strengthening their operational capacity.

At the same time, we need to free ourselves from EU impositions on national budgets that condition public investment, which is essential for all these objectives.

And we cannot allow the fight against drug trafficking to be used as a pretext for militarisation, to justify indiscriminate surveillance measures against citizens, or to propagate suspicions and prejudices of a racist and xenophobic nature, as we unfortunately just heard in the latest speeches made by the far right.

3-0325-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Monsieur le Commissaire, chers collègues, le trafic de drogue obéit aux lois classiques de l’offre et de la demande. Aussi, tant qu’il y aura des consommateurs, il y aura des trafiquants de drogue, et le trafic de drogue continuera avec son cortège de morts, de destruction de la santé d’une partie de nos populations et de déstabilisation de nos sociétés.

Si nous voulons triompher dans cette lutte contre le trafic de drogue, alors nous devons travailler à dissuader la consommation de drogue. Cela passera par trois stratégies. Premièrement, le déploiement de sanctions dissuasives contre les consommateurs de drogue. Deuxièmement, la diffusion massive, dans tous les médias, de spots d’information sur les ravages de la drogue sur la santé, mais également sur les morts occasionnées, car les consommateurs doivent prendre conscience du fait qu’ils ont du sang sur les mains. Dernier point, la confiscation systématique de tous les biens acquis grâce au trafic de drogue. C’est ainsi que nous triompherons.
3-0325-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, drug trafficking obeys the classic laws of supply and demand. Therefore, as long as there are consumers, there will be drug traffickers, and drug trafficking will continue with its procession of deaths, the destruction of the health of a portion of our populations, and the destabilisation of our societies.

If we want to triumph in this fight against drug trafficking, then we must work to deter drug consumption. This will involve three strategies. First, the deployment of deterrent sanctions against drug consumers. Second, the massive broadcast, across all media, of information spots on the ravages of drugs on health, but also on the deaths caused, because consumers must realize that they have blood on their hands. Last point, the systematic confiscation of all assets acquired through drug trafficking. This is how we will triumph.

3-0326-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, «hay noches en que estamos solos mi compañero y yo contra quince narcolanchas». Desgraciadamente, no es el comienzo de una serie colombiana de Netflix: se trata del testimonio de un guardia civil español, denunciando la indefensión con la que nuestros agentes se ven obligados a combatir al narco.

Una indefensión que tiene un altísimo coste humano. En los últimos dos años, cuatro agentes han sido asesinados en España y, en las últimas semanas, uno en Portugal. Esta escalada de violencia más propia de otras latitudes es la nueva normalidad en las costas europeas, pero Europa no puede seguir tolerándolo.

No podemos seguir dependiendo del heroísmo de nuestros agentes. Los Gobiernos europeos tienen la obligación —política y moral— de dotarles de los mejores medios para combatir al narco. Ellos no quieren palmaditas en la espalda ni homenajes en los funerales, aunque algunos ni siquiera se atrevan a hacerlo, quieren simplemente los medios para poder cumplir con su deber en defensa de todos los europeos.
3-0326-0000.englishText:
Madam President, "there are nights when my partner and I are alone against fifteen drug boats." Unfortunately, this is not the beginning of a Colombian Netflix series: it is the testimony of a Spanish Civil Guard, denouncing the helplessness with which our agents are forced to fight drug trafficking.

A helplessness that comes at a very high human cost. In the last two years, four agents have been murdered in Spain and, in recent weeks, one in Portugal. This escalation of violence, more typical of other latitudes, is the new normality on European coasts, but Europe cannot continue to tolerate it.

We cannot continue to depend on the heroism of our agents. European governments have the political and moral obligation to provide them with the best means to fight drug trafficking. They do not want pats on the back or tributes at funerals, although some do not even dare to do that; they simply want the means to be able to fulfill their duty in defense of all Europeans.

3-0327-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, thank you for your remarks. We have taken good note of all your positions. I will make some general comments.

I think that we all agree that no Member State can face security challenges alone. We are bringing the full weight of EU legal, financial and operational resources to support Member States in this fight. We have agreed on a new EU drugs strategy, an action plan against drugs trafficking, and we are already working on their implementation. We have proposed new mandates for Europol and Eurojust, and we will propose new legislation on Frontex and organised crime soon. So in all these initiatives, we count on your cooperation and support to make real progress.

3-0328-0000.sourceText:
La discussione è chiusa.

La votazione si svolgerà durante la prossima tornata.
3-0328-0000.englishText:
The discussion is closed.

The vote will take place during the next part-session.

3-0328-5000.sourceText:
Jeśli handel narkotykami kwitnie, to dlatego, że ochrona granic zewnętrznych pozostaje niewystarczająca. Państwa graniczne potrzebują większego wsparcia finansowego, nowoczesnych narzędzi i silniejszej współpracy z Frontexem, Europolem oraz Eurojustem. Zamiast mnożyć biurokrację i ograniczać wymianę informacji między służbami, Unia Europejska powinna zapewnić im skuteczne instrumenty działania. Nie ma również potrzeby tworzenia kolejnych instytucji, jeśli osłabią one kompetencje istniejących agencji.

W 2024 roku państwa członkowskie Unii Europejskiej zgłosiły ponad 1,5 miliona przestępstw związanych z narkotykami. W latach 2018–2023 liczba osób rozpoczynających leczenie z powodu problemów z kokainą wzrosła o 31%, a z powodu uzależnienia od cracku o 35%. To pokazuje, że Europa przegrywa walkę z przemytem narkotyków i zorganizowaną przestępczością.

Przestępcy nie mogą czuć się bezkarnie. Europejskie porty nie mogą być magazynami i punktami prze0ładunkowymi dla karteli narkotykowych. Wiele danych wskazuje na związek między przestępczością narkotykową a nielegalną migracją oraz nadużywaniem procedur azylowych. Osoby łamiące prawo powinny mieć pełną świadomość, że łamanie prawa będzie skutkowało szybkim powrotem do kraju pochodzenia.

Europa potrzebuje bezpiecznych granic zamiast ideologii, współpracujących służb zamiast przepisów, które uniemożliwiają im skuteczne działanie, realnej ochrony granic i zdecydowanych działań przeciwko międzynarodowym kartelom, aby przywrócić bezpieczeństwo swoim obywatelom.
3-0328-5000.englishText:
If the drug trade is flourishing, it is because the protection of external borders remains insufficient. Border states need greater financial support, modern tools, and stronger cooperation with Frontex, Europol, and Eurojust. Instead of multiplying bureaucracy and restricting information exchange between services, the European Union should provide them with effective operational instruments. There is also no need to create further institutions if they weaken the competencies of existing agencies.

In 2024, European Union member states reported over 1.5 million drug-related crimes. Between 2018 and 2023, the number of people starting treatment for cocaine problems increased by 31%, and for crack addiction by 35%. This shows that Europe is losing the fight against drug smuggling and organized crime.

Criminals cannot be allowed to feel unpunished. European ports cannot be warehouses and transshipment points for drug cartels. Much data indicates a connection between drug crime and illegal migration as well as the abuse of asylum procedures. Individuals breaking the law should be fully aware that breaking the law will result in a swift return to their country of origin.

Europe needs secure borders instead of ideology, cooperating services instead of regulations that prevent them from operating effectively, real border protection, and decisive actions against international cartels in order to restore security to its citizens.

3-0334-0000.sourceText:
L'ordine del giorno reca la discussione sulla dichiarazione del Parlamento sul Futuro del sostegno dell'UE a favore delle forze democratiche, degli attori contrari alla guerra e della società civile repressa russi (2026/2794(RSP)).

Vorrei ricordare agli onorevoli deputati che per questa discussione si terrà un unico giro di interventi di oratori dei gruppi politici. Pertanto non è prevista la procedura "catch the eye" e non saranno accettati interventi cartellino blu.

Vorrei inoltre ricordare agli oratori che, date le misure di prova attualmente in vigore e l'orario fisso di conclusione della discussione, sarà necessario rispettare rigorosamente il tempo di parola.
3-0334-0000.englishText:
The agenda calls for the discussion on the Parliament declaration on the Future of EU support for Russian democratic forces, anti-war actors and repressed civil society (2026/2794(RSP)).

I would like to remind honourable members that for this discussion there will be a single round of speeches by speakers from political groups. Therefore, the catch-the-eye procedure is not planned and blue-card interventions will not be accepted.

I would also like to remind speakers that, given the trial measures currently in force and the fixed closing time of the discussion, it will be necessary to strictly respect speaking time.

3-0335-0000.sourceText: Cienītā sēdes vadītāja! Kolēģi! Krievijas pilna mēroga uzbrukums Ukrainai, kas turpinās nu jau piekto gadu, nav tikai militārs konflikts. Krievijas neoimperiālistiskai agresijai ir un būs dziļa un ilgstoša ietekme uz starptautiskajām tiesībām, Eiropas drošību, demokrātiju un miljoniem cilvēku dzīvi. Visi Krievijas valsts instrumenti – valdība, ekonomika, finanšu sektors, propaganda, pareizticīgā baznīca – kalpo karam un militarizē sabiedrību. Tāpēc vienīgais ceļš uz Krievijas atdzimšanu un sabiedrības atveseļošanu ir Ukrainas uzvara karā. Krievijas neoimperiālisms ir jāaptur. Tikai caur sakāvi Krievija var kļūt par valsti, kurā attīstīsies demokrātija, valdīs likuma vara, būs nodrošinātas cilvēktiesības un pamatbrīvības. Tāpēc mūsu pienākums ir atbalstīt Ukrainas pašaizsardzību. Eiropas Parlaments ir demokrātijas mājvieta. Tāpēc mēs atbalstām Krievijas demokrātisko opozīciju, pilsonisko sabiedrību, cilvēktiesību aktīvistus, kuri nosoda agresiju pret Ukrainu. Viņi turpina pretestību Kremļa režīmam, neskatoties uz represijām, apcietināšanām un trimdu. Režīms nežēlīgi vēršas pret katru, kas neatbalsta agresiju. Ir ierosinātas vairāk nekā 5000 krimināllietas, cietumos smok vairāk nekā 4000 politieslodzīto. Politieslodzīto atbrīvošana ir prasība, kura ir jāiekļauj Ukrainas un Krievijas miera sarunās, kuras agrāk vai vēlāk notiks. Tomēr Krievijas demokrātiskie spēki ir sašķelti. Vēsture atkal un atkal ir pierādījusi, ka diktatūru uzvar tie, kas uzvaras vārdā atliek malā uzskatu un personāliju nesaskaņas un koncentrējas uz stratēģisko mērķi – demokrātiskas un likumpaklausīgas valsts un sabiedrības izveidošanu. Bez vienotības Krievijas demokrātisko spēku ietekme uz politisko procesu Krievijā būs maznozīmīga.
3-0335-0000.englishText: Madam Chair! Colleagues! Russia's full-scale attack on Ukraine, which is now continuing for a fifth year, is not just a military conflict. Russian neo-imperialist aggression has and will have a deep and lasting impact on international law, European security, democracy, and the lives of millions of people. All Russian state instruments—the government, the economy, the financial sector, propaganda, the Orthodox Church—serve the war and militarize society. Therefore, the only path to Russia's revival and the recovery of society is Ukraine's victory in the war. Russian neo-imperialism must be stopped. Only through defeat can Russia become a state where democracy will develop, the rule of law will prevail, human rights and fundamental freedoms will be ensured. Therefore, our duty is to support Ukraine's self-defense. The European Parliament is the home of democracy. Therefore, we support the Russian democratic opposition, civil society, human rights activists who condemn the aggression against Ukraine. They continue their resistance to the Kremlin regime, despite repressions, arrests, and exile. The regime ruthlessly targets anyone who does not support the aggression. More than 5,000 criminal cases have been initiated, more than 4,000 political prisoners are languishing in prisons. The release of political prisoners is a demand that must be included in the peace negotiations between Ukraine and Russia, which will happen sooner or later. However, the Russian democratic forces are divided. History has proven time and again that dictatorships are defeated by those who, in the name of victory, put aside disagreements of views and personalities and concentrate on the strategic goal—the creation of a democratic and law-abiding state and society. Without unity, the influence of Russian democratic forces on the political process in Russia will be insignificant.

3-0336-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la Russia non è Putin.

La Russia sono anche migliaia di donne e uomini che, in un clima asfissiante, continuano a difendere la democrazia, i diritti umani e le libertà fondamentali. Sono persone che si oppongono alla brutale guerra di aggressione della Russia contro l'Ucraina ed è proprio da loro che ogni giorno ci arrivano innumerevoli segnalazioni di cittadini repressi, detenuti, imprigionati e maltrattati solo perché si sono esposti, hanno alzato la testa e la voce dicendo la verità sulla guerra di Putin.

La propaganda del regime impedisce alle forze democratiche di esprimersi e quando qualcuno riesce a sfuggire alle maglie fittissime di questa rete, il sistema giudiziario prende la scena, confezionando sentenze ad hoc per punire attivisti, giornalisti e chiunque abbia il coraggio di alzare la voce.

L'Unione europea deve essere ferma e decisa nel suo incrollabile sostegno al popolo ucraino di fronte alla guerra di aggressione di Putin. Allo stesso tempo, l'Unione deve continuare a sostenere gli attivisti russi per i diritti umani, gli attori pro‑democrazia e gli attivisti contro la guerra, persone che spesso rischiano la propria incolumità e la propria vita per il loro impegno e per presentare un'altra Russia: la Russia libera, democratica, una Russia dello Stato di diritto. Una Russia così – ricordiamoci – è possibile.
3-0336-0000.englishText:
Madam President, honourable colleagues, Russia is not Putin.

Russia is also thousands of women and men who, in a suffocating climate, continue to defend democracy, human rights and fundamental freedoms. They are people who oppose Russia's brutal war of aggression against Ukraine and it is precisely from them that we receive countless reports every day of citizens who are repressed, detained, imprisoned and mistreated simply because they have exposed themselves, raising their heads and voices to tell the truth about Putin's war.

The regime's propaganda prevents democratic forces from expressing themselves and when someone manages to escape the very dense meshes of this network, the judicial system takes the stage, concocting ad hoc sentences to punish activists, journalists and anyone who has the courage to speak out.

The European Union must be firm and resolute in its unwavering support for the Ukrainian people in the face of Putin's war of aggression. At the same time, the Union must continue to support Russian human rights activists, pro-democracy actors and anti-war activists, people who often risk their own safety and lives for their commitment and to present another Russia: a free, democratic Russia, a Russia of the rule of law. Such a Russia – let us remember – is possible.

3-0337-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Caros Colegas, meus caros amigos, façamos um pouco de História.

Erros europeus desde o fim da Guerra Fria, a queda do Muro de Berlim: muito pouco diálogo político com a Rússia e total dependência energética desse país. O resultado era previsível porque nos afastámos politicamente e abraçámos uma dependência económica e energética.

Meus caros amigos, longe, muito longe de aceitar este regime na Rússia, pelo contrário, criticá-lo vivamente. Agora, nós não temos de nos imiscuir nos assuntos internos de outros países, de países terceiros, ainda por cima alheios à União Europeia.

A prioridade deve ser fixar e resolver os problemas da Europa, antes de arranjar agendas externas que nem sempre são claras nem honestas. Portanto, vamos tentar, mais uma vez, que a Europa se comporte à altura e que resolva os seus problemas em vez de andar a tentar resolver os dos outros.
3-0337-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Dear Colleagues, my dear friends, let us make a little History.

European errors since the end of the Cold War, the fall of the Berlin Wall: very little political dialogue with Russia and total energy dependence on that country. The result was predictable because we drifted away politically and embraced economic and energy dependence.

My dear friends, far, very far from accepting this regime in Russia, on the contrary, we strongly criticise it. Now, we do not have to interfere in the internal affairs of other countries, of third countries, moreover foreign to the European Union.

The priority must be to set and resolve Europe's problems, before taking on external agendas that are neither always clear nor honest. Therefore, let us try, once again, for Europe to behave as expected and to resolve its own problems instead of going around trying to solve those of others.
3-0337-0000.factCheck: The claim that Europe had very little political dialogue with Russia and total energy dependence on it since the Cold War is false; the EU and Russia maintained an active strategic partnership with regular high-level summits until 2014, and while Europe was heavily reliant on Russian fossil fuels, it was never totally dependent, with Russia supplying about 24.4% of the EU's total energy needs in 2020.

3-0338-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Cieszę się, że rozmawiamy w Parlamencie Europejskim o innej Rosji, o Rosji, która nie będzie śmiertelnym zagrożeniem dla wolnego świata i która nie będzie ociekała krwią niewinnych ofiar. Czy taka Rosja jest możliwa? Kiedy spojrzymy na historię tego kraju, to trudno znaleźć podstawę do optymizmu. Zarówno carska Rosja, jak i czerwona Rosja były agresywnymi państwami imperialistycznymi. Putin czerpie z obu tych tradycji. Takie wartości jak demokracja, prawa człowieka, prawa obywatelskie w Rosji nigdy się nie zakorzeniły.

Ci, którzy marzą o tym, aby z Rosji uczynić państwo cywilizowane, są po prostu mordowani. Tak stało się z Anną Politkowską, Borysem Niemcowem, Aleksiejem Nawalnym. Dziś w Rosji nie ma żadnej zorganizowanej opozycji. Nie oznacza to, że nie należy wspierać tych, którzy, będąc w większości na emigracji, deklarują niechęć wobec dyktatury. Wsparcie to musi być jednak adekwatne do realnie podejmowanych działań oraz rzeczywiście wyznawanych wartości. Należy również pamiętać, że niemal 20% obywateli współczesnej Rosji to przedstawiciele mniejszości narodowych. Ich aspiracje narodowe zasługują na szczególną uwagę.
3-0338-0000.englishText:
Madam President! I am glad that we are talking in the European Parliament about another Russia, about a Russia that will not be a mortal threat to the free world and that will not be dripping with the blood of innocent victims. Is such a Russia possible? When we look at the history of this country, it is difficult to find a basis for optimism. Both Tsarist Russia and Red Russia were aggressive imperial states. Putin draws from both of these traditions. Values such as democracy, human rights, and civil rights have never taken root in Russia.

Those who dream of making Russia a civilized state are simply murdered. This is what happened to Anna Politkovskaya, Boris Nemtsov, and Alexei Navalny. Today, there is no organized opposition in Russia. This does not mean that we should not support those who, mostly in exile, declare their aversion to the dictatorship. However, this support must be adequate to the actions actually undertaken and the values truly professed. It should also be remembered that almost 20% of the citizens of modern Russia are representatives of national minorities. Their national aspirations deserve special attention.

3-0339-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, la géographie nous l’impose: parce que la Russie est européenne et que c’est avec elle que nous partageons ce continent, il nous faut trouver les voies et moyens de coexister dans une paix solide et durable.

Cela demande deux choses: la première est de toujours plus aider l’Ukraine à infliger à Vladimir Poutine la défaite qu’il mérite. La stabilité de notre continent exige que plus personne ne puisse croire, en Russie, que la force brutale puisse triompher du droit et que les missiles puissent reconstituer l’empire des tsars. Peut-être ce jour est-il plus proche qu’on ne le croit – on verra –, mais la certitude est que rien ne sourit plus à Vladimir Poutine, qu’aucune dictature ne survit à l’humiliation d’une déroute militaire, et qu’une page se tournera donc bientôt à Moscou, dans trois jours, trois mois ou trois ans.

Ce jour-là, nous devons le préparer, et c’est pour cela que nous avons entamé et que nous poursuivrons un dialogue avec l’opposition russe. Avant même que la victoire de l’Ukraine ne lève un vent de liberté à Moscou, il faut que les Russes – non pas le Kremlin, mais les Russes – nous entendent leur dire que nous ne voulons rien d’autre que vivre à leurs côtés, dans la sécurité et la coopération, et que, le jour venu, nous tendrons la main à une Russie libérée, enfin libre de choisir l’Europe et la démocratie.
3-0339-0000.englishText:
Madam President, geography imposes it upon us: because Russia is European and it is with Russia that we share this continent, we must find the ways and means to coexist in a solid and lasting peace.

This requires two things: the first is to increasingly help Ukraine inflict upon Vladimir Putin the defeat he deserves. The stability of our continent requires that no one in Russia can any longer believe that brutal force can triumph over law and that missiles can rebuild the empire of the tsars. Perhaps that day is closer than we think – we shall see –, but the certainty is that nothing smiles upon Vladimir Putin any longer, that no dictatorship survives the humiliation of a military rout, and that a page will therefore soon be turned in Moscow, in three days, three months or three years.

That day, we must prepare for it, and that is why we have begun and will continue a dialogue with the Russian opposition. Even before Ukraine's victory raises a wind of freedom in Moscow, the Russians – not the Kremlin, but the Russians – must hear us tell them that we want nothing other than to live alongside them, in security and cooperation, and that, when the time comes, we will reach out a hand to a liberated Russia, at last free to choose Europe and democracy.

3-0340-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, for too long, the EU's Russia policy has been reactive: sanctions after aggression, statements after repression, emergency support after arrests. This is not enough. This is not strategic. We need a real EU strategy on Russia with two pillars: deterrence against the current regime and the 'de-Putinisation' of the Russia of the future. This should be a European security objective.

The Brussels Dialogue conference last month showed that this is possible. For the first time, officially, the European Parliament, with support of Commission and EEAS, brought together Russian democratic forces in a structured dialogue with the EU institutions, including voices from Russia, following the initiative of Mr Kubilius a couple of years ago. The presence of Commissioner Kubilius, but also of Commissioner Marta Kos, was also important because enlargement also includes a wider strategic neighbourhood. This dialogue should mark the beginning of a more structured and political engagement with Russians who fight against Putin's regime. A Russia that remains imperialist remains a threat to Ukraine and to all of us. Europe cannot impose democracy on Russia, but we can support those Russians who fight for it, who die for it.

That is why in the next MFF we need a dedicated Global Europe funding line for Russian civil society. I call on the Commission and the Council to work on an update of the EU strategy on Russia. Stop treating Russian civil society as a side issue. They are our allies. They are our best, important weapon against Putin and for Ukraine. And this Parliament will do our best to support them and all of us.

3-0341-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, missiles and drones are killing people in Kyiv every night at the moment. Putin has shown that he is a modern‑day fascist leader by trying to conquer Ukraine militarily, but also by attacking those in his own country who oppose his imperialist ideology and who do not fit into his patriarchal and heteronormative notion of the nation. It is not only our moral obligation, but also in our own interest to support the Ukrainians that are fighting for independence and are fighting against Putin's authoritarianism.

Likewise, it is also in our own interest to support those democratic Russian opposition forces who share these objectives. This means engaging in dialogue but also recognising the diversity of actors in Russian civil society, including those representing linguistic and ethnic minorities. This means supporting independent media projects and also providing refuge in Europe for those who really need it, not sending back people belonging to the LGBTQI community or those that are resisting Putin and resisting his war on Ukraine.

3-0342-0000.sourceText:
�� Господин Председател, мечтата на колективния Запад винаги е била да види Майдан в Москва. В продължение на десетилетия Западът обучаваше и финансираше много хора и организации в Русия, надявайки се те да се превърнат в неговата пета колона и сами да съсипят страната си. Но въпреки милиардите долари и евро, дадени за тази цел, мнозинството от руските граждани отхвърли данайския дар на западните лицемери. Нормалните руски граждани отлично разбират, че тези хора, въпреки всичките си високопарни слова пет пари не дават за демокрацията, свободата и просперитета на Русия. Единственото, което искат, е тотален контрол върху Руската федерация и да я грабят безнаказано.

Западът много иска да се повтори ситуацията от 90-те години, когато техният любимец Елцин и приближените му олигарси изпълняваха безпрекословно желанията на чуждите властови центрове и разпродаваха страната си. Днешното ръководство на Русия отдавна отхвърли тази васална зависимост и затова Брюксел и Вашингтон правят всичко възможно, за да го свалят. Само че нито излетите колосални суми, нито истеричната пропаганда постигнаха тази цел. Чуждестранните агенти на влияние в Русия или избягаха при своите покровители, или замълчаха засрамени.

Тотално сбъркана е политиката на колективния Запад по отношение на Русия. Вместо да водят откровен диалог с Москва, западните ръководители решиха, че могат лесно да съсипят тази държава. Сметнаха, че на безценица ще си купят руския елит така, както са правели западните колонизатори с местното население в Африка и Америка. Повярваха, че днес тлъстите грантове и безплатните воаяжи до Брюксел и Вашингтон за руснаците ще бъдат това, което някога са били искрящите мъниста за американските и африканските племенни вождове.

Да, отделни НПО-та и политици се продадоха, но в крайна сметка се оказа, че огромният финансов ресурс, отделен за антируска пропаганда, не е довел до нищо. Продължаването на тази стратегия ще доведе до същия нулев резултат.
3-0342-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the dream of the collective West has always been to see a Maidan in Moscow. For decades, the West trained and funded many people and organisations in Russia, hoping they would become its fifth column and ruin their own country themselves. But despite the billions of dollars and euros spent for this purpose, the majority of Russian citizens rejected the Danaean gift of Western hypocrites. Normal Russian citizens understand perfectly well that these people, despite all their high-flown words, do not give a damn about democracy, freedom and the prosperity of Russia. The only thing they want is total control over the Russian Federation and to plunder it with impunity.

The West desperately wants to repeat the situation of the 1990s, when their favourite Yeltsin and his close oligarchs unquestioningly carried out the wishes of foreign power centres and sold off their country. The current leadership of Russia long ago rejected this vassal dependency, and that is why Brussels and Washington are doing everything possible to overthrow it. However, neither the colossal sums spent nor the hysterical propaganda achieved this goal. Foreign agents of influence in Russia either fled to their patrons or fell silent in shame.

The policy of the collective West regarding Russia is totally flawed. Instead of conducting an open dialogue with Moscow, Western leaders decided they could easily ruin this country. They figured they would buy the Russian elite for a pittance, just as Western colonisers did with the local population in Africa and America. They believed that today, fat grants and free junkets to Brussels and Washington for Russians would be what sparkling beads once were for American and African tribal chiefs.

Yes, individual NGOs and politicians sold out, but ultimately it turned out that the huge financial resource allocated for anti-Russian propaganda has led to nothing. The continuation of this strategy will lead to the same zero result.

3-0344-0000.sourceText: L'ordine del giorno reca la discussione sulla dichiarazione della Commissione su Focolaio di Ebola nella Repubblica Democratica del Congo e in Uganda: solidarietà e preparazione dell'Unione europea in termini di salute globale (2026/2803(RSP)).
3-0344-0000.englishText: The order of business calls for the debate on the Commission statement on the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda: EU solidarity and preparedness in terms of global health (2026/2803(RSP)).

3-0345-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, the Ebola outbreak continues to expand rapidly in a region marked by conflict, displacement and fragile health systems. It is a crisis within a crisis and a reminder that, in today's interconnected world, no country can face a major health threat alone. Sustained financing and global coordination are essential.

According to the European Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, ECDC, the risk of infection for people living in the EU remains very low. But this is no reason for complacency. We remain vigilant and the Health Security Committee issued an opinion on the current recommendations for a common EU approach. The EU and our Member States are prepared for an imported Ebola case, as France's rapid response has shown.

A few weeks ago, I travelled to Bunia, in Ituri, the epicentre of the outbreak, to show EU solidarity and reaffirm our support. I saw the extraordinary bravery of healthcare and humanitarian workers operating in extremely difficult conditions. But I also saw that Europe's support matters. Our presence, our reliability and our ability to act quickly are recognised and highly valued by all partners. And our assistance is saving lives.

Major challenges remain. Our priority is to boost surveillance and contact tracing, deploy diagnostics and medical teams, support exit screening, keep humanitarian health access open, strengthen community trust, and ensure respect for international humanitarian law.

Since day one, we have worked with the WHO, the Africa CDC, affected countries and partners. ECDC experts have been deployed through the EU Health Task Force to support Africa CDC and strengthen exit screening. Overall, the EU is providing immediate and long-term support of EUR 493 million for humanitarian aid, vaccines, treatments and health security in the region. This includes more than EUR 1 million for the current preparedness and response effort, with EUR 16.5 million to rapidly deploy diagnostics and strengthen field testing capacities. We have invested EUR 39.3 million in CEPI, the Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, to support the development of new, broadly protective filovirus vaccines.

We have also mobilised EUR 15 million in humanitarian assistance for WHO and frontline humanitarian partners and transported more than 590 tonnes of essential supplies to eastern DRC through eight EU humanitarian air bridges.

Our response builds on years of EU investments in health security in Africa, healthcare workforce training, public health institutes and laboratory capacities, clinical trials, infrastructure, surveillance, logistics and research into vaccine therapeutics and diagnostics.

Beyond our bilateral and Team Europe action, we continue to provide significant multilateral contributions to the global health initiatives such as the Pandemic Fund, Gavi and the Global Fund, which are mobilising flexible funding to help countries respond to Ebola and maintain essential health services.

Honourable Members, while responding to the immediate crisis, we must also continue building long-term preparedness and response capacity. This is the aim of the global health resilience initiative to help countries prevent, prepare for and respond to current and future outbreaks. Containing Ebola requires solidarity, political commitment to bring a lasting solution to the conflict, sustained financing, and reliable access to lifesaving humanitarian supplies and medical equipment. I have pleaded for that already in February during my first visit to the Great Lakes region.

We must invest in what is needed today while preparing for tomorrow. This is why sustainable financing and health preparedness must go hand in hand in the next multiannual financial framework. You can count on me and my commitment to support the response, mobilise resources and advocate for humanitarian access and respect for humanitarian international law.

3-0346-0000.sourceText:
Poštovana predsjedavajuća, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, izbijanje ebole u Demokratskoj Republici Kongu i Ugandi ponovno nas podsjeća da zarazne bolesti ne poznaju granice.

U današnjem međusobno povezanom svijetu, zdravstvena kriza u jednom dijelu svijeta može vrlo brzo postati sigurnosni izazov i za Europu. Zato odgovor na ovakve epidemije nije samo pitanje humanitarne pomoći, nego i pitanje zdravstvene sigurnosti, otpornosti naših sustava i odgovorne međunarodne suradnje. Svjetska zdravstvena organizacija ovu je epidemiju proglasila međunarodnom javnozdravstvenom krizom. Upravo zato brzina reakcije, međunarodna koordinacija i razmjena stručnog znanja mogu biti presudni za zaustavljanje širenja bolesti.

Europska unija već je pokazala solidarnost pružanjem financijske pomoći, slanjem stručne potpore te ulaganjem u istraživanje i razvoj novih cjepiva, dijagnostike i terapije. Istodobno, EU pomaže u jačanju epidemiološkog nadzora, laboratorijskih kapaciteta i pripravnosti susjednih država kako bi se spriječilo daljnje širenje zaraze. Europa mora nastaviti pažljivo pratiti razvoj situacije. Iako stručne procjene pokazuju da je rizik za građane Europske unije trenutačno vrlo nizak, iskustva iz proteklih godina pokazala su koliko se zdravstvene okolnosti mogu brzo promijeniti. Zato moramo nastaviti ulagati u pripravnost naših zdravstvenih sustava, jačati sustave ranog upozoravanja, razvijati zajedničke europske kapacitete za odgovor na zdravstvene krize te produbljivati suradnju sa Svjetskom zdravstvenom organizacijom.

Borba protiv zaraznih bolesti test je naše sposobnosti da djelujemo zajednički, pravodobno i solidarno. Samo suradnjom, ulaganjem u znanost i odgovornim međunarodnim djelovanjem možemo spriječiti da lokalna epidemija preraste u globalnu prijetnju.

Upravo zato europska solidarnost i pripravnost moraju ostati temelj našeg odgovora na ovakve zdravstvene izazove.
3-0346-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda reminds us once again that infectious diseases know no borders.

In today's interconnected world, a health crisis in one part of the world can very quickly become a security challenge for Europe as well. That is why the response to such epidemics is not only a matter of humanitarian aid, but also a matter of health security, the resilience of our systems, and responsible international cooperation. The World Health Organization has declared this epidemic a public health emergency of international concern. Precisely for this reason, the speed of reaction, international coordination, and the exchange of expertise can be decisive in stopping the spread of the disease.

The European Union has already shown solidarity by providing financial assistance, sending expert support, and investing in the research and development of new vaccines, diagnostics, and therapies. At the same time, the EU is helping to strengthen epidemiological surveillance, laboratory capacities, and the preparedness of neighboring countries in order to prevent further spread of the infection. Europe must continue to monitor the development of the situation closely. Although expert assessments show that the risk for European Union citizens is currently very low, experiences from past years have shown how quickly health circumstances can change. Therefore, we must continue to invest in the preparedness of our health systems, strengthen early warning systems, develop joint European capacities to respond to health crises, and deepen cooperation with the World Health Organization.

The fight against infectious diseases is a test of our ability to act together, in a timely manner, and in solidarity. Only through cooperation, investment in science, and responsible international action can we prevent a local epidemic from growing into a global threat.

Precisely for this reason, European solidarity and preparedness must remain the foundation of our response to such health challenges.

3-0347-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, el brote que tiene origen en la República Democrática del Congo y en Uganda no es un asunto africano. Es un asunto global y también europeo.

Las enfermedades no se detienen en las fronteras. Un brote puede empezar muy lejos de Europa, pero tarda en llegar exactamente lo mismo que tarda en desplazarse una persona. Al principio, nos llegan noticias, cifras, unos cientos de casos y las primeras muertes —ya llevamos 500—. Entonces, podemos caer en el error de decir que, como es en África y no aquí, no es nuestro problema.

¿Alguien se acuerda de la pandemia? Porque es exactamente esto. Y yo sé que el ébola no es el COVID-19, pero deberíamos haber aprendido de la pandemia. Es absolutamente importante que nuestra respuesta sea doble. Por un lado, apoyo firme a los países afectados, prevención, preparación y respuesta desde la Unión Europea. Por otro lado, que nuestros mecanismos se compartan también en coordinación con los países del Sur Global.

Señora comisaria, yo le quiero dar las gracias por su compromiso, por ir al terreno, por su constante trabajo, por ser luz en un momento oscuro; porque necesitamos reforzar la vigilancia, la logística, la comunicación comunitaria, y la coordinación entre nuestros centros de vigilancia y los africanos. Y, sobre todo, porque la solidaridad no es caridad, es contener el brote en origen. Y es justicia. Pero es también la forma más inteligente de asegurar la seguridad de los europeos.
3-0347-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the outbreak originating in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is not an African issue. It is a global and also a European issue.

Diseases do not stop at borders. An outbreak can start very far from Europe, but it takes exactly the same amount of time to arrive as it takes for a person to travel. At first, we receive news, figures, a few hundred cases and the first deaths—we are already at 500. Then, we can fall into the error of saying that, since it is in Africa and not here, it is not our problem.

Does anyone remember the pandemic? Because this is exactly it. And I know that Ebola is not COVID-19, but we should have learned from the pandemic. It is absolutely important that our response be twofold. On the one hand, firm support for the affected countries, prevention, preparation and response from the European Union. On the other hand, that our mechanisms are also shared in coordination with the countries of the Global South.

Madam Commissioner, I want to thank you for your commitment, for going to the field, for your constant work, for being a light in a dark moment; because we need to reinforce surveillance, logistics, community communication, and coordination between our surveillance centers and the African ones. And, above all, because solidarity is not charity, it is containing the outbreak at its source. And it is justice. But it is also the smartest way to ensure the security of Europeans.

3-0348-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, en République démocratique du Congo, les populations subissent déjà les ravages de la guerre. Désormais, elles doivent affronter une nouvelle catastrophe: Ebola – plus de 1 500 cas, plus de 500 morts.

Mais il faut dire les choses: ce virus se propage aussi parce qu’il arrive dans des régions, l’Ituri et le Kivu, détruites par la guerre. Depuis 2021, l’est du Congo est à nouveau ravagé par les attaques du M23, soutenu par le régime de Paul Kagame. Des millions de personnes ont dû fuir, des infrastructures et des hôpitaux ont été incendiés.

Alors, comment arrêter Ebola? Comment arrêter quand il n’y a pas assez d’ambulances, quand les centres de soins sont détruits, quand les médecins ne peuvent même plus atteindre les malades? Oui, il faut envoyer de l’aide humanitaire, mais fermer les yeux sur les vrais responsables de ce chaos, c’est accepter que la situation continue; c’est nous rendre complices.

L’Union européenne doit enfin agir, comme le demande le Parlement depuis plusieurs années: sanctionner le Rwanda et M. Kagame et faire pression pour mettre fin à cette guerre. Pourquoi tant de complaisance pour le Rwanda? C’est le moment de montrer qu’on sait faire aussi une action politique, et pas uniquement une action humanitaire!
3-0348-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in the Democratic Republic of Congo, populations are already suffering the ravages of war. Now they must face a new catastrophe: Ebola – more than 1,500 cases, more than 500 deaths.

But we must call things by their name: this virus is also spreading because it is arriving in regions, Ituri and Kivu, destroyed by war. Since 2021, eastern Congo has once again been ravaged by attacks by the M23, supported by the regime of Paul Kagame. Millions of people have had to flee, infrastructure and hospitals have been burned down.

So, how to stop Ebola? How to stop it when there are not enough ambulances, when care centers are destroyed, when doctors can no longer even reach the sick? Yes, we must send humanitarian aid, but closing our eyes to the real culprits of this chaos means accepting that the situation continues; it means making ourselves accomplices.

The European Union must finally act, as Parliament has been demanding for several years: sanction Rwanda and Mr. Kagame and put pressure to end this war. Why so much complacency towards Rwanda? This is the moment to show that we also know how to take political action, and not only humanitarian action!

3-0349-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC est une des plus graves de l’histoire. De plus, le conflit armé dans l’est de la RDC rend la lutte presque impossible. Sans sécurité, il est impossible de stopper l’épidémie.

L’Afrique, chers collègues, est un partenaire essentiel. C’est notre voisin. Face à un virus qui menace toute une région, nous ne pouvons pas rester spectateurs: nous devons protéger les civils, protéger le personnel de santé et garantir un accès à l’aide humanitaire. Et nous devons renforcer notre soutien aux organisations locales, comme l’hôpital de Panzi du Dr Denis Mukwege, qui sont en première ligne dans la lutte contre Ebola.

Nous devons aussi rétablir la sécurité dans la région. Comme d’autres intervenants l’ont dit, nous devons commencer à sanctionner le Rwanda. La paix doit revenir là-bas pour permettre le combat contre Ebola. Notre devoir est clair: sauver les vies. Chaque jour compte.
3-0349-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, the Ebola epidemic in the DRC is one of the most serious in history. Moreover, the armed conflict in the eastern DRC makes the fight almost impossible. Without security, it is impossible to stop the epidemic.

Africa, dear colleagues, is an essential partner. It is our neighbor. Faced with a virus that threatens an entire region, we cannot remain spectators: we must protect civilians, protect health personnel, and guarantee access to humanitarian aid. And we must strengthen our support for local organizations, such as Dr. Denis Mukwege's Panzi Hospital, which are on the front line in the fight against Ebola.

We must also restore security in the region. As other speakers have said, we must begin to sanction Rwanda. Peace must return there to allow the fight against Ebola. Our duty is clear: save lives. Every day counts.

3-0350-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, questo virus, che in molti abbiamo paragonato a quanto è accaduto qualche anno fa con il COVID, è un virus molto più letale, molto più pericoloso: non esistono cure, non esistono vaccini e non esiste nessun modo per fermare le emorragie all'interno del corpo e all'esterno del corpo di questi poveri pazienti.

Noi dobbiamo veramente sostituirci a quanto gli Stati Uniti hanno fatto con il loro passo indietro rispetto all'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità. Se non lo vogliamo fare perché crediamo che l'aiuto e la solidarietà siano importanti, dovremmo farlo per egoismo, perché, come tanti hanno detto, a partire anche dalla Commissaria, i virus non hanno bisogno di un passaporto per attraversare un confine.

Il fatto che ci siano già stati 1 500 contagi, 500 persone che hanno perso la vita e vedere quelle immagini – dove, signora Commissaria, è vero che è stato fatto uno sforzo, ma, di fatto, sul territorio, dove queste persone muoiono, non hanno neanche la possibilità di avere quegli strumenti di protezione per i medici e per gli infermieri, tant'è vero che ne sono morti quasi venti – e anche per le stesse persone che assistono o vanno a trovare i loro cari.

Dobbiamo fare di più e dobbiamo farlo adesso, perché questo virus è veramente pericoloso e mortale.
3-0350-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, this virus, which many of us have compared to what happened a few years ago with COVID, is a much more lethal, much more dangerous virus: there are no cures, no vaccines and no way to stop the hemorrhages inside the body and outside the body of these poor patients.

We truly must step in to replace what the United States has done with its step back from the World Health Organization. If we do not want to do this because we believe that aid and solidarity are important, we should do it out of selfishness, because, as many have said, starting also with the Commissioner, viruses do not need a passport to cross a border.

The fact that there have already been 1,500 infections, 500 people who have lost their lives, and seeing those images – where, Madam Commissioner, it is true that an effort has been made, but, in fact, on the ground, where these people die, they do not even have the possibility of having those protection tools for doctors and nurses, so much so that almost twenty of them have died – and also for the very people who assist or go to visit their loved ones.

We must do more and we must do it now, because this virus is truly dangerous and deadly.

3-0351-0000.sourceText:
Senhora Presidente, Senhora Comissária, bem sei que supervisionou pessoalmente o embarque de paracetamol para o Congo para ajudar no combate ao surto de Ébola. Mas é poucochinho, não é?

Queria fazer-lhe duas perguntas sobre ações concretas da União Europeia.

Em primeiro lugar, estamos perante uma variante para a qual não há nenhuma vacina comercial, mas sabemos agora que há avanços científicos que entusiasmam. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai, então, investir nestes avanços científicos para termos a vacina.

A segunda questão é sobre os serviços de saúde locais. Os Médicos Sem Fronteiras têm dito, e muito bem, que é preciso investir diretamente lá. Têm, aliás, pedido investimento direto para que os serviços de saúde possam não só monitorizar como controlar, tratar a doença. E a minha pergunta é se a União Europeia vai aumentar o seu apoio, porque tem de o fazer. Os casos detetados em Paris e Berlim mostram, aliás, que é do seu próprio interesse fazê-lo.

E uma nota final: a União Europeia tem particulares responsabilidades, porque se nas zonas de conflito é mais difícil controlar o surto de Ébola, não esqueçamos que somos parceiros comerciais daqueles minerais do sangue que estão a provocar os conflitos nas zonas mais afetadas.
3-0351-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I am well aware that you personally oversaw the shipment of paracetamol to Congo to help combat the Ebola outbreak. But it is a bit meager, isn't it?

I wanted to ask you two questions about concrete actions by the European Union.

First of all, we are facing a variant for which there is no commercial vaccine, but we now know there are exciting scientific advancements. And my question is whether the European Union will, therefore, invest in these scientific advancements so that we can have the vaccine.

The second question is about local health services. Doctors Without Borders have rightly said that it is necessary to invest directly there. In fact, they have been asking for direct investment so that health services can not only monitor but also control and treat the disease. And my question is whether the European Union will increase its support, because it has to do so. The cases detected in Paris and Berlin show, in fact, that it is in its own interest to do so.

And a final note: the European Union has particular responsibilities, because if in conflict zones it is more difficult to control the Ebola outbreak, let us not forget that we are trade partners of those blood minerals that are causing the conflicts in the most affected areas.

3-0352-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, thank you all for this first exchange.

I totally agree that the Ebola outbreak is not an African problem. It's about all of us, because no one of us is in security until everyone is in security. We live on the same planet. So we have to acknowledge and to remind us that a virus does not need a visa to cross borders.

When it comes to investments in vaccines, the Commission is currently replenishing its rescEU stockpiles for a range of relevant medical countermeasures in Europe, also for remdesivir, an antiviral authorised in the EU against COVID-19, but which is considered and recommended by WHO as potential therapeutics against Ebola. Together with Member States, we are looking into the possibility of rolling out clinical trials with potential therapeutic candidates.

The European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership is supporting the development of monoclonal antibodies against Ebola and other filoviruses with EUR 3.4 million. And the Commission has invested over the past years heavily into the development of vaccines and therapeutics for filoviruses like Ebola and Marburg. I have to say that this Ebola Bundibugyo was already a priority. We already acknowledged that it was a threat coming soon.

Last month we launched also a call for tenders with EUR 16 million to establish an investigational vaccine reserve for human pathogenic filoviruses for which no authorised vaccines are currently available addressing Marburg, Sudan, Ebola but also Bundibugyo viruses.

3-0353-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, colleagues, it is again an outbreak of terrible sickness. We have Ebola in many parts of Africa, even one case on European soil. We have seen the hantavirus spreading over springtime.

I want to emphasise one important point, because this is the very beginning of one or the other sickness, and we do not know where it will lead in either case. But I have already observed extremists claiming that the sickness does not exist, that the sickness has been made up by what they call 'elites'. But these extremists are the ones who define themselves whom they call 'elites', and they create the conspiracy theory that the 'elites' would create information about the sickness to control people.

No – this is academic research, this is scientific data that what we are doing is based on. This is why, especially the European role with our approach of human dignity, of individual freedom, is to take it seriously when such outbreaks take place and to always rely on evidence, academic evidence, and to confront extremists in the very beginning when they start their conspiracy theories.

3-0354-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Commissioner, I fully agree with what you just said about the situation related to vaccines, antibodies and so on, but what we see is climate-sensitive disease spread. Of course pandemics and epidemic threats are ongoing, we have no chance to deny it, but in opposite, we have fragile and shrinking global health financing and global health support.

Now when we are discussing about financing and our global health, how much money we can put in, we see that we are also reducing financial capacities. Humanitarian aid and cross-border preparedness require a lot of financial means and, of course, all means which can help us.

But we are facing a situation and we can help the Commissioner and ask the Council to pay more attention to global threats because otherwise we have no strategies. Please keep in mind that the United States goes out from the WHO. It's clear there are a lot of challenges.

3-0355-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, l’épidémie d’Ebola qui sévit en République démocratique du Congo et en Ouganda est avant tout une tragédie humanitaire. Plus de 1 700 personnes ont été infectées, et des centaines ont perdu la vie. Derrière ces chiffres se cachent des familles, des communautés et des professionnels de santé, qui luttent pour survivre dans ces circonstances difficiles.

Le contexte d’insécurité et de tensions régionales rend la situation bien plus complexe dans l’est de la RDC. Le conflit est en cours, et l’instabilité liée à la crise entre la RDC et le Rwanda complique l’accès des travailleurs humanitaires, perturbe fortement les services de santé et accentue les mouvements de population à travers les frontières.

J’appelle la Commission et le Conseil à compléter notre aide humanitaire par un engagement diplomatique renouvelé, en exhortant toutes les parties à mettre en œuvre un cessez-le-feu immédiat afin de garantir l’accès humanitaire et de protéger les civils. Car protéger des vies nécessite non seulement une aide médicale, mais aussi la paix et la stabilité, pour que les communautés puissent se rétablir.
3-0355-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, the Ebola epidemic raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda is above all a humanitarian tragedy. More than 1,700 people have been infected, and hundreds have lost their lives. Behind these figures lie families, communities, and health professionals who are struggling to survive in these difficult circumstances.

The context of insecurity and regional tensions makes the situation much more complex in eastern DRC. The conflict is ongoing, and the instability linked to the crisis between the DRC and Rwanda complicates access for humanitarian workers, severely disrupts health services, and accentuates population movements across borders.

I call on the Commission and the Council to complement our humanitarian aid with renewed diplomatic engagement, urging all parties to implement an immediate ceasefire to guarantee humanitarian access and protect civilians. Because protecting lives requires not only medical aid, but also peace and stability, so that communities can recover.

3-0356-0000.sourceText:
Madame la Présidente, Madame la Commissaire, les nouvelles sur Ebola sont horribles, évidemment. C’est une maladie qui tue, qui fait peur aussi – transmissible, très mortelle –, mais, en même temps, il faut aussi qu’on ose s’attaquer aux causes fondamentales du problème.

En République démocratique du Congo, qu’est-ce qu’il faudrait pour combattre de manière efficace Ebola? Il ne s’agit pas uniquement de recherche d’un vaccin; il s’agit aussi d’un système de santé publique performant, de prévention – la détection! –, de pouvoir aller chercher, de pouvoir avoir les pratiques au niveau des enterrements, aussi, travailler avec les communautés locales.

Mais, pour tout cela, il faut des moyens. Et ces moyens-là, ils manquent, ils font défaut. Pourquoi? D’un côté, effectivement, parce qu’il y a tout simplement la guerre avec des acteurs impliqués comme le Rwanda, que nous sponsorisons toujours. Mais, deuxièmement, aussi à cause du pillage des ressources naturelles, organisé par les États-Unis et les multinationales européennes.

La RDC perd des sous, perd de l’argent, perd de la richesse à l’Occident et n’a donc plus les moyens pour investir dans ce système de santé publique. Donc, c’est sur cela qu’il faut travailler: sur notre politique commerciale, contre les multinationales occidentales européennes qui pillent les richesses du Congo.
3-0356-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, the news about Ebola is horrible, obviously. It is a disease that kills, and is also frightening – transmissible, highly lethal –, but at the same time, we must also dare to tackle the root causes of the problem.

In the Democratic Republic of Congo, what is needed to fight Ebola effectively? It is not just about finding a vaccine; it is also about a high-performing public health system, prevention – detection! –, being able to reach out, being able to have practices at the level of burials, too, working with local communities.

But for all of that, resources are needed. And those resources are lacking, they are missing. Why? On the one hand, effectively, simply because there is war with actors involved like Rwanda, whom we are still sponsoring. But secondly, also because of the looting of natural resources, organized by the United States and European multinationals.

The DRC is losing money, is losing funds, is losing wealth to the West and therefore no longer has the means to invest in this public health system. So, that is what we must work on: on our trade policy, against the Western and European multinationals that are looting the wealth of Congo.

3-0357-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, sinds 2019 weten we helaas meer dan ooit dat virussen geen grenzen kennen. Hoewel de risico's voor Europa momenteel zeer laag zijn, zien we dat de humanitaire tragedie in Congo en Oeganda vandaag nog niet volledig ingedekt is. Gelukkig kan er gerekend worden op een sterke interventie van de Wereldgezondheidsorganisatie, van de Europese Unie en van haar lidstaten, met lokale ondersteuning van de gezondheidszorg en investeringen en onderzoek naar vaccins en behandelingen, versterken we ook de globale en dus ook de eigen weerbaarheid hier bij ons tegen nieuwe varianten, zoals dat hier het geval is.
