Door samen te werken, onze Afrikaanse partners te ondersteunen en te investeren in innovatie, redden we niet alleen levens ter plaatse, maar versterken we ook de gezondheid en de veiligheid van onze eigen burgers. En net dat toont aan dat er meer dan ooit nood is aan een sterke Europese gezondheidsunie. Iets waar ik ook binnen de biotechverordening naar streef. We kunnen niet wegkijken van dergelijke tragedies, dus blijft een sterke steun vanuit Europa meer dan ooit noodzakelijk. En daarvoor rekenen we op u.
3-0357-0000.englishText:
Mr President, since 2019 we unfortunately know better than ever that viruses know no borders. Although the risks for Europe are currently very low, we see that the humanitarian tragedy in Congo and Uganda is not yet fully covered today. Fortunately, we can count on a strong intervention by the World Health Organization, the European Union and its member states. With local support for healthcare, investments, and research into vaccines and treatments, we are also strengthening global and therefore our own resilience here at home against new variants, as is the case here.

By working together, supporting our African partners and investing in innovation, we not only save lives on the spot, but we also strengthen the health and safety of our own citizens. And precisely that shows that there is more need than ever for a strong European health union. Something that I also strive for within the biotech regulation. We cannot look away from such tragedies, so strong support from Europe remains more necessary than ever. And for that, we count on you.

3-0358-0000.sourceText:
Voorzitter, er zijn meer dan 1 500 bevestigde gevallen van ebola in Congo en Oeganda; meer dan 500 doden. Een uitbraak die zich uitbreidt naar nieuwe gebieden. Wat zo pijnlijk is, is dat we dit hebben zien aankomen: mondiale bezuinigingen op ontwikkelingssamenwerking, het afbreken van USAID. We wisten dat de crises hierdoor zouden toenemen, juist in landen waar conflicten en rampen al groot zijn. Meer geld naar infrastructuur, meer geld naar de winning van kritieke grondstoffen en minder geld naar armoedebestrijding, gezondheidszorg, onderwijs, minder geld naar de weerbaarheid van gemeenschappen. En dit is het directe gevolg.

De consequenties zijn desastreus, niet alleen voor de mensen die nu ziek zijn en die risico's lopen. Ebola ondermijnt de weg naar stabiliteit en ontwikkeling voor hele gemeenschappen. Het is een voorkoombare ziekte. Het voorkomen kost geld, het kost aanwezigheid, het kost vertrouwen. Vertrouwen dat jarenlang is opgebouwd en nu in rap tempo wordt afgebroken. Dit kan en moet anders, niet alleen incidenteel, maar ook structureel.
3-0358-0000.englishText:
Mr President, there are more than 1,500 confirmed cases of Ebola in Congo and Uganda; more than 500 deaths. An outbreak that is spreading to new areas. What is so painful is that we saw this coming: global cuts to development cooperation, the dismantling of USAID. We knew that this would cause crises to increase, precisely in countries where conflicts and disasters are already severe. More money for infrastructure, more money for the extraction of critical raw materials and less money for poverty reduction, healthcare, education, less money for the resilience of communities. And this is the direct consequence.

The consequences are disastrous, not only for the people who are now ill and at risk. Ebola undermines the path to stability and development for entire communities. It is a preventable disease. Prevention costs money, it costs presence, it costs trust. Trust that has been built up over years and is now being broken down at a rapid pace. This can and must be done differently, not only incidentally, but also structurally.

3-0359-0000.sourceText:
Fru Formand! Det er jo fuldstændig rigtigt, som kommissæren siger, at før vi er sikre alle sammen, er ingen sikre. Men jeg har samtidig lyst til også at fejre og gøre opmærksom på, at vi her i Europa faktisk har lært af det, vi har været igennem.

Vi har nu myndigheder, som holder øje; HERA, ECDC, som faktisk hver dag sørger for at sikre, at vi kan sove trygt om natten.

Mens alt det her er sket – og det har flere kommenteret på – så har USA sænket deres investeringer. USA har trukket sig fra WHO, USA har trukket sig helt ud af USAID, og i samme tidsrum har vi selvfølgelig prøvet at kompensere så godt som muligt. Vi har oprustet, og kommissæren har gjort en kæmpe indsats.

Jeg vil gerne spørge kommissæren; Kan kommissæren fortælle os, helt konkret, hvad foregår der lige nu? Hvilke aktiviteter er der sat i gang for at holde situationen under kontrol? Og frem for alt, hvad gøres der for at afhjælpe i landene netop nu?
3-0359-0000.englishText:
Madam President! It is indeed completely right, as the Commissioner says, that before we are all safe, no one is safe. But I also want to celebrate and point out that here in Europe we have actually learned from what we have been through.

We now have authorities that keep watch; HERA, ECDC, which actually ensure every day that we can sleep safely at night.

While all of this has happened - and several have commented on this - the US has lowered its investments. The US has withdrawn from the WHO, the US has completely withdrawn from USAID, and during the same period we have of course tried to compensate as best as possible. We have rearmed, and the Commissioner has made a huge effort.

I would like to ask the Commissioner; Can the Commissioner tell us, quite concretely, what is going on right now? What activities have been initiated to keep the situation under control? And above all, what is being done to provide relief in countries right now?

3-0360-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, dear Commissioner, one in three people does not survive Ebola. And recently the first case in France was detected. This outbreak should remind us that infectious diseases do not stop at borders. It demonstrates the need for a resilient health system worldwide.

Despite declining international help, African countries are, little by little, strengthening their own health systems through improving surveillance, regional cooperation and targeted investment. Europe should support this African‑led transition by investing in laboratories, healthcare workers and outbreak preparedness while supporting African ownership of their respective health systems.

A stronger African healthcare system is not only in Africa's interest; it's in Europe's interest. Investing in an African‑led health resilience is an investment in shared global health security.

3-0361-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, verehrte Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Der Ebola-Ausbruch in Ostafrika erinnert uns daran: Gesundheit kennt keine Grenzen. Der globale Gesundheitsschutz schützt auch unsere Sicherheit.

Unsere erste Verantwortung gilt den Menschen vor Ort; sie brauchen schnelle medizinische Hilfe und starke Gesundheitssysteme. Gerade jetzt, da sich internationale Partner, insbesondere die USA, aus Teilen der Entwicklungszusammenarbeit und der globalen Gesundheitsfinanzierung zurückziehen, wächst Europas, wächst unsere Verantwortung.

Doch dieser Ausbruch ist auch eine Mahnung an Europa. Die Lehre aus Ebola lautet: Vorsorge statt Abschottung. Pandemien bekämpft man dort, wo sie entstehen, nicht erst an unseren Außengrenzen.

Aber Gesundheitspolitik ist längst auch Sicherheits‑ und Wirtschaftspolitik. Wer über resiliente Lieferketten und sichere Rohstoffpartnerschaften spricht, muss auch in globale Gesundheit investieren.

Ebola ist deshalb ein Prüfstein, ob wir globale Gesundheit als humanitäre Verantwortung und als Voraussetzung für Sicherheit und Wohlstand verstehen. Gerade jetzt, da sich andere Akteure zurückziehen, muss Europa Verantwortung übernehmen – aus Solidarität und aus kluger Vorsorge.
3-0361-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues! The Ebola outbreak in East Africa reminds us: health knows no borders. Global health security also protects our security.

Our first responsibility is to the people on the ground; they need rapid medical help and strong health systems. Especially now, as international partners, particularly the USA, are withdrawing from parts of development cooperation and global health financing, Europe's responsibility, our responsibility, is growing.

Yet this outbreak is also a warning to Europe. The lesson from Ebola is: prevention instead of isolation. Pandemics are fought where they originate, not only at our external borders.

However, health policy has long since also become security and economic policy. Anyone who talks about resilient supply chains and secure raw material partnerships must also invest in global health.

Ebola is therefore a touchstone of whether we understand global health as a humanitarian responsibility and as a prerequisite for security and prosperity. Especially now, as other actors are withdrawing, Europe must assume responsibility – out of solidarity and out of prudent prevention.

3-0362-0000.sourceText:
Signora Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, l'epidemia di Ebola in Congo e in Uganda ci ricorda che le crisi sanitarie possono superare rapidamente i confini nazionali, come dimostra anche il caso confermato in Francia di un medico rientrato dal Congo, segnalato dall'Organizzazione mondiale della sanità.

La solidarietà europea non è soltanto un dovere umanitario, ma anche un investimento nella sicurezza sanitaria internazionale. Sostenendo i paesi colpiti, proteggiamo le comunità locali, riduciamo il rischio di diffusione oltre i confini e rafforziamo la capacità globale di prevenire future emergenze.

Per questo, l'Unione europea deve continuare a sostenere la sorveglianza sanitaria, la ricerca, la prevenzione e la risposta rapida alle crisi. Investire nella solidarietà, nel coordinamento e nella preparazione significa rafforzare la tutela della salute pubblica in Africa, ma anche in Europa, contribuendo al contempo a una maggiore capacità globale di prevenire future epidemie.
3-0362-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, the Ebola epidemic in Congo and Uganda reminds us that health crises can rapidly cross national borders, as also demonstrated by the confirmed case in France of a doctor returning from Congo, reported by the World Health Organization.

European solidarity is not only a humanitarian duty, but also an investment in international health security. By supporting the affected countries, we protect local communities, reduce the risk of spread beyond borders and strengthen the global capacity to prevent future emergencies.

For this reason, the European Union must continue to support health surveillance, research, prevention and rapid crisis response. Investing in solidarity, coordination and preparedness means strengthening public health protection in Africa, but also in Europe, while contributing to a greater global capacity to prevent future epidemics.

3-0364-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda is deeply worrying. While we cannot control when these outbreaks happen, we can – and must – control how we respond. Targeted emergency funding is appropriate.

At the same time, there is an endless number of crises in the world. Aid can provide temporary help, but ultimately, true safety cannot be outsourced. It starts with the institutions that are built within a country. A response to a crisis should not be to cross fingers and hope that new crises will not come. They will come, and at some point, aid money runs out. If at that point there are no institutions in the country that can step up, it is not the donor who has betrayed the people, it is their government.

3-0366-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, you know, this Ebola outbreak is the 17th that occurred in the region. So it means that this epidemic outbreak didn't take us by surprise. We were prepared for that. And I have to say that when I went there in February, I saw that all the ingredients were already there to provoke this epidemic outbreak.

So it is right to say that we need structural investment, and that is exactly what we are doing. In May, we presented our humanitarian communication, which is mainly addressing the fragile context, how we can help this protracted crisis, addressing the root causes in these fragile contexts and how we can implement the famous nexus: working hand in hand with humanitarian aid, development and peace actors. And that is why we propose to strengthen our humanitarian diplomacy and to work with the long‑term vision involving our international partners, but also cooperation and development at a very early stage, because indeed, humanitarian aid cannot solve what is mainly a crisis provoked by the lack of governance and wars in this region.

And to answer your questions, dear Stine Bosse, 'What are we doing now?' As I said in my introductory remarks, we first have a very quick funding response. The eighth EU humanitarian air bridge arrived in Goma last Tuesday. Another EU air bridge is planned for South Sudan on 21 July to support the preparedness effort, and we are exploring the possibility of more EU humanitarian air bridges in the coming weeks, probably to Entebbe as it is a really strategic location.

Allow me to to end on a personal note. As a former journalist, I know the effect misinformation can have on our response to crisis. People need facts they can trust to protect themselves and their families. And that is why, when I was there in Bunia, I entered into contact. I was there to communicate for us, to European citizens, but also for local communities. And I entered into contact with traditional leaders, religious leaders to encourage them to help us to build trust with the affected communities.

And lastly, a word on the next MFF. We will have three good instruments to boost research and development and medical countermeasures: the UCPM, the European Competitiveness Fund and Horizon. I count on you for strong support for the next MFF.

3-0369-0000.sourceText:
IN THE CHAIR: ESTEBAN GONZÁLEZ PONS

Vice-President

3-0373-0000.sourceText: The next item is the debate on the Commission statement on harnessing the potential of a competitive and sustainable EU Bioeconomy Strategy for EU strategic autonomy (2026/2798(RSP)).

3-0374-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, thank you for organising this debate on the bioeconomy and its potential to boost the EU's strategic autonomy, resilience and competitiveness. The timing could not be more relevant.

Europe is facing a changing geopolitical and economic landscape. Real wars, trade wars and climate change have turned global energy and raw material markets upside down. We often speak about our energy dependency, but we must also have a conversation about our material dependency. The bioeconomy is a part of the answer.

Every time we use bio‑based materials to produce plastic, chemicals, textiles or fertilisers, we increase our resilience and our independence. The recent crisis has highlighted just how vulnerable our economics are to external shocks. They have also reminded us that resilience is not built overnight – it requires long‑term investments, strategic partnerships and confidence in Europe's own resources.

In this context, building a competitive and sustainable bioeconomy has become an economic necessity and clear strategic opportunity for Europe. We know what the EU bioeconomy already means for citizens and businesses across Europe. I have seen it first‑hand in discussions with farmers, fishers, rural communities and innovative companies – and the numbers speak for themselves. The EU bioeconomy creates a value of around EUR 2.7 trillion. It employs 17.1 million people and corresponds to 5 % of EU GDP. And every job in the bioeconomy creates three indirect jobs in the EU.

I have no doubts that, with the right incentives, we can deliver more economic growth, environmental benefits and resilience. For the first time, we have taken steps to maximise this potential with our new EU bioeconomy strategy. We showed that the possibilities already exist in nature's design. We are not the only one who sees this. In October, the Irish Presidency will bring the world to Dublin for the Global Bioeconomy Summit, with the European Union as a committed partner. But strategies alone can only matter if they also lead to concrete actions – and this is only happening when policy, industry and finance move together. That is what I want to focus on today.

First, we aim to remove barriers that delay market entry, create uncertainty and increase administrative costs. We will look at sector‑specific regulations but also cross-cutting efforts, steered by the soon‑to‑be established Bioeconomy Regulators and Innovators' Forum. Some innovators tell me that they struggle with different national definitions of what can be considered as bio‑based. That matters a lot, of course, in terms of what legislation applies. So with the future Biotech Act II, we will streamline rules to remove bottlenecks and create a single market for these innovative products. We are also progressing work on bio‑based plastics, including the necessary preparatory studies and consultation to provide greater clarity for innovators and investors.

Second, we are taking concrete steps to bring investors to the table. The first meeting of the Bioeconomy Investment Deployment Group confirmed that the challenge is not a lack of capital, but a mismatch between available finance and the needs of bio‑based industrial projects. That is why we will work closely with the EIB, private investors and national promotional banks to better connect promising projects with the financing that they need to scale up.

During the Global Bioeconomy Summit, we will officially launch the Bio‑based Europe Alliance to mobilise private demand for bio‑based materials and products, and the alliance will gather EU companies committed to collectively purchasing bio‑based materials and products worth EUR 10 billion by 2030. We are already engaging with key industry associations and leading companies across Europe to ensure that this alliance starts delivering tangible market demands from day one. It is key to create long‑term opportunities for European bio‑based materials, products, technologies and applications, so we are also working on a buyers' club to leverage public and private investments for purchases of carbon farming credits, thus encouraging investments across value chains.

Honourable Members, building a thriving, innovative bioeconomy requires buy‑in from all Europe, from farmers to the financial sectors, from rural communities to regulators, from policymakers to researchers and innovators. So here the Parliament plays a crucial role. I really look forward to continue working with you on this strategy.

3-0375-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, povjerenice, kolegice i kolege, farmaceutska i biotehnološka industrija strateški su sektori za Europsku uniju.

To ispravno prepoznaje Mario Draghi u svojem izvješću o konkurentnosti u kojem naglašava da će upravo inovacije u području biotehnologije i napredne proizvodnje biti ključne za budući gospodarski rast i stratešku autonomiju Europe. Europska unija danas ostvaruje trgovinski suficit od oko 220 milijardi eura u lijekovima i farmaceutskim proizvodima, što pokazuje da riječ o jednoj od naših najuspješnijih industrija. No, taj uspjeh ne smijemo uzimati zdravo za gotovo. Konkurencija je sve snažnija, Kina agresivno ulaže u proizvodnju i biotehnologiju, Indija jača svoju poziciju kao globalni proizvođač lijekova i aktivnih sastojaka, a Sjedinjene Američke Države kroz svoje industrijske politike i poticaje privlače investicije, istraživanje i razvoj iz Europe.

Ako želimo zadržati vodeću poziciju, Europa mora djelovati odlučno. Zakon o kritičnim lijekovima i predloženi Zakon o biotehnologiji važni su koraci u dobrom smjeru. Međutim, za očuvanje europske konkurentnosti potrebno je učiniti više: osigurati snažnu zaštitu intelektualnog vlasništva, ubrzati izdavanje dozvola za strateške projekte, olakšati pristup kapitalu te pomoći europskim inovativnim tvrtkama da prerastu iz uspješnih startupova u globalno konkurentne scale-up kompanije.

Upravo zato nova strategija za konkurentno i održivo gospodarstvo EU-a mora biti više od okolišne ili poljoprivredne strategije. Njezina primjena mora povezati znanost, održivu proizvodnju biomaterijala, biotehnologiju i farmaceutsku industriju. Time ćemo ojačati europsku otpornost, povećati dodatnu vrijednost naših prirodnih resursa i osigurati da inovacije nastale u Europi ostanu u Europi.

To je put prema istinski konkurentnoj, održivoj i strateški autonomnoj Europskoj uniji.
3-0375-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries are strategic sectors for the European Union.

This is correctly recognized by Mario Draghi in his report on competitiveness, in which he emphasizes that precisely innovations in the field of biotechnology and advanced manufacturing will be key to Europe's future economic growth and strategic autonomy. Today, the European Union achieves a trade surplus of around 220 billion euros in medicines and pharmaceutical products, which shows that this is one of our most successful industries. However, we must not take this success for granted. Competition is increasingly fierce, China is aggressively investing in manufacturing and biotechnology, India is strengthening its position as a global producer of medicines and active ingredients, and the United States of America, through its industrial policies and incentives, is attracting investments, research, and development away from Europe.

If we want to maintain our leading position, Europe must act decisively. The Critical Medicines Act and the proposed Biotech Act are important steps in the right direction. However, to preserve European competitiveness, more needs to be done: ensuring strong intellectual property protection, accelerating the issuance of permits for strategic projects, facilitating access to capital, and helping European innovative companies grow from successful startups into globally competitive scale-up companies.

That is precisely why the new strategy for a competitive and sustainable EU economy must be more than an environmental or agricultural strategy. Its implementation must connect science, sustainable biomaterial production, biotechnology, and the pharmaceutical industry. By doing so, we will strengthen European resilience, increase the added value of our natural resources, and ensure that innovations created in Europe stay in Europe.

That is the path toward a truly competitive, sustainable, and strategically autonomous European Union.

3-0376-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, desde luego que la bioeconomía puede ser una gran oportunidad. Pero no podemos sustituir, comisaria, una economía basada en extraer petróleo por otra basada en extraer cada vez más recursos de la naturaleza.

Sería un error porque la biomasa no es infinita. Nuestros bosques, suelos, mares y ecosistemas tienen límites. Y respetarlos no es un freno al desarrollo, es la condición para que ese desarrollo sea duradero.

Por eso, necesitamos una bioeconomía verdaderamente circular, que aproveche mejor los residuos y los subproductos, que utilice los recursos con inteligencia y que genere más valor añadido con menos materias primas.

Tampoco podemos olvidar algo esencial: la alimentación y la biodiversidad tienen que seguir siendo prioridad. La bioeconomía nunca puede competir con la producción de alimentos ni poner más presión sobre unos ecosistemas que ya están muy tensionados.

Si queremos una Europa más fuerte y competitiva, nuestra ventaja no vendrá de producir más recursos biológicos, sino de consumir menos recursos y de crear más valor utilizando menos.
3-0376-0000.englishText:
Mr President, of course the bioeconomy can be a great opportunity. But, Commissioner, we cannot replace an economy based on extracting oil with one based on extracting more and more resources from nature.

It would be a mistake because biomass is not infinite. Our forests, soils, seas and ecosystems have limits. Respecting them is not a brake on development; it is the condition for that development to be sustainable.

That is why we need a truly circular bioeconomy that makes better use of waste and by-products, uses resources intelligently and generates more added value with fewer raw materials.

Neither can we forget something essential: food and biodiversity must remain a priority. The bioeconomy can never compete with food production or put more pressure on ecosystems that are already under severe strain.

If we want a stronger and more competitive Europa, our advantage will not come from producing more biological resources, but from consuming fewer resources and creating more value while using less.

3-0377-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, le Conseil a reconnu en mars dernier la bioéconomie comme un levier de souveraineté industrielle, de transition écologique et de compétitivité. Charge maintenant aux États de tirer parti de leurs abondantes ressources agricoles et forestières et des nouveaux instruments européens, notamment l’accélérateur industriel et le règlement sur les biotechnologies.

En France, la bioéconomie représente 2 millions d’emplois et 300 milliards d’euros de chiffre d’affaires par an. Mais la lecture des conclusions du Conseil interroge. On y parle de neutralité carbone et de suppression des obstacles réglementaires sans abaisser les normes, de simplification tout en installant une nouvelle bureaucratie, de protection du marché intérieur tout en prônant l’économie ouverte. Enfin, on détourne les enjeux de ce plan pour faire avancer la financiarisation de la nature et transformer l’agriculteur en simple fournisseur de services écosystémiques.

Pour faire de la bioéconomie un instrument de puissance géopolitique, l’UE doit sortir de ses dépendances stratégiques, mais aussi sortir de son inertie.
3-0377-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, the Council recognised the bioeconomy last March as a lever for industrial sovereignty, ecological transition and competitiveness. It is now up to Member States to make the most of their abundant agricultural and forestry resources and new European instruments, notably the industrial accelerator and the biotechnology regulation.

In France, the bioeconomy accounts for 2 million jobs and 300 billion euros in turnover per year. But reading the Council's conclusions raises questions. They talk about carbon neutrality and removing regulatory obstacles without lowering standards, of simplification while setting up a new bureaucracy, of protecting the internal market while advocating an open economy. Finally, the issues of this plan are being diverted to advance the financialisation of nature and transform the farmer into a mere provider of ecosystem services.

To make the bioeconomy an instrument of geopolitical power, the EU must break out of its strategic dependencies, but also break out of its inertia.

3-0378-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, dobbiamo riconoscere che la strategia dell'economia, della bioeconomia, è tanto.

Il termine greco "bio" riguarda il ciclo della vita.

Io mi soffermerò sul tema dei carburanti e sul loro utilizzo.

Se declinata in un'ottica di neutralità tecnologica, deve mettere anche al centro il tema dei carburanti. E parliamo di biocarburanti prodotti in Europa con materie prime europee e lavoratori europei che tengono insieme la decarbonizzazione, la sicurezza e l'occupazione.

Gli scarti animali, gli scarti dell'agricoltura, ma anche il recupero di materie prime e seconde rappresentano un buon punto di partenza per avere autonomia. Anche questo è "bio", se si considera, appunto, il ciclo della vita.

Sui carburanti, però, c'è una contraddizione. Noi oggi chiediamo – in queste ore ad Ankara, questo si dice – maggiore sforzo per la difesa, maggiore sforzo per poter essere autosufficienti, ma aerei militari che vanno a batteria non ne conosco, né carri armati, né navi, né la logistica che porta in giro i nostri mezzi e i nostri beni prodotti.

Allora dobbiamo avere un approccio della circolarità economica, garantire questo con un approccio della bioeconomia, e difendere ciò che è realmente europeo.
3-0378-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, we must recognise that the strategy of the economy, of the bioeconomy, is a great deal.
The Greek term "bio" relates to the life cycle.
I shall focus on the subject of fuels and their use.
If declined from a perspective of technological neutrality, it must also place the subject of fuels at the centre. And we are talking about biofuels produced in Europe with European raw materials and European workers, which combine decarbonisation, security and employment.
Animal waste, agricultural waste, but also the recovery of primary and secondary raw materials represent a good starting point for achieving autonomy. This too is "bio", if one considers, precisely, the life cycle.
On fuels, however, there is a contradiction. Today we are asking – in these hours in Ankara, this is being said – for a greater effort for defence, a greater effort in order to be self-sufficient, but I do not know of any military aircraft that run on batteries, nor tanks, nor ships, nor the logistics that transport our vehicles and our manufactured goods.
Then we must have an approach of economic circularity, guarantee this with a bioeconomy approach, and defend what is truly European.

3-0379-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, for decades, Finland has championed the bioeconomy. Our economy is heavily based on that, but the bioeconomy is also so much more. Bioeconomy is an answer for several wicked problems of our time. The bioeconomy is not just wood, it is how to replace fossil-based solutions that we eventually need to get rid of with renewable local solutions based on bioeconomy and largely, yes, on wood, but also all the side streams it also generates for us.

There has been a lot of talk and goodwill with the bioeconomy, but then when it comes to the actual legislation, we constantly face contradictory goals. The Commission often presents rather restrictions on bioeconomy-driven legislation, which only supports the fossil industry and not the phasing out of it. Hopefully, we would finally find the maturity to integrate bioeconomy into the actual legislation, as this is not only a question of environment, but it is a question for the economy, security and self-sufficiency of this continent. Finally, I am very grateful for the groups that you back this discussion from the Renew initiative. It is very important theme for all of us.

3-0380-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, parliamo di costruire una bioeconomia europea competitiva e poi ostacoliamo una delle sue filiere più promettenti, la canapa, dove, in pochi anni, solo nell'Unione europea, la superficie coltivata è cresciuta del 60 % e la produzione di oltre l'84 %.

Non è soltanto un settore molto versatile, che fornisce materie prime per l'edilizia, il tessile, l'alimentazione, i mangimi e molti altri prodotti "bio‑based", ma anche un settore che dà agli agricoltori nuove fonti di reddito, diversificazione e quindi più resilienza, capacità di resistere alla crisi.

La nuova strategia europea per la bioeconomia deve sostenere chi lavora in questa filiera, superando gli ostacoli politici che ancora oggi ne frenano lo sviluppo.

A loro dobbiamo dare regole chiare, criteri che incentivino l'uso di materiali "bio-based" negli appalti pubblici e nelle costruzioni, investimenti – soprattutto negli impianti di prima trasformazione della fibra – e innovazione senza preconcetti.

L'Europa dispone già delle competenze, delle imprese e degli agricoltori interessati: ora serve una strategia capace di rispondere a tutto questo.
3-0380-0000.englishText: Mr President, honourable colleagues, we are talking about building a competitive European bioeconomy and then we are hindering one of its most promising supply chains, hemp, where, in just a few years, in the European Union alone, the cultivated area has grown by 60% and production by over 84%. It is not only a very versatile sector, which provides raw materials for construction, textiles, food, feed and many other "bio-based" products, but also a sector that gives farmers new sources of income, diversification and therefore more resilience, the ability to resist crisis. The new European strategy for the bioeconomy must support those who work in this supply chain, overcoming the political obstacles that still hold back its development today. We must give them clear rules, criteria that incentivize the use of "bio-based" materials in public procurement and construction, investments - especially in primary fiber processing plants - and innovation without prejudices. Europe already has the skills, the companies and the interested farmers: now we need a strategy capable of responding to all this.

3-0381-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, la bioéconomie est souvent présentée comme un secteur d’avenir, mais encore faut-il savoir au service de qui elle est mise en œuvre.

La nouvelle stratégie européenne de la Commission n’est, comme à son habitude, pas à la hauteur de l’enjeu. Sous couvert de compétitivité et d’innovation, elle organise la prédation généralisée du vivant. La logique est toujours la même: transformer le vivant en marchandise, exploiter davantage les forêts, les terres agricoles et la biomasse en allongeant l’exploitation des brevets. Le tout, en réduisant au maximum les normes environnementales et en remettant en cause le principe de précaution.

En réalité, cette stratégie ne répond qu’à une seule urgence: celle des intérêts des industriels et des capitalistes, en facilitant la privatisation du vivant à leur seul profit. À La France insoumise, nous refusons cette fuite en avant. Seule une stratégie fondée sur le bien commun, répondant aux besoins réels des populations, garantissant la préservation des écosystèmes, pourra faire face à la crise du climat.

Stop à l’écoblanchiment, place à la planification écologique!
3-0381-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, the bioeconomy is often presented as a sector of the future, but we still need to know in whose service it is implemented.

The Commission's new European strategy is, as usual, not up to the challenge. Under the guise of competitiveness and innovation, it organizes the generalized predation of living things. The logic is always the same: to transform the living into a commodity, to further exploit forests, agricultural land, and biomass by extending the exploitation of patents. All this while reducing environmental standards as much as possible and calling into question the precautionary principle.

In reality, this strategy responds to only one urgency: that of the interests of industrialists and capitalists, by facilitating the privatization of the living for their sole profit. At La France insoumise, we refuse this headlong rush. Only a strategy based on the common good, responding to the real needs of populations, guaranteeing the preservation of ecosystems, will be able to face the climate crisis.

Stop greenwashing, make way for ecological planning!

3-0382-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, I really fully agree with Mr Sokol, that this is about growth and simplification and competitiveness for Europe. And as I see it, really, the momentum now is to make this a sustainable industry strategy. For the question on the medicine and the pharma sector, we are really pushing that we put biotech act II into place very soon.

Mr Luena, you correctly point out that the resources that we have when comes to bio are not endless, but they are renewable, they are home-grown and that is why we need to both manage them with sustainability, but also use this as the opportunity to change the decarbonisation agenda that we are into. I also want to highlight one maybe additional point on that is that another part of my portfolio is that we also need to use the circularity here.

Ms Donazzan, you mentioned defence and resilience, and this is a key point for me because as I started with my first intervention, it is about reducing our dependencies. And again, a new crisis has shown how much that costs for all of us and us as consumers.

Then on the bioeconomy, I totally agree with Ms Kulmuni from Finland, I totally agree and we know that this is not a niche. This is a big sector, I showed it a little bit with my fingers in the beginning. It is a key sector for all of Europe, a sector that we can lead if we do this right, we do this together. And I think that the time to do this is now. It's never been better or worse, but there is that we have. So absolutely, I will try to move the regulation into that security angle also.

I think that I answered Ms Guarda little bit, that for me, to harmonise and use this and link it again to circularity is exactly where I am.

Finally, to Mr Smith, as I see it, this is also an opportunity to create jobs. We already see how many jobs the bioeconomy creates in rural areas, creates for foresters, creates for farmers. So this is also again something that is beneficial for all of Europe, a win-win-win situation.

3-0383-0000.sourceText:
A Uachtaráin, tá áthas orm labhairt ar an ábhar tábhachtach seo.

Europe's bioeconomy represents one of our greatest untapped economic opportunities – by turning agricultural residues, forestry by-products, marine resources and organic waste into high-value products, we can reduce our dependence on fossil-based materials while creating new jobs, new industries, and new income streams for rural communities. We need to frame the bioeconomy as a critical element of Europe's industrial policy, innovation policy and competitiveness policy. It strengthens European strategic autonomy by producing more of the materials, chemicals, fuels and ingredients we need here in Europe from resources we already have.

I therefore welcome investments such as Ireland's new National Biorefinery Pilot Plant in County Monaghan, which helps researchers, SMEs and industry from across the country to transform promising ideas into commercially viable products, bridging the gap between laboratory research and market deployment. If Europe is serious about competitiveness, circularity and supporting our rural economy, then we must put the bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial strategy, invest in innovation and give Europe's entrepreneurs the tools they need to scale-up and succeed.

Mar a deirimid as Gaeilge: 'Tapaigh an deis'.
3-0383-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I am glad to speak on this important topic.

Europe's bioeconomy represents one of our greatest untapped economic opportunities – by turning agricultural residues, forestry by-products, marine resources and organic waste into high-value products, we can reduce our dependence on fossil-based materials while creating new jobs, new industries, and new income streams for rural communities. We need to frame the bioeconomy as a critical element of Europe's industrial policy, innovation policy and competitiveness policy. It strengthens European strategic autonomy by producing more of the materials, chemicals, fuels and ingredients we need here in Europe from resources we already have.

I therefore welcome investments such as Ireland's new National Biorefinery Pilot Plant in County Monaghan, which helps researchers, SMEs and industry from across the country to transform promising ideas into commercially viable products, bridging the gap between laboratory research and market deployment. If Europe is serious about competitiveness, circularity and supporting our rural economy, then we must put the bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial strategy, invest in innovation and give Europe's entrepreneurs the tools they need to scale-up and succeed.

As we say in Irish: 'Seize the opportunity'.

3-0386-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie kann oder wird ein wichtiger Baustein für eine wettbewerbsfähige und unabhängigere Europäische Union sein, aber mehr Unabhängigkeit bedeutet nicht, dass wir einfach Biomaterialien produzieren und fossile durch biobasierte Materialien ersetzen. Schon heute stehen unsere Ökosysteme unter enormem Druck; die Bioökonomie darf deshalb nicht einfach das alte lineare Wirtschaftsmodell mit einem grünen Etikett fortsetzen.

Unsere Antwort muss – die Kommissarin hat es auch schon gesagt – eine Kreislauf-Bioökonomie sein, weniger Ressourcenverbrauch und eine klare Orientierung an der Abfallhierarchie. Unsere Chance liegt nämlich darin, mit weniger Ressourcen mehr Wert zu schaffen. Das Kreislaufwirtschaftsgesetz, das zweite Biotech-Gesetz bieten dafür wichtige Möglichkeiten – durch eine stärkere Kaskadennutzung von Biomasse, durch klare Kriterien, wann biobasierte Materialien über ihren gesamten Lebenszyklus tatsächlich einen Vorteil bringen, durch Quoten für den Einsatz dieser Materialien aus europäischer Produktion und durch die Staffelung von Abfallgebühren entsprechend der tatsächlichen Umweltfreundlichkeit der eingesetzten Materialien.

Ich bin überzeugt, so schaffen wir eine Bioökonomie, die nachhaltiger ist, die Europas Wettbewerbsfähigkeit stärkt durch Innovation, durch Ressourceneffizienz und durch weniger Abhängigkeit von globalen Rohstoffmärkten.
3-0386-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! The bioeconomy can or will be an important building block for a competitive and more independent European Union, but more independence does not mean that we simply produce biomaterials and replace fossil materials with bio-based ones. Our ecosystems are already under enormous pressure; the bioeconomy must therefore not simply continue the old linear economic model with a green label.

Our answer must – as the Commissioner has already said – be a circular bioeconomy, lower resource consumption and a clear orientation towards the waste hierarchy. Our opportunity lies in creating more value with fewer resources. The Circular Economy Act, the second Biotech Act offer important opportunities for this – through a stronger cascading use of biomass, through clear criteria on when bio-based materials actually provide an advantage over their entire life cycle, through quotas for the use of these materials from European production, and through the grading of waste fees according to the actual environmental friendliness of the materials used.

I am convinced that this is how we will create a bioeconomy that is more sustainable, that strengthens Europe's competitiveness through innovation, resource efficiency and less dependence on global raw material markets.

3-0387-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, members, a competitive and sustainable bioeconomy is a strategic necessity. Our recent experience of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz makes that all the more clear. The EU's vision for the bioeconomy is that, by 2040, bio-based construction products like biochemicals, textiles, fertilisers, plastics and so forth will all be widely deployed across our Union. These are to be fossil-free alternatives that create stable new income streams for citizens.

Looking specifically at the potential of fertilisers, we see that the bio-based fertilisers can cut our dependence on imports, lower our carbon footprint and turn agricultural residues and organic waste into real economic value. That is why, when the Commission evaluates the fertilising products regulation, it must ask whether it is delivering market access for bio-based fertilisers appropriately. If not, we need to see action now. We need to see these products fast-tracked to the market. It's a rare case where everyone can win and we can – and have to at this stage because of what I mentioned earlier – grab that opportunity with both hands.

3-0388-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, signora Commissaria, onorevoli colleghi, ogni giorno nelle nostre case, nelle mense, nei supermercati e nelle aziende agricole milioni di tonnellate di cibo finiscono nella spazzatura.

In quei materiali c'è già una parte del futuro dell'Europa: quello che oggi scartiamo può diventare energia pulita, fertilizzanti naturali, nuovi materiali compostabili, nuove imprese, nuovi posti di lavoro.

La bioeconomia è una grande politica industriale, non solo ambientale. È una scelta di libertà, perché significa dipendere meno dalle materie prime importate e valorizzare ciò che già produciamo.

L'Europa possiede competenze, ricerca e imprese capaci di guidare questa trasformazione, ma siamo lenti.

Gli scarti organici non sono un problema da eliminare, ma una risorsa da valorizzare. Dobbiamo rendere più efficienti i nostri sistemi di raccolta e di riciclo in tutta Europa e promuovere i materiali compostabili, che rappresentano davvero la soluzione migliore. Oggi troppe filiere "bio‑based" restano bloccate da ostacoli burocratici che frenano l'innovazione.

In un mondo in cui le materie prime sono sempre più rare e più contese, continuare a sprecare risorse è un lusso che l'Europa non si può più permettere.

La bioeconomia non è un sogno per il futuro, è un'opportunità concreta per costruire un'Europa più forte, più competitiva e più autonoma.
3-0388-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, honourable colleagues, every day in our homes, in canteens, in supermarkets and on farms, millions of tonnes of food end up in the bin.

In those materials there is already a part of Europe's future: what we discard today can become clean energy, natural fertilisers, new compostable materials, new businesses, new jobs.

The bioeconomy is a major industrial policy, not just an environmental one. It is a choice of freedom, because it means depending less on imported raw materials and making the most of what we already produce.

Europe possesses skills, research and businesses capable of leading this transformation, but we are slow.

Organic waste is not a problem to be eliminated, but a resource to be valued. We must make our collection and recycling systems more efficient throughout Europe and promote compostable materials, which truly represent the best solution. Today, too many bio-based supply chains remain blocked by bureaucratic obstacles that hold back innovation.

In a world where raw materials are increasingly scarce and contested, continuing to waste resources is a luxury Europe can no longer afford.

The bioeconomy is not a dream for the future; it is a concrete opportunity to build a stronger, more competitive and more autonomous Europe.

3-0389-0000.sourceText:
Κύριε Πρόεδρε, η ευρωπαϊκή βιοοικονομία μπορεί να αποτελέσει φυσικά σημαντικό εργαλείο για την πράσινη μετάβαση, την καινοτομία, τη βιομηχανική ανταγωνιστικότητα και τη στρατηγική αυτονομία της Ευρώπης. Όμως πρέπει να είμαστε σε κάτι πολύ ξεκάθαροι: Η βιοοικονομία δεν μπορεί να γίνει μια νέα μορφή πίεσης πάνω στη γη, στα δάση, στο νερό και στη βιοποικιλότητα γενικότερα. Δεν αρκεί να αντικαταστήσουμε τα ορυκτά υλικά δηλαδή με βιολογικούς πόρους, αν αυτό οδηγεί σε υπερεκμετάλλευση οικοσυστημάτων ή σε ανταγωνισμό με την παραγωγή τροφίμων.

Χρειαζόμαστε μια βιοοικονομία κυκλική, προπαντός δίκαιη και πραγματικά βιώσιμη, με προτεραιότητα στην υψηλή προστιθέμενη αξία και στις τοπικές αλυσίδες παραγωγής. Οι αγρότες, οι δασοκόμοι, οι αλιείς και οι παράκτιες κοινότητες δεν πρέπει να είναι απλώς προμηθευτές πρώτων υλών, πρέπει να είναι συμμέτοχοι στην αξία που δημιουργείται —και ιδιαίτερα στη Μεσόγειο, όπου η ξηρασία, η λειψυδρία και η απώλεια εδαφών επιδεινώνονται. Η βιοοικονομία πρέπει να συνδεθεί με την ανθεκτικότητα, την προστασία των φυσικών πόρων και την κοινωνική δικαιοσύνη.

Στρατηγική αυτονομία λοιπόν; Ναι, αλλά μέσα στα όρια της φύσης.
3-0389-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the European bioeconomy can naturally be an important tool for Europe's green transition, innovation, industrial competitiveness and strategic autonomy. But we must be very clear about one thing: The bioeconomy cannot become a new form of pressure on the land, forests, water and biodiversity in general. It is not enough to replace fossil materials with biological resources, if this leads to the overexploitation of ecosystems or competition with food production.

We need a bioeconomy that is circular, above all fair and truly sustainable, with priority given to high added value and local production chains. Farmers, foresters, fishermen and coastal communities must not simply be suppliers of raw materials, they must be participants in the value created — and especially in the Mediterranean, where drought, water scarcity and land loss are worsening. The bioeconomy must be linked to resilience, the protection of natural resources and social justice.

Strategic autonomy then? Yes, but within the limits of nature.

3-0390-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, Europe has a hidden strength: our bioeconomy, our bio-based solutions. What is this? Well, it is the power of the new and the very old. The power of the gigantic and the very, very small. The largest trees in our forests and the smallest, smallest microorganisms. They feed, they heal, they ferment and they build.

The bioeconomy contributes almost EUR 1 trillion annually to our Union, more than 8 % of GDP, and supports 17 % of our jobs. We must use this strategic asset to build for our future food security and to deliver our clean transition.

Europe's position is under pressure. The US and China move very fast. Now our Europe needs a strong Biotech Act II to create lead markets, to buy greener, to simplify how we regulate.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

3-0391-0000.sourceText: You said that we are being pressurised by the US and China, and the Biotech Act is definitely a way how to tackle this. But do you think that is enough? Do you think the Biotech Act provides enough solutions to tackle the problem of being squeezed from both sides or do we need something more? And what concretely do you think the European Commission should do to answer this very big problem of pressure from both sides?

3-0392-0000.sourceText:
Thank you very much, Mr Sokol. Yes, a very good question indeed. And I do think that many of the things that we have done together already in this field and the Biotech Act II are very important cornerstones.

But I should mention one more thing that is desperately needed and that is, I guess, also in the hands of this Commissioner – but definitely in the hands of other Commissioners and Ms von der Leyen and all the countries – it is, of course, to make the capital markets union work much better and much stronger that we have seen to date.

We know that capital is the thing that is needed when we want to grow these businesses, and it is too scarce and it is too easy to go to the US and to get the capital. So yes, please, that also.

3-0393-0000.sourceText:
Sehr geehrter Herr Präsident, liebe Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie bietet die einmalige Chance für Europa, einen einzigartigen Wirtschaftszweig zu erschließen, der Wettbewerbsfähigkeit und die Nachhaltigkeit miteinander verbindet. Fakt ist: Ohne unsere Land- und Forstwirte wird dieser Sektor keinen Erfolg haben; sie dürfen nicht nur Lieferanten von Rohstoffen sein, sondern müssen weiter an der Wertschöpfungskette beteiligt werden.

Die Innovation ist da. Schon heute gibt es eine unglaubliche Bandbreite an Produkten und Prozessen, von Baumaterialien bis hin zu biobasierten Textilien: All das gibt es heute schon in Europa.

Jetzt müssen wir in die Breite kommen. Wir brauchen Investitionen und weniger Bürokratie. Wer biobasierte Produkte entwickeln will, darf nicht an komplizierten Genehmigungen oder widersprüchlichen Vorschriften scheitern. Deshalb sollte die Bioökonomie-Strategie bestehende Hemmnisse identifizieren und den Weg vorwärts aufzeigen.

Der angekündigte Biotech Act II muss nun die Bioökonomie weiter voranbringen. Wir brauchen schnellere Genehmigungsverfahren, innovationsfreundliche Rahmenbedingungen und bessere Finanzierungsmöglichkeiten, mit Land- und Forstwirtschaft im Zentrum. Bei uns schlummert so viel Potenzial: Lassen Sie uns jetzt Europa als Standort für biobasierte Produkte entfesseln!
3-0393-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner! The bioeconomy offers Europe a unique opportunity to develop a unique economic sector that combines competitiveness and sustainability. The fact is: without our farmers and foresters, this sector will not succeed; they must not only be suppliers of raw materials, but must continue to be involved in the value chain.

Innovation is there. Today there is already an incredible range of products and processes, from building materials to bio-based textiles: all of this already exists in Europe.

Now we need to scale up. We need investment and less bureaucracy. Anyone who wants to develop bio-based products must not fail due to complicated approvals or contradictory regulations. Therefore, the bioeconomy strategy should identify existing barriers and show the way forward.

The announced Biotech Act II must now further advance the bioeconomy. We need faster approval procedures, innovation-friendly framework conditions and better financing opportunities, with agriculture and forestry at the centre. There is so much potential slumbering within us: let us now unleash Europe as a location for bio-based products!

3-0394-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Die Bioökonomie-Strategie bietet neue Chancen für die Europäische Union: die Chance, fossile Rohstoffe zu ersetzen; die Chance, auf diesem Gebiet die Technologieführerschaft zu übernehmen, und dadurch auch die Chance, Arbeitsplätze und Wohlstand in Europa abzusichern und auszubauen, vor allem durch mehr Unabhängigkeit.

Das alles sind unterstützenswerte Ziele, und genau deshalb darf es hier nicht bei schönen Überschriften bleiben. Für mich heißt das, dass wir die Kreislaufwirtschaft weiter vorantreiben müssen und mit klaren Vorgaben gegen die Verschwendung von Ressourcen angehen. Für mich heißt das, dass wir endlich die Gesundheit unserer Böden und Gewässer sicherstellen müssen. Für mich heißt das auch, dass wir klare Regeln brauchen, mit denen unsere hohen Lebensmittelstandards und der Schutz der Verbraucherinnen und Verbraucher abgesichert werden.

Eine Bioökonomie-Strategie, die auf ein starkes Fundament fußt, werde ich gerne unterstützen.
3-0394-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! The bioeconomy strategy offers new opportunities for the European Union: the chance to replace fossil raw materials; the chance to take over technology leadership in this field, and thereby also the chance to secure and expand jobs and prosperity in Europe, above all through greater independence.

All of these are objectives worthy of support, and precisely for this reason we must not stop at nice headlines here. For me, this means that we must further advance the circular economy and tackle the waste of resources with clear requirements. For me, this means that we must finally ensure the health of our soils and waters. For me, this also means that we need clear rules with which our high food standards and the protection of consumers are safeguarded.

I will gladly support a bioeconomy strategy that is based on a strong foundation.

3-0395-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, la bioéconomie, ce sont des innovations concrètes: plastique fabriqué à partir de déchets agricoles, carburants durables, ou encore médicaments. Nous avons pour cela d’excellents chercheurs et des entreprises innovantes. Mais, trop souvent, les innovations naissent chez nous et sont industrialisées ailleurs, parce que nos entreprises ont toujours les mêmes obstacles, en Europe: des procédures trop longues, un accès au marché insuffisant et un marché européen trop fragmenté.

Nous devons changer d’échelle. Il faut pour cela davantage d’investissement, avec le soutien de la BEI et du prochain budget européen. Il faut aussi des règles qui créent de vrais débouchés pour nos produits biosourcés et qui accélèrent la construction de nouvelles usines.

La bioéconomie, c’est donc aussi une politique industrielle, une politique d’innovation et un levier essentiel pour renforcer notre autonomie stratégique. Transformons ce potentiel en emplois, en investissements et en production, ici, en Europe!
3-0395-0000.englishText:
Mr President, the bioeconomy means concrete innovations: plastics made from agricultural waste, sustainable fuels, or medicines. For this, we have excellent researchers and innovative companies. But too often, innovations are born here and industrialised elsewhere, because our companies always face the same obstacles in Europe: excessively long procedures, insufficient market access, and an overly fragmented European market.

We need to scale up. This requires more investment, with the support of the EIB and the next European budget. We also need rules that create real market outlets for our bio-based products and that accelerate the construction of new factories.

The bioeconomy is therefore also an industrial policy, an innovation policy, and an essential lever for strengthening our strategic autonomy. Let us turn this potential into jobs, investment, and production, right here in Europe!

3-0396-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear Commissioners, dear colleagues, the next breakthrough that could save lives, or make plants climate resilient, or make us produce chemicals or plastics on large scales without fossil fuels, all these breakthroughs – they could come from Europe. The question is, will it? Will it be developed and produced in Europe?

Europe has it all. Europe has the knowledge, has the talent, has the innovation. We have everything to become a global leader in biotechnology. But we must ensure that those innovations will reach patients, will reach consumers, and also, for companies, it must pay off to transform. Investing in clean innovation is not an investment just in our economy. It is, above all, an investment in healthcare, an investment in sustainability, in our environment. Bioeconomy is Europe's future. By bringing together health, sustainability, competitiveness, we can really strengthen Europe's strategic autonomy.

3-0397-0000.sourceText:
Arvoisa puhemies, arvoisa komission jäsen, riippumattomuus Venäjän tai Lähi-idän fossiilipolttoaineista ei synny siten, että rajoitamme voimakkaasti Euroopassa uusiutuvien luonnonvarojen käyttöä. Biotalous on yksi tärkeimmistä keinoistamme vahvistaa omavaraisuutta ja rakentaa vahvempaa, uusiutuviin luonnonvaroihin perustuvaa Eurooppaa. Samalla vähennämme tuontiriippuvuutta, luomme työpaikkoja ja nostamme tietysti jalostusarvoa sekä vahvistamme huoltovarmuuttamme.

Tarvitsemme johdonmukaista sääntelyä, ilmasto- ja energiatavoitteiden yhteensovittamista, teknologianeutraalisuutta ja investointien, myös tutkimuksen, määrätietoista tukemista. Esimerkiksi ennallistamisasetuksen toimeenpanoon liittyy edelleen merkittäviä epävarmuuksia, mitä tulee sen laajuuteen, hintaan ja vaikutuksiin. Jos emme luo yrityksille ennustettavaa toimintaympäristöä, investoinnit jäävät tekemättä ja riippumattomuus jää pelkäksi puheeksi. On hyvä, että EU:n biotalousstrategia tunnistaa myös biokiertotalouden valtavan potentiaalin. Nyt tarvitaan myös poliittista rohkeutta hyödyntää sitä.
3-0397-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, independence from Russian or Middle Eastern fossil fuels does not come about by us heavily restricting the use of renewable natural resources in Europe. The bioeconomy is one of our most important means to strengthen self-sufficiency and build a stronger Europe based on renewable natural resources. At the same time, we reduce import dependency, create jobs and, of course, raise the added value and strengthen our security of supply.

We need consistent regulation, the reconciliation of climate and energy targets, technological neutrality and the determined support of investments, including research. For example, the implementation of the Nature Restoration Regulation still involves significant uncertainties as to its scope, price and impacts. If we do not create a predictable operating environment for companies, investments will not be made and independence will remain just talk. It is good that the EU's bioeconomy strategy also recognizes the huge potential of the biocircular economy. Now we also need the political courage to utilize it.

3-0398-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, liebe Frau Kommissarin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Strategische Autonomie bedeutet nicht nur, Abhängigkeiten bei Chips, Energie oder kritischen Rohstoffen zu verringern; sie bedeutet auch, unsere eigenen biologischen Ressourcen besser zu nutzen. Die Bioökonomie kann Europa in zentralen Bereichen unabhängiger machen – bei der Lebensmittelversorgung, bei Energie, bei Gesundheit und überall dort, wo wir heute noch von fossilen Rohstoffen abhängig sind.

Das ist kein Nischenthema. Die europäische Bioökonomie steht bereits heute für mehr als 17 Millionen Arbeitsplätze und eine Wertschöpfung von 2,7 Billionen Euro. Arbeitsplätze in der Bioökonomieindustrie sind hochproduktiv und schaffen fast drei weitere indirekte Arbeitsplätze in Europa. Gerade für ländliche Räume und Küstenregionen ergeben sich hier neue Chancen.

Europa ist in der Bioökonomie nicht abgehängt – im Gegenteil, wir sind stark in Forschung und Innovation. Was uns noch fehlt, ist die industrielle Skalierung; dafür braucht es mehr Pioniergeist, mehr Investitionsbereitschaft, europaweite Harmonisierung und Leitmärkte für biobasierte Produkte.

Gut, dass die EU‑Kommission das Thema auf die Agenda gesetzt hat. Unsere Aufgabe ist es jetzt, dafür zu sorgen, dass Biotech-Cluster, Regulierung und Finanzierung besser ineinandergreifen, damit die Bioökonomie in Europa international wettbewerbsfähig wird und bleibt.
3-0398-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear Commissioner, dear colleagues! Strategic autonomy does not only mean reducing dependencies on chips, energy or critical raw materials; it also means making better use of our own biological resources. The bioeconomy can make Europe more independent in key areas – in food supply, energy, health and wherever we are still dependent on fossil raw materials today.

This is not a niche topic. The European bioeconomy already accounts for more than 17 million jobs and a value added of 2.7 trillion euros. Jobs in the bioeconomy industry are highly productive and create almost three additional indirect jobs in Europe. This creates new opportunities, especially for rural and coastal regions.

Europe is not left behind in the bioeconomy – on the contrary, we are strong in research and innovation. What we still lack is industrial scaling; this requires more pioneering spirit, greater willingness to invest, Europe-wide harmonization and lead markets for bio-based products.

It is good that the European Commission has put this topic on the agenda. Our task now is to ensure that biotech clusters, regulation and financing mesh better together so that the bioeconomy in Europe becomes and remains internationally competitive.

3-0399-0000.sourceText:
Herr talman! Biofiber i kläder och tyg, starka limträbalkar, snygga byggmaterial, gröna kemikalier, rengöringsmedel, smörjmedel, biobaserad färg och lim, bioplast, hållbara förpackningar, biogas, biodrivmedel, el och värme. Ja, listan kan göras lång.

Jag står ofta i den här talarstolen och säger att vi i EU måste bryta vårt beroende av fossila energikällor, insatsråvaror och kemikalier. Jag får lika ofta frågan, inte minst från den här sidan i parlamentet – de som förnekar klimatförändringarna och vill fortsätta handla med diktaturer och skurkstater – om hur det här ska gå till. Här har ni svaret: i bioekonomin. Låt oss göra det fossila till historia med bioresurser från skog, lantbruk och hav. Kan vi göra slut med det fossila?

Då duger det inte med EU-regler som ställer sig i vägen. Nu måste EU leverera enklare regler som möjliggör och inte blockerar skogsbruk, som bättre finansierar och tar vara på möjligheter och potentialen i hela vår biobaserade sektor.
3-0399-0000.englishText:
Mr President! Biofibre in clothing and fabric, strong glued laminated timber beams, stylish building materials, green chemicals, cleaning agents, lubricants, bio-based paint and glue, bioplastics, sustainable packaging, biogas, biofuels, electricity and heat. Yes, the list can be made long.

I often stand at this rostrum and say that we in the EU must break our dependence on fossil energy sources, input raw materials, and chemicals. I am just as often asked, not least from this side of the parliament – those who deny climate change and want to continue trading with dictatorships and rogue states – about how this is going to be done. Here is your answer: in the bioeconomy. Let us make the fossil fuels history with bio-resources from forestry, agriculture, and the sea. Can we put an end to the fossil?

Then EU rules that stand in the way will not do. Now the EU must deliver simpler rules that enable and do not block forestry, that better finance and take advantage of the opportunities and potential in our entire bio-based sector.

3-0401-0000.sourceText:
Poštovani predsjedavajući, ako želimo istinsku stratešku autonomiju Europske unije, moramo početi od onoga što je temelj svake ekonomije, naših prirodnih resursa i sposobnosti da ih održivo koristimo.

Upravo zato bioekonomija nije samo razvojna prilika, nego strateška nužnost. Ona Europi omogućuje manju ovisnost o uvozu, jača našu proizvodnju i istodobno daje odgovor na klimatske izazove. U tome poljoprivreda ima nezamjenjivu ulogu, no ova tranzicija mora biti pravedna. Hrvatska to najbolje pokazuje: naša Slavonija, Zagorje, Međimurje, Banija, Lika, Dalmatinska zagora, Gorski kotar i brojne druge ruralne regije imaju golemi potencijal da postanu europski centri proizvodnje biomaterijala, obnovljive energije, inovacija i kvalitetnih radnih mjesta. Ono što nam nedostaje nije potencijal, nego ulaganja, moderna infrastruktura i snažnija europska potpora.

Zato trebamo ambicioznu europsku strategiju koja će povezati bioekonomiju, poljoprivredu i regionalni razvoj te ulagati upravo ondje gdje Europa može biti najjača: u svojim regijama.
3-0401-0000.englishText:
Respected President, if we want true strategic autonomy of the European Union, we must start from what is the foundation of every economy, our natural resources and the ability to use them sustainably.

That is exactly why the bioeconomy is not only a development opportunity, but a strategic necessity. It enables Europe to have less dependence on imports, strengthens our production and at the same time provides an answer to climate challenges. In this, agriculture has an irreplaceable role, but this transition must be fair. Croatia shows this best: our Slavonia, Zagorje, Međimurje, Banija, Lika, Dalmatinska zagora, Gorski kotar and numerous other rural regions have enormous potential to become European centers of biomaterials production, renewable energy, innovation and quality jobs. What we lack is not potential, but investments, modern infrastructure and stronger European support.

That is why we need an ambitious European strategy that will connect the bioeconomy, agriculture and regional development and invest precisely where Europe can be strongest: in its regions.

3-0402-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, there is something in the leftist logic that I simply cannot understand. You claim to want a cleaner and more autonomous Europe, yet your actions contradict your words.

In the energy sector, you push electrification while undermining Europe's nuclear industry. You want batteries instead of petrol, but you oppose mines for the critical raw materials that batteries require.

The same contradiction applies to the automotive sector. You push electric vehicles while burdening European producers – it is almost like calling on China to dominate our automotive market.

When forestry companies are innovating to build a bio-based future, you oppose them and demand limitations on harvesting the material that is needed for wood-based products. The leftist logic is hurting Europe.

3-0403-0000.sourceText:
Domnule președinte, doamnă comisar, stimați colegi, sigur că Uniunea Europeană are nevoie de o strategie în domeniul bioeconomiei. Numai că, doamnă comisar, chiar dumneavoastră ați spus, că există capital, dar oare ce ne lipsește? Încrederea.

Pentru că de foarte multe ori, în această perioadă, în Uniunea Europeană s-au făcut reglementări care se obstrucționează unele pe altele. Și ca să vă dau un exemplu concret: se vorbea aici de biotehnologia farmaceutică și este foarte important să avem această independență într-o industrie de care depinde, de fapt, viața oamenilor. Dar avem o directivă - directiva privind apele uzate. Noi, Parlamentul, am votat o rezoluție să o schimbați pentru că este prost gândită și are un impact și închide pe rând fabricile de medicamente.

Vă mai pot da exemple în domeniul textil - unde am lucrat vreo 36 de ani - că ani de zile Uniunea Europeană a ars câmpul cu cânepă, considerând-o absolut neutilizabilă și dăunătoare. De fapt, este o plantă textilă ecologică, care poate fi folosită în toate domeniile și este cea mai eficientă - pentru că nu arunci nimic din ea, de la uleiuri până la reziduuri care se folosesc în domeniul construcțiilor.

Și atunci lipsa aceasta de încredere că există o continuitate a politicilor face ca investitorul să nu investească. Poate că veniți să eliminați acele bariere, pentru că mai avem o barieră, bariera tarifelor, pentru că puneți taxe vamale - și o spun mereu aici - la materii prime mai mici decât la produsele finite.
3-0403-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, of course the European Union needs a strategy in the field of the bioeconomy. Only that, Commissioner, you yourself said that there is capital, but what is it that we are lacking? Trust.

Because very often, during this period, regulations have been made within the European Union that obstruct one another. And to give you a concrete example: people were talking here about pharmaceutical biotechnology and it is very important to have this independence in an industry upon which people's lives actually depend. But we have a directive - the urban wastewater directive. We, the Parliament, voted on a resolution for you to change it because it is poorly designed and also has an impact and is shutting down pharmaceutical factories one by one.

I can give you more examples in the textile sector - where I worked for about 36 years - that for years the European Union burned hemp fields, considering it absolutely unusable and harmful. In fact, it is an ecological textile plant, which can be used in all fields and is the most efficient - because you do not throw anything away from it, from oils to residues used in construction.

And then this lack of confidence that there is continuity in policies causes the investor not to invest. Perhaps you are coming to eliminate those barriers, because we still have a barrier, the tariff barrier, because you impose customs duties - and I always say it here - on raw materials that are lower than on finished products.

3-0405-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, honourable Members, thank you very much for this debate. It was really encouraging for me. I would just briefly repeat some things.

Bioeconomy is a big sector – I talked about it in the beginning, many have repeated it – and it has big potential. We also see the great importance for our resilience with bioeconomy. Biofertilisers were mentioned – I totally agree that we can create our own home-grown fertilisers. Competitiveness will be encouraged by this, but also of course fighting climate change, decarbonisation and the dependencies that we have today.

Of course, I also see the challenges. Access to the market was mentioned by many. That is actually the one thing that is mentioned over and over again when I visit innovative companies all around Europe. The need for scale up, the need for finance, but also, as I said at the beginning, it's not always the lack of capital, but it's the mismatch of capital.

I will end my intervention stealing what MEP Sean Kelly said. He said, 'Let us now use this momentum.' That was my words maybe, but 'let's put the circular bioeconomy at the heart of our industrial agenda.'

Thank you very much for the debate.

3-0406-0000.sourceText:
The debate is closed.

With the new rules, it's obvious that there are no more Members in the room. We are only six; taking account that I'm here as well, we are seven.

3-0413-0000.sourceText: The next item is the debate on seven motions for resolutions on the threat of war crimes, the escalating violations of international humanitarian law and the human rights situation in El-Obeid, Sudan (2026/2799(RSP)).

3-0414-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, starvation, rape, enforced disappearances and torture as weapons of war. Thousands have been killed and many more have been forced to flee their homes. This is what the world was witnessing in El Fasher just months ago.

Today, the people of El‑Obeid face the same horrific fate. For months, the RSF siege entrapped half a million men, women and children. Drone strikes on fuel stations and hospitals have deprived people from food, healthcare and safety, leaving them to live in constant fear.

Europe has not done enough to prevent what could become another massacre in El-Obeid, despite our moral and legal responsibility to act. Today, we call on the Council and the Commission to change this course, impose sanctions on those responsible for this crime, and use every available lever to end the external support that is fuelling Sudan's suffering.

3-0415-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues, the clock is ticking for the people in El-Obeid, and today we have the eighth debate this mandate on Sudan. The EU has the opportunity to curb further human suffering, so I look to you, Commissioner: Article 21 of the Treaty on European Union places upon you – on the Commission – the responsibility for consistent foreign policy.

Consistent foreign policy is not giving a little aid to victims of the humanitarian disaster, and bags of support for those who sustain it. It is not condemning violations of human rights and clearing the room for the lobbyists of the very financiers of those war crimes. It is not millions of euros for humanitarian support to the Sudanese people, and billions of euros for trade to the United Arab Emirates. But it is providing support for those who need it most, imposing sanctions on those who sustain this conflict, considering the inclusion of the RSF on the EU's terrorist list, and demanding that all perpetrators of war crimes across Sudan be held accountable.

3-0416-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, 33 million: that is the number of people in Sudan who urgently need humanitarian assistance, and 16 million of them are children.

Colleagues, the situation in Sudan is worsening by the day. The RSF are now threatening an offensive on El-Obeid, putting 500 000 civilians at risk. We have already witnessed the horror of El Fasher. We cannot allow another massacre to happen. We must increase humanitarian assistance, ensure humanitarian access and support those working on the ground to save lives. But we must also hold those who are responsible to account. The Council must adopt targeted restrictive measures against commanders, financiers and external enablers – such as the UAE‑based private security company Global Security Services Group – for providing military support to the RSF.

Colleagues, our commitment to international law is tested not by our words but by our actions. The people of Sudan are suffering and we must not look away.

3-0417-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, first of all, thank you all colleagues, for the collaboration on this resolution. I put it on the agenda because we urgently need decisive action to save lives in Sudan – 33 million dependent on aid, 19 million facing hunger, and now the siege on El‑Obeid that will escalate this crisis, especially for women and children.

It's remarkable how easily some in this House pretend to care about women's rights. But behind closed doors they just care about the UAE, and I'm looking to the far‑right colleagues over there. The UAE is the state that is funding the war, and the rape and trafficking of women. Last time, too many Members on that side of the house stayed silent when we all wanted to hold the Emirates accountable. And here we are again.

Now there's even more evidence of the Emirates funding the war in Sudan. They are responsible for this genocide, and it is time they paid for it. I think tomorrow is the time to vote in favour of this resolution for women's rights.

3-0418-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señorías, supongo que han visto ustedes imágenes de mujeres en Sudán con sus hijos encima llorando de desesperación.

Ante esto hay dos opciones. Una es explicar lo que sucede en Sudán recurriendo al viejo relato del colonialismo según el cual los conflictos en el Sur Global se deben a que son unos bárbaros, a que no saben convivir en paz, a que no saben autogobernarse. Bajo ese relato siempre se han justificado las invasiones extranjeras y se ha callado ante la violencia que suponen.

Y hay otra opción: decir la verdad. Decir la verdad en el caso de Sudán implica decir que los 60 000 muertos son consecuencia de la responsabilidad de Occidente y sus aliados; que los Emiratos Árabes Unidos introducen las armas que sirven para cometer un genocidio y que extraen el oro de Sudán; que —como todos y todas sabemos— el Gobierno de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos es un Gobierno títere de los Estados Unidos e Israel; que los planes expansionistas del sionismo están detrás del genocidio que se está cometiendo en Sudán; y, otra vez más, que los Estados Unidos e Israel son la principal amenaza para la humanidad.
3-0418-0000.englishText:
Mr. President, ladies and gentlemen, I suppose you have seen images of women in Sudan with their children on top of them, crying in despair.

Faced with this, there are two options. One is to explain what is happening in Sudan by resorting to the old narrative of colonialism according to which conflicts in the Global South are due to them being barbarians, not knowing how to live together in peace, and not knowing how to govern themselves. Under that narrative, foreign invasions have always been justified and silence has been kept in the face of the violence they entail.

And there is another option: to tell the truth. Telling the truth in the case of Sudan implies saying that the 60,000 deaths are the consequence of the responsibility of the West and its allies; that the United Arab Emirates introduces the weapons used to commit a genocide and extracts gold from Sudan; that—as all of us know—the government of the United Arab Emirates is a puppet government of the United States and Israel; that the expansionist plans of Zionism are behind the genocide being committed in Sudan; and, once again, that the United States and Israel are the main threat to humanity.

3-0419-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, la situazione nella città di El Obeid, 340 000 abitanti, sta precipitando.
