Centinaia di migliaia di civili sono intrappolati nei combattimenti, mentre continuano gli attacchi contro la popolazione e l'infrastruttura civile. L'Alto Commissario delle Nazioni Unite per i diritti umani ha confermato che i civili vivono in questa città da 18 mesi sotto assedio permanente e che si rischia una nuova tragedia umanitaria.

Sia chiaro: in Sudan non esiste una soluzione militare. Entrambe le parti sono responsabili di gravissime violazioni del diritto internazionale umanitario. Per questo, chiediamo un cessate il fuoco immediato, il pieno rispetto della dichiarazione di Gedda, un accesso umanitario senza ostacoli e sanzioni più severe contro chi alimenta il conflitto e impedisce addirittura l'arrivo di aiuti umanitari.

Non ci sarà pace finché il futuro del Sudan resterà nelle mani di questi gruppi estremisti. I Fratelli mussulmani hanno alimentato per anni radicalizzazione, violenza e instabilità in Sudan e in tutta la regione.

L'Unione europea, insieme alle Nazioni Unite e all'Unione africana, deve sostenere un processo politico che escluda ogni influenza dei movimenti islamisti radicali.
3-0419-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, the situation in the city of El Obeid, with 340,000 inhabitants, is plummeting.

Hundreds of thousands of civilians are trapped in the fighting, while attacks against the population and civilian infrastructure continue. The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has confirmed that civilians have been living in this city for 18 months under permanent siege and that a new humanitarian tragedy is looming.

Let it be clear: there is no military solution in Sudan. Both sides are responsible for very serious violations of international humanitarian law. For this reason, we call for an immediate ceasefire, full respect for the Jeddah Declaration, unhindered humanitarian access and stricter sanctions against those who fuel the conflict and even prevent the arrival of humanitarian aid.

There will be no peace as long as the future of Sudan remains in the hands of these extremist groups. The Muslim Brotherhood has fueled radicalization, violence and instability in Sudan and throughout the region for years.

The European Union, together with the United Nations and the African Union, must support a political process that excludes any influence from radical Islamist movements.

3-0420-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Der Sudan gleicht der Hölle auf Erden – über 150 000 Tote, 14 Millionen Vertriebene, 25 Millionen Hungernde, massenhaft Vergewaltigungen und systematische Verfolgungen von Christen und nicht-arabischen Minderheiten. Es drohen jetzt weitere Massaker – wir verurteilen das aufs Schärfste.

Natürlich befeuert dieser Konflikt auch Massenmigration nach Europa. Wer aber den halben Sudan aufnimmt, hilft nicht dem Sudan, sondern wird selbst zum Sudan. Wir müssen daher unsere Außengrenzen schützen, und wir sollten dort helfen, wo es sinnvoll ist, nämlich in der Region, gemeinsam mit den Nachbarstaaten; das ist Diplomatie.

Es geht darum, Realismus mit Humanität zu verbinden: klare Kante gegen Kriegsverbrechen, keine Waffenlieferungen, die den Konflikt nur verlängern, regionale Stabilität statt weiterer Anreize für Massenmigration und deshalb enge Kooperation mit den Staaten der Region statt Werteimperialismus. Denn eine tragfähige Friedenslösung ist nur dann möglich, wenn man die regionalen und kulturellen Kontexte berücksichtigt; wer diese ignoriert, verschlimmert nur das Chaos.

Das ist eine Politik der Verantwortung gegenüber den Menschen im Sudan und gegenüber den Menschen in Europa.
3-0420-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! Sudan is like hell on earth – over 150,000 dead, 14 million displaced, 25 million starving, massive rapes and systematic persecution of Christians and non-Arab minorities. Further massacres are now threatening – we condemn this in the strongest possible terms.

Of course, this conflict also fuels mass migration to Europe. But whoever takes in half of Sudan is not helping Sudan, but is becoming Sudan themselves. We must therefore protect our external borders, and we should help where it makes sense, namely in the region, together with the neighbouring states; that is diplomacy.

It is about combining realism with humanity: a clear stance against war crimes, no arms deliveries that only prolong the conflict, regional stability instead of further incentives for mass migration, and therefore close cooperation with the states of the region instead of value imperialism. Because a sustainable peace solution is only possible if the regional and cultural contexts are taken into account; anyone who ignores these only makes the chaos worse.

This is a policy of responsibility towards the people in Sudan and towards the people in Europe.

3-0421-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! Powiem tak: Sudan to nasza sprawa. Sudan to nasza sprawa, bo kiedy głód staje się bronią, pojawia się co? Migracja.

Usłyszałam dzisiaj dwie złe odpowiedzi na ten temat. Pierwsza to lewicowe marzenia, że wystarczy otworzyć drzwi i świat się sam ułoży. Otóż nie ułoży się. Mieliśmy już tego przykłady. Druga odpowiedź: migracja to ryzyko – kto temu zaprzecza, nie kocha Europy.

Ta druga odpowiedź to prawicowy kabotynizm. Wiecie co? Mamy na tej sali europosła, który biega po ulicy i nagrywa ludzi tylko dlatego, że mają inny kolor skóry. To po prostu świr. Musimy wybrać inną drogę. Korytarze humanitarne – natychmiast. Rozliczenie zbrodni wojennych – natychmiast. Musimy działać, nie czekać.
3-0421-0000.englishText:
Mr President! I will put it this way: Sudan is our business. Sudan is our business, because when hunger becomes a weapon, what appears? Migration.

I heard two bad answers on this subject today. The first is leftist dreams that it is enough to open the door and the world will sort itself out. Well, it won't sort itself out. We have already had examples of this. The second answer: migration is a risk – whoever denies this does not love Europe.

This second answer is right-wing posturing. You know what? We have an MEP in this chamber who runs around the street and films people just because they have a different skin colour. He's simply a nutcase. We must choose another path. Humanitarian corridors – immediately. Accountability for war crimes – immediately. We must act, not wait.

3-0422-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, depois de Zamzam e El-Fasher, El-Obeid corre o risco de ser o epicentro de uma nova tragédia no Sudão.

El-Obeid, que alberga uma população de meio milhão de habitantes, mas também um número indeterminado de pessoas internamente deslocadas, e que está desde há meses cercada. El-Obeid onde, aos ataques contínuos de drones que destruíram infraestruturas essenciais, semeando a fome e a cólera, ameaça agora juntar-se a repetição do massacre de civis a que assistimos antes, quando as Forças Rápidas de Suporte e as Forças Armadas Sudanesas se confrontaram, alimentadas pelo exterior.

«Os países com influência têm o dever de a exercer agora para parar esta loucura», foram as palavras do Alto Representante das Nações Unidas para os Direitos Humanos. E é isso que, hoje, pedimos que a União Europeia, mas também os Estados Unidos, o Egito, os Emirados Árabes Unidos façam. Respeito pelo bloqueio na entrada de armas, sanções individuais e responsabilização, participação na construção de uma solução civil para o conflito.
3-0422-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, after Zamzam and El-Fasher, El-Obeid is at risk of being the epicenter of a new tragedy in Sudan.

El-Obeid, which is home to a population of half a million inhabitants, as well as an undetermined number of internally displaced persons, and which has been surrounded for months. El-Obeid where, to the continuous drone attacks that destroyed essential infrastructure, sowing hunger and cholera, is now threatened by the repetition of the massacre of civilians that we witnessed before, when the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces clashed, fueled from the outside.

"Countries with influence have a duty to exercise it now to stop this madness," were the words of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights. And that is what, today, we ask the European Union, but also the United States, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates to do. Respect for the arms import embargo, individual sanctions and accountability, participation in building a civil solution to the conflict.

3-0423-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, mes chers collègues, à El-Obeid, les populations subissent des bombardements, des exécutions, des viols, des déplacements forcés et des violations répétées du droit international humanitaire. Il semble que nous soyons tous d’accord aujourd’hui pour faire ce constat.

On notera cependant qu’étrangement, on entend peu les élus d’extrême gauche – et je veux parler particulièrement de La France insoumise – autour de ce sujet. Il faut dire qu’ici il n’y a d’opportunité ni d’attaquer les Juifs ni d’attaquer Israël.

Alors la réalité – certains l’ont dit –, c’est que nombre d’États sont complices de ce qui se passe au Soudan, puisque les Émirats arabes unis, qui soutiennent les forces de soutien rapides à l’origine des massacres, jouissent chez nous, c’est vrai, d’un passe-droit scandaleux acheté à coups de pétrodollars.

Oui, si nous voulons arrêter de regarder ailleurs ou sortir de l’incantation pour réellement stopper ces massacres et ces exactions, commençons par pointer les vrais responsables et prenons aussi les mesures qui sont à notre portée!
3-0423-0000.englishText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, in El-Obeid, populations are suffering from bombardments, executions, rapes, forced displacements, and repeated violations of international humanitarian law. It seems that we all agree today in making this observation.

It should be noted, however, that strangely enough, we rarely hear from far-left elected officials - and I am speaking particularly of La France insoumise - on this subject. It must be said that here there is no opportunity either to attack Jews or to attack Israel.

So the reality - as some have said - is that a number of States are complicit in what is happening in Sudan, since the United Arab Emirates, which support the Rapid Support Forces behind the massacres, enjoy at home, it is true, a scandalous special pass bought with petrodollars.

Yes, if we want to stop looking elsewhere or move beyond mere words to actually stop these massacres and abuses, let us start by pointing out the real culprits and also take the measures within our reach!

3-0424-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Vice-President, honourable Members, as we speak, the Sudanese city of El-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan stands on the brink of catastrophe. About the size of Poznań, Lyon, or Lisbon, and home to one of Sudan's largest universities, it shelters some 500 000 people, including more than 100 000 who have already been displaced at least once this year.

Today, all of them are in danger. For the past three weeks, drone strikes have hit the city. Dozens of civilians have been killed. Fuel depots, power and water supply lines and medical facilities have been struck. And around El-Obeid, the rapid support forces are amassing their forces for what could be an imminent, large‑scale assault.

We have seen this before in El Fasher in October 2025: the mass killings, the ethnically targeted violence, the sexual violence. The UN's independent international fact‑finding mission documented it. El-Obeid must not become another El Fasher.

So let me be clear on what the European Union demands. The European Union calls on the Rapid Support Forces to halt their assault immediately, and to refrain from any offensive that would place civilians at risk of mass atrocities. Credible reports of ethnically targeted violence are already emerging. International humanitarian law must be respected. Civilians must be free to leave safely. Humanitarian actors must be granted rapid, safe and unhindered access to everyone in need, underpinned by credible security guarantees.

The EU calls on those who support and have influence over the Rapid Support Forces to use that influence now. The responsibility does not rest with the warring parties alone; it rests also with those who arm them, finance them and enable them.

And the European Union is not a bystander. The European Council conclusions on Sudan, adopted in October 2025, spell out four key asks to all parties of the conflict: ceasefire, humanitarian access and protection of civilians, civilian governance and accountability. Our Special Representative for the Horn of Africa has reached out to the Rapid Support Forces at every level of their leadership, and through our regional partners. The European Union is engaged with the Quintet and with the wider international community to press for a cessation of hostilities and return to credible, civilian‑led transition.

The European Union has already imposed restrictive measures on those fuelling this conflict, linked to both the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces, and we stand ready to act again. Those who commit atrocities and those who command them will be held to account through our sanctions, through the independent fact‑finding mission to Sudan and through the International Criminal Court. Impunity is not an option.

Dear Members, we are raising the alarm now so that the international community is not left, once again, to document the massacre after it has happened. As Sudan's war has entered its fourth year, we call on the parties for constructive engagement in negotiations towards an immediate ceasefire. Only so can the suffering of the Sudanese people end.

3-0425-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, dear colleagues, as Commissioner Šuica mentioned, the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in El‑Obeid is yet another tragic reminder that the people of Sudan continue to pay the highest price for a conflict they did not choose.

Reports of discriminate attacks on civilians, the destruction of vital infrastructure and the obstruction of humanitarian assistance raise serious concerns about violations of international humanitarian law. Those responsible for atrocities against civilians must be held accountable.

At the same time, we must ensure that humanitarian organisations can reach those in need. Millions of Sudanese are facing displacement, hunger and a complete lack of basic services.

We have to call to all parties and also external actors to agree to an immediate ceasefire, engaging, meaningful dialogue and working towards a peaceful, Sudanese‑led political process that respects human dignity and the rule of law.

3-0426-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, les confieso que asisto a este debate con dosis de frustración y de impotencia, porque traemos una y otra vez el debate sobre Sudán a esta Cámara mientras Sudán se desangra y El Obeid se convierte en un símbolo de una tragedia anunciada una y otra vez.

En apenas tres semanas ha habido quince ataques con drones en la ciudad, ejecuciones sumarias, secuestros, tortura y violencia sexual en la región. Hay más de 13 millones de personas desplazadas, más de 33 millones necesitan ayuda urgente y millones viven bajo la amenaza del hambre. Pero al mundo directamente no le importa.

Debemos exigir de una vez por todas el cese inmediato de los ataques a los civiles, a las escuelas, a los mercados. El Derecho humanitario internacional no puede ser una promesa vacía ni una norma selectiva, debe ser siempre nuestra brújula de forma coherente.

Es verdad que la Unión Europea ha estado a la altura en la necesidad de la ayuda humanitaria, pero no es suficiente. Tenemos que desplegar la diplomacia humanitaria, garantizar los corredores y, sobre todo, parar esta barbarie de una vez por todas. La respuesta humanitaria necesita 2 900 millones de dólares, el 0,1 % del gasto militar, para abordar 20 millones de personas y sus necesidades. A nadie le importa y no estamos a la altura.
3-0426-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, I confess that I attend this debate with a dose of frustration and helplessness, because we bring the debate on Sudan to this House time and time again while Sudan bleeds and El Obeid becomes a symbol of a tragedy announced over and over again.

In barely three weeks there have been fifteen drone attacks in the city, summary executions, kidnappings, torture, and sexual violence in the region. There are more than 13 million displaced people, more than 33 million need urgent help, and millions live under the threat of famine. But the world simply does not care.

We must demand once and for all the immediate cessation of attacks on civilians, schools, and markets. International humanitarian law cannot be an empty promise or a selective norm; it must always be our compass in a coherent manner.

It is true that the European Union has risen to the occasion regarding the need for humanitarian aid, but it is not enough. We have to deploy humanitarian diplomacy, guarantee corridors and, above all, stop this barbarism once and for all. The humanitarian response needs 2.9 billion dollars, 0.1% of military spending, to address 20 million people and their needs. Nobody cares and we are not rising to the occasion.

3-0428-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, c’est la troisième fois en six mois qu’une discussion alarmante de la situation dramatique au Soudan est à l’ordre du jour de cette assemblée. À chaque fois, nous dénonçons les massacres, les conditions de vie, voire de survie, des populations déplacées, de millions d’enfants menacés par la famine, de femmes et de jeunes filles exposées aux violences sexuelles, sans oublier les dizaines de milliers de morts.

La dernière fois, il s’agissait également d’attirer l’attention sur l’ingérence extérieure, et notamment celle des Émirats arabes unis.

Aujourd’hui, c’est la situation d’El-Obeid qui nous préoccupe. Il est impératif que l’Union européenne mette en place des mesures de protection immédiates. Les populations d’El-Obeid doivent être protégées. L’Union européenne doit être à leurs côtés.
3-0428-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, this is the third time in six months that an alarming discussion of the dramatic situation in Sudan has been on the agenda of this assembly. Each time, we denounce the massacres, the living conditions, or even conditions of survival, of displaced populations, of millions of children threatened by famine, of women and girls exposed to sexual violence, not to mention the tens of thousands of dead.

The last time, it was also a question of drawing attention to external interference, and in particular that of the United Arab Emirates.

Today, it is the situation in El-Obeid that concerns us. It is imperative that the European Union put in place immediate protection measures. The populations of El-Obeid must be protected. The European Union must be by their side.

3-0429-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Islam is not a religion of peace. I know that might be hard for some people to hear, but the evidence is overwhelming. Some will angrily say that not all Muslims are violent. I would agree. However, Islam is the vehicle that has caused terror and suffering across the globe. Let me give you an example. Besides the devastating civil war, Sudan, for example, has suffered from jihadist terrorism and Islamist oppression. The country is ranked in the top five for Christian persecution.

When Islam becomes the majority, minorities pay the price. They are silenced, many of them even abducted, raped, murdered or have their lands taken away from them. We cannot talk about solutions without recognising the problem. The problem is Islam not respecting the dignity of human life.

3-0430-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire Šuica, je vais essayer avec une grande retenue de vous exprimer la profondeur de ma colère par rapport à vos paroles, qui dégoulinent d’hypocrisie.

Vous avez parlé du massacre d’El-Facher – des milliers de Soudanais massacrés par les Forces rapides, soutenues par les Émirats arabes unis. Vous n’avez pas osé le dire, mais vous le savez. Qu’avez-vous fait? Un mois après ce massacre, vous avez été dans les Émirats leur offrir un partenariat stratégique avec l’Union européenne. Ça revient à les encourager à continuer leur soutien aux massacres au Soudan. Et encore aujourd’hui, vous n’arrivez pas à les condamner, à prononcer ces mots et à prendre des sanctions contre eux.

La même chose, vous l’avez faite avec les Palestiniens:: le jour où les Nations unies ont publié un rapport disant qu’Israël cible délibérément des enfants palestiniens, vous allez en Israël, sourire avec le président israélien: «J’ai hâte de développer de nouveaux partenariats.»

Prenez des sanctions, arrêtez vos larmes de crocodile et condamnez les Émirats et condamnez Israël!
3-0430-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Commissioner Šuica, I will try with great restraint to express to you the depth of my anger regarding your words, which drip with hypocrisy.

You spoke of the massacre in El Fasher – thousands of Sudanese massacred by the Rapid Support Forces, supported by the United Arab Emirates. You did not dare to say it, but you know it. What did you do? A month after this massacre, you went to the Emirates to offer them a strategic partnership with the European Union. This amounts to encouraging them to continue their support for the massacres in Sudan. And still today, you are unable to condemn them, to utter those words, and to take sanctions against them.

The same thing you did with the Palestinians: the day the United Nations published a report saying that Israel deliberately targets Palestinian children, you go to Israel, smiling with the Israeli president: "I look forward to developing new partnerships."

Take sanctions, stop your crocodile tears, and condemn the Emirates and condemn Israel!

3-0432-0000.sourceText:
The debate is closed.

The vote will take place tomorrow, 9 July 2026.

3-0432-5000.sourceText: The resolution on the El-Obeid humanitarian catastrophe has been used by the left-wing and progressive groups in the European Parliament to attack the United Arab Emirates, instead of focusing strictly on resolving the humanitarian crisis in Sudan. This approach is even more problematic as the resolution ignores the role of actual malign actors, like Russia, Iran, and others, whose actions have contributed to this conflict. EP should have remained focused on the humanitarian disaster in El-Obeid by prioritizing the protection of civilians, ensuring humanitarian access, and supporting accountability for all perpetrators on the basis of verified evidence. Instead, the resolution devotes particular attention to the UAE while failing to acknowledge the broad network of external actors that has fueled and prolonged this conflict. Numerous reports have documented the involvement of Russian-linked Wagner forces and their successor structures, alongside other foreign actors, in sustaining violence and instability in Sudan. Instead of being constructive, the resolution was weaponized by the left-wing and progressive groups to attack the UAE so they could score political points in their home countries. Humanitarian resolutions should remain impartial, evidence-based, and centered on the victims. Selectively and incorrectly attributing responsibility undermines the credibility of Parliament's message and its position as an effective actor in this conflict resolution.

3-0434-0000.sourceText: The next item is the debate on six motions for resolutions on the ongoing persecution of Christians in Nigeria, notably the Kawel village massacre (2026/2800(RSP)).

3-0435-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, Commissioner, dear colleagues, the horrific attacks in Kawel village – where innocent Christians, including their pastor, were brutally killed – are yet another tragic reminder of the escalating violence against Christian communities in Nigeria. Sadly, this is not an isolated incident. Nigeria has become one of the most dangerous places in the world to be a Christian. Across the country, Christian communities face repeated attacks by Fulani militants, Boko Haram and other organised groups. Violence is part of a broader and deeply worrying pattern of persecution.

The EU must therefore strongly condemn these attacks and press the Nigerian Government to step up its fight against the armed militant groups responsible for this violence. I call on the Commission to give urgent attention to the worrying situation of Christians in Nigeria and all persecuted religious communities in Nigeria.

We had a very fruitful discussion this morning with the newly appointed EU Special Envoy on religious freedom, Mairead McGuinness, and I look forward to working with her to help Christian and other religious groups facing persecution.

3-0436-0000.sourceText:
Weer ging het afschuwelijk mis in Nigeria. Nu in het dorp Kawel, waar tientallen christenen het leven lieten bij een aanval door extremisten. Maar ik denk ook aan de tientallen scholieren die recent werden ontvoerd in de deelstaat Borno. De aanslagen en de ontvoeringen gaan maar door en nemen in intensiteit alleen maar toe.

Onze resolutie spreekt duidelijke taal. Wij roepen Nigeria op het probleem onder ogen te zien, de bevolking veel beter te beschermen en de daders te straffen.

Maar de vraag is ook vandaag: wat kunnen wij doen om het geweld in Nigeria te helpen stoppen? Welke mogelijkheden ziet u, commissaris? Ziet u bijvoorbeeld mogelijkheden om Nigeria te helpen bij het trainen van politiemensen? Natuurlijk is Nigeria primair zelf verantwoordelijk, maar als we kijken naar de escalatie van het geweld in de regio, mogen wij niet werkeloos toezien.
3-0436-0000.englishText:
Horrible things went wrong in Nigeria again. Now in the village of Kawel, where dozens of Christians lost their lives in an attack by extremists. But I also think of the dozens of schoolchildren who were recently kidnapped in Borno State. The attacks and kidnappings just keep going and are only increasing in intensity.

Our resolution speaks clear language. We call on Nigeria to face the problem, to protect the population much better and to punish the perpetrators.

But the question today is also: what can we do to help stop the violence in Nigeria? What possibilities do you see, Commissioner? Do you see possibilities, for example, to help Nigeria train police officers? Of course Nigeria is primarily responsible itself, but if we look at the escalation of the violence in the region, we may not stand by idly.

3-0437-0000.sourceText:
Mr President, innocent people were massacred at the Kawel village and our thoughts are with the families of the victims.

The violence in Nigeria is driven by disputes over land and water, climate change, poverty, criminality, weak governance, persistent impunity and deep‑rooted religious, ethnic and intercommunal tensions. Together, these pressures have fuelled a brutal cycle of revenge and breaking that cycle requires more than expressions of outrage.

To the colleagues who rightly demand the protection of Christian communities in Nigeria, I ask to look at the actions of your global conservative allies. Last year, Trump dismantled USAID with enormous consequences in Nigeria. Hundreds of schools in conflict‑affected areas were closed. One fifth of the national healthcare budget was taken away. Imagine the consequences on maternal health and on the fight against HIV.

Conservatives have defunded the very local networks, many of them Christian faith‑based healthcare providers, that offered a frontline against poverty and radicalisation.

I call on the EU to be a committed partner in supporting humanitarian aid, conflict prevention, justice reform and climate resilience, on the Nigerian authorities to protect all civilians, and on my colleagues to also make sure that right‑wing populism doesn't cut away international aid.

3-0438-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Am 22. Juni verüben bewaffnete Milizionäre im Dorf Kawel im nigerianischen Bundesstaat Plateau ein Massaker. Mindestens 22 unschuldige Menschen wurden in dieser christlichen Gemeinde, die nicht geschützt wurde, getötet.

Angriffe auf christliche Dorfgemeinschaften, auf Bäuerinnen und Bauern, auf Geistliche, Schulen und Gesundheitseinrichtungen nehmen zu, ebenso die Entführungen; Frauen und Mädchen sind massiv betroffen. Die katholische Bischofskonferenz Nigerias bekräftigt, dass Christen genauso wie Muslime Opfer des anhaltenden Terrorismus sind.

Gezielte Gewalt gegen Zivilisten wurzelt in Konflikten um politische Macht, Landstreitigkeiten, ethnische Zugehörigkeit, Sektenzugehörigkeit und Bandenkriminalität. Wir erwarten von den nigerianischen Behörden entschlossenes Handeln: eine umfassende Untersuchung des Massakers von Kawel, strafrechtliche Verfolgung der Täter und wirksamen Schutz gefährdeter Gemeinden und der Zivilbevölkerung sowie die entschiedene Bekämpfung bewaffneter Gruppen.

Wo Menschen aufgrund ihres Glaubens verfolgt werden, greift das die Religionsfreiheit an, und das ist ein fundamentales Menschenrecht, das wir schützen müssen.
3-0438-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! On 22 June, armed militiamen carried out a massacre in the village of Kawel in the Nigerian state of Plateau. At least 22 innocent people were killed in this Christian community, which was left unprotected.

Attacks on Christian village communities, on farmers, on clergy, schools and health facilities are increasing, as are kidnappings; women and girls are massively affected. The Catholic Bishops' Conference of Nigeria reiterates that Christians, just like Muslims, are victims of ongoing terrorism.

Targeted violence against civilians is rooted in conflicts over political power, land disputes, ethnicity, sectarianism and gang crime. We expect decisive action from the Nigerian authorities: a comprehensive investigation into the Kawel massacre, prosecution of the perpetrators and effective protection of vulnerable communities and the civilian population, as well as the decisive fight against armed groups.

Where people are persecuted because of their faith, this attacks freedom of religion, and that is a fundamental human right that we must protect.

3-0439-0000.sourceText:
Signor Presidente, onorevoli colleghi, silenzio, il mondo tace mentre in Nigeria si consuma una strage: decine e decine di cristiani massacrati ancora, ogni settimana, nell'indifferenza generale.

Solo nel 2025 si parla di 3 500 cristiani uccisi da mani islamiste. Non sono numeri: sono famiglie intere sterminate, villaggi rasi al suolo, chiese bruciate con i fedeli dentro.

È una strategia precisa: terrorizzare, confiscare le loro terre, sradicare un'intera comunità. Non è più un'emergenza umanitaria, ormai le caratteristiche sono quelle di un genocidio.

I cristiani sono oggi il gruppo religioso più perseguitato al mondo, ma continuate a girarvi dall'altra parte o a parlare di un'inesistente islamofobia. L'Europa non riconosce né contrasta questa persecuzione islamista.

Non possiamo più aspettare. Ogni giorno di silenzio è complice di chi ammazza i cristiani.
3-0439-0000.englishText:
Mr President, honourable colleagues, silence, the world is silent while a massacre is taking place in Nigeria: tens and tens of Christians slaughtered again, every week, amidst general indifference.

In 2025 alone, we are talking about 3,500 Christians killed by Islamist hands. These are not numbers: they are entire families exterminated, villages razed to the ground, churches burned with the worshippers inside.

It is a precise strategy: to terrorise, confiscate their lands, uproot an entire community. It is no longer a humanitarian emergency, by now the characteristics are those of a genocide.

Christians are today the most persecuted religious group in the world, but you continue to look the other way or talk about a nonexistent Islamophobia. Europe neither recognises nor combats this Islamist persecution.

We can no longer wait. Every day of silence is an accomplice to those who kill Christians.

3-0440-0000.sourceText:
Herr Präsident, Frau Kommissarin! Weltweit werden rund 400 Millionen Christen verfolgt; Christen sind damit die am stärksten verfolgte Glaubensgemeinschaft weltweit. Besonders brutal ist diese Verfolgung in Nigeria; nirgendwo auf der Welt werden mehr Christen ermordet als dort – ermordet aus einem Grund: weil sie Christen sind. So geschehen auch vor zwei Wochen: Fulani-Milizen ermordeten mindestens 23 Christen im Dorf Kawel, darunter einen Pastor. Der US-Gesandte bei der UN, Mike Waltz, sagt, das ist keine zufällige Gewalt, das ist ein Genozid, ein Genozid an Christen.

All diese Fakten sind seit Langem bekannt, doch in Europa spricht man kaum darüber. Warum? Vielleicht, weil die Opfer Christen und die Täter Islamisten sind. Wir aber sollten die Täter beim Namen nennen: Boko Haram, der westafrikanische Ableger des „Islamischen Staates“, Fulani-Milizen – kurzum islamistische Terroristen. Sie morden, entführen, vergewaltigen, foltern.

Wir können das nicht länger hinnehmen; wir müssen Druck ausüben. Nigeria muss seine Christen schützen; Nigeria muss den islamistischen Terror bekämpfen. Dafür muss Nigeria seine Institutionen stärken – Polizei, Justiz, Sicherheitsapparat. Falls nicht, darf kein Cent mehr von uns nach Nigeria fließen.
3-0440-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner! Worldwide, around 400 million Christians are persecuted; Christians are thus the most persecuted religious community in the world. This persecution is particularly brutal in Nigeria; nowhere in the world are more Christians murdered than there – murdered for one reason: because they are Christians. This also happened two weeks ago: Fulani militias murdered at least 23 Christians in the village of Kawel, including a pastor. The US Envoy to the UN, Mike Waltz, says this is not random violence, this is a genocide, a genocide against Christians.

All these facts have been known for a long time, but in Europe hardly anyone talks about it. Why? Perhaps because the victims are Christians and the perpetrators are Islamists. But we should call the perpetrators by their name: Boko Haram, the West African branch of the "Islamic State", Fulani militias – in short, Islamist terrorists. They murder, kidnap, rape, torture.

We can no longer accept this; we must exert pressure. Nigeria must protect its Christians; Nigeria must fight Islamist terror. To this end, Nigeria must strengthen its institutions – police, judiciary, security apparatus. If not, not a single cent more of our money must flow to Nigeria.

3-0441-0000.sourceText:
Señor presidente, señora comisaria, no puede ser que la matanza de cristianos por motivos religiosos no nos despierte la misma indignación que nos provocan otras matanzas y persecuciones en el mundo.

Les doy unos datos: según datos de Open Doors, 388 millones de cristianos están perseguidos en el mundo y el año pasado hubo 4 849 asesinados. Especialmente grave es el caso de Nigeria, donde se da el 72 % de estos asesinatos, la mayoría ejecutados por grupos terroristas islamistas. No podemos caer en la trampa de pensar que aquí lo que está ocurriendo son guerras entre clanes por recursos naturales. Está habiendo una persecución real de cristianos y Europa no puede permanecer callada.

Desde la Unión Europea debemos tomar medidas, debemos endurecer nuestro régimen de sanciones así como la condicionalidad y el control de nuestras ayudas a terceros países para evitar financiar aquellos Estados, como el de Nigeria, que de una manera activa o pasiva permiten esta violencia contra los cristianos y este atentado contra los derechos humanos.
3-0441-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, it cannot be that the slaughter of Christians on religious grounds does not arouse the same indignation in us as other killings and persecutions in the world cause us.

I will give you some data: according to Open Doors data, 388 million Christians are persecuted in the world and last year there were 4,849 murdered. The case of Nigeria is especially serious, where 72% of these murders take place, most of them executed by Islamist terrorist groups. We cannot fall into the trap of thinking that what is happening here are wars between clans over natural resources. There is a real persecution of Christians and Europe cannot remain silent.

From the European Union we must take measures, we must tighten our sanctions regime as well as the conditionality and control of our aid to third countries to avoid financing those States, such as Nigeria, that actively or passively allow this violence against Christians and this attack on human rights.

3-0442-0000.sourceText:
Monsieur le Président, Madame la Commissaire, chers collègues, parler de la situation au Nigeria dans cet hémicycle permet de mettre en lumière les persécutions et violences quotidiennes auxquelles doivent faire face les civils. Réduire le débat à la religion est cependant la preuve que beaucoup ici n’ont pas compris ce qui se passe dans ce pays, ou alors qu’ils ne veulent pas le comprendre. Ou simplement ils se servent de ces atrocités pour servir leur agenda politique.

Comment ne pas voir que les victimes des massacres ont un seul point commun: non pas leur religion, mais le fait d’être civil? Comment ne pas voir l’influence du changement climatique, de la pression démographique, de la raréfaction des terres dans ces conflits?

Il est de notre devoir d’élus de faire preuve d’honnêteté intellectuelle afin d’apporter un réel soutien à la population nigériane, sans quoi nous continuerons à compter les morts.
3-0442-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, dear colleagues, talking about the situation in Nigeria in this hemicycle helps to highlight the daily persecutions and violence that civilians have to face. Reducing the debate to religion is, however, proof that many here have not understood what is happening in this country, or else that they do not want to understand it. Or simply that they are using these atrocities to serve their political agenda.

How can we fail to see that the victims of the massacres have only one thing in common: not their religion, but the fact of being civilians? How can we fail to see the influence of climate change, demographic pressure, and the scarcity of land in these conflicts?

It is our duty as elected representatives to show intellectual honesty in order to provide real support to the Nigerian population, otherwise we will continue to count the dead.

3-0443-0000.sourceText:
Senhor Presidente, Senhora Comissária, quando denunciou a perseguição e o suplício de Jean Calas, Voltaire não estava apenas a fazer a defesa de um homem injustamente condenado: estava a lembrar a toda a Europa que toda a intolerância praticada em nome de Deus é, sempre, um pacto com o Diabo.

A intolerância desumaniza, simultaneamente, a sua vítima e o seu autor. Dessa denúncia nasceu um tratado sobre a tolerância que permanece uma das magnas cartas da Europa.

Por isso, quando me chegam relatos de comunidades cristãs ameaçadas na Nigéria, no Sudão, em Moçambique ou um pouco por todo o Médio Oriente, ouvimos mais do que notícias distantes. Reconhecemos os nossos demónios.

A Europa tem uma responsabilidade especial de proteger as comunidades cristãs, onde quer que elas sejam perseguidas, porque em cada Jean Calas silenciado - na Europa de ontem, ou na África e no Médio Oriente de hoje - ouvimos, de novo, a voz de Voltaire.
3-0443-0000.englishText:
Mr President, Madam Commissioner, when he denounced the persecution and torture of Jean Calas, Voltaire was not just defending a man unjustly condemned: he was reminding the whole of Europe that all intolerance practiced in the name of God is always a pact with the Devil.

Intolerance simultaneously dehumanises its victim and its author. From that denunciation was born a treatise on tolerance that remains one of Europe's great charters.

Therefore, when reports reach me of threatened Christian communities in Nigeria, Sudan, Mozambique or somewhat all over the Middle East, we hear more than distant news. We recognise our demons.

Europe has a special responsibility to protect Christian communities, wherever they are persecuted, because in every silenced Jean Calas - in the Europe of yesterday, or the Africa and Middle East of today - we hear, once again, Voltaire's voice.

3-0444-0000.sourceText:
Panie Przewodniczący! W czerwcu 2026 r. w wiosce Kawel w stanie Plateau w Nigerii doszło do brutalnego ataku na chrześcijańską społeczność. Dziesiątki osób zginęły, wiele zostało rannych, a cała wioska została zniszczona. To nie jest pojedynczy incydent, lecz element szerszego, powtarzającego się wzoru prześladowanych chrześcijan w regionie, ataków na rolników, kościoły, szkoły, duchownych. I mimo wielokrotnych ostrzeżeń władze nigeryjskie nie zapewniły ochrony, a sprawcy nadal cieszą się bezkarnością.

Potępiamy tę zbrodnię z całą stanowczością. Wyrażamy głębokie współczucie rodzinom ofiar. Wzywamy rząd Nigerii do natychmiastowego, transparentnego śledztwa, ukarania winnych i przerwania kultury bezkarności. Apelujemy o realne wzmocnienie ochrony ludności chrześcijańskiej i podjęcie konkretnych działań przeciwko fali przemocy.

Niestety, reakcja Unii Europejskiej pozostaje dalece niewystarczająca. Oficjalna linia Unii Europejskiej, w tym wypowiedzi wysokiej przedstawiciel Kai Kallas, unika jasnego określenia tych wydarzeń mianem prześladowania chrześcijan. Zamiast tego skupia się na złożonych czynnikach, konfliktach o ziemię między rolnikami a hodowcami, zmianami klimatu, działalności bandytów i terrorystów. Jednocześnie Unia z niezwykłą czujnością doszukuje się przejawów islamofobii w Europie, nawet tam, gdzie chodzi o uzasadnioną krytykę radykalnego islamu.

To wyraźny przejaw odchodzenia europejskich elit od chrześcijańskich korzeni Europy. Unia powstała w oparciu o chrześcijańskie wartości, godność osoby ludzkiej, sprawiedliwość, solidarność. Fundamenty Europy są chrześcijańskie. Nie możemy więc pozostawać obojętni na cierpienie milionów chrześcijan na świecie, od lat najbardziej prześladowanej grupy religijnej.

Takie selektywne podejście źle wróży przyszłości Europy. Osłabia naszą spójność kulturową. Ignoruje realia demograficzne i pozbawia nas zdolności do skutecznego przeciwstawienia się radykalnemu islamowi. Czas, by Europa wróciła do swoich korzeni, nie tylko słowami, ale także czynami.
3-0444-0000.englishText:
Mr President! In June 2026, in the village of Kawel in Plateau State, Nigeria, a brutal attack took place against the Christian community. Dozens of people were killed, many were injured, and the entire village was destroyed. This is not an isolated incident, but part of a broader, recurring pattern of persecuted Christians in the region, attacks on farmers, churches, schools, and clergy. Despite repeated warnings, the Nigerian authorities have failed to provide protection, and the perpetrators continue to enjoy impunity.

We condemn this crime in the strongest possible terms. We express our deepest sympathy to the families of the victims. We call on the Government of Nigeria for an immediate, transparent investigation, the punishment of those responsible, and the end of the culture of impunity. We appeal for real strengthening of the protection of the Christian population and concrete action against the wave of violence.

Unfortunately, the reaction of the European Union remains grossly insufficient. The official line of the European Union, including statements by High Representative Kaja Kallas, avoids clearly defining these events as the persecution of Christians. Instead, it focuses on complex factors, land conflicts between farmers and herders, climate change, the activities of bandits and terrorists. At the same time, the Union is extremely vigilant in detecting signs of Islamophobia in Europe, even where it concerns justified criticism of radical Islam.

3-0446-0000.englishText: Mr President, Commissioner, colleagues. The massacre carried out in Nigeria, in the village of Kawel, has shaken not only local communities, but the entire civilized world. Mr President, honourable Members, at the end of this debate, the European Union would like to express its solidarity with the victims of massacres and abductions committed in Nigeria, as well as with their families enduring grief and suffering. The European Union strongly condemns these cruel attacks targeting vulnerable populations across the country. Nigeria has been facing systematic and insecurity affecting Christians and Christian communities and places of worship.

It is important to bear in mind that violence in Nigeria cuts across ethno-religious boundaries, with victims coming from all faiths and backgrounds. The recent attack on Kawel village in Plateau State cost the lives of 21 people. Although the victims belong to a Christian community and the offenders were of Fulani Muslim origin, the underlying conflict does not only have a religious dimension. It is also closely related to extended fights between farmers and herders. It is intensified by shrinking agricultural land, difficult access to resources and political tensions.

During her recent visit to Nigeria on 23 March, HR/VP Kallas delivered the message of support to Nigerian authorities engaged in a difficult fight against Boko Haram and other extremist groups. She stressed the complexity of this phenomenon of violence with its deep-rooted socio-economic, political and historical dimensions. She pledged to continue stepping up EU-Nigeria cooperation against terrorism and violent extremism and strengthening the whole-of-society approach for the prevention of violence and conflict in Nigeria.

While keeping our strong commitment to religious freedom and non-discrimination, we must support Nigerian voices calling for sustainable peace and opposing the stigmatisation of specific communities. Over the last years, the European Union has taken action to address the dire situation in Nigeria. Together with its Member States, it has implemented many projects on prevention of violence, peacebuilding and support of populations affected by violence.

The European Union has acted to promote dialogue in Nigeria and kept regular dialogue with its religious leaders – leaders from all faiths. The European Union stands ready to work alongside Nigerian authorities and international partners to strengthen the protection of vulnerable communities in Nigeria, of course, including Christians.

3-0500-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable Members, the case of Maria Shahbaz is deeply troubling. Maria was reportedly 13 when she was taken from her family in Lahore, converted to Islam and married to an adult man. Her father went to court arguing that she was a minor and could not lawfully consent. Yet the proceedings did not deliver the clear child-protection response that such a case demands, including under international law.

We know this is not an isolated case in Pakistan. It reflects a wider pattern of abduction, forced conversion and forced marriage of girls coming from minorities. There are other key issues that challenge equal citizenship and equal protection under the law – the misuse of blasphemy allegations, the persecution of Ahmadis, the caste-based discrimination affecting Dalits and Scheduled Castes, many of them Hindu or Christian.

The European Union has not been silent. We have raised these concerns repeatedly and directly with Pakistan, including during our strategic dialogues and our joint commissions. We are perfectly aware that these issues are sensitive for our Pakistani counterparts, but they cannot be postponed, minimised or treated as side matters in our relationship.

Pakistan must do more to protect minors, ensure prompt police registration, apply child protection standards consistently and prosecute those who exploit religious or cultural grounds to deprive others of rights which are clearly enshrined in international law.

We recognise Pakistan has taken some steps, including on child marriage and child protection policy frameworks. This is undoubtedly positive, but protection is measured by outcomes: safe return of the person, investigation of forged documents, punishment of perpetrators. Only then can vulnerable individuals and communities fully trust their state, whether in Pakistan or in any country.

Pakistan is an important partner for the European Union, and precisely for that reason our dialogue must remain candid. Pakistan is the largest beneficiary of the Generalised Scheme of Preferences Plus worldwide. Preferential access to the European market is linked to implementation of international conventions, including on human rights. The continuation and renewal of GSP+ is linked to real, measurable and sustained progress in respecting the international commitments upon which it is based. Under these international commitments, equal citizenship, freedom of religion or belief and protection of minority women and girls are not optional, but obligatory.

3-0504-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, honourable and distinguished Members, Commissioner Šuica, in today's world, we are faced with cyberattacks that wish to expose vulnerabilities in our cybersecurity. Such attacks need our full attention because cybersecurity is essential to protect economic activity and critical infrastructure in our Union. Cybersecurity is also about protecting our electronic devices, such as smartphones, where we keep much of our private and professional data.

Attempts to undermine the security of our private data undermine the right to privacy and data protection and freedom of expression. But let's be clear: the ultimate target of such attacks are our democracies and the rule of law. The use of commercial spyware to monitor the press, politicians and public institutions represents a massive challenge to democratic accountability. And while Member States and the European Union are constantly stepping up their efforts to increase cybersecurity, so do those who want to harm our values and our Union. That is why we need to focus on strengthening our democratic resilience.

L’une des facettes de la résilience démocratique est la protection de nos démocraties contre les attaques, notamment les menaces hybrides, la manipulation de l’information et les ingérences étrangères, ainsi que la désinformation.

L’autre facette de la résilience démocratique réside dans la protection de la liberté de nos citoyens et de nos médias, de la tenue d’élections libres et équitables et ainsi que de la solidité des institutions et des processus démocratiques.

Je tiens à vous assurer que le renforcement de la résilience démocratique constitue une priorité majeure pour nos États membres, non seulement à l’échelon national, mais aussi à travers le partage d’informations, la coopération opérationnelle et le renforcement conjoint des capacités.

Ce renforcement de la résilience démocratique est également l’objectif du bouclier européen de la démocratie, que nous sommes actuellement en train de mettre en œuvre.

As Irish Presidency, we are committed to supporting all these efforts in strengthening democratic resilience. During the next semester, we will be paying attention to the protection of citizens online, notably our children, and the safety of political candidates and elected representatives.

I know that these are important issues for the European Parliament as well and I am sure that we will have the occasion to exchange on such matters with you in the months to come. Thank you very much for your attention.

That is why we need to focus on strengthening our democratic resilience.

One of the facets of democratic resilience is the protection of our democracies against attacks, notably hybrid threats, information manipulation, foreign interference, and disinformation.

Another facet of democratic resilience lies in protecting the freedom of our citizens and our media, holding free and fair elections, and ensuring the strength of democratic institutions and processes.

I would like to assure you that strengthening democratic resilience is a major priority for our Member States, not only at the national level, but also through information sharing, operational cooperation, and joint capacity building.

This strengthening of democratic resilience is also the objective of the European democracy shield, which we are currently implementing.

As Irish Presidency, we are committed to supporting all these efforts in strengthening democratic resilience. During the next semester, we will be paying attention to the protection of citizens online, notably our children, and the safety of political candidates and elected representatives.

I know that these are important issues for the European Parliament as well and I am sure that we will have the occasion to exchange on such matters with you in the months to come. Thank you very much for your attention.

3-0507-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear Members, the Commission has seen the media reports. Our position is very clear. Any attempts to illegally access data of citizens is unacceptable. Any alleged illegal use of spyware is, in the first place, a matter for national authorities to investigate. Mindful of their competence in that matter, European Union law provides clear and comprehensive safeguards.

The European Union has a strong legal framework for data protection and privacy. The GDPR, the data protection Law Enforcement Directive and the ePrivacy Directive offer a comprehensive protection of the confidentiality of communications and users' personal data. The ePrivacy Directive protects against communication interception and gaining access to or storage of information on users' devices without their consent. EU data protection law is fully applicable to the processing of personal data by private entities, even where such processing is required by law for national security purposes. EU data protection law also applies when public authorities process personal data for law enforcement and criminal justice purposes.

Outside of data protection, there are several other relevant legislative instruments. The directive on attacks against information systems requires Member States to ensure that illegal system access and illegal interception are punishable as a criminal offence in their national criminal law. The European Media Freedom Act provides specific safeguards for journalists and their families and sources regarding the use of spyware. This is essential to ensure a free and independent press.

Moreover, with the application of the Cyber Resilience Act, manufacturers placing hardware and software on the EU market are subject to cybersecurity requirements through the product life cycle. These obligations aim to reduce vulnerabilities in products that can be exploited by spyware to gain unauthorised access, monitor users, extract data or compromise devices. By improving the security of connected products and reducing the overall number of exploitable weaknesses, the Cyber Resilience Act will strengthen resilience against such threats.

In addition, we continue to report on the issue of spyware, when appropriate, in the annual rule of law report, from the perspective of checks and balances and that of the protection of journalists.

Gdy celem staje się parlamentarzysta badający nadużycia związane z tą cyber bronią, wtedy zagrożeniem jest nie tylko prywatność tej osoby, ale także zdolność Parlamentu Europejskiego do realizowania działań kontrolnych instytucji publicznej.

Powstaje pytanie: kto kogo kontroluje? Bo gdyby ktoś chciał stworzyć narzędzie do niszczenia demokracji, to takim narzędziem z pewnością jest Pegasus. Bo to jest narzędzie, które od strony osobistej potrafi niszczyć prywatność, wnikać w osobowość człowieka. Z drugiej strony niszczy organizacje, niszczy ugrupowania, demokrację, niszczy dziennikarzy, wolne sądy i praworządność.

Przeżyłem to osobiście, gdy jako partia w 2019 roku staliśmy się ofiarą Pegasusa. Podsyłano nam fałszywe analizy wyborcze i wiem, że takim systemem można zniszczyć człowieka. Dlatego chciałbym też podziękować na koniec badaczom z Citizen Lab i organizacjom pozarządowym oraz powiedzieć, że należy wdrożyć wszystkie rekomendacje komisji PEGA. Szacunek dla Citizen Lab, dla tych ludzi, którzy realizują zadania, które powinny być realizowane przez instytucje państwa.
3-0508-0000.englishText:
Madam President! This debate is very important, because Pegasus is not an ordinary tool. It is a system that strikes at the very heart of democracy, European values, and the fundamental freedoms of citizens.

This debate takes on special significance at a time when we learn that Member of the European Parliament Kouloglou from Greece was attacked with Pegasus while investigating, as part of the work of the PEGA committee, abuses related to Pegasus. This information is shocking. When the target becomes a parliamentarian investigating abuses related to this cyberweapon, the threat is not only to that person's privacy, but also to the European Parliament's ability to carry out the supervisory activities of a public institution.

The question arises: who is controlling whom? Because if someone wanted to create a tool for destroying democracy, Pegasus is certainly such a tool. Because it is a tool that, on a personal level, can destroy privacy and penetrate a person's personality. On the other hand, it destroys organizations, destroys groups, democracy, destroys journalists, free courts, and the rule of law.

We saw such abuses in Poland and Hungary. And when history shows that such tools fall into the hands of pathological people, demagogic, populist, morally degenerate people, Pegasus can be used to destroy privacy, democracy, and elections.

I experienced this personally when, as a party in 2019, we became victims of Pegasus. False election analyses were sent to us, and I know that such a system can destroy a person. One can interfere with the system, with the electoral process, and yet free elections are a celebration of democracy and the foundation of citizens' trust in the state.

Therefore, I would also like to thank the researchers from Citizen Lab and non-governmental organizations at the end, and to say that all recommendations of the PEGA committee should be implemented. Respect for Citizen Lab, for these people who carry out tasks that should be carried out by state institutions.

3-0509-0000.englishText:
Madam President,

All European citizens have the right to privacy and should be able to rest assured that their personal communication remains private.

But one may ask: is this still the case? Nowadays, spyware has been created through which smartphones can be accessed without one knowing and without the need for the victim to click a phishing link. This development can kill our right to privacy and, worse still, it is a threat to the functioning of our democracies.

Spyware has been used against elected officials, even against Members of this Parliament, to gain access to their phones. One of our colleagues fell victim to Pegasus spyware, precisely while working in the PEGA committee, intended to investigate this same spyware. An absurd and troubling thing.

The need for regular forensic scrutiny for all our phones is merely fighting the symptoms. Ordinary citizens, journalists, and politicians are all at risk, but they do not have the means to perform forensic scrutiny of their phones. We need real solutions, more cybersecurity measures, and perhaps new rules for the European Union to keep our phones private.

No one should have the right to interfere in our private communication. Foreign secret services use this vulnerability to try to steal sensitive information from our politicians. Spyware makes it possible to obtain confidential information to influence political debates or even the course of elections.

3-0510-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! System Pegasus to system, którego nie można kupić w sklepie. Mogą go kupić tylko rządy albo służby podległe rządom, czyli jest pod kontrolą państwa. I mam do państwa parę pytań. Czy politycy powinni być traktowani inaczej niż zwykli obywatele? Nie. Czy polityk dopuszczający się korupcji powinien być ścigany? Tak. Kontrola operacyjna powinna być prowadzona za zgodą właściwych organów państwa i pod ich kontrolą. W Polsce są to sądy. Dlaczego zatem zajmujemy się tą sprawą? Nie macie wrażenia, że oświadczenia majątkowe składane przez europosłów są nieczytelne dla opinii publicznej? Więcej jawności! Jawność jest wrogiem korupcji. 3-0510-0000.englishText:
Madam President! The Pegasus system is a system that cannot be bought in a store. It can only be bought by governments or services subordinate to governments, meaning it is under state control. And I have a few questions for you. I also know a few answers. Is corruption a serious crime? Yes. Do politicians commit corruption? We know many examples. Should police services prosecute corruption? Yes. Should politicians be treated differently than ordinary citizens? No. Should a politician who commits corruption be prosecuted? Yes. Can services use modern methods to prosecute criminals? Yes, this is essential for effective action.

Operational control should be carried out with the consent of the competent state authorities and under their control. In Poland, these are the courts. Why, then, are we dealing with this matter? Because there is no doubt that some state body, probably in a legal manner – we have no knowledge here whether there was consent or not, but I suspect it was a legal matter – was conducting proceedings.

I am convinced that instead of paralyzing crime-fighting services with attacks, we should consider what to do to make the European Commission more transparent or to make politicians' assets public. Don't you have the impression that the asset declarations submitted by Members of the European Parliament are illegible to the public? More transparency! Transparency is the enemy of corruption. Politicians also commit crimes.

3-0511-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen! Auch Jahre nach dem Untersuchungsausschuss ist bei der Frage Pegasus wenig passiert. Jetzt ist der nächste Kollege mit Überwachungssoftware überwacht worden, und die Kommission hat immer noch nicht gehandelt und noch nichts vorgelegt; hier muss endlich etwas passieren.

Aber ich muss ehrlich gestehen, ich finde diese Debatte schon etwas befremdlich. Wir sprechen hier über die Bedeutung und Wichtigkeit von privater und verschlüsselter Kommunikation, aber gleichzeitig werden wir morgen wahrscheinlich diese private, verschlüsselte Kommunikation von 450 Millionen Menschen angreifen mit der Chatkontrolle.

Wir haben jahrelang verhandelt. Wir hatten doch vor zwei Wochen schon fast eine finale Verhandlung zwischen Rat und Parlament – keine Massenüberwachung, Safety by Design, Kontrolle bei konkretem Verdacht. Aber das reicht einigen im Rat und auch hier im Parlament nicht; die wollen die anlasslose Kontrolle unserer Daten. Deswegen wird über die Chatkontrolle morgen wieder abgestimmt, obwohl wir sie schon zweimal hier im Parlament abgelehnt haben.

Man stimmt einfach so lange ab, bis das Ergebnis passt. Die privaten Chats von 450 Millionen EU‑Bürgern, die sind dann nicht mehr sicher; nicht einmal verschlüsselte Kommunikation wollen sie ausnehmen.

Liebe Kolleginnen und Kollegen, ich appelliere wirklich an Sie! Morgen – stimmen Sie gegen diesen Wahnsinn, stimmen Sie gegen die Chatkontrolle, stimmen Sie für verschlüsselte und sichere Kommunikation und vor allem, stimmen Sie für das digitale Briefgeheimnis!
3-0511-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear colleagues! Years after the committee of inquiry, very little has happened regarding the Pegasus issue. Now the next colleague has been monitored with surveillance software, and the Commission still has not acted and has still not presented anything; something finally needs to happen here.

But I must honestly admit, I find this debate a bit strange. We are talking here about the meaning and importance of private and encrypted communication, but at the same time, tomorrow we will probably attack this private, encrypted communication of 450 million people with chat control.

We have negotiated for years. Two weeks ago, we almost had a final negotiation between the Council and Parliament – no mass surveillance, safety by design, control in cases of concrete suspicion. But that is not enough for some in the Council and also here in Parliament; they want indiscriminate control of our data. That is why chat control is being voted on again tomorrow, even though we have already rejected it twice here in Parliament.

They simply keep voting until the result fits. The private chats of 450 million EU citizens will then no longer be secure; they do not even want to exempt encrypted communication.

Dear colleagues, I really appeal to you! Tomorrow – vote against this madness, vote against chat control, vote for encrypted and secure communication, and above all, vote for digital correspondence secrecy!

Madame la Présidente, chers collègues, juillet 2021: des journalistes d’investigation et des ONG révèlent que des milliers de personnes ont été illégalement espionnées à l’aide du logiciel espion Pegasus, qui accède sans clic à absolument toutes vos données sur votre téléphone. Nous voulons aussi l’encadrement strict de l’utilisation des logiciels espions et, enfin, l’arrêt immédiat de tout affaiblissement du dispositif européen de protection des données personnelles et des droits fondamentaux.
3-0512-0000.englishText:

July 2026: while member states where scandals are breaking out are too numerous to count—Hungary, Poland, Spain, Greece, Slovakia, Italy—a new red line is crossed. Κυρία Πρόεδρε, μετά από πρωτοβουλία του Αντιπροέδρου της Left Κώστα Αρβανίτη, συζητάμε σήμερα ένα πολύ σοβαρό ζήτημα κράτους δικαίου. Η επιβεβαιωμένη από το «Citizen Lab» παρακολούθηση του πρώην ευρωβουλευτή της Left Στέλιου Κούλογλου αποτελεί ευθεία επίθεση στην ανεξαρτησία του ίδιου του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου. Το θύμα ήταν μέλος της ειδικής εξεταστικής επιτροπής PEGA, που το Σώμα συγκρότησε για να διερευνήσει τη χρήση του Pegasus και άλλων παράνομων κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών στην Ευρώπη. Προφανώς, όταν παρακολουθείται ένα μέλος αυτής της επιτροπής, δεν τίθεται σε κίνδυνο μόνο η ιδιωτικότητά του· μέσα από την παρακολούθηση του πρώην συναδέλφου κάποιοι παρακολούθησαν και άλλους ευρωβουλευτές, όπως και το ερευνητικό έργο της επιτροπής PEGA.

Οι παρακολουθήσεις αυτές πλήττουν ευθέως τη δημοκρατία, το κράτος δικαίου και τη θεσμική ακεραιότητα των ευρωπαϊκών θεσμών, και μας υπενθυμίζουν ότι η ασφάλειά μας, η προστασία του κράτους δικαίου και η ανεξαρτησία των δημοκρατικών θεσμών παραμένει μία ευρωπαϊκή πρόκληση. Το πραγματικό ερώτημα είναι αν το ίδιο το Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο είναι διατεθειμένο να διερευνήσει ποιοι και για λογαριασμό ποιου παρακολούθησαν τον ευρωβουλευτή μέλος της εξεταστικής του επιτροπής. Αυτό είναι ένα ζήτημα θεσμικής αξιοπιστίας και προστασίας της εντολής των ευρωβουλευτών.

Ως Ευρωπαϊκό Κοινοβούλιο είχαμε ζητήσει από την Επιτροπή, όχι μόνο στο πόρισμα της επιτροπής PEGA αλλά και σε μεταγενέστερο ψήφισμά μας, να αναλάβει νομοθετική πρωτοβουλία απέναντι στις προκλήσεις που δημιουργούν τα κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά —και οι νέες αποκαλύψεις αποδεικνύουν με τον πιο δραματικό τρόπο ότι αυτό το αίτημα ήταν απολύτως δικαιολογημένο. Όλα αυτά συμβαίνουν τη στιγμή που στην Ελλάδα το σκάνδαλο των υποκλοπών όχι μόνο δεν έχει κλείσει, όπως επιχειρεί η σημερινή κυβέρνηση και η κυβερνητική πλειοψηφία, αλλά μπαίνει σε μια νέα, ιδιαίτερα κρίσιμη φάση. Μετά τον Νίκο Ανδρουλάκη, πρόεδρο του ΠΑΣΟΚ, τον πρώην υπουργό του ΣΥΡΙΖΑ Χρήστο Σπίρτζη, πλέον και ο πρώην πρωθυπουργός Αντώνης Σαμαράς ζήτησε επίσημα από τον Άρειο Πάγο να διερευνηθεί η παρακολούθησή του.

Σήμερα λοιπόν υπερασπιζόμαστε το δικαίωμα κάθε μέλους αυτού του Κοινοβουλίου να ασκεί ανεμπόδιστα τα καθήκοντά του. Υπερασπιζόμαστε την ανεξαρτησία των εξεταστικών επιτροπών μας. Υπερασπιζόμαστε την αξιοπιστία του ίδιου του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου, και γι' αυτό ζητούμε: πλήρη διερεύνηση της υπόθεσης από τις αρμόδιες αρχές της Ελλάδας, του Βελγίου και της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης· απόδοση ευθυνών και, επιτέλους, τη λήψη δεσμευτικών μέτρων για την απαγόρευση της χρήσης κακόβουλων κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών στην Ευρώπη.
3-0513-0000.englishText:
Madam President, following an initiative by Left Vice-President Kostas Arvanitis, we are discussing today a very serious rule of law issue. The surveillance of former Left MEP Stelios Kouloglou, confirmed by Citizen Lab, constitutes a direct attack on the independence of the European Parliament itself. The victim was a member of the PEGA special committee of inquiry, which the House established to investigate the use of Pegasus and other illegal spyware in Europe. Obviously, when a member of this committee is placed under surveillance, not only is their privacy endangered; through the monitoring of our former colleague, some individuals also monitored other MEPs, as well as the investigative work of the PEGA committee.

These wiretaps directly undermine democracy, the rule of law, and the institutional integrity of European institutions, reminding us that our security, the protection of the rule of law, and the independence of democratic institutions remain a European challenge. The real question is whether the European Parliament itself is willing to investigate who and on whose behalf placed the MEP, a member of its committee of inquiry, under surveillance. This is a matter of institutional credibility and the protection of the mandate of Members of the European Parliament.

As the European Parliament, we had asked the Commission—not only in the PEGA committee report but also in a subsequent resolution—to take legislative action against the challenges posed by spyware, and the new revelations prove in the most dramatic way that this request was entirely justified. All this is happening at a time when the wiretapping scandal in Greece has not only not been closed, as the current government and the parliamentary majority are attempting to do, but is entering a new, particularly critical phase. Following Nikos Androulakis, president of PASOK, and former SYRIZA minister Christos Spirtzis, now former Prime Minister Antonis Samaras has also officially asked the Supreme Court to investigate his surveillance.

Today, therefore, we defend the right of every member of this Parliament to exercise their duties unhindered. We defend the independence of our committees of inquiry. We defend the credibility of the European Parliament itself, and for this reason we demand: a full investigation of the case by the competent authorities of Greece, Belgium, and the European Union; the assignment of responsibilities; and, finally, the adoption of binding measures to ban the use of malicious spyware in Europe.
