Alebo vtedy, keď ste osemkrát preukázateľne zasiahli do slobodných a demokratických volieb v jednotlivých členských štátoch.

Slovenská republika, z ktorej pochádzam, bola terčom vašich hybridných operácií, kedy Európska komisia výrazne s využitím Digital Services aktu obmedzovala dosahy politikov na sociálnych sieťach. Som jeden z tých, ktorým vaša Európska komisia prikázala sociálnych sietí, aby mu vypli dosah na sociálnych sieťach. Čo to má spoločné s demokraciou? Takejto demokracii by hádam tlieskal aj súdruh Stalin a Mao Ce-tung. Toto je vaša demokracia, ktorú chcete chrániť?

Samozrejme, že je obrovský problém, ak europoslancovi do telefónu nejaká tajná služba nainštaluje program Pegasus a špehujú ho. Je to obrovský problém, ktorý treba riešiť. Ale vy chcete predsa nainštalovať špehovací program do 450 miliónov telefónov obyvateľov Európskej únie. Chcete čítať každú šifrovanú komunikáciu, vidieť každú jednu fotografiu. Chcete čítať súkromné konverzácie medzi manželmi. Veď to je úchylné, choré a zvrátené.

Dvakrát toto plénum odmietlo Chat control a pretláčate ho zase. Tak nám nehovorte o ochrane súkromia, keď vy ste najväčší porušovatelia súkromia. Ako nám môžete hovoriť o ochrane demokracie a slobody slova, keď toto plénum odhlasovalo, že ide vyšetrovať našu politickú stranu Európa suverénnych národov za to, že otvorene hovoríme veci, ktoré neporušujú žiadne zákony, ale takzvané európske hodnoty? A vy ste tí, ktorí určia, čo sú tie európske hodnoty. Príde Európska komisia a povie Demokracia, sloboda slova. Ale odtiaľ potiaľ. My vám nastavíme, o čom môžete hovoriť. Chcete deportovať nelegálnych imigrantov? Hovoríte o reemigrácii – ako v mojom prípade: porušujete európske hodnoty! Lebo európskou hodnotou podľa tejto Európskej komisie je mať v Európe vrahov, teroristov a násilníkov, ktorí sem prišli nelegálne. A takto by som mohol pokračovať donekonečna. Neustále európsku demokraciu ničíte, potláčate, zakopali ste ju do hrobu. A dnes nám hovoríte, že my vám máme veriť, že vy budete chrániť súkromie, demokraciu a slobodu slova. Prv odíďte vy, prestaňte so všetkým, čo robíte, a potom môžeme veriť tomu, že sa demokracia bude v Európe dať obnoviť.
3-0514-0000.englishText:
Madam President. I am convinced that you have lost even your last restraint. You lie to people from morning till night. Look at what you wrote there! You named this topic Protection of European Democracy.

I ask you, where is that European democracy? In the European Commission, whose president does not want to disclose information on how she purchased vaccines? In this Parliament, which pushes through Chat Control here so that it can spy on the phone of every single citizen of the European Union? Or when you demonstrably interfered eight times in free and democratic elections in individual member states.

The Slovak Republic, from which I come, was the target of your hybrid operations, when the European Commission, making significant use of the Digital Services Act, restricted the reach of politicians on social networks. I am one of those whose reach on social networks your European Commission ordered social networks to turn off. What does this have to do with democracy? Comrade Stalin and Mao Zedong would perhaps applaud such democracy. Is this the democracy you want to protect?

Of course, it is a huge problem if a secret service installs Pegasus software on a Member of European Parliament's phone and spies on him. It is a huge problem that needs to be addressed. But you want to install spyware on the phones of 450 million European Union residents. You want to read every encrypted communication, see every single photo. You want to read private conversations between spouses. Well, that is perverted, sick and depraved.

Twice this plenary rejected Chat Control and you are pushing it through again. So do not talk to us about privacy protection when you are the biggest violators of privacy. How can you talk to us about the protection of democracy and freedom of speech when this plenary voted to investigate our political group Europe of Sovereign Nations for openly saying things that do not violate any laws, but so-called European values? And you are the ones who determine what those European values are. The European Commission comes and says Democracy, freedom of speech. But up to a point. We will set for you what you can talk about. Do you want to deport illegal immigrants? You talk about remigration - as in my case: you are violating European values! Because according to this European Commission, a European value is to have murderers, terrorists and rapists in Europe who came here illegally. And I could go on like this endlessly. You are constantly destroying European democracy, suppressing it, you have buried it in a grave. And today you tell us that we are supposed to believe you that you will protect privacy, democracy and freedom of speech. First leave yourselves, stop everything you are doing, and then we can believe that democracy can be restored in Europe.

3-0515-0000.sourceText:
Pani Przewodnicząca! Po raz kolejny wychodzi na jaw informacja przekazana przez Citizen Lab, instytut akademicki, która wykazuje, że system Pegasus był wykorzystywany w tak szeroki sposób, naruszając jedne z podstawowych wartości, jakie obowiązują w Unii Europejskiej, i wartości, które powinniśmy my, w Parlamencie Europejskim, chronić. Chodzi o prawo do prywatności.

Przypomnę, że sprawa Pegasusa wypłynęła w związku z naruszeniami, których dopuściła się ówczesna władza Prawa i Sprawiedliwości w Polsce. Na tej sali siedzi ówczesny senator Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej Krzysztof Brejza, ówczesny szef kampanii wyborczej partii opozycyjnej, a obecnie poseł do Parlamentu Europejskiego. To on i jego rodzina, a także wielu innych polityków, dziennikarzy, niezależnych prawników było inwigilowanych w Polsce systemem Pegasus zakupionym przez partię rządzącą. To oni chcieli wiedzieć, co się dzieje w ich domach. Chcieli wiedzieć, jakie są plany polityczne, i chcieli wiedzieć, jak walczyć z opozycją, z obywatelami i wszystkimi tymi, którzy nie stoją po stronie rządu.

Dlatego wówczas Parlament Europejski powołał komisję PEGA. I ta komisja w 2023 roku przygotowała raport liczący 145 stron, w którym Parlament Europejski wyraźnie stwierdził, że zarówno państwa członkowskie, jak i państwa spoza Unii wykorzystywały Pegasusa, a szczególnie w Polsce i szczególnie na Węgrzech. Drastycznie naruszano w związku z tym prawo Unii Europejskiej i nie zapewniano obywatelom żadnej ochrony. Te działania Pegasusa były wielopoziomowe, ponieważ ten system szpiegowski przechodził z jednego urządzenia na drugie. Tego dotyczą teraz, przypomnę Państwu, sprawy, które toczą się przed Europejskim Trybunałem Praw Człowieka i czekamy na wyroki właśnie w tej sprawie.
3-0515-0000.englishText:
Madam President! Once again, information provided by Citizen Lab, an academic institute, has come to light showing that the Pegasus system was used in such a broad way, violating some of the fundamental values that apply in the European Union and the values that we, in the European Parliament, should protect. It concerns the right to privacy.

I would like to remind you that the Pegasus affair surfaced in connection with violations committed by the then-ruling Law and Justice authorities in Poland. Sitting in this chamber is the then-senator of the Republic of Poland, Krzysztof Brejza, the then-head of the election campaign of the opposition party, and currently a Member of the European Parliament. It was he and his family, as well as many other politicians, journalists, and independent lawyers, who were surveilled in Poland using the Pegasus system purchased by the ruling party. They wanted to know what was happening in their homes. They wanted to know what the political plans were, and they wanted to know how to fight the opposition, the citizens, and all those who did not stand on the side of the government.

That is why the European Parliament established the PEGA committee at the time. And in 2023, that committee prepared a 145-page report in which the European Parliament clearly stated that both member states and non-EU countries used Pegasus, particularly in Poland and particularly in Hungary. European Union law was drastically violated in connection with this, and citizens were not provided with any protection. These Pegasus activities were multi-level, as this spyware passed from one device to another. This is what the cases currently pending before the European Court of Human Rights are about, I remind you, and we are awaiting judgments precisely on this matter.

3-0516-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, ένας ακόμη συνάδελφός μας αποδεικνύεται ότι έπεσε θύμα παρακολούθησης με παράνομο κατασκοπευτικό λογισμικό: ο κύριος Κούλογλου, μέλος της εξεταστικής επιτροπής γι' αυτόν ακριβώς τον σκοπό, για τη διερεύνηση παρακολουθήσεων με παράνομο λογισμικό στην Ευρώπη. Είχε προηγηθεί η απόπειρα παρακολούθησης ενός ακόμη ευρωβουλευτή, του Νίκου Ανδρουλάκη, μέλους των Ευρωπαίων Σοσιαλιστών και Δημοκρατών, που καθόταν σε εκείνα τα έδρανα, προέδρου του ΠΑΣΟΚ και σήμερα αρχηγού της αξιωματικής αντιπολίτευσης στην Ελλάδα.

Ένα ζήτημα υψίστης σημασίας και για την πατρίδα μου και για την ευρωπαϊκή έννομη τάξη. Απαιτούμε πλήρη διαλεύκανση της υπόθεσης και όλων των υποθέσεων, τόσο από τις εθνικές αρχές όσο και από τους ευρωπαϊκούς θεσμούς. Είναι θέμα δημοκρατίας και κράτους δικαίου.
3-0516-0000.englishText:
Madam President, yet another of our colleagues turns out to have fallen victim to surveillance with illegal spyware: Mr. Kouloglou, a member of the committee of inquiry for this very purpose, for investigating surveillance with illegal software in Europe. This had been preceded by the attempted surveillance of yet another MEP, Nikos Androulakis, a member of the Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats who was sitting in those seats, president of PASOK and today leader of the official opposition in Greece.

A matter of supreme importance both for my homeland and for the European legal order. We demand a full clarification of this case and of all cases, both by the national authorities and by the European institutions. It is a matter of democracy and the rule of law.

3-0517-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η δημοκρατία μας απειλείται. Παράνομα λογισμικά παρακολούθησης στρέφονται εναντίον των εκλεγμένων εκπροσώπων των πολιτών. Οι αποκαλύψεις για την παρακολούθηση ευρωβουλευτή με παράνομο λογισμικό μπορεί να εκπλήσσουν την Ευρώπη· δυστυχώς στην Ελλάδα η κοινή γνώμη μέσω του δημοσιογραφικού κατεστημένου έχει συμφιλιωθεί με αυτή την εικόνα. Βλέπουμε διαρκώς έναν μηχανισμό θαψίματος υποθέσεων από το κυβερνών παρακράτος. Το κυβερνητικό σύστημα έστησε μηχανισμό παρακολούθησης του συνόλου της αντιπολίτευσης και της κυβέρνησης.

Εμείς στεκόμαστε απέναντι. Δεν εφησυχάζουμε. Ζητάμε απόλυτη διαφάνεια. Όσοι διαθέτουν κρίσιμα στοιχεία για την προμήθεια και χρήση παράνομου λογισμικού από κρατικές αρχές, όπως ο Dilian, οφείλουν να κληθούν ενώπιον των αρμόδιων επιτροπών και να καταθέσουν όλα τα αποδεικτικά στοιχεία. Κάθε άρνηση διερεύνησης, κάθε καθυστέρηση ή απόκρυψη αποδεικνύει συνενοχή. Εμείς εδώ έχουμε μια αποστολή: να φωνάξουμε με κάθε τρόπο πως κανείς δεν βρίσκεται υπεράνω του νόμου και καμία κυβέρνηση, κανένας μηχανισμός εξουσίας δεν μπορεί να χρησιμοποιεί παράνομα μέσα παρακολούθησης χωρίς λογοδοσία. Η δημοκρατία προστατεύεται μόνο όταν η αλήθεια αποκαλύπτεται, όσο ισχυρό κι αν είναι το σύστημα της συγκάλυψης.
3-0517-0000.englishText:
Madam President, our democracy is threatened. Illegal surveillance software is being turned against the elected representatives of citizens. The revelations about the surveillance of a Member of the European Parliament with illegal software may surprise Europe; unfortunately in Greece public opinion through the journalistic establishment has become reconciled with this picture. We constantly see a mechanism for burying cases by the ruling deep state. The governmental system set up a surveillance mechanism for the entire opposition and the government.

We stand against this. We do not become complacent. We demand absolute transparency. Those who possess critical evidence regarding the procurement and use of illegal software by state authorities, such as Dilian, must be summoned before the competent committees and submit all evidence. Every refusal to investigate, every delay or concealment proves complicity. We have a mission here: to shout in every way that no one is above the law and no government, no power mechanism can use illegal surveillance means without accountability. Democracy is protected only when the truth is revealed, no matter how powerful the cover-up system may be.

3-0518-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, liebe Menschen Europas! Medien und Journalismus werden häufig als vierte Gewalt der Demokratie bezeichnet. Auch wenn dies vielleicht nicht der traditionellen Gewaltenteilung entspricht, wird die Aussage deutlich: Freier Journalismus und investigative Recherche sind unabdingbar für unsere Demokratie. Das gilt auch dann, wenn Menschen aus der Politik in den Journalismus wechseln.

Wir können und dürfen die Spionageattacken auf den Europaabgeordneten und Journalisten Stelios Kouloglou nicht unkommentiert stehen lassen. Dass Politiker sowie Journalistinnen und Journalisten solche Eingriffe in ihre Privatsphäre fürchten müssen, wenn sie ihrer Arbeit nachgehen, ist absolut inakzeptabel und schädlich für die europäische Demokratie.

Demokratie kann nur funktionieren, wenn Menschen ohne Angst ihre Meinung äußern, Missstände aufdecken und Verantwortung einfordern können. Einschüchterung und Überwachung von Politikerinnen und Politikern, von Journalistinnen und Journalisten gefährden nicht nur eine einzelne Person, sondern auch das Vertrauen der Bürgerinnen und Bürger in unsere europäischen Institutionen.

Dementsprechend muss die Kommission handeln; ich glaube, das wissen Sie, ich glaube, das haben Sie verstanden. Wir müssen den Schutz vor Spyware zu einer Priorität machen, weil uns diese Problemstellung in unserer jetzigen Welt immer und immer wieder entgegentreten wird.

Hier geht es nicht nur um einen Einzelfall, hier geht es um die demokratische Kontrolle an sich. Der Schutz der Freiheit der Abgeordneten, der Schutz der Pressefreiheit bedeutet den Schutz unserer gemeinsamen europäischen Werte.
3-0518-0000.englishText:
Madam President, dear people of Europe! Media and journalism are often referred to as the fourth estate of democracy. Even if this may not correspond to the traditional separation of powers, the statement is clear: free journalism and investigative research are essential for our democracy. This also applies when people transition from politics into journalism.

We cannot and must not leave the cyberattacks on Member of the European Parliament and journalist Stelios Kouloglou without comment. The fact that politicians as well as female and male journalists have to fear such intrusions into their privacy when going about their work is absolutely unacceptable and damaging to European democracy.

Democracy can only function if people can express their opinions, uncover abuses, and demand accountability without fear. Intimidation and surveillance of politicians and journalists endanger not only an individual person, but also the trust of citizens in our European institutions.

Accordingly, the Commission must act; I believe you know this, I believe you have understood this. We must make protection against spyware a priority, because this problem will confront us again and again in our current world.

This is not just about an isolated case; this is about democratic control itself. Protecting the freedom of Members, protecting freedom of the press means protecting our shared European values.

3-0519-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, you all have your phones with you right now, as you have them at the negotiation table, at the dinner table, maybe even on your bedside table. And for some of you, someone else has been there too.

The spyware that hacked Stelios Kouloglou was silent. He didn't need to click on a link or open an attachment. So how would you know that your phone hasn't also been infected? One minute it's a private phone, the next it's the spy in your pocket.

And with the speed at which this technology is proliferating and the total lack of oversight we still allow, dear colleagues, exploits from Pegasus and Predator have already reached Russian government hackers and organised criminal groups. They are now out in the wild for anyone to use.

We urgently need to protect our democracy and our families from this threat. And this is a collective duty because any one of us can become the Trojan horse.

I get my phone checked regularly and I'm glad I know its status. Stelios got his checked and we should all be glad he did. There are certainly more people affected in this Chamber and in national parliaments across Europe. So, colleagues, get your phones checked. It is fast. It is confidential. It is very, very necessary. If you have questions you can ask me.

And one sentence to the Commission: three years ago, this Parliament wrote down how to fix it. It's your job to finally get it done. Because the greatest threat of spyware isn't what it does to our phones; it's what it does to our democracy and our security.

(The speaker agreed to take a blue-card question)

3-0520-0000.sourceText: Dear colleague, I wanted to ask you how often you check your phone, actually. But as you told us that you do it on a regular basis, could you maybe explain to the colleagues you don't do it how you can check your phone here inside the European Parliament?

3-0521-0000.sourceText:
I'm very happily doing that. We have an agency in the European Parliament – it's called DG ITEC. And we actually made this agency able to check all the phones because of our work in the Pegasus Committee, because we were kind of expecting us to be hacked at one point or another. It's quite frustrating to see it really happened.

Call DG ITEC, set up a meeting. They look at your phone, they go through whatever they have to go through, and within an hour or two they can tell you if you have been infected or not. Another way to do that is through Citizen Lab. That's the organisation that has worked together with Stelios, because he's no longer a Member of the European Parliament. They can even do it remotely.

So, as I told you, it's easy, it's fast, and I would suggest everybody does it because anyone can hack us, dear colleagues, including the Russians.

3-0522-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, dear colleagues, across our Union, spyware like Pegasus and Predator has been used against journalists, lawyers and politicians. In Hungary, journalists were hacked while investigating Orban's government. In Poland, our own colleague had his phone hacked three times by the former government. It reminds me of the former Czechoslovak communist secret police, who spied on everyone and everywhere. Back then, they didn't have the tools to listen to everything. Now governments do and they use them.

Nearly every Member State has purchased this technology. Almost none will submit to scrutiny. And when we as a Parliament asked for answers, most governments responded with silence. We cannot demand the rule of law from candidates while ignoring its erosion at home. We demand independent oversight, real whistleblower protection, and consequences for governments that stonewall our own committees. Democracy cannot defend itself in the dark.

3-0523-0000.sourceText:
Frau Präsidentin, Frau Kommissarin, Herr Minister! Wenn ein Mitglied eines Untersuchungsausschusses, der sich mit illegaler Verwendung von Spionagesoftware beschäftigt, während seiner Arbeit mit exakt jener Software, die Untersuchungsgegenstand ist, ausspioniert wird, dann ist das nichts anderes als ein massiver und unverfrorener Angriff auf Demokratie und Parlamentarismus. Und wenn tatsächlich dieselben Akteure dahinterstecken, die russische und belarussische Oppositionelle im Exil gezielt mit Spionagesoftware abgehört haben, ist das eine ungeheure Bedrohung unserer Souveränität und Auftrag, endlich entschieden zu handeln.

Europa wird von innen und außen angegriffen, und da kann nationale Sicherheit und darf nationale Sicherheit nicht das Aushebeln rechtsstaatlicher Prinzipien begründen. Bis heute wurde Predatorgate in Griechenland nicht lückenlos aufgeklärt: Wer hat den Auftrag zur Überwachung erteilt? Mit welchem Ziel? Alle Beteiligten sind zur Verantwortung zu ziehen.

Ein europäischer Rechtsakt mit klaren Mindeststandards für den Einsatz von Spyware ist überfällig, richterliche Kontrolle, strenge Aufsicht und wirksamer Schutz für Journalistinnen und Journalisten, Juristinnen, Juristen sowie Abgeordnete dringendst notwendig. Was muss noch passieren, damit die Kommission endlich handelt?
3-0523-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, Minister! When a member of a committee of inquiry dealing with the illegal use of spyware is spied upon during their work with the exact software that is the subject of the investigation, then this is nothing less than a massive and brazen attack on democracy and parliamentarism. And if indeed the very same actors are behind it who have systematically intercepted Russian and Belarusian dissidents in exile with spyware, this is an immense threat to our sovereignty and a mandate to finally act decisively.

Europe is being attacked from within and from without, and national security cannot and must not justify the undermining of the principles of the rule of law. To this day, the Predatorgate scandal in Greece has not been fully investigated: Who issued the order for surveillance? With what objective? All those involved must be held accountable.

A European legal act with clear minimum standards for the use of spyware is overdue; judicial control, strict oversight, and effective protection for journalists, lawyers, and members of parliament are urgently necessary. What more needs to happen before the Commission finally acts?

3-0524-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, señora comisaria, tuve el honor de ser miembro de la Comisión de Investigación de Pegasus la pasada legislatura y el sentido de la Comisión de Investigación es arrojar unas conclusiones que sean vinculantes para la Comisión, para que adopten iniciativas legislativas. Las recuerdo muy bien: un laboratorio europeo de referencia, y, sobre todo, declarar ilegal —por incompatible con la Carta de los Derechos Fundamentales de la Unión Europea— el uso de herramientas de espionaje masivo e indiscriminado; y no digamos el aspecto criminal que tiene su utilización contra periodistas, activistas, defensores de derechos humanos y nada menos que parlamentarios, porque Predator —que es la versión griega de Pegasus— ha sido utilizado contra Nikos Androulakis y contra Stelios Kouloglou, dos distinguidos miembros de este Parlamento Europeo, en su función parlamentaria, lo que es completamente inaceptable.

Por tanto, se tiene que declarar ilegal la utilización de un espionaje masivo y delictivo cuando se trata de espionaje contra activistas de derechos humanos, abogados o políticos y periodistas, porque solo puede ser utilizado con autorización judicial y contra criminalidad grave transnacional.

Por tanto, la Comisión está tardando en actuar y debe hacerlo.

(El orador acepta responder a una pregunta formulada con arreglo al procedimiento de la «tarjeta azul»)
3-0524-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Madam Commissioner, I had the honour of being a member of the Pegasus Inquiry Committee in the last parliamentary term, and the purpose of the Inquiry Committee is to deliver conclusions that are binding on the Commission so that it adopts legislative initiatives. I remember them very well: a European reference laboratory, and above all, declaring illegal —because it is incompatible with the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union— the use of mass and indiscriminate espionage tools; let alone the criminal aspect of its use against journalists, activists, human rights defenders and no less than parliamentarians, because Predator —which is the Greek version of Pegasus— has been used against Nikos Androulakis and Stelios Kouloglou, two distinguished members of this European Parliament, in their parliamentary function, which is completely unacceptable.

Therefore, the use of mass and criminal espionage must be declared illegal when it comes to espionage against human rights activists, lawyers or politicians and journalists, because it can only be used with judicial authorization and against serious transnational crime.

Therefore, the Commission is taking too long to act and must do so.

(The speaker agrees to take a blue-card question)

3-0525-0000.sourceText: ��blauen Karte“. – Vielen Dank, Herr Kollege, dass Sie die blaue Karte akzeptieren. Was wäre in Ihren Augen eine Sanktion, die wir gegenüber Mitgliedstaaten, die sich in dieser Art illegal verhalten, vorbringen sollten?
3-0525-0000.englishText: blue card. – Thank you, dear colleague, for accepting the blue card. In your view, what would be a sanction that we should bring forward against member states that behave illegally in this manner?

3-0526-0000.sourceText: ��blauen Karte“. – Es ist nicht nur illegal, es ist ein Verbrechen. Eine massive Spionage gegen Mitglieder des Europäischen Parlaments, mit den Rechtsanwälten, mit den Journalisten, das ist gegen die Charta der Grundrechte der Europäischen Union. Es sollte ein Verbrechen sein, und es sollte eine Strafe nach dem Strafgesetzbuch der Mitgliedstaaten der Europäischen Union nach sich ziehen.
3-0526-0000.englishText: blue card“. – It is not only illegal, it is a crime. Massive espionage against members of the European Parliament, with the lawyers, with the journalists, that is against the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union. It should be a crime, and it should entail a penalty under the penal code of the member states of the European Union.

3-0528-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, an MEP was allegedly spied on. There is a serious suspicion and must be investigated and responded to accordingly.

But let us not forget the bigger picture when it comes to illegal surveillance. Recently, French counterintelligence dismantled nine secret Chinese police stations on French soil. These secret networks were used by Beijing to monitor the Chinese diaspora and track down regime opponents in order to forcibly return them to China. That is what China tries to do across our continent: control the people who have escaped the control in China.

Those people do not have the services and protection that politicians have, but they do deserve protection. It means that we must clean Chinese surveillance networks off our streets.

3-0529-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, en Israel sus empresas de inteligencia militar nos pueden estar espiando a todos: a ciudadanos, a periodistas, pero también a diputados.

Hemos hablado de Stelios, un amigo, alguien que estaba investigando ese espionaje y resulta que estaba siendo a su vez espiado por el Gobierno griego con el software israelí Pegasus. Yo cené con él hace un par de semanas. ¿Estaba el Gobierno griego, o el de Israel, en esa cena? Es surrealista, es como encarcelar al bombero que intenta apagar un incendio.

En las distopías de Orwell, el Gran Hermano vigila a todo el mundo, pero aquí hemos ido un paso más allá: también se vigila a quien intenta demostrar que nos vigilan.

He oído al portavoz del Partido Popular de Polonia, que dice que es un gran peligro para la democracia. Pero, señorías del Partido Popular, han pasado tres años desde que el Parlamento aprobó sus recomendaciones y ustedes no han hecho absolutamente nada. ¿Por qué? ¿Quizás porque a ustedes no les espían, espían a sus adversarios políticos?
3-0529-0000.englishText:
Madam President, in Israel, their military intelligence companies may be spying on all of us: citizens, journalists, but also members of parliament.

We have talked about Stelios, a friend, someone who was investigating this espionage and turned out to be spied on in turn by the Greek government with the Israeli Pegasus software. I had dinner with him a couple of weeks ago. Was the Greek government, or Israel's, at that dinner? It is surreal, it is like imprisoning the firefighter trying to put out a fire.

In Orwell's dystopias, Big Brother watches everyone, but here we have gone a step further: we also watch those who try to prove that we are being watched.

I have heard the spokesperson for the Polish People's Party, who says it is a great danger to democracy. But, ladies and gentlemen of the People's Party, three years have passed since Parliament approved your recommendations and you have done absolutely nothing. Why? Perhaps because you are not being spied on, they are spying on your political adversaries?

3-0530-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, το σκάνδαλο υποκλοπών στην Ελλάδα, οι παρακολουθήσεις, και με κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά, ευρωβουλευτών, στρατιωτικών, δημοσιογράφων δεν είναι μεμονωμένα περιστατικά. Με ευρωενωσιακές οδηγίες και κανονισμούς, στην υλοποίησή τους από τις κυβερνήσεις, η παρακολούθηση των πάντων έγινε κανονικότητα. Η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση μάλιστα ζητά επειγόντως την έγκριση του επικίνδυνου κανονισμού μαζικής παρακολούθησης Chat Control. Από την υπόθεση Intellexa προκύπτει ότι τα κατασκοπευτικά λογισμικά επιτρέπονται από τον κανονισμό ειδών διπλής χρήσης. Είναι νόμιμη η ανάπτυξή τους· η αγορά από κρατικές υπηρεσίες, όπως η ΕΥΠ στην Ελλάδα· η χρήση τους με επίκληση της έννοιας-λάστιχου «εθνική ασφάλεια». Το ευρωενωσιακό θεσμικό πλαίσιο «ουδείς εξαιρείται των παρακολουθήσεων» μετατρέπει τις υποκλοπές, παράνομες και νόμιμες, σε εργαλείο καταστολής, πρωτίστως ενάντια στο εργατικό λαϊκό κίνημα που αγωνίζεται για τις σύγχρονες ανάγκες του.

Αυτό είναι το κράτος δικαίου της Ευρωπαϊκής Ένωσης που υπερασπίζονται τα άλλα κόμματα. Αυτά θέλει να κουκουλώσει και η κυβέρνηση της Νέας Δημοκρατίας. Η υπεράσπιση των λαϊκών δικαιωμάτων επιβάλλει τη ρήξη με την Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, κατάργηση των αντιδραστικών κανονισμών, απαγόρευση εμπορίας και χρήσης κατασκοπευτικών λογισμικών, αποκάλυψη και καταδίκη όλων των υπευθύνων.
3-0530-0000.englishText:
Madam President, the wiretapping scandal in Greece, the surveillance, and with spyware, of Members of the European Parliament, military personnel, journalists are not isolated incidents. With European Union directives and regulations, in their implementation by governments, the surveillance of everything has become the norm. The European Union even urgently requests the approval of the dangerous Chat Control mass surveillance regulation. From the Intellexa case, it emerges that spyware is permitted by the dual-use items regulation. Their development is legal; their purchase by state services, such as EYP in Greece; their use by invoking the elastic concept of "national security". The European Union institutional framework "no one is exempt from surveillance" turns wiretapping, illegal and legal, into a tool of repression, primarily against the workers' popular movement fighting for its modern needs.

This is the rule of law of the European Union defended by the other parties. These are also what the government of New Democracy wants to cover up. The defense of popular rights dictates a break with the European Union, the repeal of reactionary regulations, the ban on the trade and use of spyware, the exposure and condemnation of all those responsible.

3-0531-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, η Ευρώπη γεννήθηκε πάνω στα ερείπια ενός σκοτεινού παρελθόντος. Υποσχέθηκε στους πολίτες της ότι δεν θα φοβούνται ποτέ ξανά πως κάποιος ακούει πίσω από την πόρτα, διαβάζει τα γράμματά τους ή παρακολουθεί τις σκέψεις τους. Κι όμως, σήμερα ένας ακόμη ευρωβουλευτής —δεύτερος ευρωβουλευτής— αποκαλύπτεται ότι ήταν στόχος ισραηλινού κατασκοπευτικού λογισμικού. Όταν παρακολουθείται ένας ευρωβουλευτής, δεν κινδυνεύει μόνο ο ίδιος· κινδυνεύει η ελευθερία κάθε συνομιλίας, κάθε διαπραγμάτευσης, κάθε ψήφου μέσα σε αυτό το κοινοβούλιο. Υπάρχουν και άλλοι ευρωβουλευτές που παρακολουθήθηκαν; Μπορεί να είναι οποιοσδήποτε από μας. Το Κοινοβούλιο οφείλει να μας προστατεύσει. Η παρακολούθηση ενός ευρωβουλευτή είναι παραβίαση και προσβολή του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου.

Ζητώ από την Πρόεδρο να οργανώσει εθελοντικό έλεγχο ασφαλείας όλων των συσκευών των ευρωβουλευτών, να δούμε τι έκταση έχει πάρει αυτή η κατασκοπευτική απειλή, πόσοι παρακολουθούνται σήμερα. Ζητώ και από την Ευρωπαϊκή Επιτροπή, τη Europol και τον Ευρωπαίο Επόπτη Προστασίας Δεδομένων να διερευνήσουν ανεξάρτητα αυτή την ευρωπαϊκή υπόθεση.
3-0531-0000.englishText:
Madam President, Europe was born upon the ruins of a dark past. It promised its citizens that they would never again fear that someone is listening behind the door, reading their letters, or monitoring their thoughts. And yet, today another MEP—a second MEP—is revealed to have been the target of Israeli spyware. When an MEP is spied upon, it is not only they who are in danger; the freedom of every conversation, every negotiation, every vote within this parliament is in danger. Are there other MEPs who were spied upon? It could be any one of us. The Parliament owes it to us to protect us. The surveillance of an MEP is a violation and an insult to the European Parliament.

I ask the President to organize a voluntary security check of all MEPs' devices, to see how extensive this spying threat has become, how many are being spied upon today. I also ask the European Commission, Europol, and the European Data Protection Supervisor to independently investigate this European case.

3-0533-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, Minister, honourable Members, let me please restate once again: the Commission's position is unambiguous. Any attempts to illegally access data of citizens is unacceptable. The follow‑up and investigations into any alleged illegal use of spyware are, in the first place, a matter for national authorities.

Nonetheless, European Union law provides a comprehensive and clear set of safeguards which must be respected. I will repeat: EU data protection law fully applies to the processing of personal data by private entities, even where such processing is required by law for national security purposes.

EU data protection law is also applicable when public authorities process personal data for law enforcement and criminal justice purposes. When law enforcement authorities use intrusive surveillance software for these purposes, the Law Enforcement Directive applies. These rules must be respected, and national supervisory authorities and national courts have a crucial role to play in this respect, which we also see from the case at hand.

However, European law does not apply where public authorities directly access the data, not via telecom operator, and process them for genuine national security purposes. It flows from a European Court of Justice case‑law that threats to national security must not be interpreted over broadly and the Member States must be able to demonstrate them. It is also important to bear in mind that where European law is not applicable, the European Convention on Human Rights still applies.

Outside of data protection, there are several other relevant legislative instruments. The directive on attacks against information systems requires Member States to ensure that illegal systems access and illegal interception are punishable as a criminal offence in their national criminal law.

Ensuring a free and independent press is crucial. The European Media Freedom Act provides specific safeguards for journalists, for their families and sources regarding the use of spyware.

3-0534-0000.sourceText:
Madam President, thank you, Commissioner Dubravka Šuica, this has been an extremely informative debate, and it has shown that we need to actively protect our citizens, our press, our democratically elected politicians and our public institutions from all sorts of growing threats, but, of course, including cyberthreats and hacking.

All illegal use of spyware has to be investigated, stopped and investigated as appropriate by the national authorities. A lot has been done during the last few years, but we still have important work ahead of us. I can undertake that the Council and the Member States will continue to work closely with Parliament, with the elected Members here, and the Commission in this joint effort.

Our democracy is critical, and the protection of the rights of elected Members is in the interests of that democracy and the interests of the people. In the programme of the Irish Presidency, we describe protecting democracy as upholding the indispensable foundation of our Union. This requires a common effort from institutions and civil society alike in the spirit of a whole-of-government and a whole-of-society approach. What has been described here tonight in respect of the hacking of phones by this technology of ever increasing sophistication must be stopped, investigated and prosecuted by national authorities.

3-0537-0000.sourceText: Als nächster Punkt der Tagesordnung folgen die Erklärungen zur Abstimmung.
3-0537-0000.englishText: The next item on the agenda are the explanations of vote.

3-0539-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über die Ukraine.
3-0539-0000.englishText: We now come to the explanations of vote on the 2025 Commission report on Ukraine.

3-0540-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea Raportului privind Ucraina pentru că, în primul rând, susțin Ucraina în a câștiga acest război pornit de către Rusia agresivă împotriva ei.

Mai mult decât atât, acest raport prevede pentru a doua oară următoarea situație: ia act de faptul că Parlamentul Ucrainei a adoptat o lege care permite parohiilor ortodoxe din Ucraina, aflate sub jurisdicția Patriarhiei Ortodoxe a Moscovei, să se dezafilieze de la Biserica Ortodoxă Rusă și să decidă cu privire la propria lor afiliere. În Ucraina există astăzi sute de parohii ortodoxe românești care doresc să iasă de sub jurisdicția Patriarhiei Moscovei și să își creeze propria structură ecleziastică bisericească în Ucraina.

Acest raport laudă, în acest sens, ia act de faptul că, în august 2024, parohiile ortodoxe românești din Ucraina au depus o cerere de recunoaștere a asociației religioase - Biserica Ortodoxă Română din Ucraina. Și raportul solicită Ucrainei, autorităților ucrainene să recunoască această asociație.
3-0540-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I voted in favour of the Report on Ukraine because, first of all, I support Ukraine in winning this war started against it by aggressive Russia.

Furthermore, this report provides for the second time the following situation: it takes note of the fact that the Parliament of Ukraine adopted a law allowing the Orthodox parishes in Ukraine, under the jurisdiction of the Moscow Orthodox Patriarchate, to disaffiliate from the Russian Orthodox Church and decide on their own affiliation. Today in Ukraine there are hundreds of Romanian Orthodox parishes that want to break away from the jurisdiction of the Moscow Patriarchate and create their own ecclesiastical church structure in Ukraine.

In this regard, this report praises, takes note of the fact that, in August 2024, the Romanian Orthodox parishes in Ukraine submitted an application for the recognition of the religious association - the Romanian Orthodox Church in Ukraine. And the report asks Ukraine, the Ukrainian authorities, to recognize this association.

3-0542-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über Moldau.
3-0542-0000.englishText: We now come to the explanations of vote on the 2025 Commission report on Moldova.

3-0544-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu dem Bericht 2025 der Kommission über Serbien.
3-0544-0000.englishText: We now come to the explanations of vote on the 2025 Commission Report on Serbia.

3-0545-0000.sourceText:
Doamnă președintă, am votat în favoarea Raportului privind Serbia, în primul rând, pentru că susțin Serbia. Poți să ai o serie de critici la adresa Serbiei, la adresa Guvernului Serbiei, însă e important ca Serbia să fie susținută în acest proces de integrare europeană.

În plus de asta, la o serie de amendamente pe care le-am făcut, acest raport prevede, pentru prima dată în istoria Parlamentului European, ca autoritățile sârbești să nu mai facă distincție între comunitatea vlahă - sau etichetată ca vlahă - și comunitatea românească din Serbia. Cele două comunități etnice sunt aceeași comunitate românească. Că unii le spun vlahi, că alții le spun români, este irelevant. Ambele comunități sunt comunități românești și e important ca autoritățile sârbești să recunoască lucrul acesta.

Al doilea lucru pe care l-am cerut este ca Episcopiei Ortodoxe Române din Serbia să i se permită extinderea jurisdicției asupra întregului teritoriu al Serbiei - lucru care astăzi nu este permis. Sunt convins că acest raport va avea soluții benefice pentru comunitatea românească ortodoxă din Serbia și îi felicit pe colegii care l-au votat.
3-0545-0000.englishText:
Madam President, I voted in favour of the Report on Serbia, first of all, because I support Serbia. You can have a number of criticisms regarding Serbia, regarding the Government of Serbia, but it is important for Serbia to be supported in this European integration process.

In addition to this, following a series of amendments that I made, this report provides, for the first time in the history of the European Parliament, that the Serbian authorities should no longer make a distinction between the Vlach community - or labelled as Vlach - and the Romanian community in Serbia. The two ethnic communities are the same Romanian community. Whether some call them Vlachs, whether others call them Romanians, is irrelevant. Both communities are Romanian communities and it is important for the Serbian authorities to recognise this.

The second thing I asked for is that the Romanian Orthodox Diocese in Serbia be allowed to extend its jurisdiction over the entire territory of Serbia - something that is not permitted today. I am convinced that this report will have beneficial solutions for the Romanian Orthodox community in Serbia and I congratulate the colleagues who voted for it.

3-0546-0000.sourceText:
Gospa predsednica, ljudje v Srbiji evropske vrednote branijo bolj pogumno kot marsikdo v tej dvorani. Podpore od Evropske unije, vsaj tiste na najvišji ravni, ne dobijo niti malo, kvečjemu nasprotno. Potem se pa čudite, zakaj v Srbiji ni zaupanja v Evropsko unijo. Od kdaj je stabilnost brez demokracije stabilnost in od kdaj se sporočila za nenapredek pošiljajo z idejami o odpiranju novih pristopnih poglavij? V tem poročilu, ki sem ga seveda podprla, smo upravičeno ostri - vsaj nekdo, kajne? Ker v Evropskem parlamentu si vsaj še upamo reči bobu bob.

Ni pa to poročilo ocena Srbije kot države, ni ocena ljudi, je ocena oblasti. Moja podpora gre ljudem v Srbiji tistim, ki se borijo proti korupciji, za svobodne medije in za državo, v kateri zakon velja za vse. Njihova prihodnost je evropska.

Pa če smo že pri času za odpiranje novih poglavij oziroma poglavja številka 3 – absolutno. Prvo poglavje: demokracija, drugo: odgovornost in tretje: institucije, ki delujejo. Dokler tega ni, pa pač ne morete odpirati nekih drugih poglavij, gospa von der Leyen, odprite raje oči.
3-0546-0000.englishText:
Madam President, people in Serbia defend European values more courageously than many in this chamber. They receive little to no support from the European Union, at least at the highest level, quite the contrary. Then you wonder why there is no trust in the European Union in Serbia. Since when is stability without democracy stability, and since when are messages for non-progress sent with ideas of opening new accession chapters? In this report, which I naturally supported, we are rightfully harsh—at least someone, right? Because in the European Parliament, we at least still dare to call a spade a spade.

However, this report is not an assessment of Serbia as a country, nor is it an assessment of the people, it is an assessment of the authorities. My support goes to the people in Serbia, those who are fighting against corruption, for free media, and for a country where the law applies to everyone. Their future is European.

And since we are on the subject of the time for opening new chapters, or rather chapter number 3 – absolutely. Chapter one: democracy, chapter two: accountability, and chapter three: institutions that work. Until that is the case, you simply cannot open some other chapters, Ms von der Leyen, open your eyes instead.

3-0548-0000.sourceText: Wir kommen nun zu den Erklärungen zur Abstimmung zu den Folgen der türkischen Invasion von 1974 für zyprische Frauen und Mädchen, den von den türkischen Streitkräften verübten Verbrechen und den Konsequenzen für die Gleichstellung der Geschlechter.
3-0548-0000.englishText: We now come to the explanations of vote on the consequences of the 1974 Turkish invasion for Cypriot women and girls, the crimes committed by the Turkish armed forces, and the consequences for gender equality.

3-0549-0000.sourceText:
Κυρία Πρόεδρε, καταδικάζουμε την τουρκική εισβολή και κατοχή της Κύπρου, τα αποτρόπαια εγκλήματα που διέπραξε ο τουρκικός στρατός σε βάρος Κυπρίων, γυναικών και κοριτσιών, τον βίαιο εκτοπισμό, τη σεξουαλική κακοποίηση, τους βιασμούς, τον διαχωρισμό των οικογενειών, το τραύμα, τον στιγματισμό και τις ανυπολόγιστες μακροπρόθεσμες βαριές συνέπειές τους, στερούμενες και την παραμικρή στήριξη. Πέραν από την αυτονόητη αποζημίωση που υποχρεούται το τουρκικό κράτος να καταβάλει στα θύματά του, απαιτούμε να ανοίξουν τα κλειστά στρατιωτικά αρχεία, να γίνει αποτελεσματική έρευνα στα Κατεχόμενα με ταυτοποίηση και απόδοση των λειψάνων, αποζημίωση, στήριξη των οικογενειών των αγνοουμένων μέχρι να διακριβωθεί κάθε αγνοούμενος.

Και σήμερα, 52 χρόνια από την εισβολή, 32 από την ένταξη της Κύπρου στην Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, η απάντηση ενάντια στα διχοτομικά σχέδια και τη ΝΑΤΟποίηση του νησιού είναι: Κύπρος ανεξάρτητη, ένα και όχι δύο κράτη, μία και μόνη κυριαρχία, ιθαγένεια, διεθνής προσωπικότητα, με άμεση αποχώρηση των κατοχικών στρατευμάτων, χωρίς εγγυητές και προστάτες, χωρίς ξένα στρατεύματα και βάσεις, κοινή πατρίδα Ελληνοκυπρίων-Τουρκοκυπρίων με τον λαό της αφέντη στον τόπο του.
3-0549-0000.englishText:
Madam President, we condemn the Turkish invasion and occupation of Cyprus, the heinous crimes committed by the Turkish army against Cypriot people, women and children, the violent displacement, sexual abuse, rapes, separation of families, the trauma, the stigmatization and their incalculable long-term heavy consequences, lacking even the slightest support. Beyond the self-evident compensation that the Turkish state is obliged to pay to its victims, we demand the opening of the closed military archives, an effective investigation in the Occupied Territories with identification and return of remains, compensation, and support for the families of the missing persons until the fate of every missing person is ascertained.

And today, 52 years since the invasion, 32 years since Cyprus's accession to the European Union, the response against partition plans and the NATOization of the island is: an independent Cyprus, one and not two states, a single sovereignty, citizenship, international personality, with the immediate withdrawal of the occupying forces, without guarantors and protectors, without foreign troops and bases, a common homeland of Greek Cypriots and Turkish Cypriots with its people as master in their own land.

3-0550-0000.sourceText:
Señora presidenta, durante mis mandatos como presidente de la Comisión de Libertades, Justicia y Asuntos de Interior, tuve el honor de ser el ponente permanente para las personas desaparecidas en Chipre, cuya parte norte fue invadida por Turquía en 1974. Por tanto, me comprometí con esos miles de personas desaparecidas cuyas familias esperan todavía reparación y justicia.

Hemos votado sobre una propuesta de Resolución que incide sobre un aspecto sensible: la violación masiva de derechos humanos que supuso la violencia sexual perpetrada contra mujeres y niñas en la ocupación del norte de Chipre. Y, sin duda, la propuesta de Resolución incide en la igualdad de género, en los derechos humanos y en el Estado de Derecho.

Pero lo cierto es que hay una cuenta pendiente en la que esta Unión Europea se tiene que comprometer plenamente. Esa cuenta pendiente tiene una dimensión con Turquía, que todavía figura en la lista de los Estados candidatos a la adhesión, pero sobre todo con Chipre, cuya integridad territorial nacional continúa pendiente y en cuyo Parlamento nacional todavía hay asientos vacantes que esperan la representación de la comunidad turca de Chipre del Norte.
3-0550-0000.englishText:
Madam President, during my terms as Chair of the Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs, I had the honour of being the permanent rapporteur for missing persons in Cyprus, the northern part of which was invaded by Turkey in 1974. Therefore, I committed myself to those thousands of missing persons whose families are still waiting for reparation and justice.

We have voted on a motion for a resolution that focuses on a sensitive aspect: the massive violation of human rights represented by the sexual violence perpetrated against women and girls in the occupation of northern Cyprus. And, undoubtedly, the motion for a resolution focuses on gender equality, human rights and the rule of law.

But the truth is that there is unfinished business in which this European Union must fully commit itself. That unfinished business has a dimension concerning Turkey, which is still on the list of candidate countries for accession, but above all concerning Cyprus, whose national territorial integrity remains pending and in whose national parliament there are still vacant seats awaiting the representation of the Turkish community of Northern Cyprus.

3-0551-0000.englishText: This item on the agenda is now closed.

3-0555-0000.sourceText:
Die nächste Sitzung findet morgen, Donnerstag, den 9. Juli 2026, um 8.00 Uhr statt.

Die Tagesordnung wurde veröffentlicht und ist auf der Website des Europäischen Parlaments verfügbar.
3-0555-0000.englishText:
The next sitting will take place tomorrow, Thursday, 9 July 2026, at 8.00 a.m.

The agenda has been published and is available on the European Parliament's website.

3-0557-0000.sourceText:
Das Protokoll dieser Sitzung wird dem Parlament morgen zu Beginn der Nachmittagssitzung zur Genehmigung vorgelegt.

Die Sitzung ist hiermit geschlossen, und ich möchte mich bei den Dolmetschern für die Unterstützung während der heutigen Plenarsitzung bedanken.
3-0557-0000.englishText:
The minutes of this sitting will be submitted to Parliament for approval tomorrow at the beginning of the afternoon sitting.

The sitting is hereby closed, and I would like to thank the interpreters for their support during today's plenary sitting.
